articleTitle: Influence of Sintering Voids on Thermal Resistance of MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the advancement of information technology and power electronics, there is an increasing demand for semiconductor devices with smaller volumes and higher power densities. Therefore, excellent heat dissipation capability is crucial for maintaining the performance and reliability of power semiconductor devices. For power semiconductor devices like MOSFETs, the chip functions as the primary heat source. The heat generated by the chip primarily dissipates through sintered solder, making the quality of the sintered solder layer a pivotal factor in determining the heat dissipation characteristics of the device. However, sintered voids, a common process defect, can significantly hinder heat flow, resulting in an elevation in the junction temperature. To investigate this phenomenon, we prepared MOSFET samples with varying sintered void configurations by adjusting the sintering processes. Utilizing finite element simulation and thermal resistance measurements, we examined the impact of void proportion, position, and distribution on the thermal resistance of MOSFETs. Our findings indicate that increasing the proportion of sintered voids from 1 % to 40% leads to a rise in thermal resistance by 60.5% for devices with a single central void, by 47.3 % for those with a single corner void, and by 49.3% for devices with dispersed voids. This variation is primarily attributed to the influence of sintered voids on the heat conduction path. This comprehensive study is expected to enhance the process reliability of MOSFETs and assist in establishing user screening criteria.

articleTitle: Removal Method of Sidewall Scalloping in TSVs for Silicon Interposers and Applications of Smooth Vertical Cavities in Wafer-Level System Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: When fabricating through-silicon-vias (TSVs) for interposers using a Bosch process to etch deep vias, scallops are usually generated on the sidewalls of the vias, which can lead to early device failure. In this paper, we present a practical method to reduce the sidewall scallops of deeply etched vias, employing a post-etching process with a low-concentration potassium hydroxide (KOH)-based solution. After etching in the KOH-based solution for 20 hours, the scallops on the sidewalls of the deeply etched vias became virtually unnoticeable, and the surface roughness was improved to less than 5 nm. The experimental results showed that the relatively low concentration of KOH, coupled with the addition of Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) significantly reduced the sidewall scallops, while having negligible impact on the morphology of the vias. The process was carried out at room temperature instead of a high temperature annealing step, and was fully compatible with the backend of line (BEOL) processes. Besides, as an application of our sidewall scalloping removal method, vertical Fabry-Perot cavities were deeply etched on a silicon wafer and subsequently smoothed using the post-etching process. The clear observation of the Fabry-Perot interference spectrum was attributed to the smooth and vertical sidewalls, which significantly reduced light reflection losses. This measurement result indicated the potential for fabricating a variety of optical MEMS (Micro Electromechanical Systems) devices integrated in the silicon interposers using a combination of the Bosch process and post-etching technique.

articleTitle: Transient Electrical-Thermal-Mechanical Coupling Model and Short-Circuit Failure Analysis of Wire-Bonded IGBT Module
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The short-circuit (SC) failure of wire-bonded IGBT module (WB-IGBT) was investigated by combining testing and transient finite element (FE) simulation. First, the SC tests were conducted to 1.2-kV/75-A WB-IGBTs, and the characteristic parameters variations during the SC failure process were obtained. The failed modules were inspected by scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Second, the transient electrical-thermal-mechanical (ETM) coupling FE model for WB-IGBT was proposed, and the SC failure process was simulated. The weak points and failure mechanism were analyzed. Third, the effects of the metallization layer thickness and the bonding wires radius on the stress at the bonding points were simulated and analyzed. The results indicated that the bonding wires lifted off due to the high stress caused by the high SC current. Increasing the metallization layer thickness as well as the bonding wires radius helped to reduce the stress at the bonding points.

articleTitle: 3D Printing Electrodes in Micro Shell Resonant Gyroscope Heads
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The micro shell resonant gyroscope <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mu \text{SRG})$</tex> is a solid-state vibration gyroscope based on elastic wave precession at the micro shell resonator rim with high precision, simple structure, and long-term reliability. The fabrication of driving/detecting electrodes for high precision excitation and measurement is of great importance and remains challenging. This paper reports the design, fabrication, and characterization of a 3D printable lateral conformal cylindrical electrodes for the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \text{SRG}$</tex>. With the 3D printing process, the electrode structure is fabricated in only two steps. It creates a controlled capacitance gap and simultaneously metalized resonator and transverse electrodes. An umbrella-shaped cylindrical electrode structure is 3D printed to ensure that the separate lateral electrodes are at different potentials after metal film coating. This work has demonstrated a potential mass-produced <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \text{SRGs}$</tex>, paving the way for the development of portable inertial navigation micro hemispherical resonator gyroscopes.

articleTitle: Reliability of Graphene Enhanced Thermal Interface Material under Mechanical Cycling
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The requirement for efficient heat transfer to ensure the reliable operation of electronics devices is paramount. Thermal interface materials (TIMs), such as thermal grease and phase change materials, are extensively used globally to reduce thermal contact resistance and ensure optimal performance. In this paper, reliability of a graphene-enhanced TIM is characterized. In real applications, under certain circumstances, TIMs may experience mechanical compression or external pressure, leading to repetitive compression. This compression can affect the performance and mechanical stability of the TIMs. To study this, a Micron-Displacement Pressure Measurement Device with elevated ambient temperature measurement capability is used. This equipment enables us to study mechanical compression at specific temperatures and pressures, allowing the TIM to undergo multiple cycles of compression. In total, the mechanical cycling tests were done up to 5000 cycles. Through this procedure, the durability and potential fatigue damage of the graphene enhanced TIM is studied. The results show that the graphene enhanced TIM does not have significant thermal or mechanical degradation up to 5000 cycles. This suggests that reliability of the graphene enhanced TIM under mechanical loading is extremely good leading to potential use in electronics power module cooling applications.

articleTitle: Dynamic Pin Pulling Modeling for the Micro-Pads of High Density Packaging Substrate
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: High-density ball grid arry (BGA) package substrates with micro-pads can experience failure phenomena such as pad stripping, falling off, and even cratering throughout the entire process from electronic packaging to normal operational service. Among these, physical contact, multiple reflow soldering, rework processing, repeated power cycling, and drop impacts are significant causes leading to pad failures. In industrial applications, board-level drop, vibration, shock, and collision tests are typically employed to evaluate the fatigue strength of pads under repetitive loading. The reliability of these pads has become a focal point of industry concern. Currently, there is a lack of dynamic testing technology in the industry that is affordable, highly stable, and easily adoptable for measuring the delamination strength of fine-pitched pads. This paper, building upon our team's previous work on static pad testing and the contents of IPC-9708 standard, establishes a dynamic testing technique for fine-pitched pads under certain acceleration and exemplifies its application using bare pads (O pad) through ANSYS simulation analysis. This technology more accurately simulates the actual stress conditions experienced by pads in use, thereby enabling a more precise assessment of pad reliability. Furthermore, by employing dynamic simulations, curves that align with real-world scenarios are obtained, providing strong support for subsequent analysis of key factors influencing pad failure.

articleTitle: PFAS-Free Underfill Material Evaluation for FCBGA Package
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Per- and poly-fluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are man-made chemical substances with high stability and persistence to prove Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs). PFAS can exist in the environment for a long time and accumulate in humans to cause cancer. Due to the environmental impact and persistence of PFAS, more and more countries around the world are considering legislation to ban the use of PFAS. PF AS is widely used in the consumer and semiconductor industry. PFAS plays an important role in the semiconductor industry to banning PF AS will be a huge challenge. Following the requirements of environmental protection, most industries are also beginning to evaluate PFAS-free materials to meet these environmental requirements by implementing PF AS controls. PF AS is contained as a surface treatment agent in underfill materials for the assembly package. This paper discusses alternative materials and challenges for PF AS. Both the PFAS-free underfill and the PFAS-containing underfill material are analyzed the material properties by thermal analysis instruments such as Thermal Mechanical Analyzer (TMA) and Dynamic Mechanic Analyzer (DMA). In this paper, the fluidity test, shear strength, underfill void, fillet height/ width, and package warpage are evaluated to compare PFAS-containing underfill with PF AS-free underfill. The PF AS-free underfill can pass reliability. PF AS- free underfill is succussed to replace PF AS-containing underfill.

articleTitle: LC Virtual Separation Method: An Accurate Modelling Approach for Equivalent Circuit Models of Complex TSV Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this paper, the capacitance characteristics of the TSV structure are analysed from the viewpoint of electromagnetic simulation and circuit simulation. It is concluded that the method of superposing and summing the capacitance of each decomposed structure is not applicable to this structure. On this basis, a method to obtain an equivalent circuit model (ECM) of the TSV structure is proposed based on de-embedding - the LC virtual separation method. The model is validated by testing in the frequency range of 0–40 GHz.

articleTitle: Thermomechanical Analysis of SiC Power Module Based on Insulating Metal Substrate with High Thermal Conductivity Epoxy Resin
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: This article presents a power module based on thick-copper insulating metal substrate (IMS), where epoxy resin (EP) with high thermal conductivity, ranging from 1 (W/mK) to 15 (W/mK), is used as the insulation layer. A 2.5mm thick-copper layer under the power device is adopted for high thermal capacity, which is crucial to reduce the transient temperature swing of the power module, especially for operating in heavy-load with high pulse current. Compared with the conventional structure based on Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>-AMB (active metal brazing) substrates, the proposed power module with IMS substrate allows a similar thermal resistance when the thermal conductivity of the EP layer reaches 3.97 (W/mK), for the specific power module built for this study. Moreover, when the EP reaches a thermal conductivity of 15 (W/mK), the IMS-based power module would enable a junction temperature 12.86% lower than the one based on Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>-AMB. In addition, the thermal time constant of the IMS-based module is 244.87% longer than the one built on the AMB substrate, allowing a 15°C reduction in temperature swing when 50 W of power cycles is applied, which is crucial for the thermomechanical reliability of the power module.

articleTitle: A Soluble Polyimide Improves the Performance of UV-Curable Solder Resist
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: UV-curable solder resist (SR) is widely used in advanced packaging substrate. However, due to the network structure generated by the photothermal double curing reaction, the elongation at break and heat resistance of UV-curable SR film cannot meet the requirement of advanced packaging substrate with high reliability. Although polyimide has the advantages of high elongation at break and high heat resistance, its application in UV-curable SR is limited due to its difficulty in dissolving in organic solvents. In this paper, we try to apply soluble polyimide (SPI) to the field of UV-curable SR by regulating the solubility of SPI and the formula of UV-curable SR. The results show that the solubility of SPI can be improved by adjusting the flexibility of the chemical structure and reducing the molecular weight of the polymer. The excellent solubility of SPI can greatly improve the elongation at break of UV-curable SR (elongation at break of 8.4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>). In addition, the introduction of SPI has also improved the thermal stability of UV-curable SR (glass transition temperature <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(T_{g})$</tex> of 185.07 °C, 5% thermal weight loss <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(T_{5\%})$</tex> of 335.1 °C). Moreover, the introduced SPI can also reduce the dielectric constant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(D_{k})$</tex> and dielectric loss <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(D_{f})$</tex> of the film <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(D_{k}$</tex>= 2.86@5 GHz, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D_{f}=0.0151{@}5$</tex> GHz). However, due to the limited solubility of SPI and epoxy acrylate resin systems, excessive SPI content of the UV-curable SR formula will cause internal phase separation, resulting in performance degradation of the UV-curable SR film. In summary, the SPI developed in this work has great potential application for improving the performance of UV-curable SR for advanced packaging in the future.

articleTitle: Numerical Modeling and Experimental Study on Wafer Warpage of Embedded Interconnect Bridge in Organic Interposer
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) and high-performance computing (HPC) applications continue to grow in sophistication, the demand for data transfer is also increasing, which poses novel challenges to memory bandwidth and input/output (I/O) density. Faced with the limitations of traditional organic interposer in high density and multifunctionality, a localized ultra-fine interconnect multi-chip heterogeneous integration solution using embedded interconnect bridge in organic interposer is presented in this paper. However, the mismatch of coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) between silicon-based bridge-chips and Ajinomoto Build-up Film (ABF) can cause wafer deformation under thermal stress, which is a critical issue that needs to be controlled effectively for successful subsequent processes of embedded interposer package. Aiming to analyze the problem of wafer warpage in embedded interposer package, a four-layer model is proposed with a bridge-chip embedded layer, a top build-up layer, a core layer that contains copper clad laminates (CCL), and a bottom build-up layer. Furthermore, the finite element analysis (FEA) is validated through Shadow Moiré experiment. The error between simulation and experimental results is less than 5%, which indicates that the four-layer model can predict wafer warpage behavior with high precision. In the warpage optimization analysis, the impact of structural parameters of embedded bridge-chips such as thickness, dimension, distance and height of copper pillars on wafer warpage is investigated based on the design of simulation approach and Taguchi method. It is found that the bridge-chip dimension is the critical factor controlling the wafer warpage behavior, and reducing it can significantly lessen the warpage.

articleTitle: Size Effect of IMC Growth in Liquid-Solid Reflow Reaction at SAC305/Cu Interface
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the advancement of 3D packaging, the dramatic reduction in solder joint dimensions significantly impacts interface reactions, the formation of intermetallic compounds (IMCs) at interfaces, and the evolution of grains within the solder. Notably, the reaction of Sn from the solder with Cu from the substrate forms brittle IMCs at the interface, critically affecting the reliability of solder joints. This study investigates the growth of IMCs in SAC305/Cu solder joints of varying sizes under different reflow time. Furthermore, it simulates the temperature field during the reflow process to explore the impact of solder size on the growth behavior of interface IMCs. Results demonstrate that as solder joint size increases from 300 μm to 600 μm, the thickness of the interface IMC layer decreases, with Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> being the predominant IMC. At 60 seconds of reflowing, with the increase in solder size, the most of Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> grain morphology transformed scallop shape to roof shape. Additionally, the most of Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> grain transformed ridge shape to scallop shape with the increase of reflow time. Kinetic analysis of IMC thickness growth reveals that with decreasing solder joint size, the growth mechanism of interface IMCs transitions from bulk diffusion-dominated to grain boundary diffusion-dominated. Simulations of the temperature field show that, within the initial one second of reflow soldering, solder joint temperature exhibits a pronounced size effect. Smaller joints achieve higher temperatures under identical reflow time, providing a greater nucleation driving force, resulting in smaller, more numerous Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> grains in the early stages of reflowing. Therefore, small size solder joints quickly complete the transition from ridge shaped to scallop shaped.

articleTitle: A Rapid Thermal Analysis Approach for Power Module Design Considering Non-Linear Thermal Conductivity
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The evaluation and analysis of the thermal characteristics of power modules is a crucial aspect of power module design. However, as the operating temperature of the module increases, thermal conductivity cannot be considered a constant. Its thermal analysis becomes a non-linear problem, rendering the existing approaches ineffective in accurately calculating the thermal characteristics of power modules. This constrains the design and application of power modules. Therefore, this paper proposed a rapid thermal analysis approach based on the Kirchhoff transform for evaluating the steady-state temperature distribution of power modules, taking into account thermal conductivity nonlinearity. This approach is capable of calculating results when thermal conductivity is nonlinear, based on the results of constant thermal conductivity. Its accuracy is verified by simulation. The error is reduced to half of its original value. Furthermore, the computation is completed in less than O. Ss. The proposed approach has the potential to widen the temperature range of power module design and is of considerable significance.

articleTitle: Plated Copper on Thick Film Ceramic Substrates and Their Packaging Applications for Deep-Ultraviolet LEDs
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Direct plated copper (DPC) ceramic substrates are gradually increasing their application scope in power electronic device packaging due to their advantages of excellent thermal conductivity and high integration density (vertical interconnection). However, the working reliability of DPC ceramic substrates under high temperatures (above <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$300\ ^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>) is far from satisfactory, behaving as low bonding strength at the interface of metal layer and ceramic. In order to fix this problem, a new style of plated copper on thick film (PCTF) ceramic substrate was proposed for this work. The shear strength at the interface of the Ag layer and ceramic substrate is up to 80 MPa, which is 60% higher than that of DPC substrate, and the tensile strength is above 32.2 MPa, which is 165% higher than that of DPC substrates. In addition, the shear strength between the Cu and Ag layers is up to 88.5 MPa, with a tensile strength of more than 23.44 MPa. Moreover, packaging DUV LEDs with PCTF substrates in our experiments. As a result, the packaged DUV LED presented good optical and thermal properties. The PCTF ceramic substrate designed in this work showed great potential application in high-power device packaging.

articleTitle: Application Research of Intelligent PID Parameter Optimization Algorithm for XY Linear Motor Motion Platform in Wire Bonder
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In the domain of semiconductor packaging, the efficacy and efficiency of wire bonder hold paramount importance for product integrity and manufacturing productivity. The XY linear motor motion platform, constituting a pivotal element within wire bonder, intricately dictates the precision and stability of the bonding procedure. While conventional PID controllers offer a degree of control over XY linear motor motion platforms, their parameter optimization often necessitates extensive empirical iterations and frequently falls short of achieving optimal control outcomes. Confronted with sizable quantities of inconsistently performing motors and intricate production settings, this predicament substantially escalates production expenditures while concurrently diminishing operational efficiency. Herein, a novel approach utilizing BP neural networks for real-time PID parameter auto-tuning is proposed, markedly enhancing tuning efficiency vis-à-vis manual methodologies. Addressing the inherent challenge of initializing weights and thresholds in BP neural networks, this study advocates for the adoption of the artificial fish swarm algorithm to optimize the initial weight selection, culminating in the design of the AFSA-BP-PID controller. Subsequently, leveraging the dynamic model of Permanent Magnet Linear Synchronous Motors (PMLSM), a Matlab/Simulink simulation framework is constructed to juxtapose and scrutinize the dynamic error and tuning duration of PID, BP-PID, and AFSA-BP-PID controllers. The findings evince the efficacy of the AFSA-BP-PID control algorithm in augmenting the dynamic performance of permanent magnet synchronous linear motors while concurrently abbreviating system tuning intervals.

articleTitle: Study on Modification of Epoxy Resin Reinforcing Adhesive Commonly Used in Aerospace Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Epoxy resin reinforcing adhesive has become the most commonly used reinforcing adhesive in the aerospace field because of its wide bonding range, high bonding strength, small coefficient of thermal expansion, and no volatile substances after curing. At present, the mainly used epoxy adhesives, such as DG-4, HY-916, etc., are all two-component adhesives, which need to be mixed before use. However, due to the good fluidity after preparation, and the need to restrict the flow of adhesive under typical working conditions, the adhesive could not be dispensed until the viscosity of the glue is suitable by standing at room temperature for a period of time. In this study, DG-4 epoxy resin adhesive was selected for doping modification. Three doping species were selected, namely polyamide wax, modified hydrogenated castor oil and hydrophobic nano-SiO2. And the optimal doping method of the adhesive was obtained by adjusting the doping species and the doping amount. Through the kinetic viscosity test and shear strength test, the glue doped with 5% (mass fraction) polyamide wax has the best performance. The thixotropic coefficient of the glue increased from 0.864 to 1.093, while the shear strength increased slightly, which was because that the polar groups on the surface of the doped material were fully activated in the adhesive environment to form swelling particles, and the hydrogen bonds between the swelling particles and the interaction force between the doped material and the epoxy resin matrix could bear a certain load, which was conducive to stress transmission. In addition, there were no significant changes in the glass transition temperature (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>), coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) and thermal vacuum outgassing properties of the doped glue. Furthermore, the doped adhesive has passes the reliability assessment and can be used in aerospace products. In general, this study improved the operating performance of adhesive under typical working conditions. The proposed modification method not only ensured the microscopic immersion, but also avoided adhesive flow at the macroscopic level, which reduced the difficulty of operation and improved production efficiency while ensuring product quality.

articleTitle: Design of Miniaturized Package for SiC High-Voltage Device
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this paper, a miniature packaging solution for SiC high-voltage device is presented. The solution involves assembling a single SiC device by soldering between two ceramic substrates, utilizing metal post switches and then filling the gap with potting material. With dual ceramic substrates design in the package, the miniature packaging is characterized by small size, high voltage and double-sided cooling structure. The ceramic substrates are designed and manufactured using DPC (direct copper plating) technology along with through-ceramic-vias (TCV s) to deliver structural support, current paths, and channels for heat dissipation. Compared to T0247 packages, the miniaturized packages exhibit a reduction in size by 90% and a decrease in parasitic inductance by 80%. The high-voltage insulation tests conducted demonstrate that the miniaturized package can endure voltages up to 3 kV while maintaining a low leakage current in the nanoampere range.

articleTitle: Electromigration Behavior of Cu/Sn-58Bi/Cu Solder Joints Under Alternating Current Stressing
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The electromigration (EM) behavior of ball grid array (BGA) Cu/Sn-58Bi/Cu solder joints under alternating current (AC) stressing with different frequencies at a current density 1.2×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> was investigated systematically in this study. The microstructure and shear performance of solder joints after EM were analyzed through scanning electron microscope (SEM) and dynamic mechanical analyze (DMA), respectively. The results show that (1) The growth of intermetallic compounds (IMC) after electromagnetic (EM) under AC stressing presents both polar and non-polar modes. In the polar growth of IMC processes, the thickness of IMC increases with rising numerical value frequency of AC; (2) The shear strength of solder joints after EM with AC stressing shows a slightly decreased, while they are close at different AC frequencies; (3) With the increase in AC frequency, the fracture location of the solder joints shifts from the solder matrix to the interface between the solder and IMC layer, and the fracture mode shows ductile-brittle transitions.

articleTitle: The influence of peak sintering temperature of alumina ceramics on the mechanical properties of alumina ceramics
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: High temperature co-fired alumina ceramics are widely used in ceramic shells and other devices due to their high reliability, high technical maturity and low price, which plays a role in encapsulating the substrate. At present, the most common problem in the application process of alumina ceramics is the cracking defects in the welding or application process, which may cause abnormal electrical performance of the device. In this paper, the phase-locked device is taken as the research object. In the use process of the device, a batch of ceramic substrates is prone to cracking. After mechanical performance analysis, it is found that the bending strength of the batch of ceramic substrates is lower than that of the normal batch. Further analysis by EBSD and other microscopic means shows that the grain size distribution of the batch of ceramic substrates is different from that of the normal batch of ceramic substrates. The grain size of the ceramic substrate is closely related to the sintering process. The root cause of the cracking of the locking device is the failure of the exhaust system of the ceramic manufacturer, which leads to the fluctuation of the peak sintering temperature, and the mechanical performance decreases.

articleTitle: Effects of 2.5D/3D Stacking Structure on Signal Integrity of Chiplet Interconnection
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In the post-Moore era, the chiplet technology based on advanced packaging would be a quite promising solution for the high-performance AI chips. The chiplet technology with 2.5D/3D stacking package architecture transforms traditional on-chip interconnection into chip-to-chip (C2C) interconnection. The C2C interconnection usually comprised of through-silicon-via (TSV), metal wiring (RDL) and bonding bumps with varying structures, sizes, materials and spatial layout, which could affect the signal integrity of the C2C channel. To further develop the chiplet technology, quantitatively evaluating the signal integrity performance of C2C interconnection in chiplet 2.5D/3D packages is very important. In this paper, the effects of C2C interconnect structures (RDL, TSV, bump) and their related parameters (size, pitch, and number of stacked layers) on signal integrity were investigated by simulations with HFSS and ADS tools. The simulation results show that the thickness of the dielectric layer between the RDL significantly affects the signal transmission capability of the channel. Besides, as the TSV spacing increases, the S11 and S21 of the channel are gradually improved, but the crosstalk is likewise increased. In combination with the optimized design parameters, the S21 of the 1650 μm long 5-layer stacked C2C interconnection channel is better than -4.1 dB in the 56 GHz range, but the S11 is above -20 dB after 17 GHz, which can be attributed to the impedance discontinuities in the complex C2C interconnection structure. This work reveals the signaling capabilities of the RDL-TSV-bump interconnection, which can provide a reference for chiplet 2.5D/3D packaging design.

articleTitle: Application and Optimization of Laser-Assisted Bonding (LAB) in Multi-Chip Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Multi-chip integration on the large substrate for Chiplets technology has emerged as a prevailing trend in the semiconductor industry. Thus, large substrates are urgently demanded. However, warpage is quite serious for this kind of substrate. This study presents a solution to this problem by laser-assisted- bonding (LAB) technology, which utilizes instantaneous laser heating to achieve melting and bonding. We have developed a LAB-X-100 series equipment that effectively bonds the flip-chip devices to a large substrate. This largely reduces the substrate warpage from over 150 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> to less than 50 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Multi-Scale and Multi-Process Simulation of Integrated Fan-Out Packaging for Reliability Improvement
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In 2016, TSMC introduced the Integrated Fan-Out (InFO) packaging technology, which has been widely adopted in Apple's A-series processors. This packaging technology offers superior performance, high I/O density, and low energy consumption. However, reliability issues have emerged. To address these issues, our research has developed a comprehensive InFO model that includes four different types of chips, aiming to understand the inner mechanisms of warpage and stress concentration throughout the entire manufacturing and operational process. Finite Element Analysis (FEA) was conducted using ABAQUS software, combined with material models capable of accurately characterizing the thermo mechanical properties of silicon chip and Epoxy Molding Compound (EMC). The study employed a multi-scale approach to establish the cross-scale models for thermomechanical simulation. The global model considered the effects of gravity, EMC backgrinding, post mold cure time and temperature, revealing their crucial roles in optimizing warpage. The first level sub-model focused on die gap, demonstrating that increasing die gap alleviates stress concentration. The second level sub-model quantitatively analyzed the impact of the mechanical constitutive model of the underfill on the reliability of microbump. The research provides theoretical guidance for enhancing the reliability of information packaging and advancing the advanced packaging technology of integrated circuits.

articleTitle: In-Situ Reduction Sintering of Micro-Copper Paste for High-Power Electronic Application
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Developing new packaging materials with a high melting point was eternally desirable for better reliability at higher service temperature. A pre-oxidization strategy was proposed to develop a novel micron copper paste. With the pre-oxidization of micro-Cu. a layer of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Cu}_{2}\mathrm{O}$</tex> nano-particles with a diameter of 15 nm was uniformly prepared on its surface. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Cu}_{2}\mathrm{O}$</tex> nano-particles were then in-situ reduced by the selected reducing agent into nano-Cu particles to promote the sintering process. The sintering activity of the powder was increased with the excess surface energy of nano-Cu particles, making the transformation process of the sintering system from high-energy to low-energy easier to actuate. The sintered microstructure was denser compared with the microstructure obtained from the unoxidized Cu particles. At <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$250^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>, the optimal shear strength of the interconnect microstructure reached 50.7 MPa, which was sintered under 20 Mpa for 10 min. The designed reduction agent and the in-situ sintering process were beneficial to the power chip interconnection, which also provided an excellent strategy for reliable paste preparation at a low cost.

articleTitle: Study on Opto-Mechatronic Hybrid Integration Technology Based on 2.5D Advanced Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Based on the development trends of micro-electro-mechanical systems (MEMS) and micro-optoelectronic systems, in this paper, a hybrid integration technology for opto-mechatronic micro systems based on 2.5D advanced packaging technology is proposed for the integration of optoelectronic detectors, MEMS sensors, and processing chips. Utilizing a collaborative design approach, a hybrid integration interposer based on Through-Silicon Via (TSV) technology was designed, with TSV diameter/depth of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10 \ \mu \mathrm{m}/100 \ \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>, Redistribution Layer (RDL) line width of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$25 \ \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>, and optical well window of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$600\times 900 \ \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>. The interposer integrates high-aspect ratio TSV technology and large-size optical well window etching technology compatibly. This hybrid integration technology with wire-free interconnections methods reduces the traditional wire-bond interconnection resistance, improves the signal quality of optoelectronic detectors and conditioning chips, and reduces parasitic effects in optoelectronic systems. The hybrid integration process and design technology of opto-mechatronic microsystems developed based on TSV technology have reduced the system volume from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$50\text{mm}\times 50\text{mm}\times 10\text{mm}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$11\text{mm}\times 11\text{mm}\times 2.45\text{mm}$</tex> while ensuring high performance. This technology is laying the foundation for the development of 2.5D/3D opto-mechatronic hybrid integration based on interposers.

articleTitle: Influence of Structural Defects on Insertion Loss of Differently Shaped TSV
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Through Silicon Vias (TSV) technology is the key structure for stacking chips in three-dimensional(3D) integrated circuits, which can provide higher packaging density and lower transmission loss by reducing the interconnection length between chips. Structural defects may occur in TSV structure during the fabrication process, which will influence the signal transmission performance of TSV. In this paper, finite element approach is used to simulate the influence of different structural defects on the signal transmission performance of differently shaped TSV. The simulation results indicate that defects will lead to a decrease in the S21 parameter of TSV and an increase in the S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> parameter of TSV compared to that of defect-free TSV. The increase of the diameter of the voids, the height of the pinholes, and the pad offset will result in an increase in insertion loss S21 and a decrease in return loss <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{S}_{11}$</tex>. The degree of the reduction in the S21 of differently shaped TSV with defect at 20 GHz was analyzed in detail. The rectangular TSV with voids experienced the greatest proportion of decrease in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{S}_{21}$</tex>, while the cylindrical TSV with voids had the smallest proportion of decrease in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{S}_{21}$</tex>. Among the TSV with pad misalignment, the rectangular TSV experienced the greatest proportion of decrease in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{S}_{21}$</tex>, while the conical frustum TSV had the smallest proportion of decrease in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{S}_{21}$</tex>. The triangular TSV with pinholes experienced the greatest proportion of decrease in S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>, while the rectangular TSV with pinholes had the smallest proportion of decrease in S21.

articleTitle: Influence of Substrate Thermal Conductivity on Material Ablation Threshold During UV Laser Debonding Process
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In the post-Moore era, advanced packaging such as wafer-level packaging and 3D packaging has become an important way to go beyond Moore's Law. In the advanced packaging process, temporary bonding/debonding (TBDB) is mainly used for wafer thinning, holding and wafer reconfiguration. Among them, laser debonding, which has the advantages of non-contact, high efficiency, stress-free, and environmentally friendly, has become the mainstream method in the field of TBDB. In the wafer bonding pair structure, temporary bonding materials typically contact device layers with different thermal conductivities, such as silicon wafer, re-distribution layer (eg. copper, polyimide) and under bump metal (eg. titanium, chromium). However, the mechanism by which the thermal conductivity of the device layer affects the laser ablation threshold of the release material has rarely been reported. Here, we selected three wafers with different thermal conductivity, namely, glass, CuO/silicon wafers, and bare silicon wafers, as device layers. The mechanism of the influence of the thermal conductivity of the device layer on the ablation threshold of the released material was explored. The ablation threshold of the release material under different device layers were derived by fitting the square of the ablation width as a function of power based on the zero damage method. As the thermal conductivity of the device layer gradually increases, the width of the ablation spot decreases, which indicates an increase in the ablation threshold of the release material. The results of this work provide a reference for optimizing the laser debonding process in the face of diverse device wafers from customers.

articleTitle: Cross-Scale Reliability Simulation of Chiplet Devices Based on Sub-Modeling Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As chip manufacturing processes continue to shrink to 3nm, the manufacturing difficulty and costs increase significantly while the yield rates decrease dramatically. Leveraging the advantages of heterogeneous integration, chiplet technology, which integrates chips with different process parameters from various manufacturers and fabrication nodes, has emerged as a crucial solution in the post-Moore era. However, the higher power density, increased interconnect density, and complex interconnect structures of chiplet devices pose severe reliability challenges. Additionally, the structural sizes within the devices often span three orders of magnitude, making rapid and accurate reliability assessments a challenging research problem. This study employs finite element simulation and the submodeling method to construct a cross-scale model for the overall chiplet device and it's C2 and C4 micro-interconnect solder joints, improving simulation efficiency. Subsequent simulations of powered thermal cycling were conducted and compared with standalone thermal cycling simulations. The results indicate that regions with concentrated chips lead to rapid temperature rises, and the Joule heating generated by the current primarily affects the plastic deformation process of the micro-interconnect solder joints. In chiplet devices, the plastic deformation of the C4 solder joints is significantly higher than that of the C2 solder joints. Finally, fatigue life predictions were conducted for both types of solder joints.

articleTitle: Numerical Study on Copper Electroplating Additives and Periodic Segmented Current for Through Silicon via Metallization
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Through silicon vias (TSVs) have been considered as an efficient way to establish vertical signal exchanging channels among stacked dies, offering advantages such as higher density, lower latency, and reduced power consumption. However, ensuring high-quality filling of the central conductor within TSVs is crucial, as issues such as incomplete filling and extended process time may arise if the electroplating condition is not optimized. In this study, the finite element method is employed to explore the effects of various electroplating parameters, including accelerator, suppressor, current density, and current mode on the filling quality of blind vias with diameter of 20 μm and depth of 110 μm. Based on the observation of particles' concentration, deposition thickness and current density, it is noticed that during the growth of the suppressor concentration, the filling profile will gradually evolve from sub-conformal to super-conformal, which is beneficial for full filling. However, eventually excessive accumulation of the suppressor at the bottom of the via can lead to the profile reverting to sub-conformal. Increasing the accelerator concentration can widen the range of the suppressor concentrations conducive to full filling. Moreover, the utilization of proper periodic segmented current is advantageous for achieving complete filling.

articleTitle: A Rapid Detection Method for TiN Residue On Al Bondpads
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: A KOH testing method is introduced, which could be used as pre-diagnose TiN residues on Al bondpads. Experimental results showed that it is possible for us to pre-diagnose whether there are TiN residues on bondpads or not using the KOH pre-diagnose testing method. The experimental results show that if there are TiN residues, the “Island-like” pad surfaces will be formed on the Al bondpads. In order to finally confirm presentence of TiN on Al bondpads, Auger electron spectroscopy analysis is recommended to do further confirmation.

Author Keywords: KOH testing and Auger electron spectroscopy analysis

articleTitle: Impact of 300 MeV Proton Irradiation on β-Ga2O3 Schottky Barrier Diodes Under Varying Bias Voltages
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: This paper investigates the impact of 300 MeV proton irradiation on ß -Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>SBD under different reverse bias voltages. Compared to 300 MeV proton irradiation without bias, the introduction of a 300 V reverse bias results in a decrease of forward current density <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{F}})$</tex> by half. According to capacitance-voltage (C- V) measurements, the carrier removal rate increases from 25 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>to 40 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>, This phenomenon is attributed to secondary damage to the material caused by recoil nuclei generated by proton irradiation, which are accelerated by the electric field. When the reverse bias voltage increases to 400V and 500V, the 300 MeV protons induce single event burnout (SEB) in the device, resulting in “voids” formed by the melting of the Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> material. Simulation results from Geant4 and TCAD indicate that the burnout phenomenon is caused by the implantation of secondary particles under high bias, leading to an increase in the lattice temperature inside the device. The maximum lattice temperature increases with the reverse bias voltage, and when the bias voltage is sufficiently high, the local lattice temperature inside the device reaches the melting point of the Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> material, ultimately leading to SEB.

articleTitle: Stretchable Silver Nanowire Aerogel Composites Films for Electromagnetic Interference Shielding
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the rapid development of 5G technology, the proliferation of wireless communication devices has surged, leading to an increasingly severe issue of electromagnetic pollution. Electromagnetic radiation not only disrupts the normal operation of electronic equipment but also poses potential hazards to human health. Consequently, there is a burgeoning demand for high-performance electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding materials. Furthermore, the rapid popularity of flexible wearable devices has put forward requirements for lightweight and stretchable electromagnetic shielding materials. Silver nanowire (AgNW) has emerged as a focal point in recent research on EMI shielding material because of its exceptional electrical conductivity and flexibility. However, during the stretching process, silver nanowires are prone to detach from the stretchable substrate surface, and the exposed silver nanowires underneath are susceptible to corrosion by water and oxygen, thereby diminishing the reliability during usage. Herein, we prepared AgNW aerogel (AgNW A)/Ecoflex stretchable films through mechanical compression and polymer-assisted impregnation. The film can withstand a tensile strain of 300%. Due to its high-density interconnected silver nanowire network and porous structure, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$75-\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> -thick film exhibits an exceptionally high electromagnetic shielding effectiveness of 106.5 dB. Furthermore, after undergoing 5000 times tensile cycling with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon=50\%$</tex>, the shielding effectiveness remains stable.

articleTitle: Modulation of magnetic and dielectric properties of La-substituted barium ferrite based on BBSZ for microwave device applications
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The low temperature co-fired ferrite (LTCF) technology is critical for improving microwave device performance and enabling miniaturization and integration of electronic systems. In present work, La-doped Ba<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>.<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>Sr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.5</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2-x</inf>La<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">23</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">41</inf> (x = 0.00 to 0.75 with a step of 0.15) ferrite was prepared by a solid-phase reaction method at low temperatures with the addition of 1.5%wt BBSZ (H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>BO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-ZnO) as flux. The XRD results show that the second phase, W-type phase, is always present in the samples and becomes more pronounced in the samples as the amount of La doping increases. The relative densities of all samples are above 92%, and SEM reveals that the samples have a well-densified structure. Particularly, at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x$</tex> = 0.3, the saturation magnetization increases from 56.15 emu/g to 58.78 emu/g, and the permeability μ’ of the sample shows a 38% increase at 200MHz. For dielectric properties, the dielectric constant є’ of the samples remains stable within the frequency range of 10 to 500 MHz, with a maximum value of 21.18, and the dielectric loss maintains a low value. Consequently, these La-doped barium ferrites demonstrate considerable promise for extensive use across electronic devices.

articleTitle: Simulation, Prediction and Verification of the Thermal and Electrical Properties of Sintered Copper Joints with Random Pore Structure for Power Electronics Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Copper sintering has gained great attention as a die-attach technology for power electronics because of its potential cost effectiveness and high reliability under harsh working conditions. However, the mechanism of how the intrinsic pores within such sintered joints influence the thermal and electrical properties still needs further investigation. The evolution of pores within such sintered joints is difficult for in-situ observation during the sintering process and reliability tests, while the porosity level greatly affects the thermal and electrical properties. In this work, four two-dimensional (2D) models with various random pore structures were established based on the Quartet Structure Generation Set (QSGS) algorithm. Then, finite element method (FEM) simulations were conducted to simulate the heat and current conduction in the sintered materials. Subsequently, the distribution of temperature as well as the electric potential in the porous sintered materials were further discussed. Lastly, both the thermal and the electrical conductivities were calculated, followed by a concluded parabolic relationship of thermal and electrical conductivities with the porosity. These findings offer insights into optimizing and predicting copper sintered joint performance and accelerate the wide application of copper sintering.

articleTitle: Investigation on Effects of Die Attach Adhesive on Thermal Stress and Stability of Silicon MEMS Resonator
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Die-attach is a typical process that causes thermal stress in micro-electromechanical system (MEMS) device-level packaging, in which the high nonlinearity and temperature dependence of die attach adhesive materials are the main reasons that affect the output stability of silicon differential resonant accelerometer (SDRA). To investigate the effect and mechanism of adhesive material characteristics on stress and stress-temperature coefficient of resonant in SDRA, a full-scale finite element analysis model of SDRA is established in this paper. The properties of adhesive viscoelastic materials are characterized by using generalized Maxwell model and stress relaxation test of dynamic mechanical analyzer(DMA), and were transformed into simulation of available relaxation coefficient and relaxation time. In order to observe the viscoelastic effect, the stress history curves of resonator beam with different material models in the temperature range of—40 to 80°C were compared. The simulation results indicate that the resonator beam stress of the viscoelastic model is about 20% lower than that of the temperature-dependent model, and will decrease slowly with the passage of time at constant temperature. Based on the established viscoelastic model, the influence of adhesive modulus on the stress and stress-temperature coefficient of resonator beam is studied. The comprehensive results indicate that the output accuracy and stability of SDRA can be improved by using low modulus adhesive and working away from its glass transition temperature (Tg) as far as possible.

articleTitle: 3D Printing of AlN Polyimide Composite Ink for Wafer Channel Filling
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of next-generation information technologies such as 5G and artificial intelligence, Moore's law is approaching its physical limit. Three-dimensional heterogeneous integration is becoming a new direction in integrated circuit development of post-Moore's Law era. Wafer-level packaging represents a crucial approach to heterogeneous integration, where the bonding technology in the chip to wafer plays a central role. Particularly, in the chip to wafer process, the filling of wafer channel is vital for enhancing the mechanical strength of the wafer and facilitating subsequent processing steps. In the process of filling micro-channels, the slurry must meet a series of stringent requirements: the particle size must be small and uniform, dispersion stable, viscosity appropriate and controllable, and the solid content high. For this purpose, this paper designs and synthesises an aluminum nitride (AIN) nanoparticle /Polyimide (PI) composite slurry for direct ink write (DIW) 3D printing to fill wafer channels. AIN nanoparticles were decorated with silane coupling agent (KH550) to reduce aggregation, and the decorated nano-AIN particles were dispersed in the PI solvent and N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP), and then a small amount of high-viscosity PI solution was added to achieve uniform composite ink. The as-prepared uniformly dispersed AIN/PI composite ink shows a viscosity of 3430 mPa.s, which is suitable for DIW 3D printing to fill tiny channels. The high volumetric solid content of 85% makes this composite ink more efficient in terms of filling compared with traditional trench filling techniques such as chemical vapor deposition and atomic layer deposition. The cured AlN/PI composite film exhibits high thermal stability with a coefficient of thermal expansion (11.69 ppm/C) similar to that of silicon-based materials. These high temperature resistant PI composites exhibit excellent performance and hold broad application prospects in the field of chip-to-wafer heterogeneous integration.

articleTitle: Embedded IPD Integration Solution for Large Chip Module Fan-Out Package
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: I. Abstract This paper will provide an overview of Si based capacitor/IPD integration evolution trends seen in the industry across different package platform, including 2.5D TSI DTC and embedded IPD on FO-EB and FO-MCM. From viewpoint of electrical performance, it figured out the comparison of 2.5D and FO EB (Embedded Bridge) with different IPD allocation respectively. We also indicated the difference of various IPD type (IPD in SOC, Stand-alone IPD, IPD in FO) Besides, the comparison of integrated capacitor technology (MLCC, 2D MiM, and TSI with DTC) are discussed accordingly. Finally, package level reliability of FO-EB with IPD integration be demonstrated successfully.

articleTitle: Study on the Effect of Test Condition on Thermal Resistance of the Press-Pack IGBT Module
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Press-Pack IGBT modules (PP-IGBT) are the key components in an electronic system. It is of great importance to study on the thermal resistance especially for thermal resistance, reliability, and life prediction. But to measure the thermal resistance accurately is relatively difficult. It is necessary to study the influence of test conditions on the thermal resistance of the PP-IGBT for better measurement. The influence of six factors of test conditions is studied in this paper. In this paper, experiments were designed and carried out, and finite element method (FEM) and structure function were also used for the verification and the analysis. The measurement process of on-state voltage at low current of temperature sensitive electrical parameter (TSEP) method was used to measure the thermal resistance. The experimental results show that the gate voltage, flow velocity and heating current have little effect on the thermal resistance under normal operating conditions, and pressure, ambient temperature and sensing current affect the thermal resistance in various ways.

articleTitle: Compact SIW Diplexer Based on Through Silicon Vias (TSV) for D-Band
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: An SIW diplexer is proposed for millimeter-wave D-band (110–170 GHz), utilizing Through Silicon Vias (TSV) technology. The diplexer design incorporates a combination of dual-mode and single-mode resonators to achieve inter-channel isolation, thus eliminating the need for conventional T - junctions. Common input offset <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t_{i0}$</tex> is established to adjust the degree of external coupling for both modes simultaneously. The use of fewer resonant cavities results in lower insertion losses (ILs). A second-order diplexer with centre frequencies (CFs) of 121.5 and 142 GHz and FBWs of 3.23% and 3.7% is designed on high resistivity silicon substrate for demonstration. In the two pass-band, the lowest ILs simulated are 2 and 2.1 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{dB}$</tex>, while the minimum return losses (RLs) stand at 17 and 16 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{dB}$</tex>, respectively. High isolation above 32 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{dB}$</tex> from 110 to 170 GHz can be achieved. The diplexer size is 3.3 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{g^{2}}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Research on Improving the Welding Strength of Pads by Laser Cleaning Based on 3D Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As an important process to realize 3D integration, the cleanliness of the pad affects the welding strength of laser-based solder jet bumping and wire bonding directly. Laser cleaning is a process for cleaning organic pollutants on pads. Its advantages are high precision, high efficiency, non-contact, and cleaning the slit of 3D integration. Firstly, a laser cleaning experimental platform was established to clean the organic pollutants on micro-printed circuit and the pads on the nickel- palladium gold substrates. The cleaned and non-cleaned areas were selected for SEM analysis, and the element mass ratio of were obtained for further analysis. Secondly, the 60um gold balls were planted on those cleaned and non-cleaned areas. The destructive shear force are tested to analyze welding strength. Finaly, the laser cleaning flatness were studied through the infiltration of eutectic with different laser parameter. The result of experiment and analysis is that the laser cleaning can effectively remove the organic pollutants and improve welding quality. The optimum cleaning parameters and flatness parameters were obtained.

articleTitle: Research on the Application of Active Thermoelectric Cooling Technology in the Field of Power Chip Heat Dissipation
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the continues progress of the advanced integrated circuit manufacturing technology, power chips are rapidly developing towards high integration, miniaturization, and high-frequency. The improvement of chip performance is accompanied by a continuous increase in power consumption and heat flux density. Overheating is a significant cause of power chip failure, which severely affects the chip's stability, reliability, and lifespan. Therefore, it becomes urgent to develop efficient and sustainable thermal management solutions for power chips. Thermoelectric cooling technology, based on the Peltier effect, can convert electrical energy into thermal energy. Currently, thermoelectric cooling devices (TEC) can achieve continuous and precise control over the cooling temperature by adjusting the operating voltage and current, with a cooling temperature reach -70°C at room temperature. Moreover, thermoelectric cooling devices have several advantages, such as high temperature control precision, fast response speed, compact structure, no moving parts, and low maintenance requirements. Therefore, developing thermoelectric cooling technology and applying it to efficient cooling and temperature control of power chips is of great significance for promoting the development of power chips towards integration, miniaturization, and higher frequencies. In order to solve the problem of efficient temperature control and heat dissipation in power chips, this study will apply thermoelectric cooling technology to the field of power chip heat dissipation. Based on a established temperature control, testing, and feedback system, the operation performance of the power chip will be characterized to evaluated the temperature control effects of the thermoelectric cooling device against traditional air cooling and liquid cooling methods. Through this research, the feasibility and effectiveness of active thermoelectric cooling technology for temperature control and heat dissipation in power chips can be thus verified.

articleTitle: Electroplated Low Temperature Self-Annealing Cu Film for Cu-Cu Bonding
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Cu-Cu bonding is a critical technology in three dimension integrated circuit (3D IC) integration. In this study, thermal instability Cu film, in which grain self-annealing was carried out at a relatively low temperature <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(75\ ^\circ \mathrm{C})$</tex>, was prepared through direct current (DC) electroplating. Experimental results indicated the self-annealing behavior of electroplated Cu film was significantly affected by the electrolyte aging time and electroplating current density. The Cu film electroplated with a fresh electrolyte could not derive self-annealing, but after 1 day of aging, the electroplated Cu film showed an obvious self-annealing performance at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$75^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>. In addition, the current density was demonstrated to dominate the microstructure of Cu film, with a high current density <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(0.015 \mathrm{A}/\text{cm}^{2})$</tex>, the electroplated nanocrystalline Cu exhibited a uniform grain size distribution while the low current density group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(0.005 \mathrm{A}/\text{cm}^{2})$</tex> showed a bottom-to-up increasing grain size distribution. Meanwhile, the high current density electroplated Cu film shows a fast self-annealing velocity, the as-deposited nanocrystalline grew to microcrystalline within 10 min at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$7 5^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>. As the electroplated Cu grain is nanocrystalline, the excessive energy stored in the grain boundary could be the main driving force for rapid self-annealing. Considering the Cu-Cu bonding is a solid-solid diffusion process, the Cu diffusion process could be accelerated with a rapid self-annealing rate. Hence, the thermal instability Cu film has a great potential to achieve low temperature Cu-Cu bonding. Keywords=Nanocrystalline Cu, Electroplated Cu film, Low temperature self-annealing

articleTitle: Research on Bump Preparation Technology Based on Fully Automated Ball Bonding Process
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: This article analyzes the method of bump preparation on chip pads using the fully automatic wire bonding ball-planting process. Through orthogonal analysis, it discusses the effects of bonding pressure, bonding time, and ultrasonic power on the interface bonding strength of gold bumps, thereby obtaining the optimal process parameters for chip pad bump preparation. The experimental results show that the shear strength of the gold bumps on the chip pads is greater than or equal to 0.76mg/um<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, the offset of the bumps is less than one-quarter of the gold bump diameter of the bump. This research has successfully simplified the complexity and high coast of the traditional bump preparation process, providing an effective technical solution for the chip packaging industry.

articleTitle: Development of 3-D Wafer Level Packaging for SAW Filters Using Non-photosensitive dry Film Capping
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The advent of 5G necessitates advanced packaging technologies compared to traditional RF packaging, prompting 3-D wafer level packaging (3-D WLP) to progress towards smaller sizes, improved electrical performance, and reduced costs. A non-photosensitive dry film (SIF03) with high strength and high modules of elasticity was utilized as capping layer, which exhibits excellent pressure capability. Finite element modeling (FEM) simulation was employed to evaluate the reliability of package structure, we compared the performance of this film with others, the deformation of roof films on different substrates, and the deformation of roof films with different cavity wall layer thicknesses during reflow process and molding test. At the same time, the packaging scheme has passed the process verification, which has been successfully applied in the SAW filter package.

articleTitle: Liquid-Cooled Heat Dissipation Technology for Co-Packaged Optics over 12.8 Tbps
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the rise of machine learning and artificial intelligence, data center power usage has increased continuously in recent years, and the bandwidth demand for switches continues to grow. As a result, the traditional pluggable optical modules with high latency and low signal quality can no longer meet the demands of bandwidth growth. As a result, co-packaged optics (CPO) technology has emerged. However, CPO introduces many new challenges, one of which is thermal management. This article explores the liquid-cooling heat dissipation technology for CPO systems over 12.8 Tbps. We designed a heat dissipation structure to address the special heat dissipation needs of CPO systems and verified the structure's excellent performance through simulation and experiment. The simulation value is reasonable and fits the experimental results. At 290W input power, the measured junction temperature of the ASIC is 51 °C, and the temperatures of the 16 optical chips ranged from 28 °C to 29 °C, with a maximum temperature difference of 0.6 °C, demonstrating the efficiency and reliability of this design.

articleTitle: High Speed D2D Interface Design and Analysis on Advanced Package
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The research and discussion in this paper, there are package design with the structure of FOCoS (Fan Out Chip on Substrate) for an actual high-performance computing IC device with ASIC (Application Specific Integrated Circuit) chips and HBM (High Bandwidth Memory) chips. In the process of this study, the die-to-die (D2D) interconnection between ASIC chip to ASIC chip is used UCIe (Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express) interface for high speed signal transmission and HBM3/HBM3e is applied on data transfer between ASIC chip and high bandwidth memories. Through electrical analysis, the suitable RDL (Re-Distribution Layer) structure and routing topology are applied on various interface.

articleTitle: Research on CDM Peak Current of High Speed Pins Based on 2.5D and 2D Package
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The trend and principle of the change of CDM peak current of IO high speed pin with pin position in 2.5D and 2D packages are analyzed in this paper. The CDM peak current value depends on the total charge and Td. Based on the results, the total discharge charge of the IO pin is insensitive to the pin position, and Td increases as the pin position moves away from the package center. This is related to parasitic parameters in the discharge path, the larger the package parasitic parameters of the pins, the longer discharge time and therefore the lower the corresponding CDM peak current. Therefore, the influence of pin position should be fully considered in the CDM current design, especially for the high-speed IO pins that are sensitive to CDM current.

articleTitle: Determination of Cohesive Zone Model (CZM) and Numerical Analysis of Interface Fracture in Sintered Silver with Different Metallization Layers
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: This paper utilizes the cohesive zone model (CZM) and method of numerical computation to conduct inverse analysis, leveraging the existing experimental results of Single-Leg Bending(SLB) tests of sintered silver joints with different metallization layers. Based on experimental data, numerical inverse analysis was conducted to determine the cohesive zone model (CZM) parameters for sintered silver joints with varying metallization layers. Initially, curves of load and displacement (P-δ) are directly obtained from the SLB tests. Subsequently, by analyzing these experimental data, the interfacial fracture toughness of the sintered silver joints with different metallization layers is determined. A two-dimensional finite element model (FEM) for the three-point bending of an SLB sample is developed. Ultimately, the cohesive zone model of the sintered silver joints with different metallization layers is established. The research findings demonstrate that the interfacial fracture toughness is highest when the metallization layer is Ni/Ag. The results suggest that the numerical solutions are in good agreement with the experimental data.

articleTitle: Thermal and Thermomechanical Performance Enhancement of Electric Vehicle Power Modules Utilizing Diamond-Copper Composite Interposers
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As the power density of electric vehicles continues to increase, the investigation of double-sided-cooling (DSC) modules are increasingly gaining attention as a significant area of research. However, Mo, as a traditional interposer material, exhibits relatively low thermal conductivity despite its good coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) matching with power chips, resulting in elevated junction temperatures.
