In this paper, we introduce a diamond-copper composite material (DC40, with a diamond volume fraction of 60%) interposer possessing high thermal conductivity and low CTE to mitigate module junction temperatures and thermomechanical stresses. Thermal and thermal cycling simulation results indicate that compared to modules employing Mo and Cu interposers, under a total power consumption of 100 W, the maximum junction temperatures decrease by 1.92 °C (1.52%) and 9.49 °C (7.08%) respectively; the power handling capacity of the chip increases by 21.5 W (14.3%) and 31.0 W (22.0%) respectively; The lifetime of the DC40 interposer DSC module is nearly equivalent to that of the Mo interposer and shows a 166.6% increase compared to the Cu interposer.

articleTitle: A Novel Layer Structural Design for Silver-indium Transient Liquid Phase Bonding Technology by Introducing a Diffusion Barrier
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Silver-indium transient liquid phase bonding (Ag-In TLP), as an interconnect technology, offers low bonding temperature, short bonding time, and high reliability, making it widely applicable for packaging electronic devices such as power devices and optoelectronic devices. In previous studies, the Ag-In bonding joints often contained voids due to excessive diffusion of indium into silver. In this research, a diffusion barrier layer between silver and indium was introduced to reduce pre-bonding diffusion, ultimately resulting in a low-porosity bonding interface. Electron beam evaporation (E-beam) and electroplating were primarily used to deposit Ag and In, and joints were obtained through flip-chip bonding processes. The bonding interface quality with diffusion barrier and without diffusion barrier have been carefully examined with SEM imaging, whereby directly demonstrating the functionality of the designed diffusion barrier. Moreover, the interfacial microstructure and element distribution of the Ag-In transient liquid phase bonding were also discussed through energy dispersive spectroscopy analysis. Through the above analysis, we found that introducing a diffusion barrier layer into the Ag-In transient liquid phase bonding process can effectively improve the quality of the bonding interface.

articleTitle: Electroplating Cu on ALD $\text{TiN}$ for Small Size TSV
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Si interposer with TSV technology plays a key role in 2.5D and 3D system integration. Via filling with smaller size is becoming more and more challenge. Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD) can fabricate diffusion barrier layer with better step coverage, film uniformity and controllable thickness in small size TSV. TiN thin film deposited by ALD can serve as diffusion barrier layer and seed layer for TSV structure simultaneously. In this paper, by optimizing ALD process parameters, a continuous TiN layer has been successfully deposited on TSV sidewall. Different pre-wetting solutions and different concentration ratios between accelerator(A) and suppressor(B) in electroplating solution has been examined to obtain the optimal parameters for electroplating Cu. The results show that ~30nm thick TiN films with resistivity of below 200 µΩ.cm can satisfy the basic function of diffusion barrier layer and seed layer for TSV structure. Pre-wetting solution-deionized water with added suppressor and additives B: A ranging from 6.5 to 7 are superior to other conditions for obtaining high-quality void-free Cu TSV. As concluded, ALD TiN can work as diffusion barrier layer and seed layer for small size TSV structure. Cu filling TSVs with diameter of 5-6µm, pitch of 15µm and aspect ratio ranging from 7 to 10 have been successfully demonstrated.

articleTitle: Research and Analysis of Reliability Evaluation Methods for Automotive Electronic Components
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In order to more accurately evaluate the reliability of automotive electronic components, this article firstly introduces conventional electronic component test items and summarizes the domestic and foreign automotive companies and industry standards for automotive electronic components. By interpreting some parts of the General Motors standard and IPC-A-610GA automotive addendum standard, this paper summarizes the commonly used temperature stress conditions for automotive electronic components, and clarifies the differences in test content and acceptable requirements among major automotive companies and IPC industry standards. GM standard mainly focus on the functionality and environmental adaptability of components, but there are certain limitations in evaluating the reliability of solder joints. IPC-A-610GA automotive addendum standard focuses more on the reliability of solder joints in automotive electronic components after soldering and test. By adopting a more refined cracking ratio algorithm, the ageing class of solder joints was more accurately evaluated, deepening the understanding of industry personnel on the test requirements of automotive electronic components. According to different automotive companies and application scenarios, targeted selection of different reliability evaluation methods and corresponding optimization of test methods can provide a more comprehensive and accurate evaluation of the reliability of automotive electronic components. It can effectively control test cycles and funding costs while assisting in the further development of the automotive industry.

articleTitle: Study on Thermal Properties of Laser-Include Graphene-Based Circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Flexible electronics has been widely used in the fields including sensors, medical devices and so on. Design and fabrication of circuits in flexible electronics has to meet requirements of light weight, bendable and good reliability so as to adapt to different applications and meet the deformation requirement. Laser-induced graphene (LIG) is a porous carbon nanomaterial formed by graphene with three-dimensional micro-structures, which has good mechanical properties and electronic conductivity as well as good chemical stability. The laser-induced technology combines graphene preparation and patterning and provides a green and low-cost method of circuit fabrication on flexible substrates. In this paper, circuits were prepared by the laser-induced technology to explore the feasibility of laser-include graphene-based circuit. Finite element analysis was carried out to study the thermal performance of circuits of various materials and patterns, and the influence of substrate material was also considered. Orthogonal data analysis is used to investigate the impact of the factors.

articleTitle: TDR Technology Detects Solder Joint Cracking of BGA Packaged Device
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: in the package of a device, when a pulse or step signal is send into the device though the pins, a part of the transmitted signal will be reflected if there is a discontinuity in the package. In this paper, the TDR (Time Domain Reflectometry) technology is used to quickly determine a solder joint Open failure within the BGA package. The characteristic impedance the transmission line of the failing solder joint is compared to the characteristic impedance of the transmission line of a bare package (without die attachment) and a “golden” unit. And the solder joint Open failure has been successfully detected by using TDR, The non-destructive testing of CT and the analysis of solder joint cross section proved that the failure sample was caused by the creep fracture of the solder joint of the device, which then caused the open circuit failure of the device. So it is verified that TDR method can be used to quickly test whether a crack/Open failure is within the package.

articleTitle: A First-Principles Study of the Structural, Mechanical and Thermodynamic Properties of Ag-In IMCs
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this work, four mechanically stable Ag-In intermetallic compounds (AgIn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, α'-Ag<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>In, ζ-Ag<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>In and γ-Ag<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</inf>In<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>) have been selected to explore their crystal structures, elastic mechanical and thermodynamic properties by first-principles calculations. Predicting the average mechanical properties of polycrystal based on the calculated elastic constants of single crystals, it can be learned that the Young's modulus of AgIn2, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha^{\prime}-\text{Ag}_{3}\text{In}, \zeta-\text{Ag}_{3}\text{In}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma-\text{Ag}_{9}\mathbf{In}_{4}$</tex> were 62.464 GPa, 96.281 GPa, 80.590 GPa, 80.169 GPa, respectively, and showed anisotropic distributions along with the shear modulus. Among them, α‘- Ag<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>In and γ-Ag<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</inf>In<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> have isotropic bulk modulus. They both have low hardness, and good ductility which can enhance the ability to resist external impacts and improve the reliability of microelectronic packages. Predictions of their heat capacities show that the heat capacities all follow T3 law at low temperatures and converge to the Dulong-Petit limit.

articleTitle: Effect of Particles Incidence Angle on GaN Epitaxial Thin Films for Optoelectronic Devices by Molecular Dynamic Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: GaN materials are widely used in optoelectronic devices. Molecular beam epitaxy is very important in the field of material growth and the angle at which molecules or atoms are incident on the substrate has a significant effect on the crystal quality and surface morphology of the epitaxial film. There are relativity few microscopic research on the impact of various incident angles affecting the quality of GaN epitaxial film. In this work, the molecular dynamics is utilized to investigate deposition process at different incident angels of GaN film. The crystal structure evolution, surface topography, roughness, dislocation distribution, atomic directional stress distribution and atomic density are calculated and analyzed. The results show that the epitaxial film roughness remains almost unchanged when the angle of incidence increases from zero to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$15^{\circ}$</tex>. The surface roughness of the epitaxial film increases rapidly as the molecules or atoms incident angle continues to increase from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$15^{\circ}$</tex>. When the angle of incidence is smaller than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$45^{\circ},$</tex> the atomic density in each layer decreases slowly from the 0th layer to the 18th layer of the film and then the number of atoms decreases rapidly. While when the incident angle of particles is greater than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$45^{\circ}$</tex> the number of particles in each layer decreases rapidly from layer 0. For the z-direction stress, the stress of the atomic layer decreases the fastest at the particle incident angle of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$75^{\circ},$</tex> and the atomic energy reaches the minimum stress at about the 10th layer. While for the biaxial stress, the atomic energy reaches the minimum at the incident angle range from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0^\circ$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$30^{\circ}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Electrodeposition of (111)-oriented nanotwinned Cu in Damascene vias
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Due to the rapid development of advanced packaging, the size of Cu interconnection are getting smaller and smaller, traditional micro-bump technology has difficulties in narrowing the interconnection pitch due to the bridging issue of Sn based solder. The hybrid bonding has emerged to meet the reliability requirement of fine pitch interconnection. The electroplating of Damascene Cu vias is the premise of hybrid bonding. In addition, nanotwinned Cu with highly (111) orientation possessed high yield strength, good electrical conductivity and high resistance to electromigration. However, due to the significant decrease of nanotwinned's density within Damascene vias as compared to thin films, the electrolyte and electroplating process of nanotwinnedCu Damascene vias need further investigation before application. In this paper, Damascene vias of size (width 4μm, depth 1 μm) was electroplated, the filled performance and the ratio of (111) orientations were analyzed. Firstly, a series of copper films were electroplated using gelatin with different molecular weight. The surface morphology and cross section of the Cu films were characterized by Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) and Focused Ion Beam Microscopy (FIB), the orientation of the Cu films were characterized by X-Ray Diffraction (XRD), and the texture coefficients(TC) were calculated. Secondly, gelatin with different molecular weights were further characterized by Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy(FTIR) and Gel Permeation Chromatography (GPC). In the end, the cross-sectional images of microstructure was observed by Focused Ion beam microscopy (FIB).

articleTitle: A New Process for Laser-Induced Gas Debonding Based on the Grid Scanning Method
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Today, ultra-thin wafers are being used in a wide range of applications in wafer-level packaging (WLP), panel-level packaging (PLP), system-in-package (SIP), 2.5D packaging and 3D packaging technologies. As ultra-thin wafers are prone to warpage or damage problems in advanced packaging processes, the semiconductor industry has proposed temporary bonding and debonding technologies. Laser debonding technology is widely used in the temporary debonding process due to its non-contact, stress-free, room-temperature friendly and flexible operation. However, the current UV laser debonding process mainly uses spot splicing to scan the entire wafer. This not only involves the risk of UV laser leakage damaging the fragile materials on the device surface, but also the large amount of carbon debris generated by laser ablation may make the device wafers difficult to clean. Here, we propose a grid scanning method for scanning the laser beam along the cut channel based on the laser-induced gas shock effect. By adjusting the laser energy density and scanning speed, the laser beam scanning path can be made to coincide with the interstitial cutting channel of hundreds to thousands of chips on the wafer, and the gas shock generated by the laser ablation release material is utilized to make the wafer bonding pairs realize stress-free separation. This approach not only improves debonding efficiency by more than 10 times, but also produces less carbon debris for cleaning after debonding.

articleTitle: Application of Low Temperature Solder Ball Sn-58Bi in Micro-Mirror Arrays Stacked Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As one of the typical micro-electro-mechanical systems, micro-mirror arrays(MMA)are applied in many optical fields. The development of large arrays is one direction of micro-mirror device evolution. However, the increase of micro-mirror units will also lead to an increase of the number of I/O and the dimension of MMA chip, bringing significant challenges to the high-density interconnection and low warpage soldering between MMA and multi-ASIC chips. In this work, Sn-1.8Ag bump and Sn-58Bi were employed to solder the ASIC and MEMS chip on front and back of the interposer respectively, enabling vertical stacking and interconnections between MMA chip and ASIC chips. Low temperature solder ball Sn-58Bi meet the requirement for low-temperature bonding of MMA (<180°C) and avoided the re-melting of ASIC bump during secondary reflow process. The microstructure and morphology of intermetallic compounds were examined, which indicated that Sn-58Bi and Sn-1.8Ag formed a stable IMC layer with pad on the chip and interposer and achieved good bonding after two reflow processes. Shear test was employed to evaluate the bonding strength of ASIC chip. The test results show that the maximum shear force of ASIC chip was 12.48 kg. The measurement results of warpage after reflow show that warpage of the interposer after reflow was only a few micronmeters. The application of low temperature solder ball has successfully realized the stack interconnection of MMA chip with size over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{30}\times \mathbf{30}\mathbf{mm}$</tex> and multiple ASIC chips in vertical direction, indicating a wide application prospect.

articleTitle: Development of Multimodal Metal Particle Pastes Using Computer Simulation Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Compared with soldering technology, metal particle sinter-joining technology can provide better thermodynamic performance and higher packaging reliability. It is considered one of the most promising technologies for achieving interconnects with high reliability and heat resistance for wide-band gap semiconductor devices. However, sinter-jointed layers are usually porous structures, and the porosity inevitably affects the sinter-joints' thermal and mechanical properties. Compared with traditional unimodal metal particle pastes, multimodal particle pastes can reduce the sinter-jointed layers' porosity and improve their performance effectively. In order to obtain the optimal ratio of multimodal micro/nanoparticle materials, a Monte Carlo simulation method was developed to achieve their random stacking. The results show that regardless of radius ratios between bimodal spherical particles, their stacking density gets the highest value when the mass of the small particles comprises ~30%. When the spherical particles with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r_{1}=0.5$</tex> and non-spherical (elliptical) particles with the principal axis <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2a=10,2b=8$</tex>, thickness <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2d=1.5$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta_{max}=10^{\circ}$</tex> were used, the stacking density gets the highest value when the spherical particles account for ~70%. Overall, the computer simulation method for evaluating the stacking density of multimodal spherical or non-spherical particles is provided and proved useful.

articleTitle: The Degradation Mechanism of Indium TIM Coverage in Ultra-Large Size FCBGA Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this work, the defect in Indium Thermal Interface Material(TIM) was investigated with Scanning Acoustic Microscope(SAM), FIB and SEM. The TIM coverage degradation of indium occured in the reflow and temperature cycling test due to the change of warpage. The degradation during reflow is related to the wettability of indium interface with the die and lid, and poor wettability of the die surface will exacerbate the degradation process of indium during reflows. The primary reason for coverage degradation after TCG1000 test is the expansion of cracks generated during the previous reflow process. The fundamental reason for coverage degradation is the stress on the TIM during reflows and temperature cycling.

articleTitle: Effect of Spinodal Decomposition Pore on Shear Strength of Silver
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: This study investigates the effect of spinodal decomposition pores on the shear strength of nano silver (nAg) used as a die attach material in electronic packaging. The formation of porous nAg structures with varying porosity levels is simulated using the Cahn-Hilliard equation, with the initial nAg concentration controlling the porosity rate. Molecular dynamics simulations are then employed to evaluate the mechanical response of the porous nAg under shear deformation. The results demonstrate that increasing porosity significantly decreases the ultimate shear strength. Furthermore, detailed analyses of surface area evolution, stress distribution, and dislocation density reveal the intricate interplay between porosity and deformation mechanisms. Highly porous nAg exhibits a more uniform stress distribution and lower dislocation accumulation compared to low-porosity structures. The findings provide valuable insights into optimizing the porosity of nAg for enhanced mechanical reliability in electronic packaging applications. The proposed modeling framework can be extended to other material systems for exploring microstructure-property relationships.

articleTitle: Aging Mechanism of Thermal Interface Materials Investigated by In-Situ Raman and Infrared Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: the aging of thermal interface material (TIM) in advanced electronic packaging has been became a key issue along with the increase of power density in chip. The high temperature generated in the chip is easy to accelerate the aging of the TIM., which affects the reliability and service life of the electronic packaging material. Although thermal interface materials., especially silicon-based thermal interface materials., are widely used in electronic packaging structures., systematic aging studies are lacking. In this study., the aging mechanism of silicon-based TIM was studied systematically by the Raman and infrared spectroscopy. Raman or infrared spectroscopy have their own limitations in studying the aging mechanism of TIM. Only by combining them can richer molecular information and more accurate aging mechanism be obtained. Moreover., a spectroscopic method for rapid nondestructive detection of aging degree of TIM was developed.

articleTitle: Optimization of Dual-Chip Heterogeneous Packaging Power Device Based on 3D Fan-Out Panel Level Packaging (3D FOPLP)
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: 2.5D packaging and 3D packaging are both emerging semiconductor packaging technologies that can achieve high-speed and high-density interconnection between chips, thereby improving system performance and integration. The 2.5D packaging utilizes silicon interposer to achieve interconnection between chips, while 3D packaging directly designs through silicon via (TSV) in the chips to achieve stacked interconnection between multiple layers of chips. The current two packaging technologies are based on wafer level silicon intermediate layer and TSV process, mainly applied to IC chips such as logic chips and storage chips. Starting from the functions and application scenarios of the power devices, these two wafer level processes are actually not very suitable for power devices. Relatively speaking, FOPLP currently performs well on small area chips such as power devices, sensor chips, and RF chips, with advantages in conductivity, heat dissipation, and cost. In this study, based on the signal interconnection requirements between dual chips, a heterogeneous stacked packaging power device MOSFET & GaN was designed and manufactured. This 3D FOPLP design utilizes redistribution layers on the epoxy molding compound (EMC) dielectric layer and laser drilling between multiple layers of EMC to achieve vertical conduction between stacked chips and complete the electrical interconnection of the entire device. Compared to traditional wire bonding, the volume of this device based on 3D FOPLP technology has been reduced by about 60%, the static drain-source on-resistance (RDS(on)) was reduced by about 20%. The application of chip stacking integration to achieve the shortest interconnection and minimum packaging size in multi-chip power devices can achieve higher integration, better heat dissipation performance, and higher power transmission efficiency, thereby meeting the needs of multi-chip high-performance power devices.

articleTitle: Electromigration-Induced Failure of Low-Temperature Sn-57Bi-1Ag Solder Interconnect Under Low Frequency Pulsed Direct Current Stressing
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The electromigration behavior of low- temperature Sn-57%Bi-1%Ag (wt.%) solder interconnects subjected to the low frequency pulsed direct current stressing was investigated. The pulsed direct current stressing induced damages in low-temperature Sn-57Bi-1Ag solder interconnects. Subsequently, the melting of solder in the center of interconnects occurred, and consequently leading to the failure of solder interconnects induced by the liquid-solid electromigration. Bi-rich layer (12.6 μm) at the anode of solder interconnects under 75 % duty factor (DF) was thicker than those of solder interconnects under 25 % and 50 % DF (4.8 and 8.2 μm, respectively). However, the average lifetime of solder interconnects under 75 % DF was 150.4 h, which was longer than those of solder interconnects under 25 % and 50 % DF (35.8 and 51.0 h, respectively). As the duty factor decreased, the electromigration lifetime of solder interconnects was significantly shortened, which was attributed to the fatigue stress caused by the pulsed direct current stressing.

articleTitle: Study on the Influence of Automatic Mounting Parameters of Conductive Adhesive on the Reliability of Components
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Conductive adhesive bonding is widely used in hybrid integrated circuit products, and is the main form of package interconnection for capacitors, two triodes and IC chips. With the continuous reduction of the size of internal components in highly reliable hybrid integrated circuits and the continuous improvement of circuit assembly density, the control and optimization of adhesive parameters, including dispensing form, dispensing amount and mounting pressure, have an increasing impact on the reliability of component packaging. The problems of conductive adhesive silver migration, interface delamination and contact resistance stability have become the main failure modes of conductive adhesive bonding interconnection. This paper intends to carry out research on optimization of automatic mounting parameters of conductive adhesive bonding components. Through testing and analyzing the identification process parameters and mounting process parameters of automatic mounting equipment, effective mounting parameters for different bonding components are obtained. The results show that the installation accuracy, pass rate and contact resistance stability of the components can be greatly improved by using the optimized mounting parameters. Meanwhile, the mounting efficiency can also be significantly improved by optimizing the program and parameters.

articleTitle: The Challenges of Wafer Blade Dicing by Minimize Die Size
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Wafer sawing is an essential and critical process in semiconductor manufacturing. After the development of the industry, wafer dicing has shown diversification, mainly including laser cut (laser grooving or laser stealth cutting), plasma dicing and blade dicing etc. For silicon (Si) wafer dicing, the process defects of laser cut (such as chipping/crack) are better than traditional blade dicing, but the cost is higher; Plasma dicing can achieve no chipping and crack issues, but the running costs are also high, and the wafer design has special requirements for saw-lane. Blade dicing causes chipping due to mechanical stress, but the cost is low, and the technology is mature in normal Si wafer, so it is still widely used. Therefore, in the practical application process, considering the investment of operating costs and quality, silicon wafer dicing tends to focus on traditional blade dicing. With the continuous innovation and technological breakthrough of science and technology, the semiconductor industry has been widely used, promoting the rapid development of the industry. Also, the change of market environment, product market competition is more and more fierce, need to improve product cost performance. Reducing die size to increase die quantity per wafer is a way to cost down. So, wafer fabrication houses continuously face challenges in manufacturing semiconductor devices because the devices continue to get tinier and more complicated. For wafer dicing, also has challenges once die size too small, especially blade dicing because the blade dicing will be limitations, such as die chipping & die shift or fly die and so on. This paper will be focusing on developing appropriate dicing blade type, dicing tape and dicing parameters (spindle speed, feed rate etc). Find the best recipe for blade dicing. The challenge for newly introduced smaller die wafer is overcome, the die size is reduced from current W+50 um to W-10 um, the die quantity (Qty) per wafer increased 65%. This results in an around 40% cost saving in wafer manufacturing. Our process characterization includes 5 flows: (1) Feasibility study; (2) Pre-screen DOE (Design of experience); (3) Full DOE; (4) Validation run. Feasibility study is mainly to evaluate different degrees of viscous dicing tape and different dicing blades with different diamond granularity to preliminarily narrow the selection range. In pre-screen DOE, it is carried out with 2 types of dicing tapes and 3 different types of blades based on the feasibility study results. In full DOE, the key factors are selected from pre-screen DOE sawed in dicing study matrix. The collected data are analyzed by Minitab-a professional data processing software. Optimizing sawing parameters and identifying key factors from the data graph are essential to ensure precision. It is imperative to conduct verification experiments during validation run and final validation to validate these findings.

articleTitle: Effect of compressive stress on microstructural evolution of Sn-Bi-Ag/Sn-Ag-Cu hybrid BGA solder joints assembled by low-temperature soldering
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The effect of compressive stress on the microstructure of low-temperature Sn-49Bi-1Ag/Sn-3.0Ag-0.5Cu hybrid BGA solder joints was investigated. The diffusion behavior of Bi atoms was determined by the competition of chemical potential gradient and strain-assisted effect. At the low temperature of 358 K, irregular Bi phases coarsened and the degree of coarsening increased with increasing compressive stress. Bi atoms in the mixed zone migrated along the strain direction, accumulated at the solder/Cu interface, resulting in the decreasing mixed percentage. At the high temperatures of 383 & 393 K, Bi phases gradually dissolved in ß-Sn matrix. The compressive strain inhibited the growth of interfacial IMC layer and retarded the Bi atoms diffusion from the mixed zone towards the un-melted Sn-Ag-Cu solder at all test temperatures.

articleTitle: Improvement of Bonding Strength for Ag Sinter Joining Direct on Al Heatsink in SiC Power Module
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Ag sinter paste for SiC die to AMB (Active Metal Brazing) substrate bonding have been used in the electric vehicle. To further meet the high temperature operation requirement, a bonding material with high thermal conductivity for AMB substrate to Al (aluminum) heatsink is also necessary to replace the TIM (Thermal Interface Material). In this study, we used the Ag sinter paste to direct bonding to Al alloy substrate in a low temperature low pressure sintering condition. In addition, to improve the bonding strength for the Ag sinter paste joint to Al substrate, Al surface treatment process including surface grinding, chemical solvent treatment (Surface corrosion method) and blasting treatment were proposed and investigated. The results show that the initial shear strength of Ag sinter paste direct to Al substrate was decreased for the surface grinding and chemical solvent treatment but can be improved by treating the Al surface with a blasting process. For the blasting treatment, the shear strength of joint structure was 41.4 MPa, which was improved and larger than that without surface treatment of 35.9 MPa.

articleTitle: Low-Loss, Temperature-Stable, and Li-Enriched Li2.12ZnTi3O8 Dielectric Ceramics for LTCC Applications with V2O5 Addition
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Herein, the sintering characteristics, phase composition, microscopic morphology, Lattice Vibration Characteristics, and dielectric properties in the microwave and terahertz frequency scales of the novel low-temperature cofired ceramics (LTCC) L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i2.12</inf>ZnTi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</inf> + <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x$</tex> V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x$</tex>=0.5-2.0 wt.%) were prepared and investigated. The L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i2.12</inf>ZnTi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</inf> + 1.5wt.% V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> ceramics, sintered at 925 °C for 4 hours, exhibit the optimal microwave dielectric properties: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon_{r}=22.42,Q\times f= 49592$</tex> GHz, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau_{f}=7.9$</tex> ppm/°C (@8.6 GHz). The generation of VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and liquid phase leads to poorer dielectric properties, while higher densities and larger grain sizes are the main reasons for better microwave dielectric properties. In the terahertz band (0.2 - 1.2 THz), <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon_{r}$</tex> ranges between 15 and 25 with a dissipation factor as low as 0.001. This suggests that L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i2.12</inf>ZnTi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</inf> + <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x$</tex> V2O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> ceramics also have a wide range of applications in the terahertz band. L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i2.12</inf>ZnTi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</inf> + 1.5wt.% V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> has exhibited excellent compatibility with silver electrodes. All these results indicate that L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i2.12</inf>ZnTi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</inf> + 1.5wt.% V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> has a promising application in the LTCC field.

articleTitle: Influence of Cu9Ga4 Growth on Shear Behavior of Cu-Ga Full IMC Joint
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this study, the growth pattern of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma_{3}-\text{Cu}_{9}\text{Ga}_{4}$</tex> phase in Cu-Ga intermetallic compound (IMC) joints, as well as the shear strength and fracture behavior of the joints were investigated. The results show that the growth rate of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma_{3} - \mathbf{Cu}_{9}\text{Ga}_{4}$</tex> phase gradually slows down with the increase of reaction time; at the same time, with the increase of the thickness of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma_{3}-\text{Cu}_{9}\text{Ga}_{4}$</tex> phase, the hollow defects in IMC joints decrease and the shear strength of IMC joints increases. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma_{3}-\text{Cu}{9}\text{Ga}_{4}$</tex> IMC joint was generated when the reaction time reached 60 h, and the joint shear strength reached 37.2 MPa, which was a substantial increase compared to the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma_{3}-\text{Cu}_{9} \text{Ga}_{4} / \theta- \text{CuGa}_{2} / \gamma_{3}-\text{Cu}_{9} \text{Ga}_{4}$</tex> IMC joint. In addition, cracks tend to expand along the voids in the joints due to the stress concentration at the voids.

articleTitle: The Impact of Supported Solder Layers on the Reliability of Automotive IGBT Power Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: During power cycling tests, automotive power module solder layers experience aging due to repeated temperature fluctuations and cyclic stresses, leading to increased thermal resistance and rapid device failure. In practical manufacturing processes, uneven solder layer thickness can adversely affect device reliability. This paper proposes a supported solder structure to address the issue of uneven solder distribution. Through simulations and experiments, the study focuses on the impact of traditional and supported solder layers on device reliability, particularly in terms of thermal performance variations and solder layer inclination. Utilizing minute-level power cycling tests, thermal resistance changes were monitored throughout the cycling process, and void rates before and after the tests were compared. The findings demonstrate that the supported solder structure effectively reduces thermal resistance and minimizes void rates in the solder layer. As power cycling progresses, the supported solder shows superior reliability compared to traditional solder. These results highlight the significance of the supported solder structure in enhancing the reliability of power semiconductor devices, providing valuable insights for practical engineering applications.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on Femtosecond Laser-Induced Microjet-Assisted Trepan Drilling of Silicon Wafer
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Femtosecond laser drilling technology has garnered significant interest in electronic packaging due to its precision and non-thermal characteristics. However, challenges like debris redeposition and energy dissipation can decrease the quality of the laser processing. This study employs femtosecond laser-induced microjet-assisted trepan drilling technique for fabricating through-holes in silicon wafers. During the processing, microjets generated by the femtosecond laser to consistently and efficiently clear ablation debris and cavitation bubbles, ensuring superior hole quality. A comparative experimental analysis with processing under identical parameters in air was conducted, demonstrating that the microjet-assisted trepan drilling technique significantly mitigates debris deposition and recast layer formation. It also enhances the roundness and straightness of the holes and boosts the material removal rate of the trepan drilling process. The fracture stability of silicon wafers processed with this technique was validated through three-point bending tests. Consequently, this study achieved the processing of high-quality through-holes on silicon wafers, offering valuable insights for micro-through-hole fabrication in electronic packaging.

articleTitle: A novel thermal interface materials based on porous metal copper filled tin for die attachment in power device packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As electronic devices continue to develop towards higher integration and miniaturization, the power density also increases, which in turn leads to a significant rise in the amount of heat generated by the devices. Therefore, efficiently dissipating more heat and maintaining the system at lower temperature levels has become a bottleneck issue for power devices. Porous copper, with its advantages of high thermal conductivity, high specific heat capacity, and low manufacturing costs, has a wide range of potential applications for power device packaging. Nevertheless, existing reports have primarily concentrated on the preparation of porous metal copper materials, lacking research on their interconnection techniques and long-term reliability. This paper used orthogonal experiments to study the effect of metal porous copper filled tin. Under the optimal process parameters (250 °C, 8 MPa, 10 min), the shear strength of the interconnection structure is 36.3 MPa. After 500 h of high-temperature storage, the shear strength of the interconnect structure reached 44.3 MPa, whichwas 122<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> of the initial shear strength. In addition, the thermal conductivity of the interconnect structure after 500 hours of high-temperature storage was 206.7 W·m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>K<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>, which was 71.3% of the initial thermal conductivity. In other words, during long-term service, the mechanical and thermal properties of porous copper were excellent, making it suitable for interconnects in power devices.

articleTitle: Design of a New Millimeter-Wave 3D Stacked RF Front-End System Level Package
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In the context of the gradual popularization of 5G mobile communication, the number of RF devices has increased significantly, and the complexity of RF systems has increased day by day. The RF system integration package is gradually developing in the direction of system level package, which puts forward the demand of miniaturization, multi-function and easy integration. In this paper, an RF system level package antenna module with a size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$26\text{mm}\times 26$</tex> mm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex> 0.974mm and a center frequency of 97Ghz is designed. It integrates four RF front-end chip and a transceiver chip in the size of the antenna. It integrates a three-layer patch microstrip antenna with a total of 256 array elements and 64 channels in the package, and uses the H-shaped slot to achieve feed, so as to achieve more complex system integration. Packaging PCB boards using HDI materials has the advantage of facilitating a large number of integrations. After considering the requirements of electromagnetic isolation and effective interconnection, the detailed structural design is given in this paper. The electromagnetic characteristics of the RF system-level package module are simulated and evaluated. The simulation results show that when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\vert \text{SII}\vert < -10\text{dB}$</tex>, the bandwidth of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2 \times 2$</tex> array antenna is 5GHz, and the gain is 11.46dBi at 97GHz. The RF signal transmission path loss (S21) is controlled below 1.5dBi, and one RF SiP module channel gain is 9.8dBi.

articleTitle: Wire Sweep Improvement Study in Large-Scale Molded Quad-Flat-No-Lead Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The growing need for plastic encapsulation microelectronics (PEMs) as an alternative to traditional package forms of high reliability and high cost has led to the emergence of quad-flat-no-lead (QFN) packages as a viable option. Their relatively low cost and plausibility for mass production make them an attractive choice. Nevertheless, in order to achieve the complete replacement of traditional packages such as ceramic packages or metal packages, it is necessary to explore in advance a number of reliability issues and methods to improve production processes. One of the common reliability issues in plastic encapsulation is wire sweep, which can cause open circuit, short circuit and parasitic effects. These effects can degrade the performance of microelectronic components for radio frequency (RF) appliances. This paper examines the impact of wire profile parameters, including wire loop span, wire loop height and wire bonding geometries, on wire sweep outcomes. A transfer molding experiment with a QFN product for RF uses is conducted and a mathematical model is developed to study and predict wire sweep. The results indicate that wires with a length exceeding than 2 mm in PSA LOOP exhibits the greatest stiffness in resisting wire sweep. The wire loop height is the primary factor influencing wire sweep. It is recommended that the wire loop height be as low as possible in order to alleviate wire sweep. The mathematical model based on the PI theorem and the Dose Resp regression model outweighs traditional theories in accuracy. This paper presents a guideline for the wire sweep improvement in QFN production in a large-scale mold.

articleTitle: A Novel Nontraditional Approach to C2W Cu/SiO2 Hybrid Bonding
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Chip-to-wafer (C2W) hybrid bonding is a promising technology in the three-dimensional integrated circuit (3D IC) area. For C2W Cu/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> hybrid bonding, the hydrophilic SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> pre-bonding step is very important because low pre-bonding strength will result in the hybrid bonding failure during the subsequent annealing process. Traditionally, ultralow dielectric surface roughness needs to be achieved through precisely controlled chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) to ensure good direct bonding quality. In this study, we proposed nontraditional pre-bonding process conditions by applying heat and high pressure simultaneously to relax the strict CMP process requirement for hybrid bonding. By using this unconventional pre-bonding approach, successful C2W Cu/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> hybrid bonding with high shear strength can be potentially achieved even with poor SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> surface roughness. Various characterization experiments were performed to confirm the effectiveness of this nontraditional pre-bonding method.

articleTitle: Influence of Alloying Elements on Bonding Interface of Palladium-Plated Copper Wire in Humid and High Temperature Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this paper, a new type of palladium plated copper wire (PW-B) is designed and developed independently. This kind of copper wire is to prevent halide corrosion by regulating the trace alloying elements in the copper substrate and adjusting the intermetallic compounds formed at the welding interface with the aluminum pad, so as to improve the reliability of the product. In this paper, high accelerated stress reliability test is carried out to verify the reliability of the material under high temperature and high humidity environment. The results show that PW-B has good reliability in the extreme environment of high temperature, high humidity and halide action, and is expected to be applied in automotive electronics in the future.

articleTitle: Compact Spatially Symmetric Double-Sided Embedded Packaging Method for Parallel SiC MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: This paper proposes a compact spatially symmetric double-sided cooling packaging method with the aim of enhancing the parallel current-sharing capability of SiC MOS-FETs while fully exploiting their inherent advantages in high-frequency and high-temperature performance. Firstly, this packaging method utilizes a spatially symmetric layout to achieve complete symmetry in parasitic parameters and thermal resistance of parallel SiC MOSFET chips, thereby enhancing the parallel operation capability of the devices. Furthermore, the compact structure reduces the main power switching loop parasitic inductance to 1.8 nH, while the use of high-thermal-performance materials and the implementation of a double-sided heat dissipation path reduce the junction-to-cover thermal resistance to below 0.058 °C/W. These advancements facilitate the optimal utilization of the SiC MOSFET chips' high-temperature and high-frequency capabilities. Moreover, spatially symmetric terminal lead-out method enables the measurement of parallel characteristics for the parallel-connected chips, providing a tool for the study of parallel characteristics in power semiconductor devices. The effectiveness of this packaging method is validated through double-pulse experiments.

articleTitle: Study on the effects of silicone-modified curing agent on the toughness of underfills
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Andvanced packaging technology is improving rapidly in recent years, which raise great demand in underfill with higher toughness. However, the application of traditional additive-type flexibilizers in advanced packaging are limited due to the weak mechanical properties caused by their low compatibility with epoxy. In this work, a silicone-modified aniline curing agent (SAN) was prepared through condensation reaction of aniline and polymethyl hydrosiloxane to improve the toughness of underfill and solve the “ trade-off” between the toughness and weak compatibility of epoxy-based composites. The results of infrared spectroscopic analysis demonstrate that siloxane chain segment was successfully grafted with aniline through hydrosilylation reaction. The influence of SAN on the toughness of UF was investigated using fracture tests. The obtained results demonstrate that by adding 6 wt.% of SAN, the toughness of UF-2 was significantly higher than that of neat UF both at 25°C and -55°C. Furthermore, the toughness mechanisms of SAN were studied by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and in-situ bending test. The results certified the toughness mechanism of SAN was attributed to the flexible silicone chain segment, absorbing energy and forms floccus, limiting the crack growth, which were known as crack deflection and in-situ homogeneous toughening mechanism.

articleTitle: A Novel Low- Temperature Cu/SiO2 Hybrid Bonding Based on Functional Group Selective Construction
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Hybrid bonding technology is a high-density 3D integration technology that can significantly reduce the interconnect distance, allowing multifunctional chips to be processed independently. Therefore, it can enhance the flexibility of chip processing and mitigate production costs. However, in order to take into account the different degrees of high temperature tolerance of various heterogeneous chips and avoid the problems of wafer warping and device failure caused by inconsistent thermal expansion coefficients, it is urgent to develop a low temperature hybrid bonding process. At present, Cu and SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> remain the prevailing choices for interconnect materials in hybrid bonding technology. The key to achieving Cu/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> low temperature hybrid bonding is to simultaneously obtain an oxide-free Cu surface and a hydroxy-enriched SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> surface using the same surface activation process. Therefore, a novel approach for synergistic activation bonding has been devised and implemented, which involves the utilization of Ar/H2 plasma activation and citric acid immersion. By this way, strong Cu/Cu and SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> bonding pairs can be simultaneously achieved at 200°C. The evaluations through tensile testing and scanning electron microscopy reveal that both Cu/Cu and SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> exhibit sufficient strength to endure mechanical polishing without any interface defects. In summary, our method presents a promising solution for the low-temperature hybrid bonding of Cu/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, which promotes the future development of multifunctional chips 3D integration.

articleTitle: Research on Multi-Material Property Matching for 3D Printing in Electronic Information Packaging Equipment
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this paper, aiming at solving the problems of the various material types and the poor matching of the multiple materials in piezoelectric inkjet 3D printing, the compatibility test and analysis were carried out from four dimensions, namely the matching of ink physical properties and piezoelectric inkjet heads, the matching of the dielectric ink and the conductive ink formability, compatibility matching and functional performance matching. Through the testing and analysis of the relative dielectric constant, loss angle tangent, square resistivity and the physical properties, combined with the printing process verification, the material types and combinations of curved conformal circuit boards that could meet the design and process requirements are selected, which provides a good foundation for the promotion of piezoelectric inkjet 3D printing technology, and may accelerate the integrated manufacturing and rapid manufacturing of curved conformal circuits.

articleTitle: Three-Point Bending Test and Finite Element Analysis of Flexible Termination Multilayer Ceramic Capacitors
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Flexible Termination Multilayer Ceramic Capacitors (FTMLCCs) introduce a flexible electrode layer composed of resin and conductive filler on top of the typical three-layer electrode structure. This flexible layer can absorb significant bending deformation, thus protecting the internal ceramic structure without increasing the capacitor size or compromising its capacitance. In this study, FTMLCC of 1812 product was chosen as the research subject to quantitatively analyze the protective effect of the flexible electrode and the failure mechanism of cracking under bending loads. Simulation analysis was conducted to study the stress and strain distribution of the capacitor after three-point bending. Additionally, bending tests were performed on Multi-layer ceramic capacitors(MLCC) containing flexible electrodes, and a impedance analyzer was employed to address the issue of online monitoring of FTMLCC failures. By combining stress-strain testing to confirm the strain magnitude of the Printed Circuit Board(PCB) during bending, the strain result of PCB in experiments were compared with numerical simulation results to validate the rationality of the numerical model. The failure point of capacitor is located by infrared thermal imaging technology. The electrode structure, the defects of the flexible layer and the failure mode of FTMLCC were studied by metallographic analysis.

articleTitle: Study of the Delamination Mechanism at the Interfaces Between Cu and Polyimide Layers for WLCSP
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Fan-out packaging has emerged as a key packaging technology to meet the demands of critical integrated circuit chip products. Due to its light weight, thin design, compact size, and cost-effectiveness, this product aligns perfectly with the current trend of microelectronic devices that prioritize miniaturization, high functions, multi-functionality, and affordability. Its extensive use in mobile phones and other portable devices highlights its significance. However, despite its numerous advantages, concerns regarding reliability still persist. Thermal stress induced by the different thermal expansion coefficients between materials often leads to stress concentration, particularly in the region of the redistribution layer (RDL). Current research indicates that the RDL region is more susceptible to thermal stress gradients than the solder joint region. In this study, a semi-additive process was used to fabricate the RDL metal layer with surface mounted technology (SMT) and ball grid array (BGA) attached to it. The fabrication process included the deposition of dielectric layers, the mapping of the interdigital transducer (IDT) cavities, the deposition of a titanium/copper adhesion layer and the electroplating of the seed layer. after undergoing processes such as wet deb on ding, wet etching, polyimide solder mask film (SMF) patterning and print reflow, the product exhibited abnormal white discolouring around the solder balls due to delamination between the RDL and SMF. This delamination was primarily caused by a weak bond between the copper and the SMF due to insufficient material thickness and a mismatch in thermal expansion coefficients between the RDL and the SMF. Microscopic analysis of surface whitening samples, together with finite element modelling, shed light on the mechanisms behind copper/ polyimide (Cu/PI) cracking. Stress cracking around the solder balls during reflow was identified as a key factor leading to delamination. By optimising the RDL and SMF thicknesses, it was found that increasing the SMF thickness reduced the normal stresses on the SMF, while decreasing the Cu thickness also reduced the stress levels. By adjusting the appropriate RDL and SMF thicknesses, the problem of whitening around the chip solder balls was successfully addressed.

articleTitle: Luminescence properties of a novel K3Ca2(SO4)3F: Eu3+ red phosphor to improve R9 for WLED
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Phosphor as an essential light conversion material, directly affects optical properties of WLED. Conventional WLED device packaging predominantly employs the method of combining yellow phosphors with a blue LED chip. Using this technology, most WLED exhibit a deficiency in the red light spectrum and have low R9. Red phosphor can serve as an effective solution to such issues. Therefore, there is a pressing need to innovate and introduce new red phosphors to enhance the R9 value and thereby augment the performance of WLED. This paper proposes a novel K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Ca<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>F: Eu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> red phosphor to improve R9 for WLED. The findings indicate that the K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Ca<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>F: Eu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> phosphor can be activated under 397 nm and emit red light emission at 619 nm. The most favourable doping concentration for Eu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> ions was 13 mol%. The optimal sample achieved a color purity of 96.01 % and a lifetime of 0.419 ms. When the temperature reached 150 °C, the luminescence intensity of K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Ca<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>F: 13mol<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>Eu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> remained 89.5% of that at room temperature. K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Ca<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>F: Eu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> phosphor and commercial YAG: Ce yellow phosphor were mixed and encapsulated onto a near-ultraviolet LED chip to obtain a warm WLED device. The device emitted bright light with Ra of 66.1, R9 of 44 and CCT 4417 K under a driving current of 300 mA. We confirm the substantial potential of the K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Ca<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>F: Eu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> red phosphor for application in WLED lighting.

articleTitle: Programable Magnetic Driven Quantum Dot Microplates for Optical Information Encryption
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Quantum dots are a novel class of nanoscale luminescent materials, distinguished by their size-dependent emission color and remarkable color purity, holding significant value in optical applications. However, encapsulating quantum dots is imperative due to the presence of heavy metal elements and their low tolerance to water and oxygen. In this study, we utilized a non-toxic, odorless, and environmentally friendly green material, polydimethylsiloxane, employing a template method to fabricate thin films with a microplate structure by pre-etching the desired patterns onto silicon wafers on molds. Leveraging the excellent non-contact and rapid response properties of magnetic fields, we encapsulated quantum dots along with iron powder within the microplates. Thus, through manipulation of the magnetic field, we could achieve deflection angles of the microplates exceeding 50°, enabling the display of encapsulated quantum dots in colored patterns. By further manipulating the magnetic field to control the curvature of the microplates on the film, we could reveal all information only when the bending amplitude was sufficiently large, thereby enabling the hiding and displaying of patterned QR code information. This study successfully encapsulated quantum dots and iron powder within microplate structures and utilized magnetic manipulation to indirectly control quantum dots, thus ensuring information confidentiality.

articleTitle: Pressureless Large-Area (15 × 15 mm2) Bonding by Novel Silver Paste for WBG Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Among the most effective die-attach materials for achieving wide-bandgap (WBG) device performance in harsh environments is sintered silver. However, organic residues and low shear strength largely limit the practical application of sintered silver in large-area interconnections. In this paper, by proposing a novel silver paste, robust large-area (15 × 15 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) interconnections are achieved at pressureless and 300 °C sintering temperature in air atmosphere. The relationship between the shear strength and microstructural changes in the areal distribution in large-area interconnections is studied in detail. The shear strength distribution law in large-area interconnections is studied in detail. The average shear strength of the bonding joint is 29.6 MPa, the edge shear strength is the lowest at 25.4 MPa, and the shear strength distribution is uniform. The development of novel silver paste has successfully solved the problems of low shear strength in large-area sintering, and greatly promoted the practical application of high-power density dies.

articleTitle: Investigation on the Numerical Modeling of Continuous Welding Stress Evolution Behavior in SiP
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As an important packaging form of high density integration of electronic products, SiP ceramic envelope is widely used in the aerospace, navigation and communication and other fields. Due to the difference in thermal deformation between the ceramic substrate and the metal enclosure, obvious residual stress is generated in the welding area, and the superimposed stress in the subsequent process will aggravate the cracking failure risk of SiP ceramic envelope. However, the cumulative evolution behavior of stress in SiP ceramic envelope under continuous welding conditions has not been clarified. In this paper, a thermo-elastic-plastic numerical model of welding stress of SiP ceramic envelope is established to study the cumulative evolution behavior of welding stress of SiP ceramic envelope under brazing, surface mounting, seam welding and temperature cycle conditions. Based on the stress state regulation, low stress welding technology of SiP ceramic envelope is obtained. The results show that: (1) the stress caused by the thermal mismatch between the ceramic substrate and the metal enclosure is concentrated in the four corners of the sealing frame, and when the parallel seam welding of the cover plate increases the structural stiffness of the metal enclosure, the thermal mismatch between the metal enclosure and the ceramic substrate will be aggravated. With the decrease of temperature, the stress level continues to increase. Although the stress level decreases in the high temperature due to the plastic flow and thermal mismatch relief, the stress level increases significantly when the temperature is lowered. (2) Through the use of AuSn solder and MoCu composite frame design can significantly reduce the stress level of SiP ceramic envelope, improve packaging reliability, and the stress relief by the composite frame design is better.

articleTitle: Research on Corrosion Failure Mechanism of Aluminum Electrolytic Capacitors
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Aluminum electrolytic capacitors are widely used in circuits such as power supplies, energy management systems, audio amplifiers, etc. due to their high electrical capacity, good voltage stability, and low impedance characteristics. The application in consumer electronics, industrial control, communication products, instruments, and other fields is particularly significant. However, aluminum electrolytic capacitors are prone to corrosion failure due to their typical structure of adding electrolyte to the internal aluminum foil, making chloride ion pollution a core issue in aluminum electrolytic capacitor. In recent years, due to the COVID-19 and other factors, some chlorine containing disinfectant was used for disinfection and sterilization, which brought risks to the reliability of aluminum electrolytic capacitors. In order to study the corrosion mechanism of aluminum electrolytic capacitors caused by organic solvents containing chlorine, the failure point was located through electrical parameter testing and microscopic analysis. And the source of abnormal chloride ions was confirmed through ion chromatography analysis and on-site investigation. The corrosion failure was reproduced using pre-treatment of chlorine containing substances and high temperature operating life test. The results indicate that chlorinated organic solvents could penetrate the capacitor plug and decompose into free chloride ions, ultimately causing corrosion of the anode aluminum foil. Based on the failure mechanism of corrosion in aluminum electrolytic capacitor, corresponding optimization protection methods were proposed to improve the reliability of capacitors. By optimizing the manufacturing process of capacitors, improving the purity of electrolyte, and improving the operating environment of capacitors, the occurrence rate of corrosion failure can be effectively reduced, and the reliability and service life of capacitors could be improved.

articleTitle: Novel Copper Filling Methods for 2 μm × 20 μm TSVs With an Electroless Deposited Co or Atomic Layer Deposited Ru Seed Layer
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As the interconnect integration density continues to increase, there is a growing trend to investigate high-quality and low-cost approaches to fill through-silicon vias (TSVs) with small critical dimensions (CDs) and high aspect ratios (ARs). In this study, we tried to fill <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2 \mu \mathrm{m}\times 20\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> TSVs with alkaline Cu electrochemical deposition (ECD) followed by acidic Cu ECD based on two different liners. One is a Co liner fabricated by low-cost electroless deposition (ELD), while the other is a Ru liner fabricated using atomic layer deposition (ALD). For both two TSV filling technical paths, alkaline Cu ECD plays important roles in reducing Co layer corrosion and mitigating high-resistance TSV bottom Ru layer issues respectively, demonstrating promising applications in advanced packaging.

articleTitle: The Application of THz-TDR in Failure Analysis of ICs in FCBGA Packages
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: IC failure analysis includes not only wafer failure, but also package failure. Especially for complex packaging devices, conventional non-destructive methods such as FCBGA, X-RAY or CT can not accurately locate the packaging defects in integrated circuits. In this paper, the principle of non-destructive terahertz time-domain reflectometry (THz-TDR) is introduced, and its application in IC failure analysis is illustrated. The TDR uses a laser signal generated by a signal generator to send a high-frequency pulse with a fast rise time to the IC. When an impedance discontinuity is encountered, part of the pulse energy is reflected back, and by monitoring the time at which these reflected signals arrive at the oscilloscope and comparing them to the size of the original pulse, it is possible to determine if there is an impedance change in the line. The open circuit and short circuit faults in the integrated circuit can be quickly located using the TDR machine.

articleTitle: Chip-to-Antenna Plane Transmission Structure Design for Antenna in Package
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: This paper presents a study of the millimeterwave phased array integration technology based on threedimensional heterogeneous redistribution layer (RDL), and we explore the influence of heterogeneous RDL on the RF characteristics of millimeter-wave phased array microsystems. At the same time, we compare the characteristics of different packaging processes, analyze the low-loss interconnect structure under high-complexity packaging, reasonably design the chip-to-antenna planar transmission structure. The simulation results show that the optimized design has a return loss S11 < -10 dB in the frequency band from 33 GHz to 57 GHz and a VSWR value VSWR = 1.0022 corresponding to the point of resonance frequency 47.65 GHz, which provides the possibility of realizing the design of the packaged antenna structure with low-loss, high-integration, and high-reliability.

articleTitle: In-Situ Low-Temperature Bonding for Silicon-on-Quartz Substrates
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Heterogeneous integration exploits the complementary advantages of different semiconductor materials to achieve a major performance leap in manufacturing new-generation chips and devices. Bonding of silicon and quartz glass is widely used in the fabrication of MEMS devices and micro fluidic chips. In general, high bonding temperatures are required to achieve high bonding energy for interfacial reinforcement. However, for heterogeneous materials, the large mismatch in thermal expansion coefficients between heterogeneous materials can limit the bonding temperature and interface strength. In addition, non-in-situ bonding can cause manufacturing inefficiencies and interfacial defects. In this paper, we propose a strategy for low-temperature in-situ bonding of silica and quartz glass at ~150°C. The bonding is performed by mild water vapor-assisted free radical bonding. Mild water vapor-assisted radical activation increases the density of hydroxyl groups on the surface of silica and glass, which improves the surface properties. As a result, we have successfully achieved low-damage and high-strength (~1.8 J/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) bonding between silicon and quartz glass for Silicon-on-Quartz (SOQ) substrates.

articleTitle: Impedance Modeling and Analysis of Multi-pair P/G TSVs and Solder Balls in 3D ICs
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
