abstract: With the rapid development of high integration and low power consumption requirements for 3D TSV ICs, chips are stacked vertically and connected by through silicon via (TSV) to achieve inter-layer transmission. At present, the density of 3D integration technology is rising, and besides, the number of TSVs and solder balls is increasing. The electromagnetic coupling between them causes serious PI problems, so it is necessary to study the influences of TSV and solder ball size parameters on PDN impedance. In this paper, the impedance modeling and analysis of multi-pair power/ground TSVs (P/G TSVs) and solder balls in 3D integrated circuits are researched. Aiming at the structure of two-layer stacked PDN interconnected by multiple pairs of TSVs and solder balls, HFSS modeling is used to analyze the influences of changing the radius, height, oxide layer thickness, and horizontal and vertical distances of nine pairs of TSVs and solder balls on PDN impedance in 0–20 GHz frequency band. It is found that the height of the solder balls is the main factor affecting the resonant frequency. When the height of the solder balls is changed, the resonant frequency will increase. In addition, TSV radius, height, solder ball height and the vertical distance of P/G TSV pairs have significant effects on the maximum parallel resonance peak. The height of the solder balls increases from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{5}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{25}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex>, and the maximum parallel resonance peak value increases from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{54.78}\ \boldsymbol{\Omega}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{75.8}\ \boldsymbol{\Omega}$</tex>, increasing by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{21.02}\ \boldsymbol{\Omega}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Significantly Enhanced Thermal Conductivity and Dielectric Properties of Epoxy Composite Films Derived by Constructing Networks of Surface Coated Alumina Fillers
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Electronic packaging technology is experiencing rapid evolution, marked by increased device integration and power density. The effective dissipation of accumulated internal heat during device operation lies as a pivotal factor in determining the long-term reliability of devices. Thermally conductive polymer composites, extensively employed in the realm of electronic packaging, exhibit relatively limited thermal conductivity. The strategy of integrating copious amounts of ceramic and conductive particles into the polymer matrix has been shown to significantly enhance the thermal attributes of the composites. However, this approach concurrently imposes detrimental effects on their mechanical and electrical characteristics, manifested by reduced fracture strength and a notable increase in dielectric loss. Herein, the thermal conductivity of the epoxy composite is enhanced upon the addition of alumina particles surface coated with polydopamine (Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-PDA), which facilitates their uniform dispersion within the epoxy resin matrix and enables dense interfacial adhesion between the filler and the resin. This methodology circumvents the adverse impacts on mechanical and electrical properties that typically accompany increased filler content. According to the Dinger-Funk densest packing theory, a thermal conductive network is established by the orderly arrangement of multi-sized filler particles, which substantially elevates the thermal conductivity. Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> -PDA/Epoxy composite films display an exceptional thermal conductivity of 1.62 Wm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>K<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>, alongside low dielectric loss (D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</inf>0.006 at 1 kHz), a low coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE, a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>~54.5 ppm K<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> between 30–120 °C). The success in applying the polydopamine surface coating strategy and the multi-sized densest packing theory not only underscores a significant leap in the field but also paves the way for advancing the performance of thermally conductive composites.

articleTitle: A Predictive Maintenance Approach for Power Converters Using Artificial Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this paper, a predictive maintenance approach using Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) to analyze the ripple waveforms is proposed to estimate the degradation status of electrolytic capacitors in power converters. An off-the-shelf full-brick DC-DC power converter was used to build a 380 V to 24 V power conversion system for investigation. Powered by advanced Digital Signal Processor (DSP), a universal ripple sensing module was developed to acquire and process the ripple waveforms of voltage and current on the electrolytic capacitors from the primary and secondary sides of the power conversion system. Accelerated aging test of the electrolytic capacitors was performed and ripple waveforms of the power conversion system with the electrolytic capacitors at different degradation status were obtained by the ripple sensing module. An ANN model was established by analyzing the evolution of ripple waveforms with the aging time. To verify the capability and accuracy of the ANN based predictive maintenance approach, independent aging tests were performed in parallel and the obtained ripple waveforms were used to determine the degradation status of electrolytic capacitors. The results show that predicted aging time agree well with experimental data.

articleTitle: Simulation of Electrojet Printing of Nano Metal Paste as Interconnect Bonding Intermediate
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Nano metal paste has broad prospects as interconnect bonding intermediate with high density bumps, but the existing nano metal transfer technologies limit the accurate coverage of bumps by nano metal paste. In this study, a direct transfer technology based on electrojet printing is proposed to achieve accurate coating of micron bumps. The process of electrojet printing was simulated, and the effect of driving voltage and nano metal paste on the electrojet printing behavior were explored. The simulation results show that the cone jet of 3.6 µm is generated Efficiently at 3800 V. In addition, the decrease in the efficiency of electrojet printing due to the increase of surface tension and viscosity coefficient of solution can be attenuated by increasing the driving voltage.

articleTitle: Various Shaped Phosphors-in-Glass Lenses by Isobam-APS gel Casting for white Light Emitting Diodes
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Blue chips with a color converter make up the majority of white light diodes (WLEDs). In lighting fields, WLEDs often need lens to control divergence angle of light, at the same time, the reliability of WLEDs also needs to be improved. In this paper, Isobam-APS gel casting was used to create Phosphors-in-Glass (PIG) in a variety of shapes. The PIG was obtained by sintering amorphous silica nanoparticles and commercial YAG:Ce<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> phosphors. The PIG was a color converter, also as a lens. The samples' surface morphology and phase were examined using X-ray powder diffraction (XRD) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). The results indicated that the phosphors were not eliminated in the course of preparation. The emission and excitation spectra of the PIG were determined by fluorescence spectrophotometer at temperatures from 25°C to 250°C. When the temperature was 150°C, the excitation and emission intensity of the PIG retained 85% of intensity at 25°C. The PIG emitted yellow light with quantum efficiency high as 96.39%. The PIG was combined with blue chip to obtain WLED. Under 3V, 100mA test, the luminous efficiency of the WLED was 94.08 lm/W. In conclusion, PIG obtained from amorphous silica nanoparticles and YAG:Ce<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> has the advantage of superior efficiency, heat conductivity and quantum efficiency for its inorganic material. Various shaped Phosphors-in-Glass lenses can be prepared by this method, high performance WLEDs made of a blue chip and PIG lens are more competitive in various lighting fields.

articleTitle: Bipolar Degradation of SiC MOSFET Body Diode Under Constant Current Stress
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Bipolar degradation constitutes a significant long-term reliability concern that can affect the durability of Silicon Carbide (SiC) devices. In this study, the application of a large constant current for 186 hours to the body diode of the 1.2 kV SiC metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors (MOSFETs) resulted in the nucleation and expansion of stacking faults due to the recombination energy release from electron-hole pairs. This is attributed to inherent flaws in the SiC material, such as basal plane dislocations or other dislocations. These stacking faults have a significant impact on carrier lifetime and become pathways for reverse leakage, resulting in increased forward voltage and on-resistance of the body diode. Furthermore, the observed changes are in opposition to those observed after high-temperature negative gate-bias stress, indicating that the observed degradation of the device is attributed to the constant current applied to the body diode.

articleTitle: Finite Element Analysis of the Sintered Layer and Buffer Layer on SiC Module Reliability
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Thermal fatigue failure is a key issue that affects the long-term reliability of silicon carbide (SiC) power modules. It is urgent to select appropriate packaging materials to release the thermal mismatch between module layers. However, packaging using traditional sintered layer solder cannot meet the demands of module reliability under high power density working conditions. In this paper, the effect of the sintered layer with a novel nano-silver (Ag) solder on the reliability of SiC power modules is investigated by using the finite element analysis (FEA) method. Simulation results of thermal-mechanical modeling under power cycling conditions show that increasing the thickness of the Ag sintered layer can effectively reduce the thermal stress of the module without affecting the chip junction temperature. Moreover, the effect of introducing a molybdenum buffer layer on releasing module stress and improving module lifetime is further explored.

articleTitle: Packaging Evaluations of SiC MOSFETs Based on Cu-Clip Interconnection Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As SiC devices evolve towards higher power density, higher integration, higher voltage tolerance, higher switching frequency, and higher junction temperature tolerance, traditional Si-based packaging technologies can no longer meet the packaging requirements of SiC power devices. To further exploit the excellent characteristics of SiC MOSFETs, such as high thermal conductivity, wide bandgap, high switching speed, high operating temperature, and low on-resistance, it is imperative to explore new packaging processes suitable for current SiC devices. This paper employs the Clip interconnection architecture to replace traditional wire bonding, significantly enhancing the current-carrying capacity and heat dissipation capability of the circuits, while effectively reducing parasitic inductance. Compared to Al wire bonding, the Cu Clip interconnection architecture reduces the power loop resistance to 8.7% and the parasitic inductance to 57%. When a fixed power or current is applied to the power loop, the Cu Clip significantly improves the device's heat dissipation and current-carrying capabilities. Additionally, the effects of using Cu and Ag solders for Cu Clip sintering on SiC MOSFETs performance are compared, followed by an electro-thermal-magnetic performance evaluation of the SiC MOSFETs packaging process based on the Cu Clip interconnection architecture.

articleTitle: Design and Characteristics of Thermoelectric and Liquid Cooling Composite Active Heat Dissipation of Power Electronics
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Heat dissipation is an unavoidable problem in the field of power electronics, resulting in numerous failures and performance degradation. A composite heat dissipation of thermoelectric and liquid cooling was realized by utilizing the interstitial space between N-type and P-type thermoelectric materials as a microchannel for liquid cooling, and this composite heat dissipation can effectively improve the heat dissipation capability of power electronics. The influence of the different heat dissipation methods, including natural heat dissipation, thermoelectric cooling, liquid cooling, and composite heat dissipation of thermoelectric and liquid cooling, on the operating temperature of power electronic was firstly analyzed and compared. Furthermore, the effects of thermoelectric driving voltage and fluid flow rate on the operating temperature of power electronics were further investigated under the combined heat dissipation method of thermoelectric and liquid cooling. The results indicate that thermoelectric and liquid cooling composite active heat dissipation is a more effective active thermal management technique compared to single thermoelectric or liquid cooling.

articleTitle: Ultra-High Frequency Acoustic Micro-Imaging Simulation on Defect Detection at the TSV-Cu Bulk/Bonding Interface
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Three-dimensional integration technology based on through-silicon vias (TSVs) is an effective approach to achieving high-performance and miniaturized system-level packaging. Internal defects within TSVs and hybrid bonding interfaces are more likely to occur and are harder to detect. Traditional methods are no longer able to meet the detection requirements, making non-destructive testing of micro defects such as voids and cracks in TSVs a new challenge. In this work, a non-destructive testing method for micro defects in TSV-Cu based on ultra-high frequency acoustic micro-imaging is proposed, targeting internal defects with different pore sizes and bonding interfaces. According to the theory of ultrasound propagation, the finite element method (FEM) is used to analyze the acoustic-solid coupling field excited by focused acoustic pressure. The propagation process of ultra-high frequency ultrasound in TSV-Cu is studied, and the interaction mechanism of different types of internal defects on the acoustic wave response and the propagation law of ultra-high frequency ultrasound and the distribution of energy fields are analyzed, observing the reflection, projection, and refraction of sound waves during propagation. The influence of micro defects on the propagation of ultra-high frequency ultrasound, characteristic extraction of weak echo signals, and identification of tiny defects in TSVs are conducted, supplemented by theoretical analysis to verify and optimize the detection method, ultimately achieving efficient and high-precision detection of micro defects in TSVs. The research results provide an effective technical means for the reliability analysis of three-dimensional integration products and will promote the basic theories and technological innovation of IC packaging testing.

articleTitle: Investigating Coalescence Kinetics in Cu Nanoparticle by Molecular Dynamics and 3D Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: This study presents a dual approach combining molecular dynamics simulations and experimental analysis to explore the sintering behavior of copper (Cu) nanoparticles. Our simulation model comprises 240 nanoparticles, through which we systematically examine the coalescence kinetics during the sintering process. The simulations provide a detailed view of the particle interactions, structural evolution, and the mechanisms driving nanoparticle fusion at the atomic level. Complementing the simulations, we conducted 3D reconstructions using Focused Ion Beam Scanning Electron Microscopy (FIB-SEM) to characterize the microstructure of the sintered nanoparticles. This hybrid approach not only deepens our understanding of the fundamental processes governing the sintering of Cu nanoparticles but also bridges the gap between theoretical predictions and experimental observations, offering insights into the optimization of sintering processes in practical applications.

articleTitle: Understanding the Sintering Mechanism of Cu@Ag Nanoparticles for Power Device Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Due to the small size effect, nano-metal paste is regarded as the famous die-attach material. Nano metal paste has excellent thermal conductivity, which could be used to prepare high-temperature resistant interconnect joints at low temperatures. Unfortunately, during the sintering process, nano-silver paste has a high porosity and is prone to electromigration. Nano-Cu paste is prone to oxidation, which is not conducive to the mechanical properties of interconnect structures. The nanocomposite paste of Cu and Ag has gradually gained widespread attention, such as Cu-Ag mixed structure and Cu@Ag coating structure. These can effectively hinder the oxidation of Cu nanoparticles and the electromigration of Ag nanoparticles, which is beneficial for improving the service characteristics of power devices. However, the sintering mechanism of composite nanoparticles has not been revealed, and the industrial application of composite paste lacks theoretical analysis. In this paper, molecular dynamics (MD) is used to describe the sintering behavior of Cu@Ag composite nanoparticles. The effects of Ag surface coating thickness and sintering heating speed on sintering properties were investigated. The MD results show thinner Ag shells and slower heating rates are beneficial for atomic diffusion and improve the reliability of nanoparticle sintering. The degree of sintering is closely related to atomic motion and energy conversion. The phase transition form of nanoparticles is affected by the heating rate.

articleTitle: Coupling Characteristics of BGA Solder Balls at High Frequencies: A Simulation Study on Electromagnetic-Thermal-Mechanical Interactions Considering Skin and Proximity Effects
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the development of high-frequency and high-density System-in-Package (SiP) technologies, the coupling of electromagnetic, thermal, and mechanical stresses has become a significant reliability issue for packaging interconnect structures. This study investigates the electromagnetic-thermal-mechanical coupling problem of BGA solder balls in packaging interconnect structures, analyzing the multi-physics coupling characteristics under high-frequency conditions, as well as the impact of skin and proximity effects on current distribution and electromagnetic losses of the solder balls. The electromagnetic losses of the BGA were calculated at frequencies of 100 kHz and 5 GHz. Considering the influence of the temperature field on the material conductivity, a bidirectional electro-thermal coupling simulation was performed to obtain the temperature variation induced by electromagnetic losses. When the frequency increased from 100 kHz to 5 GHz, the electromagnetic losses caused the maximum temperature of the solder balls to rise by 18.5%. The temperature gradient was applied to the stress field to calculate the equivalent thermal stress of the solder balls, revealing that the thermal stress was primarily concentrated in the transition region between the solder ball and the pad. After optimizing the solder ball model, the thermal stress results became more accurate, and the maximum thermal stress at the transition between the solder ball and the pad decreased by 18.2%, indicating improved mechanical performance.

articleTitle: A Study on Low-Cost Stress Release of Ultra-Thin Glass Bridges for High-Frequency and High-Speed Signal Interconnects
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the vigorous development in the fields of artificial intelligence and high-performance computing, the nanometer fabrication process of integrated circuits is gradually approaching its physical limits. Therefore, the importance of extending and expanding Moore's Law through chip three-dimensional heterogeneous integration has become increasingly prominent. To meet the demand for high-frequency and high-speed signal interconnection, employing ultra-thin glass bridges as part of a high-density packaging solution has become an inevitable trend. However, the severe stress-induced warpage caused by ultra-thin glass has remained a core bottleneck. It is noteworthy that there is scarce literature proposing methods to improve the warpage of ultra-thin glass wafers. Hence, this paper proposes a low-cost, simple, and effective new method to address the warpage issue of ultra-thin glass wafers. Initially, the glass wafer is temporarily bonded, followed by mechanical grinding to remove most of the glass. Subsequently, a combination of wet etching with a 10% hydrofluoric acid solution and chemical-mechanical polishing (CMP) is utilized to remove the sub-damage layer on the glass wafer, thereby releasing stress. During the grinding process, the wafer is subjected to mechanical friction and thermal stress, resulting in the formation of a sub-damage layer on the surface, which may lead to warpage or even fracture. Through the proposed method in this paper, an ultra-thin glass wafer with a thickness of less than 80µm and warpage less than 0.2mm was ultimately obtained, with warpage conditions improved by over 50%.

articleTitle: Residual Stress Control Based on Electroplated Metal Grain Characteristics in Panel-Level Glass Advanced Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The low loss, coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) match, and dimensional stability of glass in large panel manufacturing makes glass advanced packaging technology a great choice for chiplet systems. However, the residual stress of the metal layer generated during the TGV (through-glass-via) electroplating process is one of the major technical bottlenecks of glass packaging, resulting in glass-metal layer delamination and glass breakage. This paper demonstrated for the first time a method to achieve regulation of the residual stress by controlling the grain growth of the plated Cu in the electroplating process. Detailed relationships among the residual stress, Cu grain characteristics, and process parameters were studied during both the plating and annealing processes. During the electroplating process, test vehicles with different plating parameters (current density, accelerator, inhibitor and leveler ratio) were fabricated, then the Cu grain characteristics were characterized using focused ion beam (FIB), and the related orientation and residual stress were measured using the X-ray diffraction (XRD) technology. The results showed that there are four types of textures in the Cu plating layer, namely (111), (200), (220), and (311), and the residual stress of Cu film varied with the plating parameters changed. During plating, the residual stress and (111) texture showed a positive correlation, and nanotwins can help relieve high residual stresses. Additionally, the recrystallization of the plating grains occurred during the annealing process, accompanied by an increase in grain size while the residual stresses were reduced. Cu films with highly (220)-oriented or (111)-oriented were more stable during annealing and exhibited lower residual stresses after annealing. Ultimately, the residual stress in electroplated Cu was successfully regulated by optimizing the plating and annealing process.

articleTitle: Research on Efficient Charging and Highly Reliable Non-Contact Welding Sealing Technology for Ultra-Thin Silicon-Based Vapor Chambers
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In recent years, with the trend towards miniaturization and integration of integrated circuits (IC), the emergence of high-temperature hotspots has become a key challenge restricting the enhancement of chip performance, urgently requiring effective thermal management solutions. Directly integrating Vapor Chambers (VC) onto electronic devices is an effective means to address hotspot issues. However, the thermal mismatch between traditional metal-made VC and semiconductor materials lead to suboptimal performance. Although the use of Thermal Interface Materials (TIM) can alleviate the effects of thermal mismatch, this approach introduces additional thermal resistance, affecting thermal management efficiency. Therefore, silicon-based VC, with their similar thermal expansion coefficients to semiconductor materials, demonstrate significant advantages and broad prospects. This paper designs and manufactures silicon-based VC with Ni pads and establishes a Charging system that uses steam to remove non-condensable gases and deionized water as the working fluid. After Charging, the Ni pads are heated by induction to melt Sn95Ag5 alloy solder, sealing the Charging port. The results show that the VC sample successfully Charged with 80 μl of deionized water, with an error range controlled within ±5 μl. Under the condition of 100°C, after continuous operation for 96 h, there were no issues of working fluid leakage from the VC sample. This study proposes an effective method for Charging and sealing silicon-based VC, avoiding the need to weld Charging tubes at the VC Charging port, thereby simplifying the testing process. This is significant for promoting the practical application of silicon-based VC cooling technology.

articleTitle: Overview of the Sulfide Corrosion Mechanism of Key Susceptible Metal Materials in Typical Electronic Components
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: This paper systematically expounds the corrosion mechanism of key susceptible metal materials in typical electronic components in a sulfur-containing atmosphere. It introduces the structural composition and sulfide-corroded metal parts of chip resistors and optocouplers, discussing the sulfide corrosion failure mechanism of some susceptible metals. The paper reviews the corrosion conditions of typical metals like copper, silver, aluminum, and tin in sulfur dioxide and hydrogen sulfide atmospheres. Finally, it proposes currently used sulfide protection technologies, providing insights for the reliability assessment and protection of electronic components and supporting the high-quality development of the electronics industry.

articleTitle: Small Sample Data-Driven Multi-Objective Optimization of MEMS Sensor Molding Process Parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this paper, for the molding defects of MEMS sensors, a multi-objective optimization and decision-making method based on small-sample data-driven molding process parameters is proposed on the basis of MoldFlow software. Firstly, using Latin-square experimental design, each test scheme is substituted into a finite element model for numerical simulation, and a multi-objective optimization model of mold temperature, melt temperature, injection time, pressure-holding time, holding pressure with wire sweep index and Warpage deformation amount, is established by using a random forest algorithm based on the simulation results, and the three hyperparameters of the model are optimized using the grid search method to improve the prediction accuracy. Secondly, multi-objective gray wolf algorithm is applied to optimize the multi-objective optimization model and obtain a Pareto Solution set and finally the subjective and objective comprehensive entropy weight-TOPSIS method is used to evaluate and decide the optimal combination of process parameters. The results show that the correlation coefficients R of the two optimization objectives are greater than 0.98, which indicates that the prediction accuracy of RF model is high, and meanwhile, after the optimization of MOGWO algorithm, the above two quality indexes are improved. The feasibility of the multi-objective optimization method for plastic package molding process parameters based on MoldFlow, RF and MOGWO is illustrated.

articleTitle: Electroplated Ni-W-P Amorphous Layer and the Interaction Between Ni-W-P Barrier and Sn-Bi Solder
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In the field of advanced electronic packaging, the common method for structural interconnection is using Sn-based solder and Cu-based substrate soldering. However, the reaction between Sn-based solder and Cu-based substrate is rapid, leading to the formation of thick and brittle Cu-Sn IMCs at the interface, causing stress concentration in the solder joint. Meanwhile, the consumption of Cu substrate results in the generation of Kirkendall voids, leading to a sharp decrease in mechanical performance and eventual fracture. During production, a diffusion barrier layer is typically introduced between the solder and substrate to suppress the formation of Cu-Sn IMCs and enhance the reliability of the solder joint. Currently, the industry often employs Ni-P plating as the diffusion barrier layer. However, the Ni-P diffusion barrier layer is prone to long-term failure. In the soldering process, Ni-P generates columnar crystalline structure Ni3P, providing diffusion pathways for atoms. By introducing the new element W, the recrystallization of the barrier layer can be effectively suppressed, promoting the formation of an amorphous structure, eliminating grain boundaries as diffusion pathways, thereby exhibiting excellent diffusion barrier performance, especially improved thermal stability. Based on this background, this work developed a ternary Ni-W-P diffusion barrier layer prepared by electroplating (with a P content of 14-15wt% and W content of 7-8wt%), which exhibits uniform dense coating and good thermal stability. The study compared the interface reactions of Cu/Ni-W-P/Sn-58Bi and Cu/Ni-P/Sn-58Bi after soldering at 180°C for different durations. The results indicate that the IMC layer at the Cu/Ni-P/Sn-58Bi interface grows rapidly, whereas under the same heat treatment, the thickness of the IMC layer at the Ni-W-P/Sn-58Bi interface is significantly smaller than that of the Ni-P interface layer, with the IMC layer mainly composed of (Ni, Cu)3Sn4 phase. The solder joints formed in Ni-W-P/Sn-58Bi are very thin and stable during different soldering processes, demonstrating the blocking effect of the Ni-W-P layer. The findings reveal that Ni-W-P coatings hold great promise as diffusion barrier layers, capable of enhancing the reliability of long-term reflow soldering procedures.

articleTitle: Research on Plastic Encapsulated Microelectronics Construction Analysis Technology Based on Failure Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Plastic encapsulated microelectronics (PEMs) is widely applied in fields such as artificial intelligence, electronic communication, automotive electronics, and household appliances, due to its excellent performance, light weight and low cost. PEMs, as an important electronic device packaged with polymer composite materials, have a significant impact on the performance of electronic devices due to their reliability and stability. However, due to the non-airtightness and inherent moisture absorption of plastic packaging materials, various failure problems could be found in PEMs during the installation and use. In the context of low cost and high reliability of electronic components, how to identify the reliability risks of PEMs has become a focus of attention. construction analysis (CA), as a risk analysis method for the design, structure, materials, and manufacturing process of electronic components through physical, chemical, and other analytical techniques, could be used to analyze the reliability risks of PEMs to determine whether it can meet the technical requirements of special application environments. In this paper, the procedure of PEMs construction analysis would be summarized. And the structural weaknesses and sensitive stresses of PEMs would be analyzed through typical cases such as delamination and poor bonding. Then construction analysis based on the failure mechanism of PEMs would be proposed. Moreover, the structural risk of PEMs would be evaluated via stress injection, non-destructive and destructive analysis techniques. The targeted optimization suggestions based on construction analysis results could proposed to improve the reliability of PEMs and provide strong support for the stable operation of electronic devices.

articleTitle: Simulation of Heat Dissipation of CPU Chip in Smart Phone
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As smartphone technology advances, enhanced performance in smaller form factors presents significant thermal management challenges, particularly for CPU chips. Herein, we studied the heat dissipation mechanism of CPU chips under various conditions, using computational fluid dynamics. We focus on three aspects: mobile phone design, test environment, and modeling type. Comparing temperature data, we found chip arrangement affects PCB layout and overall phone temperature. Simplified CPU models speed up the simulation process. Using JEDEC R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">JA</inf> and R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">JB</inf>tests, we obtained CPU thermal resistance to air and to PCB. The research aims to understand how design parameters, such as chip layout and cooling mechanisms, affect heat dissipation, thereby informing manufacturers on effective thermal management strategies.

articleTitle: Design and Realization of Multi Channel Programmable Power Supply SIP Based on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Owing to its excellent parallel computing capabilities and distinctive on-site programmability, Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) technology is deemed indispensable within specialized domains. Nonetheless, prevailing methodologies relying on discrete components to build power supply circuits for FPGA entail considerable drawbacks, including substantial footprint, elevated design expenditures, diminished stability, and pronounced electromagnetic interference, thereby circumscribing the breadth of FPGA utilization scenarios. This study endeavors to mitigate such constraints by devising a Power Management System-in-Package (SIP) featuring multiple independent and configurable power rails, tailored to the power exigencies of large-scale FPGA characterized by high core current demands and different power supply voltage levels for multiple BANKs. The proposed system integrates nine DC-DC units and one LDO unit to furnish autonomous power delivery to ten distinct power rails, each offering individually adjustable outputs. Programming control is realized through the utilization of compact logic devices for power enablement and millisecond-level timing management. The buried PCB technology is applied to encapsulate multiple active and passive devices into a single module measuring <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$22 \text{mm} \times 22 \text{mm} \times 7.4 \text{mm}$</tex>. Experimental evaluation of the module's VOUT1 reveals an approximate conversion efficiency of 89.2% under typical output conditions of 1V10A. When configured solely with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 22 \text{uF}$</tex> ceramic capacitors and subjected to a substantial load of 20A, the observed output ripple remains <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\leq 1.95\%$</tex>. The module boasts a maximum total output power of 125W and exhibits robust operational stability within an environmental range spanning from -55°C to 85°C, with a notable maximum shock resistance acceleration exceeding <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\geq 5000 \mathrm{g}$</tex>. The embedded power module implemented in this study features multiple power rails, robust environmental stability, and rapid deployment capabilities, thereby adeptly addressing the intricate power supply requisites of FPGA systems and broadening the spectrum of FPGA application scenarios.

articleTitle: Microstructure and Properties of SnInBiZn Medium-Entropy Solder Alloy
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Low-temperature Pb-free solders with excellent properties and high reliability are desired for rapid developed three-dimensional packaging technology. In this study, the SnInBiZn medium-entropy solder alloy with the melting point of about 81°C was prepared by using vacuum melting technology. The wetting angle was about 40°. The SnInBiZn medium-entropy solder alloy consisted of InBi, Sn-In-Bi ternary and Zn-rich phases, and its tensile strength was about 38.23 MPa. A thin layer of Cu-Zn intermetallic compounds (IMCs) was generated between SnInBiZn medium-entropy solder and Cu reflowed at 165°C for 5 min, and its thickness was about 0.66 µm. The slow IMC growth rate at the SnInBiZn/Cu interface can be attributed to the relatively high mixing entropy of SnInBiZn solder.

articleTitle: Study on the Failure of the Middle Solder Joints of the Large-Size FCBGA
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the advent of the 5G era, FCBGA devices with large sizes and high stacking layers are being widely used. FCBGA uses solder joints to connect chips and substrates, and has advantages in high speed, high density, and low power consumption. However, solder joints of large-size FCBGA have a high failure risk in the board-level temperature cycle process, and the common failure locations are all in the corners of substrate. In this paper, the large-size FCBGA of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$6\times \text{mm}^{\ast}6\times \text{mm}$</tex> is taken as the research object. During the test, it was found that the solder joints in the middle of substrate were prone to failure, while the solder joints at the corners have a low risk of failure. Therefore, the effects of the CTE of substrate and PCB, and solder joint shape on solder joint failure in the middle location are analyzed through simulation, and proposes to predict the risk location through simulation in the package design phase, and then design a proper dummy ball at the risk location for stress buffering, so as to avoid the failure of functional solder joints.

articleTitle: Controlling the Quality of Inkjet-Printed Quantum Dot Film by Ink-Substrate Interaction
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The use of inkjet printing to produce quantum dots (QDs) for mini-LED display applications has gained a lot of attention lately. This is because inkjet printing, as opposed to other microscale patterning methods such as photolithography and imprint, is a more effective way to pattern QDs at the microscale with intended patterns. It is worthwhile to investigate the critical factors that influence the quality of inkjet-printed QD film since they can lower the cost and increase manufacturing efficiency. This study identifies the essential variables for maximizing QDs film inkjet printing quality. A deeper understanding of the interaction mechanism is obtained by inspecting the relationship between the QD ink and the substrate. On the other hand, QD morphology is used to assess the quality of the inkjet-printed QD film. The result indicates that the drop spacing between two adjacent droplet deposits on the substrate is one of the critical criteria that influences the printing quality of QD film. It is possible to obtain the uniform QDs film by adjusting the drop spacing value.

articleTitle: Characterization and Mechanism of Sintered-Silver Die-Attach on Electroless Nickel Surface Finish with Different Phosphorus Content
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The low temperature silver (Ag) sintering technology has attracted a lot of attention as die-attach for power electronics modules packaging. The most reported studies involved sintered-Ag bonding on Ag or gold (Au) surface finish. Compared to Ag or Au, electroless nickel (phosphorus) or Ni(P) is a cost-effective and widely-used process for surface-finishing module substrates. However, research on sintered-Ag bonding on the Ni(P) surface is limited. In this study, IGBT devices were attached using pressureless Ag-sintering on electroless Ni(P)-plated substrates with different P content. Mechanical, electrical, and thermal properties were characterized via die-shear strength, static output characteristics, and thermal resistance, respectively. TEM and EDS were then conducted to investigate the bonding mechanism between sintered-Ag on Ni(P). The findings in this study helps to understand the effect of P content and promote the application of sintered-Ag die-attach on Ni(P) surface finish for power module packaging<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>This work was supported in part by the National Natural Science Foundation of China (No. 52107198), in part by the Natural Science Foundation of Guangdong Province (No. 2023A1515011854), and in part by the Fundamental Research Funds for the Central Universities, Nankai University (No. 63231154)..

articleTitle: Implementation of High Q and Low Cost 3D Inductor Embeded in Polyimide
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As we enter the post-Moore era, the demand for miniaturization and high performance in chip systems is growing increasingly. This paper is dedicated to enhancing the electrical performance of inductors while reducing their size and improving integration. In this study, polyimide (PI) is selected as the substrate material, and photolithography is utilized to create vias. Compared to traditional silicon or glass substrates, the PI substrate not only provides a higher quality factor but also simplifies the manufacturing process and reduces production costs. However, planar inductors face dual limitations of space and performance in achieving high inductance density, leading to their occupation of a larger area on the chip. In contrast, 3D inductor technology, with its higher inductance density, emerges as the preferred space-saving solution. This research employs HFSS software to construct a 3D inductor model and simulates the performance of glass-based, silicon-based and PI-based inductors in comparison. By adjusting the aspect ratio, the height and the width of the RDL (Re-Distributed Layer), an in-depth simulation and analysis of their effects on inductance (L) and quality factor (Q) are conducted, with the aim of proposing a high-Q inductor structure. The simulation results show that when the diameter of the via is 20µm and the aspect ratio is 1: 5, the inductance density of the 3D inductor is 14.4 nH/mm2, and the peak value of Q is 43.62. It is worth noting that the PI-based inductor slightly outperforms the glass-based inductor in terms of quality factor, and the Q value increases with the increase in RDL height and width. The morphology of the etched surface and adhesive removal after laser debonding exhibits satisfactory results which indicates the rationality and feasibility of the design of the integrated high Q inductor embedded in PI.

articleTitle: Advanced Au-Au Direct Bonding for Enhanced Thermal Management in Heterogeneous Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Hybrid bonding emerges as a solution to meet the growing demand for high I/O density within 3D packaging, exhibiting promising heat dissipation capabilities. Heat transfer interface is the main bottleneck for heat dissipation in integrated circuit (IC) packages, and hybrid bonding is a promising solution. While challenges such as oxidation and surface flatness issues have been overcome in hybrid bonding technology for I/O applications, the significant disparity in scale between the heat transfer and the I/O interfaces exacerbates these challenges, limiting its application for heat dissipation, particularly with the mainstream Cu-SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> hybrid bonding method. This research advocates for using inert metals, notably gold, as a bonding layer to mitigate oxidation during the bonding process. Through this strategy, we have successfully realized bonding between chips of different materials at 300°C, 9 MPa and atmospheric conditions for 1 hour without using the chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) process. Analysis of EDS and SEM results shows a good bonding interface without oxidation. Additionally, the thermal conductivity of the bonding structure can reach about 100 W·m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>·K<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> under optimized conditions. Therefore, this study introduces a high-quality, high-thermal-conductivity Au-Au bonding strategy that eliminates the need for costly CMP process, demonstrating its potential in IC thermal management solutions and heterogeneous integration scenarios. Ultimately, this research aims to optimize the established Cu-SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> hybrid bonding process and broaden its applicability.

articleTitle: Development of Fine Pitch RDL for Large Area Interposer
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Large area interposer provides a bridge between different packaging levels and components, enabling the entire packaging system to achieve higher performance and functional density. This study uses a combination of multiple field exposures to generate fine pitch Redistribution Layer (RDL) for large area interposer. RDL spaces with widths ranging from 1.5 to 10 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathbf{m}$</tex> are evaluated based on their ability to accommodate the critical dimension (CD) that the RDL distributed at the stitching. In parallel, two distinct Damascus process flows have been compared to improve the parameters of Deep Reactive Ion Etching (DRIE) procedures. Compared to semi-additive processes that produce reliability difficulties such as undercut following wet etching, utilizing inorganic thin films as dielectric layers can improve RDL dependability. Meanwhile, the experiments indicated that the dielectric layer with inorganic thin films could offer advantages in high-frequency signal integrity.

articleTitle: Mechanical Properties and Evolution Behaviors of Different Sn63Pb37 Solders Under Reliability Test
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Sn63Pb37 solder alloys had been widely used in the electronic package and material connection in the past two decades. Now, Because Pb toxicity had a harmful impact on the environment and human health, people put forward to reduce the pollution caused by Pb in solder alloys and make efforts to replace SnPb solder. However, SnPb solder could not be replaced in space environment, extreme temperature and other area which had a great demand on reliability. Microelement addition had a great influence on the solders properties. Generally, Microelement can reduce the solder melting point and improve mechanical properties. In this work, we compared two kinds of Sn63Pb37 solders with different microelement. The properties of two kinds of solders were characterized, and the welded joints under temperature cycling and high-temperature storage were compered. Firstly, the composition of two solder balls was analyzed using ICP, and then the mechanical properties of the solder were characterized using nanoindentation, hardness, and other methods. Two types of solder were respectively welded onto PCB boards with copper solder pads. After temperature cycling and high-temperature storage, the growth mechanism of intermetallic compounds at the interface, as well as the changes in defects such as cracks and pores were studied. This provides guidance for the further application of SnPb solder.

articleTitle: Realization of Full Spectrum PIG-LEDs Based on Low Melting Point Sn-P-F-O Glass Matrix
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In the lighting quality upgraded process of existing white LEDs, the selection of an appropriate glass matrix for thermal stability and high color rendering index is crucial for optimizing the light color quality of white LEDs. In this study, a low melting point phosphor-in-glass (PiG) composite material based on the Sn-P-F-O glass system was developed, and the PiG inorganic color converter was prepared by selecting the optimal formulation of the glass matrix and mixing the prepared glass precursors with different ratios of phosphors. In particular, The phosphors were a mixture of BaSb02N2:Eu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>+(BSON),Y3(AI,Ga)s012:Ce<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>+ (YAG) and CaAISiN3:Eu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>+ (CASN) phosphors. Notably, under the excitation of the blue light chip, the emission peaks of PiG cover a wide wavelength range of 420nm--780nm, realizing full spectrum emission. By investigating the effects of different combination ratios of the three phosphors on the encapsulation parameters of the full spectrum white PiG-LEDs, Designed to improve the high color rendering of LEDs significantly. The PiG was characterized using electron microscopy (SEM), fluorescence spectrophotometry, and photometric integrating sphere to analyze the surface morphology, excitation-emission spectra, and optical properties of the samples, which package it with a 460nm InGaN chip. The results of the tests showed that the PiG-LEDs exhibit high color rendering index (Ra=90.S) and low color temperature (CCT=3608K) when driven by 300mA current. The PiG prepared based on a low melting point glass matrix and optimized phosphor mixed ratio effectively improves the Ra of the PiG-LEDs and reduces the CCT of PiG-LEDs, realizing full-spectrum white light with excellent performance, which has very high potential application in the upscale lighting field.

articleTitle: Study of Multi Principal Element Solders with Low Melting Point for 3D Electronic Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Currently, three-dimensional packaging (3D packaging) is used as the most feasible technological way to break Moore's law. In 3D packaging, three different sizes of solder joints must work together to achieve highly integrated vertical interconnects. This architecture needs to be realized by multiple reflow in industrial production. Therefore, it is necessary to choose three solders with different melting points. In order to further extend the reflow temperature range and increase the flexibility of 3D integration, the development of low melting point solders is required. SnBi solder joints often suffer from brittle fracture due to the inherent brittleness of Bi, and SnIn solder joints is limited in its low tensile strength. Therefore, a series of SnBiIn alloys with different ratios were prepared. During the composition design, orthogonal experimental method was used to determine composition ratios. The effects of different composition on the micro-morphology as well as the mechanical properties of SnBiIn alloys were investigated. Samples were prepared using a vacuum induction furnace and the microstructure of the samples was analyzed. The mechanical properties of the alloys with different compositions were measured by tensile test. The results of this study provide a research basis for the design of low melting point solder.

articleTitle: A UCIe Interconnect Channel Design Up to 32Gbps on 2.5D Si-Interposer
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In the past few years, to achieve high bandwidth, low latency, and low power consumption D2D interconnection applied to HPC, data center and AI, many manufacturer has developed its own D2D serial/parallel interface protocol, such as AIB, Ultralink, LIPINCON and so on. However, the incompatibility of D2D protocls from different manufacturers seriously limited the development of D2D. Since UCIe V1.0 was launched in 2022, as a complete open industry standard interconnection, UCIe is expected to unify the D2D interface standard. Based on the UCIe protocol, the channle performance of different Si-interposer processes of TSMC such as 3MZ, 5MZ, and 5Mi is studied in this paper. we used a 3D simulation software to extract the S-parameter of the channel, then analyze the VTF loss and VTF crosstalk of the channle with RX and TX terminal, and use a no-jitter Tx model to simulate the eye diagram and jitter in circuit simulation tools. For the 3MZ process, signal routing is located in M1 and M3, and M2 is the grid ground. To ensure fan-out of all the signals, a fixed-pitch SSS pattern is designed, by optimizing the line width of signal and ground, the VTF loss and VTF crosstalk are about -6dB and -24dB at 16GHz, respectively. The eye diagram of the highest rate 32Gbps required in the protocol is met, and the maximum Jitter_PP is 3.4ps. For the 5Mz process, signal routing is located at layers M1, M3, and M5. M2 and M4 are the reference grid ground. A same SSS pattern is designed, the comparable VTF loss and VTF crosstalk to 3Mz process can be achieved by optimizing the line width of the signal and ground, all bit signals meet the 32Gbps eye-diagram mask required by the protocol and the worst Jitter_PP is 4.8ps. Different from 3Mz and 5Mz process, the 5Mi process has thicker metal layer and dielectric layer, which is benifit for design finer signal line to achieve better crosstalk with no obvious deterioration of loss. Based on the 5Mi si-interposor process, we design a GS pattern, in which signal is located in M3, M4 and M5, power and ground are located in M1 and M2. Simulation result indicated that this pattern has better performance than 3Mz and 5Mz, which also meet the 32Gbps eye-diagram mask and channle SPEC definited by UCIe protocol, and the worst Jitter_PP is only 1.8ps.

articleTitle: An Investigation of Time Dependent Dielectric Breakdown (TDDB) on Carbon Nanotube Field-Effect Transistors (CNTFETs)
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As technology nodes continue to scale down, silicon-based integrated circuits have approached physical limits. In order to sustain Moore's Law, new materials have become a major focus of research in the field of integrated circuits, with carbon-based integrated circuits considered one of the most promising new materials due to their superior electrical characteristics. Currently, reliability is a primary concern constraining the development of carbon-based integrated circuits. Time-dependent dielectric breakdown (TDDB) is a common reliability issue in field-effect transistors, and it is also prevalent in CNTFETs. This paper employs the measure-atress-measure (MSM) method to investigate the TDDB phenomenon in CNTFETs, applying 3 different constant electrical stress on multiple devices and extract the time to breakdown (tbd). Experiment results show tbd follows weibull distribution, same as silicon MOSFETs, but with a much smaller voltage accelerate factor of 16.91 compare to the typical values of silicon. It is speculated this might be due to the inferior oxide/CNT interface quality compared to silicon allows generated trap to form a leakage path under relatively low electric filed stress.

articleTitle: Failure Characteristics and Mechanisms of Sn-Based Solder Interconnections Under Vibrational Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The vibrational reliability is important for the Ball Grid Array (BGA) packaging in modern electronic devices, especially for automotive equipment that needs to be used under-designed or accidental vibrations. It is meaningful to understand the vibrational stability of the solder joints and its failure mechanism. The current research always focuses on finite element simulation of BGA packaging, as well as the statistics of the vibration lifetime. The mechanism of vibration failure, such as fatigue, crack generation, and propagation, still needs to be explored in depth. In this study, BGA samples are prepared via reflowing by using Sn-Cu-Bi-In solders, and then followed by vibration tests. The cracks are always generated in the solder ball, which located near the intermetallic compound (IMC) layer. Then the cracks propagate along the compound layer. After dyeing treatment, the chip and PCB parts of the failed BGA samples are separated to observe the fracture. The fatigue striation is found in the ß-Sn phase at the edge of the solder joint, proving that the fatigue cracks are the initial failure mode. The vibration lifetime is improved by adding Ni into the solders. The IMC layer is transformed from Cu6Sn5 to (Cu, Ni)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn5, and the latter performs better mechanical properties, leading to the development of vibration reliability.

articleTitle: Electric Breakdown Mechanism of Build-up Films under High-Temperature and High-Humidity Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Electronic products have been evolving towards high performance and high integration to meet the demands of high-performance computing, next-generation mobile communication, artificial intelligence, automotive electronics, and defense equipment. In order to achieve the highest wiring density and optimize electrical performance, flip-chip ball grid array (FCBGA) substrates are developed, utilizing multiple high-density wiring layers, laser blind vias, buried vias, and stacked vias, along with ultra-fine pitch metallization. Currently, FCBGA packaging is widely used in high-performance processors, graphics processors, network chips, communication devices, and consumer electronics. With the increase of integration level, the quality and reliability of FCBGA packaging have been highly concerned. FCBGA packaging substrates typically employ build-up films as the interlayer insulation material. The breakdown strength performance of build-up films under high-temperature and high-humidity environments is crucial to their reliable operation. Recent studies have made significant strides in elucidating breakdown strength mechanisms. However, despite these research efforts, breakdown strength research still faces formidable challenges. For instance, the complexity of breakdown mechanisms, especially in high-energy, high-frequency, and complex environments remain controversial. The intricate relation between material properties, environmental factors, and electric field characteristics complicates the understanding of breakdown variation of build-up films. This study simulated real operating conditions by subjecting samples to different conditions, comparing the trend of breakdown strength performance changes of build-up films after biased highly accelerated stress tests (BHAST). It was found that moisture ingress was the most significant factors damaging the insulation performance of build-up films, leading to the decrease in breakdown strength. When the moisture content in the build-up films increased from 0.05% to 0.49%, the breakdown strength decreased from 332 kV/mm to 250 kV/mm.

articleTitle: Thermal Analysis and Optimization of Substrate Structural Parameters in High Power Density System-in-Package
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: This paper conducts thermal analysis and optimization for a specific high-power-density System-in-Package. By employing finite element analysis software ANSYS Icepak, the structure and parameters of the substrate were optimized to reduce the chip junction temperature of the System-in-Package, thereby enhancing the heat dissipation efficiency of the device. Firstly, single-factor analysis was conducted on the substrate structure and parameters affecting the heat dissipation of the packaging, including the number of vias, via plating thickness, copper layer thickness, copper coverage, substrate thickness, and BT material, to evaluate the influence of each factor on chip junction temperature and packaging thermal resistance. Next, the significance of the six parameters on chip junction temperature was analyzed through orthogonal experimental analysis. Finally, response surface analysis was conducted on the significant continuous variables to determine the optimal combination of substrate structure and parameters after optimization. The optimized chip junction temperature was 101.798°C, and the packaging thermal resistance was 27.43°C/W. Compared with before optimization, the chip junction temperature decreased by 15.23%, and the packaging thermal resistance decreased by 19.23%.

articleTitle: Using Harmonized Parabolic Synthesis to Implement Sine and Cosine Functions
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Unary function in integrated circuits (ICs) is the fundamental of mathematical calculations and complex algorithmic processing. However, the primary problem is the trade-off among accuracy, handling capacity, cost, and power consumption. The harmonized parabolic synthesis is a novel algorithm that has merits in many ways compared with the conventional approximation measures. It reduces computational complexity by introducing parallelism and has better hardware implementation efficiency. Despite this, parabolic synthesis approximation still remains immature and requires further optimization of functional constructions, circuit designs and practical verifications. This paper focuses on the implementation of sine and cosine functions by using harmonized parabolic synthesis. The major research contents of this paper consist of elucidation of principle analysis, the development of sub-functions and the algorithm implementation process. The comparison analysis of the efficacy of Polynomial Approximation, CORDIC, etc. and the parabolic synthesis have been discussed, and the advantages of calculation precision and computational efficiency are verified. This paper shows that using the harmonized parabolic synthesis methodology can yield performance improvement in both convergence and precision.

articleTitle: Extensive Studies on Microstructural Evolution and Temperature Pt Resistance Temperature Sensors by a Combined Method of Phase Field and Finite Element Simulations
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Thin-film platinum resistance temperature (TPRT) sensors are gradually becoming an alternative to other sensors in miniaturized and integrated temperature measurement scenarios. However, the lower temperature coefficient of resistance (TCR) has been a major factor limiting their application. Previous research mainly focused on improving the TCR by heat treatment process, but relatively few work was available on the mechanism to optimize the TCR parameter. In this study, the microstructural evolution of Pt thin film during heat treatment is simulated by finite element analysis using COMSOL Multiphysics software, and the results are analyzed in comparison with previous experimental results. The simulation results indicate that grain boundary migration occurs in Pt thin film during the heat treatment process, leading to fast growth of small grains. Furthermore, the grain size is positively related to the heat treatment temperature. As the grain size of Pt thin film increases, the number of grain boundaries per unit volume decreases, resulting in a weakening of the barrier effect of the grain boundaries on the electrons and a decrease in the resistivity of the Pt thin film, which in turn brings about an increase in the TCR.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Junction Temperature Estimation of Double-Sided Cooling Power Modules for Electric Vehicles Based on Watercourse Temperature Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this paper, a method based on watercourse temperature is proposed to estimate the power semiconductor junction temperature, with the consideration of the thermal coupling effect among chips. Unlike conventional approaches, the NTC sampling temperature is not directly utilized to represent the junction temperature. Instead, this method addresses the uncertainty of the thermal impedance model, and calculates the junction temperature using the Kalman filtering method. This method comprehensively considers the actual thermal model of the module, minimizes memory usage, and accurately estimates the junction temperature of the double-sided water-cooled module based on watercourse temperature measurements. Simulation results demonstrate that the method achieves a junction temperature estimation error within 1 °C under steady-state working conditions.

articleTitle: Optimization of Thermocompression Bonding Process for Fine-Pitch Flip-Chip Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the trend towards miniaturization in the electronics packaging industry, solder joint sizes have been steadily decreasing and spacing has become increasingly dense, so narrow pitch flip-chip interconnects have attracted considerable research interest. To meet this challenge, flip-chip thermocompression bonding (TCB) has emerged as the dominant chip bonding technique. In this process, process parameters play a critical role in bond strength and reliability. However, traditional flip-chip underfill techniques, such as capillary underfill, tend to create voids in narrow-pitch interconnect applications, reducing product reliability. To address this issue, the industry has developed prefabricated underfill techniques specifically designed for narrow-pitch flip-chip interconnects, including non-conductive underfill and wafer-level underfill. This research, based on traditional flip-chip thermocompression bonding techniques, systematically investigates the effect of factors such as pressure, peak temperature, peak temperature duration and temperature ramp rate on the strength of the thermocompression bond. By optimizing these process parameters, we have identified a combination of techniques that improve bond strength.

articleTitle: A Detail Study on Heat Dissipation Performance of the Laser-Driven Illumination Based on the Vapor Chamber
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Heat accumulation on the phosphor converter is the biggest bottleneck for the development of laser lighting. To resolve this problem, a structure that combines the phosphor converter (PC) and vapor chamber (VC) was proposed and named PCVC in this work. The heat generated by the laser facula can be dissipated efficiently by the VC. A finite element analysis model (FEA) was simulated to study the heat dissipation performance. The results show that the facula temperature decreases by 24.05% compared to the control group. In addition, the optical performance was investigated by the experiment. The results show that the correlated color temperature (CCT) shift is much lower than the control group, which decreases by 79.86%. However, the results also show that heat dissipation is difficult for the sample whose phosphor converter thickness exceeds 3 mm, despite the use of VC. The carbonization process was also investigated. The results show that the carbonization and quenching problem result in less blue light being converted to yellow light, which leads to higher CCT and lower luminous flux.

articleTitle: Stress Analysis and Optimization of Laminated Solder Joints Under Bending and Torsion Loads
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The research object of this paper is the Stacked solder joints, the three-dimensional model of the solder joints is established using ANSYS software, under the bending and torsion composite loading conditions, the stress analysis of the solder joints model; according to the simulation results, the stress distribution law of the whole array as well as the single stacked solder joints is obtained. Three structural parameters are selected: the height of the solder joint, the diameter of the solder ball and the diameter of the pad, each parameter is taken as three levels, and the corresponding combinations are obtained based on the Box-Behnken experimental design according to the values of the influencing factor levels, and the regression equations of the thermal stresses of the stacked solder joints and the structural parameters are established and combined with the genetic algorithms to optimize the structural parameters of the stacked solder joints, and the optimal the height of the solder joint, diameters of the solder ball and the diameter of the pad are 0.60 mm, 0.35 mm and 0.42 mm, respectively.

articleTitle: Investigation on the Crimping Strain Characteristics and Reliability of Copper-Clad Aluminum Wire Assemblies
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: This investigation delineates the crimping strain characteristics and assesses the reliability of copper-clad aluminum (CCA) wire assemblies, particularly in aerospace applications where high reliability is paramount. The broader utilization of CCA wires is constrained by inherent challenges such as susceptibility to corrosion and complexities in achieving robust sealed crimp connections. Employing a rigorous methodological framework that includes crimp strain simulations and advanced electron microscopy techniques, this study aims to refine the crimping process and augment the material compatibility between connectors and wire insulation. The findings underscore the efficacy of annealing treatments in enhancing mechanical properties through grain refinement, thereby bolstering the reliability of the connections. This research contributes to the body of knowledge on the mechanical and chemical stability of CCA wires, promoting their expanded use in demanding reliability environments.

articleTitle: Comparison of LiTaO3 Laser Drill and Dry Etching in Wafer-Level Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In surface acoustic wave filters (SAW-filter) and body acoustic wave filters (BAW-filter), LiTa<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">O</inf>3 (LT) is often used as a piezoelectric wafer to convert electrical signals and mechanical energy into each other [1]. LT deforms under pressure, resulting in inconformity of the positive and negative charge centers, generate electrical signal. However, it is required to remove the LT underneath the filter Pad to ensure the connection between the chip and the external circuit in the wafer level packaging process of the SAW filter. In recent years, some researchers have studied the removal of LT by laser drill and dry etching [1]–[3], but they only stayed at the experimental stage. In this paper, we verify the possibility of using these two methods in industrial production, and compare their advantages and disadvantages in production. Firstly, we used the method of fluorine system gas plasma reactive ion etching. The proportion of fluorine gas in the etching chamber is CF4: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{C}_{\mathbf{4}}\mathbf{F}_{\mathbf{8}}=\mathbf{4}:\mathbf{1}$</tex>. The etching process takes about 600s. Then, we used the laser drilling method. It can drill more than 1500 holes per seconds, 1 wafer per minutes. The result shows that: 1. In wafer level packaging of SAW-filter, both methods can be used to remove LT. 2. The thickness of LT has a great influence on the choice of laser drill and dry etching, because the etching rate of LT is relatively slow. 3. The removal of thick LT layer is still a great challenge in wafer level packaging of SAW-filter. 4. The most troublesome issue of laser drilling LT is thermal and mechanical damage. 5. After both method of the SAW-filter chip packaging is completed, their reliability is good.

articleTitle: Silicon Vapor Chamber with Hierarchical Micro-/Nano Wicks
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: A two-step processing method is developed for the fabrication of micro- and nano hierarchical wick structures on silicon substrate. Deep reaction ion etching (DRIE) was used to fabricate the primary wick, while the secondary wick structure was formed by electrochemical (EC) etching on the surface of the primary wick. The processing results show that the fabricated hierarchical wick structures consist of dense arrays of microscale trench and a uniformly distributed nanoporous layer with pore diameters less than 50nm. The merit of these hierarchical structures was demonstrated by thermal tests on the silicon vapor chamber integrated with such wicks. A prototype of the vapor chamber with 30 mm × 25 mm × 1.5 mm in dimension was developed as a passive heat spreader for thermal management of electronics. Thermal performance results indicate that the integration of hierarchical wick structures can significantly reduce the thermal resistance by ~50% compared with samples integrated with only microwick structures. Such an optimization on the thermal resistance indicates that integration of such hierarchical wick could be a promising method for the optimization of silicon-based thermal management devices.

articleTitle: Research on Optimization Method of Copper Clip Bonding Package Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As a key component of power electronic devices, the reliability of insulated gate bipolar transistor (IGBT) modules has attracted widespread attention. Different structural parameters of Cu clips will have different effects on the parasitic inductance, on-resistance, and junction-shell thermal resistance of IGBT modules. Therefore, firstly, the finite element models of Cu clip structures with different structural parameters are established, and the parasitic inductance, on-resistance, and junction-shell thermal resistance of each simulation model are calculated through finite element simulation analysis. Secondly, the factorial method was used to study the effects of Cu clip size on parasitic inductance, on-resistance and junction-shell thermal resistance. Finally, the response surface method is used to optimize the structure design, and the prediction model of parasitic inductance, on-resistance and junction-shell thermal resistance is established, and the optimal combination design of parasitic inductance, on-resistance and junction-shell thermal resistance is obtained at the same time. The analysis results show that the thickness and width of the Cu clip have a greater influence on the parasitic inductance than the thickness. As the contact area between the Cu clip and the chip increases, the on-resistance and junction-shell thermal resistance decrease.

articleTitle: Fracture Modeling and Characterization of Si/Underfill/Substrate Interface Adhesion in 3D Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
