abstract: In recent years, underfill technology has been playing an increasingly important role in advanced packaging, and the associated reliability issues of bonding structures have become more significant. Particularly, the well-formed bonding interface formed by the underfill adhesive in the packaging structure determines the ability to resist cracking and delamination, which is crucial for ensuring the reliability of electronic packaging devices. Currently, most research has focused on various bonding interfaces of underfill in FC packaging. However, with the rapid development and application of advanced packaging technologies such as 2.5D and 3D, the failure issues exposed by underfill in their structures have become more prominent. In this study, a commercial underfill material was used to prepare a simplified Si/underfill/substrate bonding structure, designed to mimic the widely adopted structure of silicon interposer/underfill adhesive/substrate in actual 3D packaging. A combined experimental and finite element modeling method was proposed to determine the bonding strength of the Si/underfill/substrate structure. This method conducts interface analysis based on the theory of fracture mechanics, conducts single cantilever beam test and lap shear test on the two main failure modes of model I and model II, and then uses the test results as simulation parameters. Through iterative simulation, a cohesive zone model (CZM) characterizing crack initiation and propagation was established. In summary, the method of establishing the CZM model can not only evaluate the delamination risk of the Si/underfill/substrate interface in 3D packaging but also provide a convenient and cost-effective approach for analyzing other similar interface delamination issues.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Performance Test of Nano Cu@Ag Core-Shell Particles for Power Device Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this paper, a green and pollution-free method was developed to plate a silver layer on the surface of copper cores with diameter of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$17.4\pm 0.56$</tex> nm through replacement reduction reaction. Finally, Cu@Ag core shell nanoparticles charactered by low proportion, dense and uniform Ag shell, as well as good antioxidant property were obtained by adjusting the ratios of copper and silver elements in the reactants. Results showed that the addition of dispersant PVP and excess reducer glucose during the synthesis of Cu@Ag nanoparticles can improve not only the quality of the plating layer, but also the antioxidant properties of the Cu@Ag core shells attributed to the residual of these organic substances with reducing properties, which allowed them to be placed in the air for 40 days without oxidizing at a high temperature of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$20 0^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>, and even maintain good thermal stability at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$235. 4^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> in the case of a Cu to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{AgNO}_{3}$</tex> ratio of 4: 1 in the reactional solution. This is quite significant for the reliability improvement of power department device packaging.

articleTitle: Effect of Packaging on the Marine Fiber Optic Acoustic Sensitive Components
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Packaging is an extremely important part of marine fiber optic acoustic sensitive components, both for effective isolation from seawater and for highly sensitive acoustic detection. It is essential to study the effect of packaging on marine fiber optic acoustic sensitive components, particularly those designed for long-term deployment in the high hydrostatic pressures of seawater. In order to analyze the possible effects of packaging, a hydrostatic pressure simulator is employed to simulate the actual subsea operating environment of fiber optic acoustic sensitive components. Unfortunately, it is difficult to effectively analysis the relevant changes in the traditional method such as testing the overall optical insertion loss of fiber optic acoustic sensitive components. In this paper, we propose an innovative method to accurately monitor the fiber optic change inside the fiber optic acoustic sensitive component by adopting the advanced distributed fiber optic strain testing technique, thus to provide a technical means for analysis. In detail, we built an experimental setup as described above and conducted practical test experiments using unpackaged and packaged samples, respectively. Firstly, we tested the strain performance of unpackaged sample under different hydrostatic pressures, and the experimental results found that the test curves showed good symmetry, and under hydrostatic pressure, the optical fiber appeared to have a periodic change, and the strain amplitude of the optical fiber gradually increased with the increase of the pressure. The strain region was relatively flat, and the transition region was smooth. Further, we tested the strain performance of the packaged samples under different hydrostatic pressures, and the experimental results revealed that although the optical fiber appeared to change periodically under hydrostatic pressure, and the strain amplitude of the optical fiber gradually increased with the increase of the pressure, the test curves appeared to have an obvious stress concentration region. Finally, we conducted a comparative analysis of the two sets of experiments. The analysis of the experimental results shows that packaging has an important impact on fiber optic acoustic sensitive elements, especially the region that may trigger internal stress-strain concentration, which in extreme cases may induce optical loss exceedance or even fiber breakage. This research has certain guiding significance for the failure analysis and reliability.

articleTitle: Investigation on Wafer Heterogeneous Bonding Process and Performance of CMOS Integrated Circuit on Silicon Carbide Substrate
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: CMOS integrated circuits (ICs) were heterogeneous bonded to semi-insulating 4H-SiC wafer by using SOI or Si wafers that have completed 0.18 μm CMOS processing technology. Prebonding and debonding processes were used to remove the Si handle layer and SiO2 layer for SOI IC wafer, to thin the Si substrate for Si IC wafer. Through back grinding, the thickness of the initial SOI and Si CMOS wafer were 7 μm and 20 μm, respectively. Benzocyclobutene (BCB) was uesd as the bonding interface layer for SOI IC wafer due to the extremely thin CMOS thickness of 7 μm, and directly bonding was realized for Si IC with interface layer about 10 nm. The square resistance and off-state leakage current increase with the ambient temperature improving from 25 °C to 175 °C, which is more obvious for SOS devices than SOI devices because of the high thermal resistance of BCB interface layer. For comparison, the electrical properties of directly bonded SOS Operational Amplifier (OPA) are basically consistent with those of Si OPA. The Vos, f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3dB</inf> and SR of SOS OPA are -16 μV, 90 kHz, and 0.346 V/μs, respectively. This study provides a practical method to realize SOS CMOS IC, boosting the further exploration, thermal advantage and high-performance development of Si on SiC IC chips.

articleTitle: A design of the multi-channel microwave frequency conversion micro-module based on full wave electromagnetic simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: This paper presents the simulation and design of a multi-channel microwave frequency conversion micro-module integrated on a multi-layer ceramic substrate using a full-wave electromagnetic algorithm. The micro-module operates in a frequency range up to 40 GHz and comprises five frequency conversion channels, each isolated within individual metallic shielded cavities. Finite element method is utilized to analyze the insertion loss and return loss of the single channel, isolation between dual channels, as well as the resonant characteristics of the isolation cavity. Additionally, the RF transmission performance of the single channel is tested using a probe station, and the test curves matched well with the simulation results within 40 GHz.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation Study of a Novel Diamond Based Composite Heat Dissipation Baseplate
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Currently, power module packaging is developing towards higher power density, which requires increasingly higher heat dissipation capacity in packaging. This article designs a novel diamond based heat dissipation baseplate, introduces a new packaging material based on IGBT power module packaging floor structure, thus optimizes and innovates the structure and heat dissipation path. The thermal and mechanical properties of diamond and diamond/copper composite materials as baseplate materials are analyzed through junction temperature thermal simulation and thermal stress warping simulation. The results indicate that novel diamond based composite heat dissipation baseplate has significantly improved thermal conductivity and thermal stress warping compared to the traditional DBC/solder/copper baseplate packaging structure. At the same packaging conditions, the junction temperature drops by 16.64 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${}^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$</tex>, the warping deformation caused by solder reflux process reduced from 1.1365 mm at length and 0.715007 mm at width to 0.39598 mm and 0.2431203 mm, respectively.

Author Keywords: Diamond Based Composite Heat Dissipation Baseplate

articleTitle: Optimization of Bonding Methods for Controlling Sn Spillage in Fine Pitch Microbump Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Microbumps play a pivotal role in interlayer interconnections for advanced packaging. As chip integration density gradually increases, the pitch of microbumps continues to decrease. However, with continuous shrinkage in bump size, tin (Sn) solder spillage during high-temperature bonding has become a severe issue. Owing to the low yield strength of Sn, even a small applied pressure at elevated temperatures can induce excessive deformation. The excessive deformation of the Sn layer will not only deviate from the designed bump structure but also lead to a series of reliability concerns, such as sidewall depletion and joint bridging. Thinning the Sn layer thickness and employing reflow techniques are effective solutions to mitigate Sn spillage, but they are associated with excessive Kirkendall void formation and additional cleaning processes, respectively. In this work, an optimized bonding method for Sn-rich, fine-pitch microbump structures without a flux cleaning process is proposed. This technique combines an initial low-temperature solid-state diffusion (SSD) pre-bonding step and a subsequent rapid reflow process to complete the microbump interconnection. The influence of bonding temperature, bonding pressure, and formic acid environment on bonding quality is analyzed based on shear strength, cross-sectional images and electric tests. Ultimately, the optimized bonding parameters are determined to be pre-bonding at 200°C, 0.8 MPa for 1min, and reflow at 260°C for 1min. Reliable Cu-Sn bonding is achieved while retaining the original Sn profile as much as possible. The optimized bonding method is further validated on samples with different pitches and Sn layer thicknesses. This optimized bonding approach can facilitate accurate control of the bump profile and enable three-dimensional package integration.

articleTitle: Simulation Research on Wafer-Level Electrochemical Deposition Uniformity
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the slowing down of Moore's Law, the continued improvement of integration density has become increasingly challenging for traditional integrated circuits. 3D packaging technology offers a solution by overcoming the limitations of semiconductor processes. In this technology, interconnections between chips and substrates are achieved through Through-Silicon Vias (TSVs) and microbumps, which are fabricated using electroplating. However, this process faces issues related to the thickness of the electroplated layer. Larger wafer sizes can cause uneven current density distribution, leading to inconsistent thickness in the electroplated layer. This study focuses on the deposition process for large wafers, employing finite element analysis methods to investigate the issue. The results showed that after one hour, the thickness of the plating layer at the edge was <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10\ \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>, while the thickness at the center was <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$9.4\ \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>. These findings offer insights into improving process control for wafer-level electroplating.

articleTitle: Development of High Modulus Temporary Bonding Material for 2.5D/3D IC Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In an attempt to resolve the cracking and chipping issues of edge trimming wafer during back grinding, a newly developed high modulus temporary bonding material (TBM) with high glass transition temperature (Tg) was developed in this paper. Its specific rheological properties, such as high modulus at room temperature as well as low viscosity at bonding temperature, which enables the bonding pair to survive the whole temporary bonding and debonding (TBDB) process. The 12-inch wafer pair was bonded at 220°C and 30 kN pressure for 5 min, and the warpage (0.35 mm) is small enough to be negligible. After bonding, back grinding and a subsequent CMP process were successfully achieved. The device wafer with the adhesive layer edge together was reduced to 70 µm, and there were no chipping or breakage observed at the edges due to its high mechanical strength. Besides, a series of backside processes, such as PVD, reflow soldering simulation and wet process were conducted on the wafer pair, and there were no voids or bubbles found due to its superior thermal and chemical resistance. And the ultra-thin wafer pair was successfully separated with UV laser ablation. Finally, the adhesive was completely cleaned off with a commercial cleaning solvent by optical microscope observation.

articleTitle: The Failure Analysis of 3D-Stacked Die Packaging Flash
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The IC package has gradually evolved from traditional 2D plane package to advanced 3D-stacked package. In 3D-stacked die package, multi-layer dies are usually stacked together, and there are dense interconnection structures. The structures are complex, which brings more difficulties and challenges to the reliability and failure analysis of devices. In this paper, a failure analysis was carried out on a 3D-stacked die packaging flash. The I-V test, (3D) X-ray, OBIRCH failure location, and FIB had been used. The characteristics of the interconnection structure of the 3D-stacked die package and generalized failure analysis methods were summarized.

articleTitle: A Promising Silicon-Based Fan-Out Heterogeneous Integration Technology for V-Band InP Transceiver Chiplet Package
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: This paper introduces a V-band InP transceiver chip-let based on silicon-based Fan-out heterogeneous integration process, which adopts independent silicon-based embedded heterogeneous integration process. The chip-let, as shown in Fig 1, which integrated with six frequency multiplier, mixer, filter, amplifier and pseudo-code modulator, etc. and adopts BGA interface, has the characteristics of high integration, low loss and low power consumption. The chip works at 58 GHz ~ 62 GHz, with a receiving conversion gain of 20dB and receiving input <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{P}_{-1}$</tex> of −22 dBm. The transmission output saturation power is 14dBm, the carrier rejection is 30dBc, and the size is 5mm×4mm×0.3mm (excluding BGA).

articleTitle: Improving the Application of Whale Optimization Algorithm in PID Parameter Optimization for Linear Motor Control System of Wire Bonding Machine XY Motion Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: This study addresses the challenge of optimizing PID controller parameters in the linear motor drive system of wire bonding machines' XY motion platforms. An innovative approach is proposed, leveraging an Enhanced Whale Optimization Algorithm (IWOA) to enhance optimization efficiency, precision, and stability. By integrating adaptive weight strategies and random differential mutation tactics, the IWOA dynamically balances global search and local refinement, significantly improving optimization outcomes. The investigation begins with establishing a comprehensive mathematical model of the linear motor, followed by extensive simulations conducted using MATLAB. Results demonstrate that the optimized IWOA outperforms classical Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Genetic Algorithms (GA), and standard WOA in PID parameter tuning, showcasing superior convergence properties. To further enhance system performance, a feedback-feedforward hybrid control system is introduced to minimize tracking errors in system response. Empirical validation confirms the effectiveness of this approach in improving trajectory tracking accuracy and positional precision of the platform. Practical implementation within an industrial context, particularly in the control system of a welding machine, underscores the remarkable advantages of IWOA in PID parameter tuning. This research not only enhances optimization outcomes but also significantly elevates the overall operational performance of wire bonding machines' XY motion platforms.

articleTitle: Design Rule of Thick-Resist Lithography for Sidewall Perpendicularity and Critical Dimension Fidelity
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Redistribution Layers (RDLs) are pivotal for fanout packaging, enabling the high-density and multi-function integration. The fabrication of RDL heavily relies on the lithography process of photosensitive dielectrics (polyimide) with the thickness of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1-30\ \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>. However, it poses much challenge, particularly regarding line profiles and multilayer. There is an urgent need to investigate the effect of thick-photoresist lithography process on the resist sidewall profile and set the design rule of the process, which contributes to accelerate the process exploration of multilayer RDL. In this study, the optimization of thick-resist lithography process to get better sidewall perpendicularity and critical dimension fidelity has been explored through experiments and simulation for the negative photosensitive polyimide on the silicon substrate. Design rule for PI photolithography is then concluded. The process integration of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$315\ \text{mJ}/\text{cm}^{2}$</tex> exposure dose and 30 s development time can guarantee sidewall closed to 90°. The deviation of top and bottom linewidth from design are both within 3% at the thickness of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8\ \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>, for the widths from 8 to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$25 \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>. The trend of experimental and simulation results is the same, and deviation between experiments and simulation of critical dimensions are less than 10%. It proves that process simulation can be employed to establish additional design rules in future studies.

articleTitle: Study on Evolution Mechanism and Inspection Quantitative Criterion of Typical Defects of Flip Chip Solder Joint
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Flip-chip packaging is widely adopted in electronic systems, known for its high 1/0 density, transmission efficiency, compact size, and cost-effective manufacturing. Nevertheless, as miniaturization and intelligence development advance, micro-solder joints, which are essential for mechanical support and electrical connectivity in flip-chip chips, are confronted with growing reliability challenges. In our study, we employed the finite element numerical simulation method alongside stress load testing to probe the evolution mechanisms of microscopic defects such as inter metallic compounds (IMCs), cavities, and cracks within flip-chip solder joints. By synthesizing data from simulation analyses with the Darveaux accelerated life assessment model and experimental results, we established defect criteria for flip-chip solder joints: The thickness of IMCs must not surpass 5.0 µm; any cavity within the solder ball should have a diameter less than 35% of the local diameter, while at the substrate-sphere interface, cavity diameters should remain below 15% of the local diameter; crack length on the substrate side should be kept under 20%, and on the chip side, it should not exceed 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> of the welding interface length. These criteria serve to mitigate defect occurrence during design and manufacturing phases, offering precise benchmarks for product testing and verification, thereby significantly enhancing the quality and reliability of flip-chip packaged products.

articleTitle: Heat Dissipation Optimization Study of LTCC-Based RF SiP Components
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In order to improve the low temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) as the substrate of RF components in the work of high temperature problem, this paper aims to modify the internal structure and materials of T/R components, with the goal of improving the high-temperature working environment of T/R component chips. By doing so, it hopes to modify the heat transfer path of chips and the thermal conductivity of LTCC substrates, which will improve the heat dissipation performance of LTCC RF System-in-Package (SiP) components. Simulation is carried out using ICEPAK finite element software to simulate the model with increasing heat transfer path and increasing thermal conductivity of the structure. It is found that increasing the heat transfer path can effectively reduce the temperature of the TR component chip during operation, and the heat dissipation effect is improved less after further improving the thermal conductivity of the structure.

articleTitle: Fabrication of High Aspect Ratio TSV Interposer with Cu-Cu Direct Bonding
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: A high aspect ratio TSV (Through-Silicon Via) interposer process is introduced, which can achieve high interconnect density and better electrical performance. Scaling down the TSV diameter is attractive with the increasing requirement of higher integration density. However the thickness of the interposer should not be too thin in order to ensure the mechanical strength, so the demand for higher aspect ratio TSV is becoming more and more urgent. Normally, when the aspect ratio of TSV is less than 12:1, the insulator/barrier/seed layer are prepared by CVD and PVD, but when the aspect ratio is over 12:1, the traditional CVD and PVD processes reach their limits. ALD linear oxide and ALD barrier/seed layer were introduce to solve this problem, and this is the only feasible technical solution for high aspect ratio TSV at present. In this paper, a 2.5D silicon interposer with a ultra high aspect ratio TSV has been fabricated, by stacking two <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{6}\times \mathbf{50}\boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex> TSV wafers with Cu-Cu direct bonding. The CSAM (C-Scan Acoustic Microscopy) scan shows void free bonding result, and the SEM cross-section also support this conclusion, showing that the two TSV wafers are bonded together without obvious bonding interface, alignment accuracy between the two TSV wafers is about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0.4}\boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex>, and the TSV is about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{6}\times \mathbf{99}\mathbf{m}$</tex>, aspect ratio of TSV can reach about 16:1. The DC resistance of the daisy chain circuit are measured, the result is in general agreement with theory, and the TSV daisy chain yield is higher than 80%.

articleTitle: Study on Impedance Discontinuity and Optimization of High-Speed Signals in FCBGA Package
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: During the transmission process of high-speed signals in the FCBGA package substrate, any impedance discontinuity will cause reflection and distortion of the voltage signal, causing signal quality problems. Therefore, it is very critical to match the impedance on the transmission line and reduce impedance discontinuity to ensure the quality of signal transmission. High-speed signals are very sensitive to impedance discontinuity, so impedance matching in high-speed signals is particularly important for signal quality. This article analyzes the main reasons for impedance discontinuity when high-speed signals are conducted on transmission lines. Based on the simulation results, an optimal design method is proposed to improve the problem of impedance discontinuity of high-speed signals in engineering. Firstly, based on the transmission line theory, the causes and consequences of signal impedance discontinuity are analyzed. Secondly, the simulation software HFSS is used to analyze the influence of parameter changes of each optimization quantity on the differential signal impedance from three aspects: vias, transmission lines, and reference planes. Finally, if the process capability allows, based on the simulation results, the system optimization scheme for high-speed signal transmission is determined with the optimal differential signal impedance as the goal. The simulation results show that: when the stacking parameters and line width parameters remain unchanged, the continuity of the reference plane must be ensured. The larger the differential line spacing, the closer the differential impedance is to 2 times the single-ended impedance. When the spacing is larger than 3 times the line width, the differential impedance tends to stabilize. The via is an important impedance discontinuity point. The main optimization method is to increase the anti-pad size. The via impedance can also be optimized by reducing the via hole size, reducing the via pad size and decreasing the via length. After adopting the proposed optimization method, the differential impedance range of high-speed differential signals is 96.4Ω~103Ω when the signal frequency is 16GHz, which can meet the 5% impedance control requirement when the differential impedance is 100Ω. Compared with the initial simulation model, the minimum impedance is optimized by 14.7%. And the corresponding insertion loss and return loss are -1.11dB and -22.24dB respectively, which can meet the S-parameter requirements of insertion loss > -1dB and return loss < -20dB. The optimization effect is relatively significant, confirming the proposed feasibility of the optimization method.

articleTitle: Fatigue Reliability Analysis of Copper Pillar Bumps Based on Micro-Led
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the rapid development of automotive electronics and near-eye display, more stringent requirements are put forward for the heterogeneous integration technology of Micro-LED. The copper pillar bumps with better electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity and mechanical properties can meet the packaging requirements of higher density and smaller pitch for application of Micro-LED array. The reliability of bump and interconnect structure has a great influence on the performance and life of Micro-LED. Therefore, it is necessary to explore the influences of bump parameters on the fatigue life of Micro-LED structures to avoid the failure in copper pillar bump package. In this paper, the life prediction and parameter analysis of Micro-LED structures with copper pillar bumps are carried out. The influence of the structure parameters such as the height and diameter of copper pillar on the fatigue reliability of bumps was analyzed.

articleTitle: Mechanism Study of the Cu Foam Reinforced Sandwich Structure of Cu Sintered Joints
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this paper, the Cu foam layer is incorporated into the sintered structure, and the traditional sandwich structure is transformed into a composite sintered structure consisting of dummy chip/Cu paste/Cu foam/Cu paste/substrate. The traditional sintered joints and composite sintered joints are compared through microstructure observation and shear strength tests. The results show that incorporating Cu foam results in more connection interfaces and increased connection area for the sintered layer. The shear strength of the sintered joints without Cu foam was approximately 42.4 MPa at 250°C, 20 MPa, 5 min in air, while the average strength of the composite structure joints increased to 67.7 MPa under the same conditions. Compared with the traditional sintering structure, the shear fracture location of the composite sintering structure changes from the interface of sintered Cu particles/Cu substrate to the middle of the sintered layer. These findings provide a new method for achieving reliable Cu-sintered joints with high mechanical properties.

articleTitle: Design of Data Processing Microsystem Packages Based on High Temperature Co-Fired Ceramics
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the development of miniaturization, integration, and multifunctional electronic devices, micro system packages based on high-temperature co-fired ceramics (HTCC) have attracted more attention due to their excellent machinability, high integration, and high reliability. Taking a universal data processing microsystem ceramic package as the research object, this paper elaborates in detail on the layout, simulation, and verification of the microsystem package, which has guiding significance for the design, simulation, and verification of data processing micro system packages based on high-temperature co-fired ceramics.

articleTitle: Heat Dissipation Optimization Study of Active Phased Array Antenna Microchannel
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: This work optimizes the liquid-cooled microchannels on the cold plate using a variable-density topology optimization [1] approach to increase the heat dissipation of transmit-receive modules within active phased array antennas and their dependability. Proposing a system-level channel heat dissipation, board-level and component-level sets make up the structure of the system-level channel cooling, with channel branches distributing flow from the board-level channels to the component-level microchannels. With fluid energy dissipation [2] and average temperature as goals, a two-dimensional variable-density topology optimization approach was used to optimize the microchannel architectures in COMSOL Multiphysics software. Thermal-fluid coupling simulations were performed using ICEPAK finite element software to compare the heat dissipation performance between system-level channel cooling and cold plate cooling, as well as the heat transfer efficiency between the optimized topology channels and conventional parallel cold plates. The finite element simulation results show that the U-shaped topology significantly improves the heat dissipation efficiency at the cold plate position when compared to the parallel channel construction at that location. Z-shaped topology at the transmit/receive module cover plate location offers better heat dissipation performance than parallel channels at the module cover plate position in system-level channel construction. Furthermore, the heat dissipation efficiency of the system-level channels is much higher than that of cold plate cooling.

articleTitle: Influence Factors of Joule Heating in Microbump in Advanced Packaging Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Due to the requirement for high power and multiple functions of consumer electronic products, Joule heating in microbumps in advanced packaging technology becomes increasingly serious, which greatly affects the reliability of the device. In this paper, we quantitively investigated the influence factors of Joule heating in microbumps by both experiments and simulation. Except for current density, increasing the environmental temperature can greatly increase the accumulation of Joule heating in test samples. Besides, increasing the number of microbumps under current stress will also lead to higher Joule heating. In addition, due to the higher resistivity of the intermetallic compound (IMC) compared with solder, the power of Joule heating in a pair of full-IMC microbumps is 12.5% higher than that in the as-fabricated sample. Serious Joule heating will cause the void induced by side wall wetting in the microbump, which, however, was proved to have limited influence on the Joule heating in return. We also found thermomigration (TM) in the unpowered microbump under severe Joule heating because of the different heat dissipation abilities of its upper and lower ends. The paper demonstrated the contributing factors of Joule heating in the microbump and analyzed the reliability consequences that severe Joule heating results in.

articleTitle: A One-Hot Encoding Approach for Signal Integrity Enhancement of Intra-chip Interconnects
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As the density of package interconnect wires continues to increase and the operating frequency continues to increase, the performance of integrated circuit packages continues to improve. It also brings signal integrity problems, such as reflections, impedance mismatch, clock delay, and eye diagram distortion. Rongrong Ben et al. proposed four methods to optimize crosstalk <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</sup>. Hanzhi Ma et al. summarized the recent advances in the application of PEEC method in signal integrity analysis of neuromorphic chips based on memristors<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[2]</sup>. Manish et al. proposed a three-dimensional coplanar electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) structure to improve the signal integrity (SI) <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[3]</sup>. One-hot coding is an approach often used for feature coding and is widely used in the field of machine learning and data mining <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[4]</sup>. In this paper, authors apply one-hot coding to the circuit. Compare the signal integrity of one-hot coding circuit and uncoded circuit. The results show that one-hot coding circuits can enhance signal integrity.

articleTitle: Integrating Nanoscale Dynamics for Enhanced Evaporation: A Theoretical Framework Addressing Nonlocal Transport in Nanopores
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Evaporation from nanopores is of great interest in nature and many industrial applications. Therefore, understanding the transport processes within a pore requires integrating the dynamics of vapor and liquid flow, and interfacial interactions are essential. The vapor movement is classified as free molecular flow due to the modest size of the pore (about 100 nm) compared to the mean free path (roughly <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.1\ \mu m$</tex>). Our research will begin by determining the possibility of liquid molecules evaporating from the surface and entering the pore and the probability of vapor molecules condensing back onto the surface once they reach the pore's end. We then investigate the effects of various operating factors to identify settings that optimize nanopore evaporation.

articleTitle: Investigation of improving the uniformity of Cu dishing depth in Cu-SiO2 chemical mechanical polishing
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As chip manufacturing trends towards miniaturization and integration, the focus of the semiconductor industry has shifted from traditional 2D packaging to more complex 3D packaging, with hybrid bonding technology emerging as a critical method for heterogeneous integration. Currently, Cu-Cu/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> bonding is the mainstream hybrid bonding technique. To achieve effective bonding, wafers require surface planarization of Cu-SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> through chemical mechanical polishing (CMP). The CMP process for Cu-SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> surfaces typically consists of two steps: copper CMP and barrier layer CMP. However, due to the uneven thickness of electroplated copper, over-polishing is inevitable during the copper CMP in order to effectively remove the copper layer. This will lead to excessive dishing or recession of Cu pads with orginal thinner Cu layer electroplated and then finally affect the bonding quality. To address this challenge, in this paper, a three-step CMP method is developed, which introduces an additional SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> CMP step after the barrier layer CMP to achieve the appropriate dishing depth of the pads. In this study, the influence of pad size on the Cu pad dishing depth was investigated. The results indicated that as the polishing time increased, the Cu pad dishing became deeper and larger pad sizes resulted in a faster growth rate of the dishing depth. The polishing slurry plays an important role in the CMP process. It is necessary to find a polishing slurry with appropriate material remove rate during additional SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> CMP to reduce the Cu dishing. Through experiments, a SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> polishing slurry was selected with Cu: SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> remove rate of 1:3. Then the process parameters for the SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> CMP were optimized to achieve an ideal dishing depth for the pads. Finally, the dishing depth of pads with a side length of 15um was optimized from 100~200nm to 20~40nm. The experimental results indicate that this method can correct the Cu dishing caused by over-polishing even for large pads, eliminate the negative impact of dishing on subsequent bonding processes, and decrease the requirement for flatness of electroplated Cu on wafer.

articleTitle: Mechanical properties and electromigration reliability of Fe304 nanoparticle-modified Sn58Bi solder joints
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In recent years, Artificial Intelligence (AI) and fifth-generation mobile communications technology (5G) have driven the rapid development of 2.5D/3D advanced-package integrated circuits for applications in mobile electronics, high-performance computers, self-driving devices, the Internet of things and big data. Sn58Bi eutectic solder has become a promising low-temperature solder for 2.5D/3D packaged multi-level interconnect structures because it has the characteristics of low melting point, low cost and excellent mechanical properties. In this study, Fe3O4 nanoparticles with a size of about 10 nm and good particle dispersion were prepared by chemical synthesis, and Fe3O4 nanoparticles with different content gradients were added to regulate the organization and mechanical properties of Sn58Bi solder. The results showed that Sn58Bi solder with 1% Fe3O4 nanoparticles showed the best overall performance. The tensile strength, shear strength and plasticity were improved. At the same time, the nanoparticle modification significantly enhanced the wetting performance of the solder. Moreover, in order to investigate the atomic migration and microstructural evolution of the modified interconnects under current, the EM testing at 1×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>were carried out and the cross sections were observed. The results show that the addition of Fe3O4 nanoparticles significantly inhibited the growth rate of Bi rich phase, resulting in an improvement of the anti-electromigration performance of the interconnects. The study of its microstructure reveals that the addition of Fe3O4 nanoparticles destroyed the eutectic precipitation of the Sn-Bi two phases and promoted the generation of many micron-sized small particles of Bi within Sn phase, so these properties of the solders were affected.

articleTitle: The bonding mechanisms and reliability of pressure-assisted Cu sintering on Cu/Ag metal surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Copper sintering paste has gradually emerged as an exemplary interconnection material in wide bandgap semiconductor processes due to its cost-effectiveness, excellent thermal-electric properties, and robust resistance to electron migration. Currently, active exploration of industrial applications of copper paste is underway. However, there remains a significant lack of research on the connection mechanisms and reliability of copper sintered joints on different metal-coated substrates. To promote the application of copper sintering technology across various fields, it is imperative to investigate the bonding mechanisms and reliability of copper sintered joints on substrates with various metal coatings. Previously, our team investigated a copper paste capable of controlled in-situ copper carrier generation. Building upon this foundation, this paper discusses the bonding performance and reliability of sintered joints prepared via pressure-assisted sintering using this copper paste.

articleTitle: A Novel Intelligent Power Module in Embedded Packaging with Low Parasitic Inductance and Low Thermal Resistance
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: By combining embedding and 3D stacking techniques, a novel intelligent power module is introduced in this paper. The power stages are embedded and stacked in the organic substrates and the drivers are surface mounted on the board. The connection of gate drivers and power devices is conducted via copper wiring, leading to a shorter path and a smaller parasitic inductance. Specifically, the parasitic inductance of GS loop is decreased from 45 nH to 20 nH, reaching an almost 56% reduction. The SiC MOSFETs are stacked vertically to achieve half-bridge circuit and the inductance of DS loop is reduced from 5.4nH to 2.3 nH. Moreover, the power density is improved from 11.4 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> to 18.2 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. It is worth to mention that the heat sinks are directly bonded to the module by insulation material with high thermal conductivity, thus optimizing the heat dissipation path and improving the Rjf performance significantly.

articleTitle: Superhydrophobic-Hydrophilic Interface Control of Laser-Processed Fluorine-Doped Graphene Films for Microfluidics
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Microfluidic technology is crucial in biomedical and chemical analysis as it manipulates fluids at a microscopic scale using microchannels. In this work, a two-step, maskless laser processing technique was proposed to fabricate fluorine-doped graphene films. The graphene films processed by the first UV laser have the property of superhydrophobicity owing to the doping of fluorine atoms on the graphene surface. However, the superhydrophobic state can be converted into a hydrophilic state once a second <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{CO}_2$</tex> laser scan is on the graphene film due to the introduction of microcrack and the removal of most fluorine atoms. Thus, superhydrophobic-hydrophilic interface control of graphene films can be achieved efficiently and controllably. By adjusting laser parameters, fluorine-doped graphene films with different conductivities, surface morphologies, and wettability were prepared without the need of post-processing chemical modifications. Utilizing two types of laser scanning allows for precise control over the superhydrophobic and hydrophilic interfaces on graphene films, offering new strategies and methods for applications in microfluidics, fluid drainage and transport.

articleTitle: Non-Pressure Cu Sinter Paste for High Density Power Device Interconnection
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the rapid development of power electronic devices, miniaturization, high-power density, and high thermal reliability have become the standard for next-generation semiconductor devices. As silicon-based materials are difficult to meet the application requirements for high power density and high-temperature operation, wide-band-gap (WBG) semiconductor, such as silicon carbide (SiC) and gallium nitride (GaN), have taken the main role. Though high-power density and high switching frequency characteristics ensured those materials can lead to high performance power devices, the excessive junction temperatures (Tj) could lead to the deterioration risk for relative packaging material. Especially the die-attach materials, which integrate power chips to substrate, are easily influenced by thermal fatigue and frequency thermal cycling environment. Some new technologies, such as. high-temperature brazing materials, transient liquid phase bonding technology, and sintered silver (Ag) technology, have been investigated. All those materials have their own drawbacks such as serious processing condition, high risk of fragile, and price costing. In comparison, metal copper (Cu) sinter paste is considered an ideal wide-bandgap semiconductor connection material due to its cost-effectiveness, excellent thermoelectric properties, and good thermal reliability. However, for efficient sintering of Cu paste, most research applied pressure, reductive atmosphere and/or high processing temperature, which limited the widely application of Cu sinter paste for high density power device interconnection [1]–[3]. Therefore, it is necessary to study the bonding strength, bonding mechanism, and reliability of copper paste on metal plates in high-power devices. To address these issues, this paper reports a non-pressure Cu sinter paste interconnection technology with nano-particles and reductive solvent included. The paste could form efficient sintering in N2. So that high reliable interconnection between chips and substrate could be achieved. The shear strength, SEM and EDS were applied on sintered interconnection for evaluation. And the result showed that the Cu sinter paste showed good bondability on both Cu and Ag surface, and the key factors for high rank sintering were explored. This work provides both experimental and theoretical research for creating high-strength connections by sintered Cu pastes, and extended the potential of Cu sinter paste in high density power devices.

articleTitle: Microstructure Optimization of Magnetron-Sputtered Silver Films for Low-Temperature Interconnection
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The capacity for low-temperature interconnection of metal films correlates closely with their microstructure. Optimizing the microstructure of deposited metal films is crucial for achieving the desired low-temperature interconnection characteristic. In this paper, the effects of sputtering power on the microstructure of silver (Ag) films prepared using magnetron sputtering technology were investigated. The results demonstrated that variations in sputtering powers led to significantly distinct microstructures, including surface morphology, texture, and grain size. Specifically, with the increase of sputtering power, the microstructure of as-deposited Ag films evolved from randomly oriented nanocrystalline grains to (111)-preferred-oriented columnar grains with high-density twins, and eventually to equiaxed micron-sized grains displaying strong (111) out-of-plane texture. Furthermore, property testing results showed that nanotwinned Ag films displayed an exceptional combination of hardness and electrical conductivity, presenting great potential as promising low-temperature bonding materials. Lower sputtering powers effectively prevent grain coarsening during film thickening, making them preferable for depositing Ag films used in low-temperature interconnections.

articleTitle: Multi-Physics Simulation Modeling for SiP of RF Front-End with Microchannel
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Due to the complex structure of the heterogeneous integrated package of antenna and radio frequency (RF) front-end, it involves the coupling of electromagnetic, thermal, and force multiple physical fields. At the same time, there are also multi-scale problems in the simulation of microchannel structure and RF front-end, which greatly improves the difficulty of simulation modeling. Based on the preliminary design of an RF front-end prototype, this paper proposes a multi-physics simulation modeling method, particularly focusing on the modeling method for thermal microchannels. By establishing a multi-layer dielectric layer containing microchannels and then performing Boolean operations on the complete dielectric layer, the complete microchannels and dielectric layers are obtained. The modeling method proposed in this study can be used to predict the multi-physical field coupling relationship of the system-in-package (SiP) of RF front-end with microchannel and provides a more comprehensive and reliable simulation analysis method for electronic packaging design.

articleTitle: Effect of Redistributed Layer Metal Thermal Expansion on the Hybrid Bonding Surface Roughness
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Hybrid bonding is a promising technology to achieve 3D integrated chips with fine-pitch vertical interconects and high reliability. Many studies focus on the surface roughness during the bonding process, because the surface roughness is a key factor that will influence the bonding interface quality. However, there is no research pay attention to the surface roughness variation owing to the thermal expansion mismatch between redistributed layer (RDL) metal and dieleric mateiral during the bonding process. This paper first analysis this mechanism based on the finite element method. And conclude that fine pitch of RDL metal, thick dieletric layer and small coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) of RDL metal are beneficial to the surface roughness variation and bonding quality.

articleTitle: Novel Copper Foam/Indium Composite Thermal Interface Materials for Advanced Flip Chip Ball Grid Array Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The most common type of solder used as thermal interface material (TIM1) is indium (In) for LGA and PGA packaging. However, there is lack of applications of In TIM1 in FCBGA packaging due to the leakage or pump-out of liquid In TIM1 during the multiple reflow cycles of FCBGA packaging. Copper foam matrix embedded in In could prevent the leakage during the multiple reflow cycles for FCBGA packaging and improves the thermal conductivity of the In thermal interface materials. In this study, A novel copper foam/indium Composite TIM1 is prepared and a typical flip chip ball grid array (FCBGA) simulation model with a package size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$52.5\times 52.5$</tex> mm was created. ANSYS ICEPAK was used for thermal analysis to discuss the effects of porosity of copper foam, bond line thickness (BLT), die area and other parameters of packaging on chip heat dissipation performance. It was revealed that increasing die area and TIM2 thermal conductivity can significantly decrease the maximum chip junction temperature of Die. Besides, decreasing the copper foam porosity from 95% to 60%, the Copper foam/In composite thermal interface material Young's modulus increased from 18.6GPa to 33.2GPa, thermal expansion coefficient increased from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$27.5\times 10^{-6}/{}^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$21.3\times 10^{-6}/{}^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Empirical Modeling of NPN Bipolar Transistors Under Reverse Emitter-Base Junction Current Hot Carrier Stress
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Hot carrier stress (HCS) under reverse Emitter-Base junction current (Ireb) is a major degradation mechanism in NPN bipolar transistors. With the continuous miniaturization of devices, the internal electric fields of these devices increase, leading to a heightened possibility of HCS. This makes understanding and mitigating the HCS effect crucial for the development of reliable, high-performance electronic devices. We employed the constant current stress (CCS) method on NPN bipolar transistors subjected to Ireb stress to study HCS. Ireb and temperature dependence are investigated using an empirical HCS model. The results are beneficial in industries where long device lifespan and reliability are critical, such as in space applications, medical devices, or critical infrastructure systems.

articleTitle: Gain-Variable High-Speed Signal Processing Circuit for Large-Scale PSD Array
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensor (SHWFS), as an important component of the adaptive optics system, is employed to measure both the amplitude and phase of incident light, which has been widely used in astronomical telescopes, medicine, laser communications. SHWFS is composed of a microlens array and a photoelectric detector located on the focal plane. The most commonly used photoelectric detector in SHWFS is charge-coupled device (CCD). However, the CCD has a main disadvantage of low frame rate with the increase of detection target surface, resulting in the SHWES an inability of real-time wavefront measurement. Position sensitive detector (PSD) is a photoelectric detector specialized in detecting the position of incident light spots, characterized by fast speed, high accuracy, and high resolution. Therefore, PSD array is recognized as the most competitive candidate for SHWFS. However, a high-speed readout circuit for large target surface detection based on PSD arrays is currently lacking. This paper proposed a multi-channel analog multiplexing signal readout strategy for a compact <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$9\times 9$</tex> PSD array, including the high-speed reading circuit architecture, variable gain strategy and the imbalance suppression between the four-channel of a single PSD. The high-speed readout circuit can be mainly divided into four modules: current multiplexing, I-V conversion, ADC, and FPGA-based coordinate calculation. The high-speed signal processing circuit designed for the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$9\times 9$</tex> array achieves a readout rate of 100 kHz and a position resolution of less than 0.3μm. The application of variable gain modules can significantly extend the current range accepted by the signal processing circuits. Compared with traditional processing circuits, the proposed multiplexing signal readout strategy will achieve the performance of the high-speed, high position resolution, wide dynamic range, channel-balanced and compact area.

articleTitle: Effect of MPS on the Electrodeposition of (111)-Oriented Nanotwinned Copper
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: This study investigates the influence of the concentration of the additive MPS (a known inducer of (111) orientation in nanotwinned copper growth) on the microstructure and electrochemical behavior of (111) nt-Cu during direct current deposition. High-resolution X-ray diffractometers, backscattered electron imaging scanning electron microscopy, dual-beam focused ion beams, and field emission scanning electron microscopy were employed to characterize the crystal orientation and microstructure of (111) nt-Cu grains. Microstructural analysis of the deposit reveals that the addition of 300 ppm MPS at 40 ASD high current density promotes the nucleation of (111) nt-Cu, resulting in distinct hexagonal facets on the surface of the grains and a high-density parallel twinned layer structure within the crystal. Electrochemical analysis indicates that an appropriate amount of MPS enhances the abundance of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Cu}^{+}$</tex> intermediates, with a significantly accelerated reduction rate of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Cu}^{2+}/\text{Cu}^{+}$</tex> attributed to the high coverage of thiol-bridged chlorides, thus promoting the abundance and stability of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Cu}^{+}$</tex> intermediates during the electrodeposition process. The increase in the number of copper deposition nucleation sites, along with stress relief, reduces the interfacial energy of the film, leading to the formation of nanotwinned structures. These findings provide valuable insights into the growth mechanism of (111)-oriented nt-Cu.

articleTitle: Performance Improvement of Ultra-Thin DRAM Package Using Fan-Out Wafer-Level Package
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Ball grid array (BGA) package is the common package solution in memory products. With the demand for high-speed dynamic random access memory (DRAM) in AI training, wire bond cannot meet the electrical interconnect requirements of high-speed signals. To obtain less electrical resistance and loss during high-speed digital signal propagation, the DRAM is designed with advanced package technology, such as flip-chip (FC) and redistribution layer (RDL). Meanwhile, these technologies result in ultra-thin design, which also meet the requirement of reducing the thermal resistance and the length of signal routing to enhance the package's reliability and signal integrity. In the manufacturing opinion, the RDL-based Fan-out wafer level package (FOWLP), has the advantage of high production efficiency and the ability to achieve ultra-thin thickness, which is an efficient way to decrease the thickness of memory products and costs. Therefore, Fan-out process was applied to design a DRAM with thickness of 0.876mm, which was manufactured by using chip-first Fan-out process. Then, to verify the performance of the proposed Fan-out DRAM package, detailed comparisons among the window-BGA (wBGA), flip-chip chip-scale package (FCCSP), and Fan-out package are made, including the thermal simulation, electrical simulation, and warpage experiment test. Thermal simulation and measuring results show that the thermal and the warpage properties are better than wBGA and FCCSP. Furthermore, It is found that DRAM using the Fan-out package can reduce the parasitic parameter values.

articleTitle: The Effective Cure Shrinkage of Underfill and its Effects on the Reliability of Flip Chip Package
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Underfill (UF) is an important material for improving the reliability of flip chip interconnection in advanced packaging. How the curing process of underfill in the packaging process affects the residual stress of the encapsulation is of great significance for packaging reliability evaluation and failure analysis. In this paper, an effective curing shrinkage measurement system has been built by utilizing the Fiber Bragg Grating (FGB) method and the effective curing shrinkage of an underfill material has been measured; the warpage behavior of a Si-UF-Si three-layer structure which was designed to simulate the actual encapsulation has been experimental measured using the 3D-Digital Image Correlation (DIC) method after UF curing, and an finite element model has been built and warpage of the three-layer structure has been calculated based on the measured effective curing shrinkage of UF, results shows that the curing shrinkage and relaxation behavior of underfill affect warpage behavior oppositely and may both contribute to the warpage behavior of the three-layer structure; furthermore, based on the warpage results of the three-layer structure, the curing shrinkage effect of underfill on the residual stress of a FCBGA packaging has been analyzed by FE simulation with modified simulation parameters.

articleTitle: Avalanche Ruggedness Evaluation on Planar and Trench SiC MOSFETs: An Experimental and TCAD Simulation Study
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In the domain of power electronics, especially for applications requiring high power, high temperature, and high frequency, Silicon Carbide Metal Oxide Semiconductor Field-Effect Transistors (SiC MOSFETs) stand out due to their excellent properties such as high thermal conductivity, elevated breakdown electric field, and minimal power loss. These devices are pivotal in the reliability and safety of electric vehicles, where avalanche-induced failures represent a significant risk within automotive uses. This study extensively explores the avalanche ruggedness of both planar and trench SiC MOSFET configurations through a combination of Unclamped Inductive Switching (UIS) testing in single and multiple pulse scenarios, and Technology Computer-Aided Design (TCAD) simulations. Initial UIS experiments revealed the primary failure mechanisms and their origins in SiC MOSFETs. Following empirical analysis, TCAD simulations were employed to develop comprehensive models of these devices., enhancing the understanding of failure dynamics during UIS conditions. The integration of empirical and simulation data supports the creation of advanced strategies to reduce the risk of avalanche failures, thereby enhancing the durability and reliability of Wide Bandgap Semiconductor devices.

articleTitle: Reliability study on thermal cycling of QFP device solder joints based on morphological optimisation
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As a research method with low cost and high accuracy, finite element simulation is widely used in various fields. However, there are still some difficulties in obtaining accurate initial model in some researches. In this paper, Surface Evolver software is used to calculate the initial solder joint model of QFP device by energy minimization principle, and the model is tested experimentally. Then, the solder joint model was imported into the finite element software to establish the QFP device model, and the thermal cycle simulation test at -55-150°C was carried out to obtain the mechanical properties of the solder joint. Finally, the fatigue life prediction model is used to calculate the life of solder joints.

articleTitle: Fabrication of Continuous Ni Barrier/Seed Layer on Conformal Parylene Liner in TSVs for 3D Packaging and Heterogeneous Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Herein, we demonstrate a low-cost and low-complexity fabrication scheme for TSVs with low-k parylene liner and Ni barrier/seed layer. Two pre-treatment steps are conducted before the formation of the parylene liner by chemical vapor deposition (CVD) and the Ni barrier/seed layer by electroless plating (ELP), respectively. The first one includes the sequential pre-treatments by O2 plasma and a specifically mixed adhesion promotion (AP) solution, which enhances the adhesion between the liner and the substrate. The second one is the surface modification of the parylene liner by a sodium naphthalene solution, which significantly improves the adhesion between Ni and parylene, thus enabling the deposition of a continuous Ni layer in the deep vias. Consequently, TSVs with a diameter of 30 µm and a height of 200 µm are successfully manufactured. This work provides a feasible solution to the demands for low-cost and high-performance TSVs in the 3D packaging and heterogeneous integration applications.

articleTitle: Electromigration Behavior of Sn-3.5Ag Solder Joints with (110) and (111) Nanotwinned Cu UBMs
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The effect of UBM type ((111) and (110) nt-Cu, polycrystalline Cu) on electromigration behavior of solder joints with different orientations <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta-\mathbf{S n}$</tex> grains was investigated. The dissolution of cathode substrate and the growth of IMC at anode interface in solder joints with (111) and (110) nt-Cu UBM were slower than those with pc-Cu, and inhibitory effect of (111) nt-Cu was more significant. The electromigration lifetimes of (111) and (110) nt-Cu solder joints with medium and large angle <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta \beta{-}$</tex> Sn were longer than those of pc-Cu solder joints. The primary failure mode of solder joints with medium angle <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta \beta-\mathbf{S n}$</tex> was the excessive dissolution of cathode UBMs, and that with large angle <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta \beta-\mathbf{S n}$</tex> grains was the voids propagation at cathode. Therefore, nt-Cu acting as UBM could improve the electromigration reliability of solder joints.

articleTitle: Study on the Welding Fastness of CQFP Ceramic Package Lead
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The Ceramic Quad Flat Pack (CQFP) is a common form of integrated circuit packaging, which is composed of high-temperature co-fired ceramics (HTCC) and metal leads, and has a wide range of applications in military, aviation and aerospace fields. In order to meet the requirement of high reliability, the welding strength of CQFP ceramic package lead is studied. In this paper, the finite element simulation software is used to simulate the test process of lead tension. After establishing the model, the force of each node is simulated and analyzed by cell grid division. The stress value of each element node and the stress distribution cloud map are evaluated when the lead is subjected to 7N vertical pulling force. The simulation results show that the maximum stress value is mainly distributed at the back foot of the lead solder. According to the simulation results, the lead and solder are optimized and the lead tension test is carried out. After optimization, the lead tension test results of the structure increased from 3N to 13.2N, and the welding strength of the lead is improved. The simulation results are consistent with the experimental results, which provides an important reference for the research of the welding fastness of CQFP leads.

articleTitle: An Insertion-Based Mechanical Interlock Cu-Sn Bonding Structure for Three-Dimensional Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In three-dimensional integration, multi-chip bonding requires substantial processing time. This paper proposes a novel mechanical interlock Cu-Sn bonding structure, which can significantly reduce the occupation time of bonding equipment. The columnar bumps are inserted into the annular bumps with pressure in the bonding machine to make the plastically deformed Sn fill the annular bumps and form a mechanical interlock structure. Subsequently, Cu-Sn solid-liquid interdiffusion (SLID) bonding or solid-state diffusion (SSD) bonding is performed by thermal treatment. This structure can be applied in chiplet assembly, where multiple chips can be gang-assembled onto one certain substrate then annealed simultaneously, avoiding reliability issues caused by repeated heating of the chiplets and substrate. We conducted five sets of experiments and determined the following two process conditions. For Cu-Sn SLID bonding, the insertion parameters include 25 °C temperature, 80 MPa pressure, 120 s load hold time, and the thermal treatment parameters include 260 °C temperature, 20 MPa pressure, 60 s dwell time. For Cu-Sn SSD bonding, the insertion parameters include 25 °C temperature, 300 MPa pressure, 120 s load hold time, and the thermal treatment parameters include 150 °C temperature, 4 h dwell time. The formation of intermetallic compounds (IMCs) has been successfully observed. The shear strength is 75.62 MPa for Cu-Sn SLID bonding and 85.37 MPa for Cu-Sn SSD bonding.

articleTitle: EMIB Packages Simulation for Heterogeneous Integration of GaN and Si High-Power Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Serving as a high-bandwidth, low-latency, and low-power solution for die-to-die communication, Embedded Multi-die Interconnect Bridge (EMIB) enables selective high-density electrical connections between heterogeneous dices in the same package. In this paper, a three-dimensional finite element model of an EMIB package is developed for the heterogeneous integration of GaN and Si high-power chips. ANSYS simulation software is used and the model is analyzed for its thermal dissipation under forced air cooling condition. For the electrical properties, the experimental design variables are stack position, line width, line spacing, and substrate materials with different dielectric constants to investigate their effect on crosstalk and insertion loss. Also, characterized by the eye diagram quality, impact of trace length on signal transmission is researched, which helps optimize the location of two heterogeneous chips for thermal management. According to the simulation results, under the condition of ensuring enough height of eye diagram (0.6Vpp), the temperature of GaN chip can be controlled within 124.8 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^\circ \mathrm{C}$</tex>, and the temperature of silicon chip within <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$45.4^{\mathrm{o}}\mathrm{C}$</tex>, both of which have power density of 166 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{GW}/\mathrm{m}^{3}$</tex> and 13 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{GW}/\mathrm{m}^{3}$</tex>, respectively.

articleTitle: Design and Preparation of Ultra-Thin Conformal Shielding Coatings with Sandwich Structure for System in Packaging (SiP)
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this study, we designed and printed an ultra-thin conformal shielding coating with a sandwich structure using inkjet printing, and studied the effects of resistivity, the number of conductive layers, and the thickness and type of dielectric layers on shielding performance. The results demonstrated that the shielding effectiveness of the sandwich structure coating can reach up to 95dB, which is 8–10dB greater than that of a single metallized shielding layer. At the same time, it was found that its overall thickness did not exceed 6 µm. These studies will provide a reference and basis for the design and preparation of thinner and more effective shielding coatings.

articleTitle: Voiding Control of Indium Thermal Interface Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Thermal interface materials (TIMs) are widely used in a variety of applications. Solder thermal interface materials (sTIM) are particularly suitable for high-power electronic components. In addition, pure indium metal is the best choice for thermal interfaces, attributed to its exceptional combination of high thermal conductivity and compliance. However, voids contain low thermal conductivity materials, such as gases or flux residues, and can significantly reduce thermal conductivity. It is critical to develop a flux vehicle for indium-TIM preforms, along with an appropriate process, to avoid significant voiding. Numerous factors, including the size and thickness of the indium preforms, the surface finish of the substrates, as well as the amount and type of the liquid flux, are thought be responsible for voiding. In addition, prebaking conditions and reflow profile also have a strong influence on void formation. All of these factors were examined in this study, and the results showed that many factors could have certain effects on voids. Moreover, these effects were found to be interrelated: voiding increased as the liquid flux amount increased. Prebaking with a higher temperature for a longer time within the necessary limits contributed to the reduction of voids. It was found that a reflow profile with a higher peak temperature had more voids than a profile with a lower peak temperature. To investigate the outgassing behavior of flux, thermal gravimetric analysis (TGA) was performed for each flux. The rate of weight loss before reaching the melting point (156°C) of indium was found to have a major influence on voiding performance.

articleTitle: Solutions for Voiding Control of Lead-Free Soldering at QFN Application
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The quad-flat no-lead (QFN) package design is widely applied in many new applications due to benefits including small size, reduced lead inductance, and good thermal and electrical performance. However, it remains challenging to control thermal pad voiding under QFN due to the large coverage area and low standoff. Many parameters, such as solder paste flux type, powder size, powder quality, surface finish, and component size can impact voiding behavior. In addition, process parameters such as stencil design, printing, and reflow also have a strong impact on voiding. In this work, solder paste flux type, solder particle size, reflow profile, and reflow atmosphere were evaluated. While most variables showed some effect on voiding performance individually, the strongest effects were seen through specific combinations of variables. Solder paste flux type effects were strong and reflow atmosphere effects were moderate for SAC305 type 4 powder, both of which increased for SAC305 type 5 powder. Peak temperature and the time above liquidus (TAL) of the reflow profile also had a strong impact on the SAC305 type 4 powder.

articleTitle: Improving Thermal Transport at Graphene Film/Silver Interfaces by Titanium
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: To meet the escalating demands for thermal management driven by the rapid increase in power density and compact packaging structures, reducing the thermal resistances of non-metallic/metallic heterogeneous structures is very important for thermal management in electronic packaging. In this work, transition metal (titanium) was used to reduce the thermal resistances between graphene film (GF) and silver (Ag). The deposition of titanium between GF and Ag using the physical vapor deposition (PVD) method, creates a buffer layer between GF and substrate metal.
