The advantage of the buffer layer is that it can regulate the electron-phonon transfer between GF and metal, resulting a lower interfacial thermal resistance. The influence of transition metal Ti on the interfacial thermal resistance between GF and Ag was investigated, and it was found that the introduction of Ti can decrease the interfacial thermal resistance between GF and Ag by 23%. Our methods can achieve a lower interfacial thermal resistance between GF and Ag. The results offer an effective thermal management solution for electronic packaging.

articleTitle: Structural Design and Technology of Microchip-Packaged DC/DC Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Microchip-packaged DC/DC Converters is the latest generation of DC/DC Converters based on modular semiconductor packaging, pushing the integration, lightweight, and miniaturization of DC/DC converters to new height. This article investigates the structural design, thermal design, packaging process technology of microchip-packaged DC/DC Converter. The microchip-packaged DC/DC converts adopts a “sandwich” structure, packaged-size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{38.72}\mathbf{mm}\times \mathbf{22.8}\mathbf{mm} \times \mathbf{7.21}\mathbf{mm}$</tex>, output power of 320W, and power density of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{818}\mathbf{W}/\mathbf{in}^{\mathbf{3}}$</tex>. Compared with traditional packaging DC/DC converters, the power density increased by more than 200%. Through reliability verification, it has been proven that the operating temperature range of the developed microchip packaging DC/DC converter can reach -55°C -125°C, meets the high reliability requirements in the aerospace field.

articleTitle: Optimized Organic Tunnel for Large Area Connection of Power Module
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The third-generation semiconductor materials, characterized by wide bandgaps, exhibit the capability to operate under high voltage, large current, and high switching frequencies. Presently, sintered silver and sintered copper are commonly employed as packaging interconnects for high-power chips. However, for packaging materials of high-power density chips, attributes such as high thermal conductivity, electrical conductivity, and reliability are of paramount importance. The thermal conductivity between power modules and heat sinks also constitutes a bottleneck in realizing the full potential of power chips. The application of sintered silver in power module packaging incurs high costs and is accompanied by issues such as silver electrochemical migration. This study focuses on the interconnection process and reliability between high-power density chip packaging modules and heat sinks. By printing a layer of paste covering the entire <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$50\mathrm{x}50\text{mm}^{\wedge}2$</tex> substrate surface, as well as printing a layer containing organic tunnels, the reliability issues of large-area copper sintering are investigated. The introduction of organic dispersal tunnels addresses the low strength problem associated with large area sintering by reducing organic residues within the sintering structure, thereby enhancing the interconnection strength of sintered joints. Microstructural observations of the sintered joints reveal a well-connected interface between the sintered joint and substrate. The whole copper block was divided into four pieces. Furthermore, shear strength testing of the interconnect joints indicates that the introduction of organic dispersal tunnels significantly enhances joint strength, with shear strength increasing from 28.4 MPa to 37.3 MPa. The introduction of organic dispersal tunnels effectively addresses the issue of low strength in large-area sintered interconnect joints, thereby improving the reliability of module operation.

articleTitle: Study on Curing Kinetics and Toughening Modification of Epoxy Resin System for Solder Resist
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The curing kinetics of bisphenol A (DGEBA) and bisphenol F (BPF) curing system were studied. And the optimum curing temperature was determined by extrapolation method. A series of reinforced and toughed curing epoxy resins (EPs) were prepared by incorporating nano SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and the flexible 1,4-butanediol diglycidyl ether (1,4-BDDE) into the DGEBA/BPF system and mixed uniformly through high speed vacuum defoaming. The SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/1,4-BDDE in the 1:1 ratio (2B2Si) has an obvious effect of strengthening and toughening, at the same time, the thermal stability is improved. By enhancing the interface between the SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and EP matrix through reactions with the resin, the nanoparticle absorbed on the polymer surface could generate more sliver streaks, thereby toughening the material when subjected to impact, while the 1,4-BDDE providing the toughness to the composite. This work provides a new thread to form toughed EPs for solder resist in IC substrate for advanced packaging.

articleTitle: The Reliability of Complex Printed Circuit Board Assembly under Thermal Cycling, Random Vibration, Electromigration and Combined Loads
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The solder joints of military PCBA (Printed Circuit Board Assembly) suffer harsh environmental conditions, such as temperature cycling, great random vibration, and electromigration. In this study, the reliability of solder joints in military PCBA under single loading (including electromigration, temperature cycling, and random vibration) and combined loads has been studied by finite element simulation and experimental tests. The failure time under different loads have been calculated and compared, respectively. The failure positions have been analyzed and discussed. The results of simulation and test showed that the failure time of solder joints under comprehensive environment was much shorter than that under single loading. The failure position was located at the interface between the solder joint and the pad. In most cases, the location of the failed solder joints was at the corner of the device. A series of models such as the atomic flux divergence model were used to calculate the failure time under single loading (electromigration, thermal cycling, and random vibration) and combined loads. The life testing was carried out according to the relevant standards, and the fatigue test life was obtained. The effectiveness of the simulation life was verified.

articleTitle: Investigation of Low-Melting Sn-Bi-In Solder Joints for Flexible Interconnects
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Flexible packaging is an emerging technology in electronic device packaging, addressing the limitations of traditional methods in achieving lightweight and flexible designs. By replacing rigid substrates with flexible ones, flexible packaging enhances flexibility and bending performance, essential for the design and manufacturing of advanced electronic products. A critical aspect of flexible packaging is controlling the packaging temperature to protect components and prevent substrate damage. In our research, we developed a low-melting-point Sn-Bi-In solder alloy for flexible packaging applications. This solder alloy, designed for bonding flexible copper-clad PI films, exhibited a melting point of approximately 82°C, as determined by TG-DSC analysis. Microstructural analysis using XRD and SEM revealed a eutectic structure of (In, Bi) Sn4 and BiIn. Uniaxial tensile tests showed the solder alloy had a tensile strength of about 32 MPa, indicating good ductility. The wetting angle of the solder on a pure Cu substrate was measured at 66°, suggesting it could effectively wet and spread on both the Cu substrate and the copper-clad PI film. To analyze interface bonding strength and microstructure, we designed a sandwich structure of Cu/solder alloy/copper-clad PI flexible joints. This structure allowed for detailed examination of joint properties. The connection between the solder and the substrate was achieved at temperatures above 110°C, with the solder's flowability increasing with temperature, resulting in a reduced width of the solder joint. Shear experiments showed that the solder alloy could form reliable joint connections with Cu at 120°C. Our study demonstrates the potential of flexible packaging in electronic device manufacturing, particularly through the use of low-melting-point solder alloys for bonding flexible substrates. These findings contribute to the advancement of flexible packaging techniques and their application in developing flexible electronic devices.

articleTitle: The Comparison Study of Board Level Drop and Set Level Drop Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The IC failures induced by accidental dropping event of modern handheld electronic devices such as mobile phones may result from various failure modes such as cracking of package(PKG), solder joint, etc. Generally, the board level drop test is normally adopted to evaluate the IC failure risk instead of the set level drop test considering cost and efficiency. Recently, however, the chip crack/damage failure rate in board level drop is much lower than that of mobile set level free drop. In this paper, a comprehensive study was performed to investigate the dynamic response characteristics of drop test with a customized PCB board when subjected to board level drop test and set level free drop test. The board level drop test was carried out according to JEDEC standard using a drop test apparatus, and the set level free drop test was employed by using the free drop machine. Moreover, two Finite Element models with reference to board level drop and set level free fall drop tests were developed to simulate the actual drop test scenarios based on two simplified FEA methods (Input-G method and impact velocity method, respectively). The simulation data were compared with experimental outputs to identify the FE Models in terms of accuracy of the results extracted. The dynamic key parameters of typical locations in PCB were analyzed to characterize performance difference during two kinds of drops. The measured and simulated data of corresponding locations in set level drop are all larger than those of board level drop in terms of impact acceleration intensity and duration, the strain response and the simulated chip stress. Comparing with board level drop response, a greater acceleration impact would induce a greater strain response, subsequently, the stress subjecting to chip of IC package is greater during set level free drop. Thus, we can conclude that the impact effect of set level free drop is severer than that of board level drop from experiment and simulation results, this can give a good explanation for the fact that failure rate of board level drop is much lower than that of set level drop.

articleTitle: Effects of Brighteners on Microstructural Characteristics of Electroplated Copper
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Copper electroplating is a fundamental technique for interconnect build-up and surface finish in integrated circuit (IC) and printed circuit board (PCB) industries, taking advantages such as high electric and thermal conductivities of copper and low production and maintenance costs of electroplating process. High-quality electroplating requires good cooperations of baths, tools and parameters, among which electroplating baths play key roles that primarily affect eventual morphology, microstructure, composition and reliability of electroplated copper materials. The active synergies among electroplating additives determine the covering and throwing abilities of electroplating bath to achieve, for example, bottom-up fill or equal-thickness plating. Although more efforts have been devoted to developing novel leveler molecules, a number of research reports indicate that selection and application of an appropriate brightener have chain influences on physicochemical properties of electroplated copper such as appearance, roughness, growth mode, crystal structure, internal stress, ductility, etc. In this work, two typical brighteners, i.e., bis-(sodium sulfopropyl)-disulfide (SPS) and sodium 3-[(dimethylcarbamothioyl)sulfanyl]-1-propanesulfonate (DPS), were formulated with polyethylene glycol (PEG, MW 8000) and comparatively investigated for copper foil electroplating. The results indicate that despite that DPS and SPS show similar depolarizing/accelerating abilities, surface and cross-sectional morphologies, they lead to very distinct residual stress, texture evolution and microstructures.

articleTitle: Pool Boiling Enhancement via Surface Engineering for Thermal Management
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Due to the escalating demands for computational power, coupled with a continuous reduction in the size of electronic packaging, thermal management for electronic devices has become increasingly critical in recent years. Ensuring that the temperature of electronic chips remains below a certain threshold is essential, since overheating can result in a decline in performance and chip breakdowns. To address the intensive cooling needs of heat-emitting chips, a variety of devices and methods have been explored, such as heat pipes, vapor chambers, pool boiling, spray cooling, and jet impingement cooling. Tailoring thermal and chemical characteristics of the target heated surface is one of the key factors in enhancing heat removal efficiency. This study highlights the critical role of employing advanced surface engineering techniques which particularly focuses on the integration of a novel semi-layered microporous copper structure, developed in conformity with a multi-level micro-cubic pin fin silicon substrate. The semi-layered microporous copper structure is fabricated using polystyrene sphere as the template to assist the electrodeposition of copper, with a low current density being employed to ensure meticulous fabrication. The initial gradient of the muti-level substrate is defined using silicon dioxide as the mask, setting the depth to encapsulate the PS template effectively. This foundational layer is crucial for confining the PS template securely in place. The second gradient is defined using photoresist as the mask to etch micro pin fin structures into the substrate, aimed at enhancing the adhesion between the substrate and the PS template and expand the heat exchange area. This meticulous structuring prevents the template from detaching during large-scale electroplating operations, ensuring the integrity of the micro fabrication process. The semi-layered microporous copper and the multi-level micro-cubic pin fin silicon substrate are both strategically designed to augment nucleation sites and enlarge the heat exchange surface area during the boiling heat transfer process within a pool boiling system. Further enhanced by the jet flow disturbances aimed directly at the heat transfer surface, facilitating rapid bubble removal and liquid replenishment, which contributes to delaying the onset of dry out. By employing Novec 649 as the coolant under a jet flow rate of 2.5L/min, we've reached a critical heat flux of 90/Wcm2 on a semi-layered microporous copper structure over a large heated area of 1.5 x 1.5 cm. This research provides valuable knowledge that can inform the development of highly effective surface engineering designs in high heat flux management systems.

articleTitle: Soldering Process Research of Large Size FC with Tin Based Bump and Ceramic Substrate
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The soldering technology of flip chip has become one of the mainstream technologies. Both the mass reflow flip chip attach process and the thermosonic flip chip (TSFC) bonding process was used widely to achieve flip chip soldering. Traditional SnPb alloy has been widely used. For environment and health concerns, SnAg alloy systems were regarded as the substitute for the SnPb solder alloys. So it is necessary to find an suitable flip chip soldering technology for large size FC with SnAg bump to achieve mass production. In this work, we found the reflow soldering were more suitable to a large size FC with tin-based bump and a ceramic substrate. An Sn-Ni IMC layer was formed with a thickness of 3 um in the interface. The metallurgical reaction between bump and pad provided a strong strength for the interface. More than 95% of the solder joints after reflow were fractured inside the solder joint. Therefore, a well bond formed by reflow soldering.

articleTitle: Warpage Analysis and Optimization of IGBT Package Module in Reflow Process
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Insulated gate bipolar transistor (IGBT) power modules, renowned for their excellent electrical performance and switching characteristics, find extensive application in fields such as photovoltaic power generation, new energy electric vehicles, and rail transportation. However, the asymmetric structure and significant mismatch in the coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) within IGBT modules lead to substantial warpage deformations and residual stresses during the reflow process of encapsulation. These inherent issues adversely affect the reliability of IGBT modules, thereby reducing the operational lifespan of the products. This paper conducts a theoretical analysis and simulation verification of the warpage issue in IGBT modules during the reflow soldering process. We establish a thermal-structural coupled simulation approach based on finite element analysis (FEA) for the reflow soldering process. Utilizing the method of reverse pre-warping, we conduct simulated optimization of IGBT modules, reducing the original warpage from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+146\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-20\mu\mathrm{m}$</tex>, thereby effectively improving module warpage and achieving good coplanarity. Pre-warping IGBT modules before reflow soldering significantly enhances the module's reliability and extends the product's service life.

articleTitle: The Reverse Bias Reliability of SiC MOSFET Under Different Conditions and Failure Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: SiC MOSFET typically require a gate voltage below −5V for a complete channel close due to the inherent characteristics. In practical applications, when SiC MOSFET is turned off, it needs to withstand a negative gate voltage, while subjecting to a high bus voltage at the same time. The negative gate voltage need to be considered when studying the reverse-bias reliability of SiC MOSFET. At present, few literatures study the reverse-bias reliability of SiC MOSFET between zero gate voltage and negative gate voltage. Existing standards require that the gate and source of the device be shorted during HTRB test. However, the HTRB test at negative gate voltage is abler to investigate the voltage tolerance of SiC MOSFET in practical applications. In this paper, the HTRB test at zero gate voltage and negative gate voltage is carried out to study the reverse-bias reliability of 1200V, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$25\mathrm{m}\Omega$</tex> SiC N-channel device, and the failure mechanism is analyzed. The results show that the differences in the reverse-bias reliability at different gate voltages have not been found yet since the test start, and the high temperature caused by the high power consumption generated by the leakage current creates a hot spot on the chip surface and causes a short circuit on the device.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Characterizations of A Low-Warpage Interposer Embedded with Polyimide-liner TSVs for SIP Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Through-silicon-vias (TSVs) with polyimide (PI) liner have shown advantages in terms of small parasitic capacitance, good thermal-mechanical reliability, and low fabrication cost. However, their interposer-level properties such as the interposer warpage are still lacking. In this paper, a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.0 \text{cm} \times 1.5 \text{cm}$</tex> interposer embedded with PI -liner TSV s is fabricated and characterized. Based on our reliable fabrication flow, TSVs with a diameter of 30 um and a depth of 200 um are suc-cessfully fabricated in a high yield of nearly 97%. The leakage current between a single TSV to the Si substrate is only 1.04 pA at 20 V, proving the good electrical performance of the fabricated TSV s. Besides, the maximum interposer-level warp-age after the double-sided chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) processes is only 17.5 urn and the local roughness of the polished substrate is below 24.8 nm. Such low-warpage inter-poser embedded with TSVs using low-k PI liner are promising for the advanced packaging technology and heterogeneous integration architecture including the system-in-package (SiP) applications.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of Piezoresistive Pressure Sensor for Automotive Application
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Pressure sensors play an important role in aerospace, automotive, medical, and consumer electronics. This paper investigated the structural design of a specific one, the micro piezoresistive pressure sensor, to enhance the linearity and accuracy. The typical absolute type pressure sensor of 4 bar full scale output (FSO) is fabricated based on dry etching and Si-Si fusion bonding. The results showed that the sensitivity reached to 5 mV/V/bar, and linearity error of 0.2% FSO at full temperature range of -40 to 150 °C. The long-term stability of 0.2% FSO after storing 150 °C for 1000 hours satisfy the specification of AEC-Q103 standard.

articleTitle: Study on Factors Affecting the Insulation Performance of Ultra-Fine Pitch Ceramic Packaging Substrates for Billion-Gate FPGA
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Ceramic packages are widely used in high-reliability fields such as aerospace because of their superior characteristics. In recent years, with the rapid development of the integrated circuit industry, high-performance integrated circuits represented by billion-gate FPGA puts forward higher requirements for ceramic packaging, and high-density ceramic packaging substrate constantly faces new challenges in performance and reliability. Among them, with the increasing integration of integrated circuits, the density of the substrate routing increases and the pitch of the pad decreases continuously. The risk of insulation failure of the ceramic packaging substrate caused wide attention in the industry. Based on practical engineering cases, this paper analyzes the factors that affect the surface insulation resistance of ceramic packaging substrate. The results show that impurities and gold adhesion between pads changes of ceramic materials are the main factors affecting surface resistance. The size of impurities and gold adhesion exceeding 30% of the distance between pads can cause insulation test ignition failure. The conclusion of this paper provides a reference for the production and testing of ultra-fine pitch ceramic packaging substrate.

articleTitle: Finite Element Analysis of the Effect of Process Variables and Defects on the Reliability of Nanosilver Processes
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: RF devices can operate at high power densities, which generates a large thermal concentration, thus affecting device reliability. Sintered silver has excellent performance and is an effective method to solve this problem. However, low-temperature pressureless nanosilver sintering can be defective in process fabrication. In this study, actual sample defects and discrepancies were counted based on the occurrence of voids due to dispensing defects, tilting due to manufacturing, and thickness differences due to process variations so that simulation models could be built and analyzed. The results show that larger voids, caused by dispensing defects, increase thermal resistance and decrease sample lifespan. Tilting does not notably increase thermal resistance. Defects tend to form on the thinner, inclined side. Choosing an appropriate nanosilver thickness without increasing thermal resistance significantly boosts the reliability of the device. According to response surface analysis, thickness is crucial in affecting reliability in this specific process variation.

articleTitle: Low Dk/Df Thermosetting Siloxane Hybrid Material for Advanced Packaging Substrate
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Advanced packaging is an indispensable technology for high performance semiconductor devices with high-speed data transmission to realize the hyper-connected society such as internet of things (IoTs), artificial intelligence (AI), and metaverse. To achieve high speed data transfer from the device to device without any error, utilizing material of low dielectric constant (Dk) and low dissipation factor (Df) at high frequency range for advanced packaging substrate has been considered as a key factor. Recently, many low Dk/Df materials have been proposed, for example, modified polyimide (MPI), epoxy, polyphenylene ether (PPE) and polybenzoxazole (PBO). However, the dielectric properties and stability in humid condition of above materials are significantly improper for high-speed applications. Here, we present thermosetting siloxane hybrid materials (Singi G™-1 and 2) with low Dk/Df value in high frequency ranges with high dielectric stability in harsh humid condition. Thermally cured Singi G™-1 and 2 represents low Dk/Df value of 2.9/0.0016 and 3.0/0.0018 respectively at 10 GHz with no variation after aging in harsh humid condition (85<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∘</sup>C /100 RH%). We also fabricated Singi G™-1 and 2 prepreg with glass fabric of quartz and NE-glass. The Singi G™-1 prepreg with quartz and NE-glass fabric showed Dk/Df value of 3.2/0.0014 and 3.43/0.0022 at 10 GHz respectively, whereas the Singi G™-2 prepreg with NE-glass fabric showed Dk/Df value of 3.48/0.0024. Finally, we demonstrated microstrip TEST coupon with Singi G™-1 and its prepreg (quartz) as substrate to evaluate the transmission characteristics. The fabricated Singi G™-1 and quartz prepreg based microstrip showed transmission loss (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>) of -1.77dB/100mm and -1.41dB/100mm at 10 GHz respectively, which were low enough to be utilized as advanced packaging substrate for high-speed data transmission.

articleTitle: Failure Analysis of Open Circuit at Output Terminal of the Voltage Comparator
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: This paper explains the process of failure localization and mechanism analysis for a voltage comparator failure case. The output terminal of the voltage comparator is open circuit. The analysis adopted a series of analysis ideas such as non-destructive troubleshooting, internal positioning, and data statistical analysis. The material of the failure component bonding wire is aluminum. Aluminum corrosion products and external remainder particles led to virtual bonding of the bonding wire. The result of the non-destructive bond pull test showed a value of 0 grams. The debonding position was located in the external bonding area. The corrosion products contained C, O, Al and Cl. Aluminum corrosion of the output bonding wire was an internal failure phenomenon of the voltage comparator. Inspection revealed the movement trajectory of remainder particles. The corrosion location was in the external bonding area. There were similar remainder particles near the corrosion site. The remainder particles adhered to the ceramic. They extended towards the sealing ring position on the long side of the shell side wall. This was consistent with the suspicious hole location found during the appearance inspection. Conduct a profile analysis along the long edge of the leaking sealing ring. The grinding and polishing work was paused at the outer edge of the sealing ring. There was a hole between the metal sealing ring and the ceramic. There was no obvious tungsten layer at the position of the hole. When the grinding and polishing work progressed to a quarter of the width of the sealing ring, the holes decreased. At this point, the tungsten layer at the sealing ring position was discontinuous. The discontinuous position was nickel. When the grinding and polishing work progressed to about one-third of the width of the sealing ring, the holes disappeared. The tungsten layer presented a continuous state. There was the hole between the metal sealing ring and the ceramic substrate. The components needed to be cleaned after installation. During the cleaning process, soldering fluxes and cleaning agent entered through the holes. Ultimately, it led to aluminum corrosion. Repeated parallel seam welding leads to the formation of pores at the junction. The same batch of components had the same problem. And the rejection rate of unqualified sealing was much higher than other batches of the same model. This paper summarizes the research ideas and results. In future work, the feasibility of repeating parallel seam welding processes is worth pondering. This article can help manufacturers improve the robustness of device casings. At the same time, assist the manufacturer in formulating a reasonable range of sealing process parameters. Data statistical analysis methods should be widely applied in failure analysis. By comparing and analyzing different dimensions, it can identify the real potential problem. It can provide reference for similar failure analysis in the future.

articleTitle: Experimental Demonstration of an Advanced Package-Integrated Thin-Film Thermoelectric Cooler for on-Chip Cooling
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The evolution of micro systems towards miniaturization and integration has driven continuous advances in on-chip thermal management technology to meet performance requirements such as high power and high frequency of chips. Thin-film thermoelectric coolers (TFTECs) are a solid-state cooling technology that can be integrated into electronic packages. While TFTECs have been recognized as a potentially optimal solution for electronic cooling, their fabrication process is complex and costly, making it challenging to achieve high performance and integrated applications. In this paper, we propose a method for fabricating TFTECs at the wafer-level using magnetron sputtering, photolithography, and wet etching techniques. The thickness of each leg is 10 μm. The device resistance and cooling temperature difference of the TFTEC are characterized to verify its functionality. Furthermore, the localized and real-time cooling performance of the TFTEC is evaluated by integrating it into a thermal test vehicle (TTV) using a flip-chip ball grid array (FC-BGA) package. At an input current of 50 mA, the TFTEC can cool a hotspot on the TTV chip by approximately 1.3 °C. This work can provide a promising on-chip thermal management solution for power devices and modules.

articleTitle: Experimental and Modeling Analysis on Mechanical Performance of Wafer-Level Micro-Sized SnAg Solder Bump
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the innovation of mobile communication, automotive electronics, and artificial intelligence technologies, the functions of related chips are becoming more and more diversified, leading to a continuous increase in the number of I/O ports carrying electrical signals. Bump is the physical manifestation of I/O, and its miniaturization development and reliability research have gradually become important research directions in packaging interconnection. In this study, 30μm diameter Sn-1.8Ag solder bumps were successfully fabricated on a 12-inch wafer by electroplating method, and the average shear strength of the bump was measured to be 68.18MPa by bump shear test. Many studies have shown that design parameters such as bump diameter, height, and structure affect the bump shear strength. To shorten the development cycle of the bump design, a bump shear model was established using the smooth particle hydrodynamics-finite element method(SPH-FEM) coupled method, and the force-displacement curve obtained by the simulation was relatively consistent with the experimental results. In addition, thanks to the advantages of the SPH method in dealing with large deformation problems, the solder in the simulation showed fracture behavior similar to that in the real bump shear test, which was difficult to achieve with traditional FEM simulation. Based on the above model, the bump shear model was simulated after changing the bump diameter. The simulated bump shear strength increased as the bump diameter increased. The shear strength of the bump with diameters of 32.6μm, 36μm, and 39μm were tested and compared with the simulation results. It was found that the simulation results were consistent with the experimental results in terms of trend.

articleTitle: Multi-Physics Coupling Simulation of Picosecond Pulsed Laser Ablation of Single-Crystal Silicon
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Single-crystal silicon is currently the most widely used wafer substrate material, and the use of silicon materials in the world accounts for more than 95% of the total semicon-ductor materials. In order to separate the chip from the wafer, laser grooving is used before the blade dicing. Through simulation research, the laser grooving process can be visualized, so as to obtain the dynamic physical field information that is difficult to be measured in the experiment can be obtained, and the laser grooving mechanism can be deeply understood to provide support for experimental research. In this paper, a simulation study of picosecond pulsed laser ablation of single-crystal silicon under multi-physics coupling was carried out by COMSOL. The results show that the ablation threshold of single-crystal silicon by picosecond pulse laser is 162.87mJ/cm2 under one pulse. The incubation effect of laser ablation of single-crystal silicon under multi-pulse effect was found, and a power law model was established. The evolution of temperature field during laser ablation of single-crystal silicon was investigated, and the evolution mechanism of groove morphology was elucidated.

articleTitle: Research and Application of Distributed Thermal Resistance Model for High-Reliability Power Circuit in Space Application
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The power circuit for aerospace equipment includes power converters, drive circuit, etc. Due to the need to withstand extreme physical and environmental conditions such as high and low temperatures, vacuum environments,radiation,etc., thick-film assembly and hermetic sealing processes are usually used. With the high-reliability hybrid integrated circuits for aerospace applications developing towards high-density and high-power, the failure problems caused by heat dissipation have gradually become prominent. The concentrated heat generation of high-power components in the module is likely to cause local over-temperature failure. However, as a component of the complete machine system, the thermal model of the circuit product is greatly simplified during the thermal simulation process of the complete system, and cannot truly reflect the actual temperature of the internal power chip of the product. This article models and simulates a typical power hybrid integrated circuit based on FOLTHERM software, and measures the temperature distribution inside the module using infrared imaging technology. A distributed thermal resistance network model covering the power devices inside the module is proposed. Using the temperature of the reference point at the bottom of the casing as the benchmark, the model calculates the temperature of key power devices. The error between the calculated results, simulationresults, and measured results is less than 3°C. The model is compatible with the overall thermal network model of the system, improving the thermal simulation accuracy by more than 50% in the thermal simulation of the entire electronic system. This lays the foundation for precise thermal management of high-reliability aerospace electronic systems.

articleTitle: Degradation Evaluation of Neutron Irradiation Effect on AlGaN/GaN Metal-Insulator- Semiconductor High Electron Mobility Transistors
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: We investigate the degradation effects of neutron irradiation on AIGaN/GaN metal-insulator-semiconductor high electron mobility transistors (MIS-HEMTs) in this work. The performance of the devices is characterized through relevant electrical current-voltage (I-V) test and capacitance- voltage (C-V) test. The result indicates that the electrical parameter of the device degrades after neutron irradiation, such as positive shift of threshold voltage, reduction in output drain current, and the increase of the on-resistance. Additionally, combining with the frequency-dependent conductance method, it displays that shallow energy level- interface states at the AIGaN/GaN heterojunction increase, along with slightly shifting to deeper energy level after neutron irradiation. Neutron irradiation introduces more interface states and increase the scattering which degrading the carrier concentration and mobility, causing related degradation on electrical performances. This study provides useful reference value for the application of GaN-based devices in the aerospace.

articleTitle: High Resolution 1024×768 Micro-LED Display Using Flip-Chip Bonding
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Micro-light-emitting diode (Micro-LED) displays are self-emitting display that integrate III- V compound semiconductors onto silicon (Si) complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) backplane. These displays offer several advantages, including high brightness, low energy consumption, high contrast, long life, and robustness against harsh environment. In this article, micro-LED panels featuring a 1024×768 pixel array within an active area of 0.6 inch were fabricated by bonding the GaN micro-LED array onto the active matrix of a CMOS driver backplane. Optoelectronic testing of the blue micro-LED array reveals peak external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 28.8% and wall-plug efficiency (WPE) ranging from 24.5% to 26.6% at a driving current of 300 mA. The micro-LED panels exhibit excellent image quality, characterized by high brightness, high contrast, and uniform emitting, indicating high quality of the flip-chip bonding process and the overall fabrication process.

articleTitle: Natural-MMT-Modified Uniform Silver Nanowires Networks for Flexible Joule Heating Textile
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Silver nanowires (AgNWs) have been a research hotspot for more than a decade. Due to their high electrical conductivity, transparency and flexibility, AgNWs are regard as a substitution of indium tin oxide (ITO) in a wide range of applications. However, due to their high surface energy and nanoscale size, AgNWs are easily agglomerated with each other during the solution-based process, resulting in a significant degradation of uniformity of the networks, posing threats to conductivity and joule heating performance of AgNWs devices. Researchers have tried to improve the uniformity by modifying AgNWs inks with dispersants. However, previous studies mainly focus on synthetic nanomaterials which are environmentally harmful and expensive. Herein, we proposed a dispersant based on nano-modified natural Ca-montmorillonite (Ca-MMT). By modifying AgNWs dispersion with the dispersant, the uniformity of the conductive network on the viscose nonwoven substrate was improved. The heating textile prepared exhibited an average sheet resistance of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{1.616} \ \mathbf{\Omega}/\mathbf{sq}$</tex> with the standard deviation of sheet resistance less than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0.2} \ \mathbf{\Omega}/\mathbf{sq}$</tex>. Analysis was also conducted to explore the mechanism. This work explores a green and economic method to improve AgNWs networks' uniformity.

articleTitle: A Study on Fabrication and Heat Dissipation of Polycrystalline Diamonds
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this paper, we have theoretically investigated the effect of grain size on the thermal conductivity of diamond by molecular dynamics (MD) calculations, and experimentally prepared different grain sizes of diamond. Through the calculation results, it can be known that the thermal conductivity of diamond increases with the size of the grains. Then, we have prepared polycrystalline diamond (PCD) films by MPCVD equipment and investigated the effect of growth temperature on the grain size of PCD films. Combining the scanning electron microscopy (SEM) results with the growth conditions, we find that the grain size of PCD films is positively correlated with the growth temperature. Subsequently, the PCD films have been tested by Raman spectroscopy and XRD pattern, the results show that all the samples are PCD films and the grain size results obtained by XRD full width at half maxima analysis are in agreement with the SEM results. The research results of this paper may be helpful to promote the application of PCD films in high-frequency and high-power electronic devices.

articleTitle: Simulation of Chip Surface Damage of PP-IGBT Under Electro-Thermal-Mechanical Loading Condition
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistor (IGBT) is a fully controlled power semiconductor device, which is the core device for energy conversion and transmission, and is called the CPU of power electronic devices. It is widely used in engineering applications such as AC transmission, photovoltaic access and other power systems. Fretting wear is one of the most common failure modes of PP-IGBT modules. During the turn-on and turn-off process of the PP-IGBT module, the IGBT chip is affected by the thermal stress caused by the extrusion of the Mo layer, the expansion and contraction of the interface material, and the lateral and longitudinal fretting displacements occur. The IGBT chip and the surface are destroyed, which eventually leads to the failure of the IGBT chip. In this paper, the electric-thermal-mechanical coupling model of PP-IGBT is established by finite element method, and the contact stress, temperature and relative displacement field of the model are calculated. The cumulative damage of the Al metallized plate on the chip surface was calculated by the stress field and displacement field. The results of the finite element analysis model show that the temperature of the IGBT chip changes periodically with the power on and off. The highest temperature appears in the active region of the chip center. The maximum contact stress of the PP-IGBT device appears in the center of the chip, and the maximum relative displacement appears at the boundary.

articleTitle: Study on The Effect of Enclosed delamination on Insulation Properties of High Voltage Switch Silicone Gel Package
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The high-voltage switches are frequently subjected to complex environmental conditions, leading to enclosed delamination between the silicone gel and the substrate, resulting in a decline in insulation. This paper has established a flashover voltage test method for enclosed delamination using stress simulation, and investigated the impact of time, curing temperature, electric field uniformity, and polarity on flashover voltage. The results show the flashover voltage of the enclosed delamination initially increases with time, then decreases, and eventually reaches an equilibrium level equivalent to the condition of no silicone gel potting. This is attributed to gas penetration into the delamination, leading to a dynamic equilibrium of air pressure and components over time, thereby altering the flashover voltage. Samples cured at lower temperatures exhibit a shorter equilibrium time. The flashover voltage of positive polarity is lower than that of negative polarity.

articleTitle: Reliability Analysis of 2.5D Package Structure Based on Thermal-Moisture-Mechanical Coupling
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the widespread application of 2.5D packaging in high-end devices, comprehensive analysis of packaging reliability has become increasingly important. This paper addresses the limitations of previous studies that focused solely on thermal field analysis for evaluating the reliability of 2.5D packaging. It integrates moisture-mechanical models, thermo-mechanical models, and thermal-moisture-mechanical coupling models to conduct a multi-physics coupling analysis, investigating the impact of humidity on 2.5D packaging. The simulation models undergo temperature humidity bias testing and thermal cycling testing after moisture preconditioning to analyze the reliability of the packaging under hygro-thermal expansion stresses. The research results indicate that thermal-moisture stress is more significant in the upper-layer microbumps relative to the lower ones, with the greatest reliability risk occurring at the apex corners of the outer circumference of the solder ball array. Concurrently, under thermal cycling test conditions,it is observed that the maximum equivalent stress induced under the combined influence of thermal and humidity loads escalates by 63.6% in comparison to the maximum equivalent stress induced by thermal loads alone. This article provides certain insights into the reliability of 2.5D packaging in thermo-hygro environments, aiding design professionals in a more thorough assessment of reliability within packaging design.

articleTitle: Logo Detection of Integrated Circuit Based on CycleGAN Method and Improved YOLO-v4-tiny Model
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Focusing on the application requirements for precise detection of Integrated Circuit (IC) logos, and aiming at the problems of difficulty in obtaining database samples, uneven sample sizes, and low detection accuracy, a logo detection of IC Based on cycle-GAN method and improved YOLO-v4-tiny model is proposed. This article uses the cycle-GAN method to amplify small sample images in the IC logo image dataset. Next, the Coordinate Attention (CA) attention mechanism is embedded in the YOLO-v4-tiny model to improve the accuracy of feature representation in lightweight networks, thereby improving detection accuracy. The experimental results show that the cycle-GAN data augmentation method can effectively expand the dataset, and it has been validated on commonly used networks that the enhanced dataset can effectively improve the accuracy of integrated circuit logo detection. In addition, the improved YOLO-v4-tiny model achieved a mAP index of 98.17% on the augmented dataset, which can meet the accuracy index of the integrated circuit logo detection system and reduce the computational resources required for deployment.

articleTitle: Bonding Performance of Pressure Copper Sintering Paste on Different Metalized Substrate/Die
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this work, a pressure copper (Cu) sintering paste, which has been promoted to high power application with high thermal and electrical conductivity, was developed. The sintering of the pressure Cu-paste in a nitrogen atmosphere on different metal surfaces (Cu, silver (Ag), and gold (Au)) was investigated. The pre-dry (temperature and time) and sintering parameters (temperature, pressure, and time) were adjusted to achieve strong joints. Compared to the Ag and Au surfaces of the substrate or dummy die, the highest shear strength over 65MPa was achieved on a Cu surface with the advanced Cu sintering paste. This property breaks the regular procedure of requiring Ag or Au plating for dies or substrates for Ag sintering paste. The sintering conditions for the pressure Cu paste are 250-280°C, 12-25MPa, and 3-10min under a nitrogen atmosphere. After 1,000 cycles of thermo-cycling testing (TCT) at −65°C–150°C, the pressure Cu sintered joints showed stable performance without delamination. Furthermore, this Cu sintering paste can be applied by both printing and dispensing, which are widely used in the electronic industry.

articleTitle: Mold Void Improvement for Stack Die Overhanging Structure Inside Automotive Gate Driver Package
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Vehicle electrification is driving advanced functional safety, control and protection features in automotive EV (electric vehicle) electronics. Many on-board systems such as EV traction inverters, DC/DC converters, and on-board chargers are powered by or connected to high voltage power sources. These require the use of gate driver components to control Si IGBTs (insulated-gate bipolar transistor) and SiC MOSFETs (silicon carbide metal oxide semiconductor field effect transistor) in these systems while maintaining communication to the other lower voltage vehicle circuits. The combination of functional, safety and HV (high voltage) isolation requirements of such gate drivers necessitated development of a novel package technology known as GICL (galvanically isolated communication linkage) [1] [2]. For safety and functional reasons, the package must maintain galvanic isolation between the LV and HV domains after both short duration voltage spikes (system irregularities) and after long term exposure to the working voltages. This applies to both the package external surface and internal volume. A 32 lead SOIC (small outline integrated circuit) package with leads on only two sides was selected to meet the creepage and clearance requirements. Internal isolation was achieved by placing a high voltage dielectric barrier between two stacked die which could communicate by inductive (magnetic) coupling. The package internal configuration and isolation strategy are shown in Fig. 1. Device functionality was partitioned into two die, one for each domain. The stacked structure permitted communication elements on each die to directly transfer data using inductive coupling across the galvanic isolation barrier. The overhanging isolation barrier is designed for sufficient isolation distance between HV die and LV die. But its existence also brings challenges to mold process development on mold void. Mold void can be found at the corner between the isolation barrier overhang and HV die in Fig. 2. Several optimization of design and process had been tried to improve mold void. It is very difficult to 100% eliminate the mold void. As mold compound reaction proceeds, the spiral flow decreases and the viscosity becomes lager. Air is easy to be trapped and form mold void under isolation barrier overhang in Fig. 2. Vacuum mold is as one promising solution to decrease the air-content in the mold cavity were evaluated and confirmed that it can eliminate the mold void under isolation barrier area. This paper will show the vacuum mold process for SOIC package with stack die, overhang structure, Then it summarized evaluation results including vacuum mold parameter development and its process responsibility, reliability evaluation results.

articleTitle: Revealing the Effect of Chemical Bonds on Interface Thermal Resistance of Graphene Film/Cu Laminate Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: To meet the demand for thermal management for heat generated by high-power devices quickly and eliminate the temperature of hot spots, this work introduces an enhanced heat dissipation material manufacturing method and reveals the effect of chemical bonds on the interface thermal resistance of graphene film/Cu laminate structure. The heat dissipation material consists of a graphene film/Cu laminated structure interconnected through carboxyl polydopamine chemical bonds. This structure effectively combines the good mechanical properties of Cu with the exceptional thermal properties of graphene film. Chemical functionalization using different solvents is employed to introduce active groups between graphene film and Cu interfaces. By utilizing chemical bonds to enhance phonon transport at the interfaces, the thermal resistance of the graphene film/Cu substrate inter-connection structure is markedly reduced. The effects of different functionalization durations and their effects on thermal resistance were investigated, and the results show that the thermal resistance of the interconnection structure can reach as low as 2.92 ± 0.08 K/W after eight hours of functionalization of the Cu substrate. This chemically bonded graphene film/Cu composite presents a practical heat dissipation solution for high-density electronic packaging.

articleTitle: Study on Soldering Process and Reliability of Antenna on Package on Multifunctional Rigid-Flex PCB
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the continuous development of packaging technology and substrate technology, more and more functions are integrated into components and substrates, such as antenna on package and multifunctional rigid-flex PCB. Meanwhile, multifunctional integration also increases the difficulty of assembly. Based on the actual needs of a certain product, this article has conducted a study on the soldering process and thermal reliability of ceramic array devices on multifunctional R-FPCB, focusing on the protective measures for the rigid flex zone and the reflow soldering process of AOPs. The reliability of solder joints of fine pitch AOPs and CBGAs was discussed through thermal cycle tests (-55°C~100°C). It was confirmed that a high-precision magnetic positioning tool is ingenious method for the assembly of R-FPCB and an appropriate soldering temperature curve is needed. The results show that the size of pads has great influence on the long-term reliability of high lead solder joints, and edge bonding can improve the thermal cycle life of ceramic array devices, but none of them has passed 500 thermal cycle tests. Last of all, the study results of this paper, especially the soldering reliability analysis of AOPs, can provide technical guidance for the highly reliable assembly and soldering of R-FPCB modules and ceramic devices.

articleTitle: High-Throughput Thermophysical and Structural Characterizations of Semiconductors Using Transient Thermoreflectance
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Pump-probe thermoreflectance (Pump-probe TR) is a non-contact technique for thermal properties characterization of materials, which is also used to analyze material quality and detect defects. For wafers, uniform thermophysical properties and thickness are critical to avoid localized thermal hotspots and device failure. Traditional spot detection methods for fitting unknown parameters are time-consuming and labor-intensive when handling large datasets. This work proposes a high-throughput method for semiconductor thermophysical and structural characterizations, integrating automatic scanning measurements with deep learning techniques. A multilayer perceptron (MLP) model processes the data, demonstrating reliability through global scanning of Au-sapphire samples, revealing variations in thermal boundary conductance (TBC). The method also detects material defects and is validated in industrial applications with GaN-on-Si samples, offering high accuracy and speed. In addition, we demonstrated the feasibility of the method for structural characterization of materials by scanning measurement of the thickness of Si thin film. This high-throughput method can reduce data processing time to the millisecond level, significantly reducing time and labor compared to traditional methods, making it particularly efficient for high-volume wafer thermophysical and structural characterization.

articleTitle: A Dual-Chip Heterogeneous Packaging Power Device by 2.5D Fan-Out Panel Level Packaging (2.5D FOPLP)
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Compared to wafer level packaging (WLP), the current FOPLP technology has better performance in small area chips such as power devices, sensor chips, and RF chips, with advantages in conductivity, heat dissipation, and cost. At present, the FOPLP technology for single-chip packaging power devices has become relatively mature. The research on the application of existing FOPLP technology in multi-chip heterogeneous packaging power devices is receiving increasing attention. In this article, a dual-chip heterogeneous packaging power device MOSFET & GaN was devised and achieved based on 2.SD FOPLP technology using epoxy molding compound (EMC) dielectric layer instead of silicon interposer. Simultaneously realizing the signal conduction between chips and signal interconnection of the entire device through laser vias based on EMC dielectric layer. Compared to traditional wire bonding, the volume of this device based on FOPLP technology has been reduced by about 40%, the static drain-source on-resistance (RDS(on)) of device based on 2.5D FOPLP technology was reduced by about 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>. Hence, the device based on FOPLP can bring significant improvements in integration, heat dissipation performance, and electrical connection, improving the overall electrical performance of multi-chip heterogeneous packaging power devices.

articleTitle: Study on the Effect of Film Process on Interface and Interconnection Reliability in the TSV Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The through silicon via (TSV) is a critical technology to provide short vertical interconnects for 2.5D/3D advanced packaging. But the large mismatch of thermal expansion coefficient (CTE) between Cu and Si/SiO2 results in thermal stress that compromises the thermal mechanical reliability of TSV structures. In this study, the defects caused by thermal stress during film process were investigated by Focused Ion Beam (FIB). Through the Finite Element Analysis (FEA), we have assessed the influence of the liner layer thickness <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{THK}_{\text{liner}})$</tex> between Cu and Si and the interlayer dielectric thickness <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{THK}_{\text{ILD}})$</tex>, on the induced thermal stress. Our study elucidates the interplay between the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{THK}_{\text{liner}},\text{TRK}_{\text{ILD}}$</tex> and thermal stress, confirming that these parameters significantly reduce thermal stress when the THK<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">liner</inf> is set to approximately <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.4\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> and the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{THK}_{\text{ILD}}$</tex> to around <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>. These dimensions are thereby identified as the optimal process parameters for stress minimization. This work can provide an important technical means for the manufacture of TSV with high interface and interconnected reliability, and provide an important reference for practical engineering problems in the high density 2.5D/3D integration.

articleTitle: A Silicon-based Fan-out Technology with High Aspect Ratio TSV for RF Heterogeneous Integration Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Advanced packaging technology has demonstrated its unique technical advantages in miniaturization and high-density integrated application of RF Microsystems. Among many advanced packaging technologies, fan-out packaging technology has been widely used in recent years because of its advantages of high integration, high fabrication flexibility, simple process and low process cost. However, the traditional fan-out wafer-level package (FOWLP) and fan-out board-level package (FOPLP) are mainly aimed at CMOS chip packaging applications, and they face many technical problems in compound RF chip packaging applications, such as RF grounding, heat dissipation of high-power RF chips, air bridge protection of RF chips and signal transmission in vertical. In view of the above problems, this paper proposes a fan-out technology based on silicon-based TSV interposer. By making silicon-based interposer with two different depths of TSV, deep TSV is used for vertical interconnection of signals, and shallow TSV is used for grounding of RF chips. After the interposer is prepared, a cavity is dry etched on the back of shallow TSV for chip embedding. The chip is bonded in the cavity with conductive adhesive with high thermal conductivity. After the bonding process, the vacuum gluing technology is used to spin-coat polyimide as a passivation isolation layer between the chip and the RDL layer. In this paper, a silicon-based Fanout integration of GaAs chip has been successfully fabricated, and the RF performance has almost no attenuation compared with the die mounting test. Results On the surface, the silicon-based fanout technology proposed in this paper can realize the lossless packaging of compound chips with air bridge structure, and has good grounding and heat dissipation performance, which has obvious technical advantages compared with the traditional Fanout technology.

articleTitle: Low-temperature Thermal Shock Simulation and Life Aging Test of Indium Flip-chip Interconnection Using Liquid Helium for Superconducting Integrated Circuit Package
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Superconducting integrated circuits, known as Single Flux Quantum (SFQ) circuits, operate at cryogenic temperatures, specifically 4.2K, leading to a significant temperature difference of nearly 300K from room temperature, inevitably causing reliability issues in flip-chip interconnects. Current research on the reliability of flip-chip interconnects in cryogenic environments predominantly focuses on the liquid nitrogen temperature range, with limited studies in the liquid helium temperature range. This paper provides a reference for such research. In this study, the stress and strain in indium bumps of flip-chip interconnects under cryogenic thermal shock were simulated. Finite element simulations provided the stress- strain distribution in the bumps under cryogenic thermal shock. An Anand viscoplastic model for indium bumps was established. Additionally, the Darveaux lifetime prediction model was used to estimate the lifetime of indium bump flip-chip interconnects under cryogenic thermal shock. The stress-strain was predominantly concentrated at the interface of the bumps with the chip and substrate, reaching a maximum at a temperature of −269°C, with a maximum equivalent stress of 31.1 MPa and a maximum equivalent strain of 0.0024. The simulation predicted a lifetime of 824 cycles. Furthermore, cryogenic shock tests revealed that the flip-chip modules experienced cryogenic failure and recovery at room temperature. SEM cross-section analysis showed cracks in the bumps at low temperatures. Subsequently, process optimization was conducted to fabricate a new batch of flip-chip modules and the low temperature thermal shock test was planned.

articleTitle: Investigation of Embedded Microchannel Heat Transfer Performance Based on High Power Integrated Chip
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The high-power integrated chips face severe thermal management problems, and the embedded micro channel cooling method is an effective heat dissipation technique for high density integrated chips. This paper analyzes the influence of heat transfer performance of microchannel structural parameters in chips. The microchannel structural parameters are optimized by comprehensive performance evaluation factors and finally the optimal heat transfer performance is obtained. The results show that the pressure drop increases as the microchannel heat transfer performance increases. Comprehensive evaluation showed that the side length, height and spacing of square fins with 0.3mm, 0.18mm and 1.2mm, respectively, had a better overall performance evaluation factor.

articleTitle: Epoxy Films with High Dielectric Constant for System in Package Prepared via Modified Electrostatic Atomization
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Development of electronic technology drives electronic devices towards miniaturization and high power density, and the buried capacitor technology is an effective method to improve packaging density. Epoxy resin is frequently used as one of the preferred materials for buried capacitors in electronic packaging systems owing to its excellent insulation properties, corrosion resistance, and ease of processing. However, the low dielectric constant and breakdown strength of traditional epoxy resin films limit their application in high-density electronic packaging. Conventional methods of modifying or compositing epoxy resin thin films to improve their properties are difficult to simultaneously increase the dielectric constant and breakdown strength while maintaining the low loss of epoxy resin. In this study, we use the principle of electrospinning to electrostatically atomize the epoxy resin solution and form a thin film on a carrier film. By comparing the properties of the atomization film with those of the traditional film made by the method of scrape coating, the dielectric constant (D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf>) and breakdown strength (E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf>)of the atomization film increases by about 20% on average, and the medium loss is as low as 0.0115 (25 °C, 1 kHz). This approach provides a method for enhancing the dielectric performance of epoxy resin films, which supports the miniaturization of electronic systems.

articleTitle: Laser Processing of Highly Conductive Graphene Electrodes for Micro-Supercapacitors
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Micro-supercapacitors (MSCs) have become promising micro-storage devices in the field of microelectronics due to their advantages of small size, high power density, and excellent cycling stability. In this work, a composite laser processing technique was reported to convert cyanate ester resin into highly conductive graphene (LIG) films using CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and fiber lasers in ambient air, respectively. Under the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser pyrolysis of resin and subsequent fiber laser annealing, the resulting LIG film exhibits an ultra-low sheet resistance (1.67 Ω per square), which is one order of magnitude lower than that of polyimide (PI)-induced LIG films, indicating the advance of the composite laser processing technique. The effect of substrates with two thermal conductivities on the morphology, sheet resistance and electrochemical performance of the LIG films was also investigated. Benefiting from the excellent thermal conductivity of metal substrate, LIG/Ti-MSCs with titanium substrate provide an areal capacitance of 26.4 mF/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> at a scan rate of 5 mV/s, which is higher than that of LIG/PI-MSCs with PI substrate (~17.6 mF/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) under the same conditions.

articleTitle: A Novel and Efficient Non-Destructive Fault Isolation Methodology for Package-on-Package Module Based on Electromagnetic/Circuit Co-Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: This paper proposes a non-destructive simulation-based fault isolation methodology based on the time-domain reflectometry (TDR) technique. The main idea of the proposed methodology is to replace the extra prepared samples with efficient simulations of circuitries in good and faulty conditions. By extracting the S-parameters of the vertical interconnect with dominant length and modeling all horizontal interconnects as circuit elements in a simple and efficient way, the good and faulty circuitries of the module under test can be emulated in circuit simulator. Based on the comparison and analysis of the simulated and measured TDR impedances, the interconnect fault is successfully isolated without the help of extra prepared samples.

articleTitle: UV-Curable Anisotropic Conductive Paste (ACP) for RFID Tag Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The hot-pressed ACP is commonly used to realize the connection between the chip and the antenna in the RFID tag packaging. However, the temperature of thermal curing process is usually too high to be suitable for some substrates that are not resistant to high temperature. Low-temperature packaging is currently one of significant challenges in RFID tags. To achieve the challenge, this work proposes an UV-curable anisotropic conductive paste to realize the packaging of RFID tags in low-temperature scenarios. We successfully demonstrate the low-temperature packaging of RFID tags using as-prepared UV-curable ACP. The morphology study indicates that the chip is bonded well on the antenna via UV-curable ACP. Importantly, the UV-curable ACP shows an excellent room-temperature storage performance, which is superior to those thermal-curable ACP. In addition, the signal of RFID tags, measured through the ultrahigh-frequency (UHF) electronic tag performance comprehensive test system is stable. The results indicate that UV-curable ACP satisfies the packaging of RFID tags in low-temperature scenarios, expands the application range of ACP, and provides a new packaging method for RFID tags.

articleTitle: Prediction of Shear Strength of SAC305 Solder Bumps Based on Production-Informed Machine Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Advanced packaging technology is regarded as an important breakthrough in the current semiconductor industry. Bump is one of the key structures in the flip-chip interconnection. With recent advancements in computing power, machine learning algorithms have risen again and begun to be applied in the semiconductor industry. Therefore, this study trained machine models to predict bump shear strength using experimental data. By adopting orthogonal experimental design and full factorial designs, the 48 different reflow experiments were carried out and each was with a group of samples of 18 different design parameters. Then, based on the obtained data set from experimental data, the Linear Regression model, Gaussian Process Regression model, Decision Tree model, Artificial Neural Network model, and Random Forest model were established and optimized. The models could predict shear strength through the 3 inputs of design parameters and 6 inputs of reflow parameters. Finally, the evaluation showed that Random Forest is the best model on this issue, the MAPE of which is less than 3.6% and the R2 of which is greater than 0.95. Solder size, UBM size, temperature zone 2 temperature, and dwell time, are the four most concerned process parameters. The methodology and results of this study are helpful for the parameter setting in bumping production.

articleTitle: Effect of Different Solder Layer Damage on Junction Temperature of IGBT Module
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: During the operation of IGBT (Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistor), the power loss and junction temperature of the IGBT module vary with the usage conditions. This is mainly due to the mismatch in thermal expansion coefficients of different materials, which leads to thermal stress repeatedly acting on the solder layer. As a result, the solder layer may fail. Therefore, investigating solder layer damage is crucial for enhancing the reliability of IGBT modules. In this study, a three-dimensional finite element model of the IGBT module is established. The damage to the solder layer is investigated by simulating the reduction of solder layer area in different regions. Specifically, junction temperature <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(T_{\mathrm{j}})$</tex>, and maximum temperature <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(T_{\max})$</tex> of various IGBT modules under power cycle conditions are recorded. This is done when the solder layer of the chip and copper baseplate is separately reduced by 10%, and when the areas of both solder layers are simultaneously reduced by 10%. Finally, the effects of solder layer damage in different regions on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{\mathrm{j}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{\max}$</tex> are analyzed. The results obtained through finite element analysis indicate that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{\mathrm{j}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{\max}$</tex> reach their maximum values when the areas of both solder layers are decreased simultaneously. Conversely, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{\mathrm{j}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{\max}$</tex> are minimized when the area of the copper baseplate solder layer is reduced. Moreover, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{\mathrm{j}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{\max}$</tex> increase as the area of the solder layer decreases.

articleTitle: Mechanical Simulation and Characterization of Flexural Fracture of Stacked Die Memory Package
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Memory packages for mobile applications are getting thinner in body and higher in capacity, which brings up a challenge for package strength, especially for flexural strain of MCP (Multiple Chip Package). Finite Element Analysis (FEA) demonstrates that bending strain is highly dependent on package configuration and molding compound material. It has been observed that molding compound behaves with a distinct elastic-plastic property, while silicon dies fractures in a brittle mode, which is unable to withstand excessive strain [1]. In addition, based on simulation and experimental observations, three failure modes with the corresponding failure locations have been identified as molding compound cracking first, die cracking first, and interfacial delamination first. Simulation prediction capability of package break strain has been established based on the three failure modes. The simulation results agree well with testing measurements using strain gauge. It also is demonstrated that the dominant failure mode can change when package structure changes. Molding compound effect on package break strain also has been studied. It is shown that the selection of molding compound for high break strain should take failure modes into accounts, generally, high ductility molding compound is beneficial to obtain a better bending strain at the package surface.

articleTitle: The Impact of Mismatched Parasitic Inductances on Current Distribution in Parallel GaN HEMTs Under Transient-Overcurrent Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
