abstract: Current imbalances occur in parallel GaN HEMTs when there are inconsistencies in circuit parasitic parameters. This imbalance is exacerbated under transient overcurrent conditions, increasing the susceptibility of GaN HEMT devices to damage. To study the effect of mismatched parasitic inductances on the current distribution in parallel GaN HEMTs, this paper conducts a simulation analysis of three scenarios of mismatched parasitic inductances under transient overcurrent conditions. The results show that the three types of parasitic inductances affect the current imbalance in parallel GaN HEMT devices differently. The gate parasitic inductance has a minimal impact on current imbalance and can be disregarded. Mismatched drain and source inductances have a significant effect on transient current imbalance in parallel GaN HEMT devices. The drain parasitic inductance is only in the power loop, while the source inductance is in both the power and gate drive loops, affecting the gate voltage during device conduction. This causes a difference in the turn-on timing of the two parallel GaN HEMT devices, leading to greater transient current differences under transient overcurrent conditions.

articleTitle: The Application Verification Method of DC/DC Converter Used in Aviation Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As a key part of aviation system, the reliability of DC/DC converter affects the reliability of the whole system. Nowadays, most domestic aviation system in China still uses imported DC/DC converter, which greatly affects its independent and controllable ability. In order to realize the localization and substitution work, besides accelerating the development process of DC/DC converter, we need to establish a complete set of application verification methods so as to evaluate the usability of DC/DC converter in aviation system. Based on this, this paper proposes a complete set of application verification method (suitable for aviation system) through four aspects, which are production process factor investigation, function and performance verification, quality & reliability verification and application adaptability verification. Finally, the proposed application verification method is used to verify one domestic DC/DC converter and the result proves its effectiveness. This method provides a theoretical basis for supporting the quality assurance and application reliability evaluation of domestic products.

articleTitle: RGO/Ag Composite Ink for Ultrafine Conformal Electronics by Aerosol Jet Printing and Pulsed Light Sintering
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As Moore's law approaches its limit, traditional silicon-based planar circuits are evolving intelligence and flexibility, which imposing new demands on the manufacturing of precise circuits. Aerosol jet printing (AJP) can print conformal patterns on the three-dimensional curved surfaces, attributed to its higher working distance and greater solid content of ink. However, the traditional conductive ink for AJP such as silver nanoparticles (AgNPs), requires a post-processing temperature exceeding 150°C. Such a high temperature renders it incompatible with many kinds of flexible substrates such as PET, and restricts the application of AJP. In this paper, reduced graphene oxide (RGO) and AgNPs were composited to produce the excellent conductive ink for AJP, and conductive patterns were obtained using pulsed light sintering (PLS), the resistivity had decreased by 53.4% compared to the traditional ink. Furthermore, the influence of carrier gas flow, sheath gas flow, and nozzle shape on the pattern morphology were explored. The overspray of AJP was solved by process parameters optimization, the key role of focusing ratio was revealed and achieved the stable printing of 8 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> path finally. The influence of nozzle shape was explained, which achieved stable printing of conformal circuits on PI, PET, acrylic resin and glass. This study provides new ideas for the ink materials and post-processing methods of AJP and greatly expands its application prospects.

articleTitle: Thermo-mechanical fatigue life prediction of SiC power device based on finite element simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: This paper establishes a prediction method for the thermo-mechanical fatigue life of SiC power devices based on electro-thermal-mechanical coupling finite element simulation. The Anand constitutive model is used to describe the cyclic mechanical behavior of sintered silver at high temperature, and the Coffin-Manson equation is used to evaluate the thermo-mechanical fatigue damage of sintered silver. Firstly, a non-contact strain measurement and control technology is developed. Secondly, this paper conducted static shear tests on sintered silver interconnect specimens at different strain rates and temperatures, and found that the shear strength of the material decreases with decreasing shear strain rate and decreases with increasing temperature. Moreover, the material constants of the Anand constitutive model for sintered silver were identified based on the static shear stress-strain curve. Thirdly, cyclic shear tests were conducted on sintered silver interconnect specimens, and finite element simulation of the tests were also conducted. The effectiveness of the simulation was verified by comparing the experimental and simulated stress-strain results. Afterwards, the electro-thermal-mechanical coupling finite element simulation of a SiC power devices under power cycling was conducted, and the key dangerous parts of the device under power cycling were identified, then the stress-strain response history of the key dangerous parts was further extracted. Finally, the Coffin-Manson equation was used to calculate the thermo-mechanical fatigue damage and predict the failure life of SiC power devices. By comparing the experimental and predicted life results, it was found that the prediction error was within a factor of 2, indicating that the established method can provide satisfactory prediction results and provide key technical support for the fatigue life design of SiC power devices.

articleTitle: Carbon/Aluminum Composites with High Thermal Conductivity for Thermal Management Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this work, high performance graphite film/aluminum composites and diamond/aluminum composites were prepared for in-plane and isotropic high thermal conductivity requirements, respectively. The interfacial modification of graphite film/aluminum composite was carried out by matrix alloying. The ramifications of incorporating magnesium and silicon elements into the aluminum matrix were explored concerning the thermal conductivity and mechanical characteristics of the composite. The GF/AlO.8MgO.5Si composite achieved a remarkable in-plane thermal conductivity of 707 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{W}/(\mathrm{m}\cdot \mathrm{K})$</tex>. The interface modification of diamond/aluminum composite involved the surface coating of diamond particles with metal layers such as Ti and Cr, resulting in the composites achieving the highest thermal conductivities of 680 and 699 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{W}/(\mathrm{m}\cdot \mathrm{K})$</tex>, respectively. Both the graphite film/aluminum composites and diamond/aluminum composites exhibited outstanding three-dimensional and in-plane thermal conductivities, respectively, showcasing significant potential for utilization in electronic packaging thermal management materials. This investigation serves as a valuable reference for interface modification techniques of carbon/aluminum composites

articleTitle: Research and Introduction of the Process Flow of 3D-IC Thermo-Compression Intelligent Collective Bonding Equipment
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Three-dimensional integrated (3D IC) technologies have attracted substantial academic interest due to their enhanced performance and reduced interfacial dimensions. Conventional 3D packaging for chips of four layers must be stacked and bonded four and three times, respectively, bringing about the low reliability of bumps and productivity. Additionally, the decreasing size and spacing of solder bumps present challenges for defect detection. This paper proposes a collective intelligent bonding equipment for flip-chip 3D packaging. The equipment includes a bonding head system, downward vision, chip shift table, upward vision, bonding zone, in-situ monitoring system, and substrate movement platform. The bonding head system, downward vision, chip shift table, upward vision, and bonding zone complete the collective bonding. The defect detection is accomplished by the in-situ monitoring system. The chips need to be stacked four times, and the time of bonding is once. Meanwhile, during the bonding process, the defects can be monitored in real-time by the in situ monitoring system based on active infrared technology. Four layers in chips can be simultaneously bonded, and alignment accuracy is ±15μm@3sigma. The breakage, misalignment, and other defects can be monitored during the bonding progress. The introduction of this equipment will enhance productivity while ensuring bump reliability. Moreover, its successful development holds significant importance for the advancement and manufacturing of semiconductor packaging equipment domestically.

articleTitle: Research on linear active disturbance rejection synchronous control of gantry moving platform
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In the rapidly developing microelectronics packaging industry, the demand for high-speed and high-precision equipment is becoming more and more urgent. Gantry motion platform has been widely used in the field of chip packaging because of its excellent performance. However, the platform faces a key challenge, namely the mechanical coupling between linear motors, which affects positioning accuracy and synchronization performance. In order to solve this problem, the linear active disturbance rejection controller (LADRC) is introduced in this study, which is a simplified version of the active disturbance rejection controller and has received much attention because of its easy parameter adjustment. It is suggested to combine the cross-coupling synchronization algorithm with the control method based on LADRC to optimize the gantry platform servo system. In order to further improve the response speed of the platform, a feedforward controller (FFC) is also added in the study. In addition, the linear extended state observer (LESO) is used to monitor the dynamic changes and disturbances of the system, and the corresponding compensation is made, which improves the anti-interference ability and stability of the servo system. The simulation model of gantry movement platform control system is established, and the effectiveness of LADRC strategy is verified. The results show that LADRC combined with feedforward compensation is superior to PID control in terms of reaction speed, anti-interference ability and synchronous tracking, and can meet the requirements of high speed and high precision in microelectronics packaging industry.

articleTitle: A Study on Evaluation of the Copper Ion Electrochemical Migration Inner the Multilayer Flexible Circuit Board *
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The evaluation of electrochemical migration of electronic products is traditionally to investigate the impact of soldering auxiliary materials or process residues on the reliability of electronic assemblies<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1] [2]</sup>, and physically confirm whether dendrites exist on the surface of the circuit board by observing with a microscope. Due to the overlay structure and material characteristics, cracks or gaps may occur in the adhesive layer of the multi-layer flexible printed circuit (FPC) board or on the interface between the adhesive and PI due to moisture absorbing and aging, which can provide a space micro-environment of the electrolytic cell and the cation migration channel. Thus there is also a risk of electrochemical migration of copper ions in the inner layer between adjacent and insulated conductors on the same layer with the participation of bias voltage and moisture. In this paper, a test flow and method for evaluating the electrochemical migration of copper ions in the inner layer of FPC multilayer board are proposed, and the copper dendrites are presented through positioning and cross-section techniques, which confirms that the failure risk of electrochemical migration of copper ions in the inner layer of FPC multilayer board is present, which indicates that it is necessary to evaluate the electrochemical migration of the high reliable FPC boards before leaving the factory or using in batch, which can provide the scientific proof for material selection, process improvement and avoid failure risk.

articleTitle: In-Situ Observation on Liquid-Solid Electromigration Behavior of (111) nt-Cu/Sn/Cu Interconnects
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The microstructural evolution of (111) nt-Cu/Sn/polycrystalline Cu solder interconnects undergoing L-S EM was characterized in-situ and real-time by synchrotron radiation X-ray imaging. The growth rate of interfacial inter metallic compound (IMC) at the polycrystalline Cu anode (5.8μm/min) was 29 % higher than that at the (111) nt-Cu anode (4.5 μm/min). The consumption rate of nt-Cu UBM acting as the cathode was 2.0 μm/min, which was 20 % lower than that of Cu UBM (2.4 μm/min). Moreover, after L-S EM for 12 min, (111) nt-Cu remained original orientation feature accompanied by horizontal lamellar structures and no recrystallization or abnormal grain growth was observed, indicating the superior stability of nt-Cu UBM. The high electromigration resistance of (111) nt-Cu was attributed to the following factors. Firstly, the (111) exhibits the lowest surface energy among all crystal planes, resulting in lowest migration of atoms under the current stressing in (111) nt-Cu. Secondly, the twin boundary structure of (111) nt-Cu significantly impedes migration of Cu atoms. Additionally, tri-junction points formed by the intersection of twin boundaries with grain boundaries also hindered electromigration of Cu atoms.

articleTitle: Electrodeposition and Mechanical Properties of Gradient-Structured Cu with (220) Preferred Orientation
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The technology of electroplated copper is widely used in the manufacturing of interconnect materials for semiconductor devices. However, the conventionally electro-deposited copper foils are characterized by variable thermal stability, diminished tensile strength, and inadequate ductility, which are detrimental to their robustness and reliability in practical scenarios. To enhance the mechanical properties of electroplated copper, this paper employed a direct current electro-deposition method to fabricate copper foils with a (220) preferred orientation. Initially, samples were prepared at different current densities, and it was found that the current density significantly affects the microstructure and mechanical properties of the copper foil. Subsequently, by uniformly varying the current density, gradient-structured copper foils were prepared. The testing revealed that these samples exhibited enhanced tensile strength, reaching up to 411 MPa, while also achieving a commendable elongation rate of 6.8%. The findings of this paper are beneficial for improving the mechanical properties of electroplated copper foils and provide a reference for optimizing the mechanical properties of other materials.

articleTitle: Nano-Modification Fine-Pitch All-Copper Interconnect Technology Based on Spark Ablation
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: This study precisely targeted a key area and proposed an all-copper interconnect technology based on spark ablation assistance, utilizing a direct deposition bonding process without masks to achieve fine-pitch interconnection between substrates and chips. The paper designed a test structure with daisy chain protrusion size/spacing of 40/40μm, where the nano-copper-modified analog substrates and chips were thermally bonded to obtain an interconnection joint.

articleTitle: The Influence of Chip Aspect Ratios on the Crack Evolution in the Die-attach Layer Simulated Using the Fracture Phase Field Method
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: This paper presents a simulation of the crack evolution in the die-attach layer of a 3D IGBT TO package model (Si chip-Pb92.5Sn5Ag2.5 solder-Cu substrate) under thermal cycles, considering different chip aspect ratios (1, 1.5, and 2) but with the same chip area (6.25mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) using the fracture phase field method. The influence of three different chip aspect ratios on crack propagation was investigated and the interrelationship between the stress and the crack in the die-attach layer was discussed. The results reveal that the crack consistently initiates at the corner of the chip/solder interface and propagates to the center in an arc shape, irrespective of the chip aspect ratio. The crack initiation and propagation will be promoted by the increase of the chip diagonal asymmetry (i.e., the chip aspect ratio), and the crack propagation rates in the sections are faster when the section lengths are longer. Additionally, the crack propagation rates and maximum stress in the die-attach layer decrease in all three cases as the connecting area between the chip and the die-attach layer diminishes.

articleTitle: Manual bidirectional dislocation flip chip alignment technology based on image preprocessing
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: High-precision bonding of flip-mounted chips is the key technology of advanced packaging of integrated circuits, and the up-down camera technology currently used has problems such as large Z-height difference and camera motion errors. In this paper, the up-down camera is divided into two cameras, and a new high-precision flip chip alignment method is proposed by using virtual image preprocessing technology, which can greatly reduce the z-direction motion stroke of the placement head and reduce the accuracy error. Aiming at the mechanical structure characteristics of the short-range bidirectional dislocation flip bonding system, a device for evaluating the alignment accuracy is designed, which is called the characteristic parameter mask. Based on this error evaluation system, a chip alignment error model is established, an image virtual alignment method is proposed, and the alignment accuracy of the new method is analyzed. An optical alignment system was built to correct the sub-micron alignment mark for auto-tuning to verify the effectiveness and reliability of the preprocessing of images acquired by the bidirectional misalignment camera. Experimental results show that the proposed method can be applied in high-precision manual flip chip alignment, which can shorten the bonding distance to the sub-micron range, and the alignment accuracy can reach less than 0.7 microns, which meets the requirements of accuracy, adaptability and real-time alignment of wafer and chip flip bonding.

articleTitle: Analysis and Optimization of Equivalent Source Inductance for Balancing Dynamic Current of Multi-Chip SiC Power Modules Based on Cu-Clip Bonding
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In recent years, the surge in global energy demand coupled with a growing focus on environmental protection and the enhancement of energy efficiency has exposed the physical limitations of traditional silicon-based power semiconductor devices. The adoption of multi-parallel chip configurations has become essential to boost the module's current capacity. Nonetheless, layout asymmetry in multi-parallel SiC modules can lead to disparities in parasitic inductance among chips, further causing uneven current distribution. To address the challenge of uneven parallel current distribution, this study delves into the mechanisms of self-inductance and mutual inductance among current paths, deriving a dynamic current equilibrium equation based on magnetic coupling effects and equivalent inductance. This equation serves as a theoretical foundation for optimizing dynamic current distribution among parallel chips. Leveraging this equation, the structure of the Cu-clip is optimized to reduce current non-uniformity from 55% to 16%. Additionally, by employing finite element software to extract parasitic parameters from two different module layouts, a double-pulse simulation model incorporating each current segment's self-inductance and mutual inductance is developed. The discrepancy between simulation and actual measurements is a mere 2%, underscoring the model's accuracy.

articleTitle: Simulation Analysis of Tin Absorption Morphology of CCGA Solder Columns Based on Energy Minimization
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Tin absorption on the solder column represents a unique phenomenon occurring during the assembly process of CCGA devices. This phenomenon, where solder ascends along the column, diminishes the effective length of the CCGA solder column, thereby significantly impacting the reliability of the solder joints assembled. Two CCGA geometric models were established for 90Pb10Sn column and 80Pb20Sn column with spiral copper, respectively, considering the influence of factors such as solder column structure, solder volume, column wetting angle and pad wetting angle on the solder joint morphology. Based on the principle of energy minimization, the actual solder joint morphology under different factor levels was calculated, providing a reasonable process combination for actual production processes.

articleTitle: Multi-Chip 3D Integration Using Mechanical Interlock Bonding (MIB) Technology and Optimized TSV
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The fabrication of through silicon via (TSV) and multi-chip integration are the key technologies in 3D integration and Chiplets technology. Traditional Cu-Sn solid liquid inter-diffusion bonding (SLID) technology usually needs 20–30 minutes, and the total bonding time is directly proportional to the number of chips. In this study, TSV process is optimized to lower the sidewall scallop size and fulfill conformal Cu filling of TSV. Then chips used for three-chip integration are fabricated using the optimized semiconductor process. Finally, Cu-Sn Mechanical Interlock Bonding (MIB) technology is applied for three-chip bonding. The bonding process includes twice pre-bonding at room temperature and 200°C respectively, and one-time annealing at the temperature of 260 °C. The total pre-bonding time is about 10 minutes and annealing time is 20 minutes. Resistance test results and cross-section image show electrical and mechanical interconnections have been built. The MIB technology has short total bonding time, which show great advantage in the multi-chip integration.

articleTitle: Research on deep trench capacitor structure design and its effect on capacitance density and breakdown voltage
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Integrated capacitors can realize the functions of signal coupling, filtering, and noise reduction, offering higher integration, performance and reliability. In this work, the deep trench capacitors are fabricated on Si substrates by employing key process technologies including high-density deep Si etching, highly conductive metal electrode sputtering, and high-K dielectric atomic layer deposition. The effects of the shape, size and arrangement of deep trench capacitors on capacitance density and breakdown voltage are investigated. This work provides theoretical and experimental exploration for the structural design of high-density integrated capacitors and for further improving the capacitance density and reliability of integrated capacitors.

articleTitle: Molecular Dynamics Assisted Corrosion-Resistant Evaluation of Encapsulation Materials on Copper Used in Power Electronics Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Corrosion protection is one of the most important issues when copper is applied in power electronics packaging as bonding wire, die attachment, interconnection, and DBC substrate. Covering a layer of corrosion-resistant encapsulation material is a worthy consideration to protect copper. In this paper, the corrosion-resistant effects of two organic encapsulation materials, polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) and hexamethyldisiloxane (HMDSO), on the copper surface were performed by molecular dynamics simulations. Firstly, the Cu-coating bilayer models were constructed, and the binding performances of the encapsulation material/copper interface were evaluated through calculating their interaction energy, proving that the organic coatings can form interconnection on copper surface. Then, the diffusion processes of corrosive gas molecules (H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>S, H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O and O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) into the copper layer under different coating conditions were simulated, and both coatings exhibited good corrosion protection performances. The above results indicate that both PDMS and HMDSO have promising potential for copper corrosion protection in power electronics packaging. This may provide some guidance for corrosion protection of copper material used in power electronics packaging.

articleTitle: A Study on the cleaning efficiency of chip-let Micro-structure
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Recently the AI and big data application is booming and the chip-let technology is reaching another step height. The chip 3-D integration is more and more complex and the critical dimension of the chip interconnection is getting smaller and smaller. Taking the chip-let pre under-fill process as an example, when the bump pitch on the IC chip is less than 40 micron, the flux cleaning before the under filling process, neither traditional face up cleaning method nor the high pressure spray cleaning method works, in other words, the flux around the bump can not be washed away by the above two methods. Because when the bump height reaches less than 40µm, the liquid tension becomes a major effect for the liquid flow. The surface tension will blocking the cleaning liquid goes into the inner side of the chip, a lot of residual is found after cleaning, especially at chip center. A novel cleaning method is introduced in this paper, that is to clean the chip with the bump height under 40µm under a vacuum environment, for example the vacuum pressure is less than 150torr. The cleaning procedure is as follow: first the wafer or/chip-let is put into a vacuum chamber, then the chamber is pumping down to a pre-set vacuum, then the cleaning liquid in injected onto the wafer surface. Because the surface tension has a dramatic change in vacuum environment, there is almost no air in and between the chip-let structure, the cleaning liquid can go inside and out freely. The cleaning efficiency is increased a lot, and the test results showing that all the flux on both the top die and the bottom die is flushed away, there is no residual. The vacuum cleaning method is a novel cleaning technology, which is called as 3rd generation of the flux cleaning method. It will be used more and more as the chip-let technology moving forward.

articleTitle: A Self-Healing Substrate for Liquid-Metal Based Wearable Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Rapid development and evolution are needed in the era of information human wearable sensors for the data collection basis of the Internet of Things. To deal with the issues of poor flexibility in the existing sensing schemes, as well as the inability of devices to self-heal, we synthesized a silicone self-healing material—PP3, which could serve as a flexible substrate for wearable sensors. The fracture stress of this material is 0.34 MPa, with a record elongation at break of up to 290%; its self-healing efficiency can reach more than 80% after 12 h of repair at room temperature. We printed liquid metal based on gallium as the flexible circuit over the PP3 substrate by modifying the surface of the substrate. Here, based on the self-healing property of PP3 and the fluidity of liquid metal, we realize triboelectric sensors with overall self-healing capability able to monitor pressure in the range of 5–180 kPa; their maximum sensitivity reaches 0.9/kPa under low pressure, and good stability is maintained for the triboelectric sensors after 400-cycle tests.

articleTitle: Defect Assessment Methodology of Plastic Encapsulated Devices Based on Scanning Acoustic Microscope Inspection
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Scanning acoustic microscope (SAM) inspection is becoming an essential nondestructive procedure to defect delamination, voids, cracks in the plastic encapsulated devices. The C-scan SAM (C-SAM) is the most widely used mode since it can provide a planar defect view efficiently at specific depth level. However, the accuracy of the inspection largely depends on the operator's experience and may lead to opposite conclusions about the inspection results. This study focuses on two typical failure cases using C-SAM inspection, the justification of accuracy and defect verification were studied by microsectioning via optical microscope (OM), scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS). This work provides guidance for the reliability of plastic encapsulation based on scanning acoustic microscope inspection.

articleTitle: Effect of Chip Package Interaction on Cu/Ultralow-k Interconnect Fracture in Flip Chips
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The introduction of ultralow-k (ULK) materials aims to solve the back-end-of-line (BEOL) resistance and capacitance (RC) delay, but their higher porosity leads to lower fracture strength. During flip chip package integration, thermo-mechanical stresses often lead to cause chip package interaction (CPI) induced reliability problems such as interlayer dielectric (ILD) cracking or delamination. In this paper, the stress and fracture behavior of ULK in BEOL during reflow soldering of flip chip is investigated based on the sub-model approach. A 2D symmetric global model and a sub-model of Cu/ULK interconnect layer in BEOL are established using ABAQUS software. First, sub-model was inserted at different locations of the dangerous bump to identify potential high stress areas. Then, fixed length cracks were inserted in BEOL layers of the sub-model to simulate cracking. The J-integral was utilized to calculate the energy rate released (ERR) at the front edge of the 2D crack. The effect of Young's modulus of ULK on ERR was also investigated. The results show that the first principal stress peak of ULK occurs above the edge of the AL pad during reflow cooling; the ERR at the crack front edge gradually increases with the increasing number of layers; also, the ERR increases with the increasing of the modulus of ULK. This study contributes to an in-depth understanding of the stress and fracture of BEOL in flip-chips during reflow soldering.

articleTitle: Exploring the Aging Characteristics of Poly(Ionic Liquid)S-Based Thermal Interface Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Thermal interface materials (TIMs) are essential for managing heat in electronics. Silicone systems face challenges such as leakage of silane molecules, limited mechanical flexibility, poor filler compatibility and weak interfacial adhesion. In contrast, poly(ionic liquid)s (PILs) have emerged as promising alternatives due to their exceptional mechanical flexibility, thermal stability, robust interfacial adhesion across various substrates, filler compatibility, self-healing properties, and reprocessability. Yet, a critical gap exists in the thermo-physical and reliability characterization of PILs and their composites. This study introduces a novel TIM composed of PILs and Ga-based liquid metal (LM). The strong interaction between PILs and LM imparts the obtained composites a certain degree of flexibility and superior interface adhesion, making it suitable for use as TIMs. Specifically, the obtained TIM (80% mass fraction of LM) possesses a thermal conductivity of 1.2 W/(m.K) and exhibit an interfacial adhesion strength of 1.1 MPa with silicon, excellent thermal stability (>350°C). Furthermore, the aging characteristics of PIL and its composites with LM were also evaluated in terms of coverage change. This work established a critical foundation for the feasibility study of PIL as a TIM matrix.

articleTitle: A Novel Build-up Film for FCBGA Application
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the rapid development of network technology, as well as the continuous progress of AI technology and computing technology, the field of SoC design for high- performance computing chips has also ushered in revolutionary changes. Electronic packaging technology, a traditional field, combined with cutting-edge technologies such as nanotechnology, new material technology, and biotechnology, has given rise to an emerging discipline that injects new vitality into traditional integrated circuit packaging. In the design of IC packaging substrate, the composition of the laminated film insulation medium is particularly crucial, which is mainly composed of organic polymer materials and inorganic fillers carefully combined. This composite material exhibits excellent performance in high-frequency signal transmission while maintaining low dielectric constant (Dk) and low dielectric loss factor (Df), effectively achieving high fidelity and low latency communication effects. In order to meet the growing demand for high fidelity and low latency communication, higher standards have been proposed for the dielectric properties of polymer materials, driving continuous innovation in materials science. In the current technological context, Build-up film with extremely low dielectric constant (Dk) and dielectric loss factor (Df) has become a focus of industry attention. This article proposes an innovative low dielectric resin composite, which achieves excellent performance with a Dk/Df of only 2.80/0.004 through free radical polymerization technology combined with a high proportion of inorganic fillers. This resin composite not only has extremely low dielectric loss, but also maintains good thermal stability, with a thermal expansion coefficient of only 18ppm/° C, ensuring dimensional stability under temperature changes. In addition, the young's modulus of the resin composite is as high as 13Gpa, which enables multi-layer packaging to effectively prevent warping and cracking during the processing. At the same time, the peel strength of the resin composite reached 0.53N/mm, which ensures that the copper foil can firmly adhere to the packaging surface after copper plating treatment, preventing detachment, thereby improving the reliability and durability of the packaging.

articleTitle: Research on Longitudinal Ultrasonic Vibration Assisted Flip Chip Bonding Process
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The current flip-chip bonding technology still faces defects such as surface thermal burnout of chips due to excessively high process temperature and significant mechanical stress leading to solder joint fracture and chip damage. This paper proposes a longitudinal ultrasonic-assisted flip-chip bonding process. By introducing ultrasonic vibration of a certain frequency in the bonding direction, stress on the device during the bonding process is reduced, leading to lower bonding temperatures and improved bonding quality and reliability. However, unreasonable ultrasonic bonding parameters may result in the fracture at the bonding interface by hammering effect. Based on the longitudinal ultrasonic-assisted bonding experimental platform was constructed to conduct bonding experiments. Through orthogonal contrast experiments, it has been determined that longitudinal ultrasonic assisted technology could reduce the bonding temperature at most by 180°C and bonding duration by 3-5s with ultrasonic parameter of 26W/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> sound intensity and 4~4.66MPa prebonding pressure. This study provides valuable insights for optimizing flip-chip bonding processes.

articleTitle: The Effect of Voids in Electrically Conductive Adhesives on the Physical Properties
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The rapid development of microelectronics has led to increased integration of electronic components, making traditional soldering methods inadequate for sustainable industries. Electrically conductive adhesives offer environmental benefits and processing advantages. This study investigates the impact of voids on ECAs' volume resistivity, thermal conductivity, and Young's modulus using a novel combination of the Monte Carlo method and finite element analysis. Results show that voids significantly increase volume resistivity and decrease thermal conductivity and Young's modulus. The type of gas within the voids had minimal impact on thermal conductivity. Effective void management is crucial for optimizing ECA performance in electronic packaging.

articleTitle: The Mechanical Properties and Elastic Anisotropy of Ni3Sn4 Intermetallic Compound
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ni}3\text{Sn}4$</tex> phase, as an intermetallic compound, plays a crucial role in evaluating the reliability of soldered connections, serving as a vital indicator for assessing the robustness and longevity of these joints. In this study, the anisotropy of shear modulus, Young's modulus and bulk modulus of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ni}_{3}\mathrm{S}\mathrm{n}4$</tex> monoclinic crystals is studied by first principles calculation. The results show that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ni}_{3}\text{Sn}4$</tex> is an anisotropic material, and the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ni}_{3}\text{SN}_{4}$</tex>-based structure is stable. The three-dimensional modulus curves and yz, xz, xy projections of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ni}_{3}\text{Sn}4$</tex> intermetallic compounds are given. The shear modulus has the strongest anisotropy and the volume modulus the weakest. Finally, the thermodynamic performance parameters of the Debye temperature of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ni}_{3}\text{Sn}4$</tex> were calculated based on the obtained elastic parameters. The calculated Debye temperature closely aligns with reported values, thus validating the accuracy of our mechanical parameter calculations.

articleTitle: A Method for Assessing the Fatigue Life of Automotive Power Modules Based on Multi-Physics Field Coupling
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: This paper addresses the reliability issues of automotive-grade power modules, comparing failure modes and fatigue life calculation methods under thermal cycling, random vibration, and coupled thermal-vibration loads. Utilizing a crystal plasticity finite element model, a simplified model of the automotive-grade power module is constructed to analyze its failure modes under these three types of loads. Under thermal cycling loads, stress and strain distribution in the solder layers of automotive-grade power modules are analyzed, revealing stress concentration at the four corners on the surface of the solder layer. Under random vibration loads, the resonance points of the module are obtained by extracting the PSD response curves of the dangerous positions in the soldering layers of the automotive-grade power modules. Under coupled thermal-vibration loads, the random vibration issues of the module at normal, low, and high temperatures are considered, revealing the pattern of changes in the module's inherent frequency with temperature. The Coffin-Manson equation is used to calculate the life under thermal cycling conditions. The fatigue life of the IGBT module under random vibration conditions is calculated using the strain-based Manson-Coffin equation, and vibration damage values at different temperatures are analyzed according to Miner's linear cumulative fatigue damage theory. Finally, an incremental damage analysis method is applied to calculate and analyze the fatigue life under coupled thermal-vibration load conditions. The research results indicate that, compared to the natural modes of the structure at normal temperatures, the material's thermomechanical parameter changes and the thermal environment at high temperatures lower the structural mode frequency. Analyzing and comparing vibration fatigue life results at high and normal temperatures, it is evident that the module's fatigue life significantly decreases when thermal stress is considered.

articleTitle: Ultrafast Laser Additive-Subtractive Manufacturing of Planar Micro-Devices on Flexible Substrate
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Flexible electronics has shown great promise in smart electronics, offering wearable, bendable, and foldable solutions from consumer electronics to healthcare. Wherein, reliable interconnection between polymer-based flexible substrates and metal film electrodes is essential to accommodate the stress and deformation failure during service. In this work, ultrafast laser hybrid additive-subtractive manufacturing has been proposed for reliable and highly efficient fabrication of microscale circuits on flexible substrate. Patterned metal structures can firstly be achieved with low-frequency ultrafast laser during subtractive process. The bond between remained metal film and polymer is strengthened with subsequent high-frequency ultrafast laser irradiation. High size resolution of the subtractive manufacturing and robust bond after the additive manufacturing allow reliable manufacturing of various micro devices on flexible substrate using ultrafast laser irradiation with different parameters.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Asymmetric Structure of Packaging Substrate in IGBT Power Module
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistor (IGBT) modules, as common power semiconductor devices, are widely used in fields such as wind power generation, solar power generation, electric vehicles, rail transportation, and household appliances. The operating environments for these modules often involve high voltage and high power, which imposes higher demands on the reliability of IGBT modules. This paper establishes a simulation model for a three-phase inverter power module. Initially, the heat sink undergoes reverse pre-bending treatment. Simulation results show a reduction of 77% in residual stress during the welding process, but significant residual stress still remains. In response to this situation, a novel asymmetric structure of Direct Bonded Copper (DBC) substrate is proposed. The thickness of one copper layer of the DBC substrate is fixed, while that of the other layer varies to observe the evolution of maximum stress in the solder layer. It is observed that reducing the thickness of the lower copper layer in the DBC significantly improves the thermal stress issue in the solder layer during welding, at the same time, it will not affect the heat conduction performance of the power module during operation.

articleTitle: Influence of Ball Milling Process on the Micro-Morphology and Magnetic Properties of M-Type Hexagonal Ferrites
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Conventional yttrium iron garnet-based circulators require the use of an external magnet to provide the biasing field. Hexagonal ferrites with uniaxial anisotropy can avoid the use of external magnets to achieve the self-biasing function, thereby significantly reducing the size, weight, and cost of the circulator. In order to realize the self-biasing function, modulating the hexagonal ferrite so that it has a high remanent magnetization ratio <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol{M}_{\mathbf{r}}/\boldsymbol{M}_{\mathbf{s}})$</tex>, controllable magnetization strength <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol{M}_{\mathbf{s}})$</tex> and coercivity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{H}_{\mathbf{c}})$</tex> is an urgent problem. In this work, Ba<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.9</inf>La<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.1</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11.9</inf>Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.1</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19</inf> was prepared by solid-phase method, and the changes of its magnetic properties at different ball milling rates were firstly explored. On the basis of the determined ball milling rate, the factor of ball milling time was continued to be added. The magnetic properties of Ba<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.9</inf>La<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.1</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11.9</inf>Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.1</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19</inf> were modulated by the combination of ball milling rate and time process, and its <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{M}_{\mathbf{r}}/\boldsymbol{M}_{\mathbf{s}}$</tex> could be increased from the initial 0.804 to 0.885. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{H}_{\mathbf{c}}$</tex> fluctuated between 2.07-2.94 KOe, and the corresponding <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{M}_{\mathbf{s}}$</tex> increased from 58.31 emu/g to 66.83 emu/g. The best overall performance was achieved at ball milling time and rate of 18 h and 33 Hz, respectively: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{M}_{\mathbf{s}}=\mathbf{62.46}\ \mathbf{emu} /\mathbf{g}, \mathbf{H}_{\mathbf{c}}=\mathbf{2.07}$</tex> KOe, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{M}_{\mathbf{r}}/\boldsymbol{M}_{\mathbf{s}}=\mathbf{0.885}$</tex>. This provides an important reference for the preparation of hexagonal ferrites with high performance.

articleTitle: AI-Based Finite-Element Simulation Automation Workflow Applied to Automotive Electronics Field
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Electronic component is one of the key design elements considered during the development of automotive ECU (Electronic Control Unit). As the current state-of-the-art method, FEM (Finite-Element Method) simulation is widely used for thermal design optimization and solder joint reliability assessment of electronics at early stage of ECU development. To address the challenges of modeling fidelity and efficiency, the AI (Artificial Intelligence) integrated automated simulation workflow platform is developed. Leveraging standard and Bosch in-house developed Python libraries called “pyact”, an Ansys-based automation toolset has been developed which accelerates the simulation workflow. With the assistance of AI methodologies, more precise electronic component models could be expected during calibration process. This paper presents 3 different industrial practices and examples focusing on the board level thermal management and solder joint reliability assessment. The first industrial example presents the standardization and automatization of the reliability simulation workflow of chip-resistor components. Utilizing Ansys ACT (Application Customization Toolkit), basic APIs (Application Programming Interface) of ACT are encapsulated into the Python library as pyact, enabling a fully automated simulation workflow to predicted solder joint lifetime. To further realize the fast assessment of reliability and component virtual release, an AI metamodel is derived from automated simulation-based DoE (Design of Experiments). For pursuit of accuracy for simulation models, the second industrial example presents the combination of Bayesian Optimization with BGA (Ball Grid Array) warpage calibration process to outperform the traditional manual methods. The third industrial example outlines another application of Bayesian optimization into the Zth (Transient Thermal Impedance) calibration process for component thermal models. Utilizing the multi-objective optimization algorithm, the Zth curves from different sources & thermal paths can be fitted with high-quality by the machine. In conclusion, the integration of AI with simulation automation significantly benefits thermal management and solder joint reliability evaluations in ECU development.

articleTitle: Electromigration Reliability of SnAgCu Solder Joints in WLCSP
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: This study focuses on the electromigration behavior and the mean-time-to-failure (MTTF) analysis of SnAgCu solder joints in the temperature range of 130 to 160°C with current density of 0.96-1.59×l04 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The Sn4.0Ag0.5Cu (SAC405) solder bumps are in a WLCSP assembly with Ti/Cu UBM on the chip side and Cu pad on the substrate side. The effective activation energy and exponent associated with current density of SAC405 solder joint are obtained, which is 0.89 eV and 2.23. The electromigration simulation of a three-dimension dual bumps model was employed to investigate atom density and void formation in the solder joints. The goal was to establish a relationship with the experimental electromigration results and to devise a technique for predicting the lifespan of electromigration. Threshold failure atom density 0.966 was gained. The test structures may experience both electromigration and thermomigration under severe condition. The most vulnerable area is the junction between RDL and UBM on the solder ball where the electron flows downwards. The direction of thermomigration in relation to electromigration plays a vital role in determining the failure rate and final morphology of the solder joints.

articleTitle: Wafer-Level Packaging Technology Of W-Band Antennas Based On Through Glass
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Millimeter wave antennas have the advantages of broadband, high transmission rates, low latency and small size, and are widely used in radar systems, communication networks, intelligent mobile devices, and the Internet of Things. Compared to traditional dielectric substrate, glass has the characteristics of good insulation, uniform and stable high-frequency performance, low loss and low cost, and is a good substrate for manufacturing millimeter wave antennas. The glass-based wafer-level packaging (WLP) technology adopts a micro-nano manufacturing process which allows for millimeter-level channel spacing and micron-level wiring size. Additionally, it enables three-dimensional interconnection with the backend through vertical vias. As a result, it is highly suitable for manufacturing miniaturized antennas in the W-band. In this paper, a new W-band wafer-level integrated packaging antenna and a transmission structure based on Through Glass Via (TGV) are designed and manufactured. The focus is on two parts of the manufacturing process. First, the paper explores the application of laser-induced and wet etching technology of TGV, as well as the metal lithography redistribution technology on the glass wafer. These technologies enable the vertical interconnection of millimeter wave signals and the horizontal interconnection of distribution lines. Second, the paper discusses the adoption of the copper-tin bonding process between multilayer glass wafers to achieve system-level packaging of the antenna. A miniaturized test fixture for antennas was designed, and the performance test of the micro-nano antenna was completed. The antenna consists of five layers of glass wafers with a thickness of 230 µm or 100 µm. The overall package size of the antenna is 10×9×l mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, with a single radiator measuring only 0.55×0.55 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, In the frequency range of 78 GHz to 88 GHz, the antenna reflection coefficient is below -10, and the insertion loss of the transmission line is less than 3.1dB, which meets the design requirements.

articleTitle: Research on the Cleaning Machine Suitable for the in-Package Board-Level Stacking Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The SiP board-level stacked package achieved through BGA technology is crucial to improving integration. For the cleaning of flux after RF SiP board-level stacking, the research designs a multifunctional centrifugal spray cleaner. It introduces its whole structure, workflow, and central working units. The cleaning application tests show that the cleaning result meets the GJB5807-2006 Requirements for ionic residues on the surface of third-grade high-reliability electronic products of less than 1.56ug (NaCl)/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. This equipment, featuring diversified cleaning methods, small size, low water consumption, and a high degree of automation, can effectively improve flux cleaning for complex electronic products after stacking.

articleTitle: Failure Analysis Based on Vehicle-Grade Transient Voltage Suppression Diodes
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Electrostatic discharge and electrical overstress are commonly encountered challenges in the utilization of electronic components. These occurrences are particularly detrimental in the manufacturing, packaging, testing, and operational settings of integrated circuits. Within the automotive sector, the vehicle-grade transient voltage suppressor (TVS) stands as a pivotal protective measure against electrostatic discharge and electrical overstress, safeguarding electronic devices across diverse automobile modules. The comprehensive understanding and meticulous analysis of the failure mechanisms of the vehicle-grade TVS are of utmost importance for ensuring its reliable performance in this domain. Therefore, in accordance with established failure analysis and detection procedures, a thorough investigation was conducted into the failure of vehicle-grade TVS devices during the temperature cycle test. Microscopic inspections revealed the presence of cracks in the device's shell, while subsequent experiments further exposed delamination and solder leakage issues. Upon further examination, including sampling, grinding, and polishing of the device, it was discovered that internal chip cracking had occurred due to the popcorn effect. Utilizing advanced techniques such as electron microscope scanning and energy spectrum analysis, it was confirmed that dendrites formed within the solder and adhered to the chip surface, a phenomenon attributed to electromigration. Internal delamination, chip fragmentation, and dendrite formation were identified as the primary factors contributing to the device's failure. This comprehensive study contributes to system-level failure analysis and detection efforts for vehicle-grade TVS devices. It also provides valuable insights for considerations related to environmental usage, the selection of plastic sealing materials, and the assessment of reliability.

articleTitle: Low Loss Assembly of Micro Shell Resonators
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The micro shell resonator is the core sensing component of the high precision micro shell resonator gyroscope. High quality factor of micro shell resonator represents low loss, which is essential to the performance of the gyroscope. In this paper, a model of the micro shell resonator is built in the finite element software and the loss of the resonator is studied by simulation. The shell resonators are assembled on the substrates and the quality factors of the resonators were tested by Laser Doppler Vibrometer with different adhesives and substrates. The simulation results indicate that the size and property of adhesive affect the Q value of the resonator. In the LDV test, the Q value of the second-order mode of the micro shell resonator assembled by adhesive SPI 05001-AB have an increase of 522.60% compared with the adhesive Crystalbond 590. With two different substrates, the change of Q value of the third-order reached two orders of magnitude. Hence, a suitable adhesive and substrate configuration can reduce the loss of micro shell resonator and the results can be applied to the assembly process of resonator and planar electrode to achieve higher performance gyroscope.

articleTitle: The Effect of EMC Material Properties on the Large-Area Silver Sintering Process in Power Module
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the development of transfer-molded power module devices in electric vehicle field, a large area silver sintering process has become one of the feasible solutions for connecting substrate to heat sink, due to the high thermal conductivity and reliability it can offer. However, silver sintering needs to be carried out under specific temperature and pressure conditions. During the sintering process, thermal stress can occur inside the power module due to the thermal mismatch between the epoxy molding compound (EMC) and the Si3N4 ceramic substrate, resulting in module warpage with a crying or smiling face. Severe warpage often leads to a high failure rate in large-area silver sintering. However, this problem can be mitigated by selecting an appropriate EMC material. Additionally, the mechanical behavior of EMC materials is closely related to temperature, which can also affect the failure rate of the silver sintering process. Although the effect of EMC material on the silver sintering process is very significant, there are few relevant studies on it. In this paper, the failure mechanism of the module in the sintering process is analyzed by the finite element simulation method (FEM). At the same time, simulation model is used to explore the effects of EMC's material parameters such as thermal expansion coefficient (CTE), glass transition temperature (Tg), and modulus on power module warpage and ceramic substrate stress. The simulation results offer crucial guidance for the selection of EMC and the setting of process parameters in silver sintering.

articleTitle: A Novel O2/N2 Plasma Photoresist Ashing Process with High Stripping Rate and Uniformity under Radio Frequency Bias Voltage
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The development of wafer-level packaging (WLP) technique relies heavily on the preparation of large-area redistribution layers (RDL). One crucial step in RDL fabrication is photoresist stripping, as the quality of this process affects greatly the integrity of RDL lines and the reliability of the packaging. In this study, the effects of two different plasma sources, radio-frequency (RF) inductively coupled plasma (ICP) and microwave (MW) remote plasma, on the removal of photoresist over large areas on eight-inch wafers were systematically investigated. Using the Taguchi method, the quality response characteristics of various equipment parameters (frequency, temperature, power, gas flow rate and gas composition) on the stripping rate and stripping uniformity were evaluated. Additionally, a single-factor level analysis of each equipment parameter was conducted to delve deeper into the influential trends of each factor on the ashing process. The results indicate that the major factors influencing the stripping rate are ionization frequency and temperature, whereas ionization frequency and O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> concentration in mixed O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> plasma predominantly affect the stripping uniformity. The stripping rate significantly increases with raising temperature and power. Additionally, the presence of a small amount of N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> in the O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> plasma brings about increase in the stripping rate, although pure oxygen plasma is preferable for achieving lower uniformity. By setting RF bias in the MW remote plasma, the stripping rate is increased from below 100 Å/min to over 250 Å/min, while maintaining the uniformity below 20%.

articleTitle: High Thermal Conductive Liquid Metal/Hydroxy Silicone Oil Thermal Grease with Anti-Leakage
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the development of microelectronic devices, miniaturization and high-power density pose new challenges to chip thermal management, effective thermal management during chip packaging is paramount. Thermal grease, as a type of thermal interface material, finds widespread application in the field of electronic packaging. However, there still exist challenges regarding how to further enhance the thermal conductivity of thermal grease and address issues such as filler leakage. Compared to other rigid fillers, eutectic gallium-indium alloy offers unique advantages as a filler in manufacturing high-performance thermal interface materials, meeting the required thermal and mechanical behaviors. Here, we present a thermal grease prepared by blending hydroxy silicone oil with eutectic gallium-indium alloy, characterized by high thermal conductivity and non-corrosiveness. Experimental investigations into the thermal properties and rheological behavior of this thermal grease, along with analyses of its surface and internal structure, elucidate its mechanisms. It is evident that liquid metal/polymer thermal grease holds vast potential in the realm of chip packaging.

articleTitle: Properties of activated formic acid using for low- temperature all-copper interconnect assisted with nanoparticles paste
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Currently, electronic packaging technology is towards miniaturisation and high interconnect density to meet the demands for high performance, high reliability and low cost electronic devices. As the pitch and size of the microbumps decreases, it becomes significantly more difficult to establish reliable interconnections on the chip due to the increased risk of bridging. To overcome the inherent limitations of solder-based interconnects and to meet the need for higher current densities, all-copper interconnects with high conductivity are a promising approach. However, the impact of Cu pillar surface flatness on the bonding interface remains a bottleneck in all-copper interconnect technology. In this paper, a Cu nanoparticle paste assisted sintering method in an activated formic acid atmosphere was presented to improve the low- temperature bonding performance for all-copper interconnects. The hydrogen radicals generated by the activated formic acid atmosphere effectively protect the Cu nanoparticles from oxidation resulting in the formation of a dense sintered layer even at 250°C for 10 min. And a shear strength of 32 MPa was obtained for 30 min. Moreover, the resistance and specific contact resistance of the bare Cu pillar was 2 mΩ and 10 Ω. µm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, respectively. In addition, the sintering mechanism assisted with Cu nanoparticles was explained. This method can effectively reduce the requirements of Cu pillar surface electroplating process during wafer fabrication, and has potential applications in all-copper interconnect technology.

articleTitle: Quantitative Structural Hierarchy of Phase Separation Dynamics in Miniaturized Solder Joints
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The microstructural hierarchy descriptor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mu \text{SHD})$</tex> is used to investigate the effects of geometry and shear stress on the kinetics of phase separation in miniaturized solder joints. All joints are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${3.5}\ {\mu} \mathrm{m}$</tex> in height and subjected to aging at 125 °C. From a scale perspective, the results reveal a negative linear correlation between the logarithm of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \text{SHD}$</tex> value <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\log_{10}S_{J}^{1})$</tex> and the logarithm of aging time <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$({\log}_{10}t)$</tex> on smaller scales <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${J} \leq {4}$</tex>, but turns out to be positive on a larger scale <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${J}={6}$</tex>. Compared to an hourglass joint, smaller-scale features decrease faster, but larger-scale features increase slower in a barrel joint. Shear stress has been found to decrease kinetics on smaller scales <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J\leq 4$</tex>, but increase it on a larger scale <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J=6$</tex>. For barrel joints, the top region exhibits faster kinetics on smaller scales <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J \leq 4$</tex> compared to other regions, while for hourglass joints, the top region exhibits slower kinetics. Shear stress leads to a horizontal and a vertical orientation in the top region of the barrel and hourglass joints, respectively.

articleTitle: Die Shift on Chip First Panel Level Fan-Out Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Die shift is one of the most critical issues facing by the chip first and face down fan-out process. Unlike factors such as CTE mismatch that induce theoretically predicable die shift, unexpected offset usually happens which makes chip position compensation a big challenge. This paper analysis related factors contributing to die shift in the sight of die bonder condition, compound property such as shrinkage, HRT (Heat Release Tape), and mold flow. It also presents experimental data on how the factor affect die shift and come to the summary that both smaller positive mold compound shrinkage and rougher chip surface will do help on the chip position. Improving the die shift issue involves aspects including enhancing material properties encompassing thermal and chemical stability, equipment precision and process/product design. Furthermore, process innovation is suggested to mitigate the impact of material inherent characteristics on die shift.

articleTitle: Comparison of Two Cell Topologies for 1.2kV 4H-SiC MOSFETs with Different JFET Width
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Silicon carbide (SiC) power MOSFETs are increasingly favored over silicon-based devices due to superior material characteristics, including high breakdown electric fields, enhanced thermal conductivity, and elevated saturated electron mobility. To optimize performance by minimizing ON-state and switching losses, it is crucial to reduce ON-resistance (R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf>), reverse transfer capacitance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{C}_{\text{rss}})$</tex>, and gate-to-drain charge <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{g}\mathrm{d}})$</tex>. Additionally, lower high-frequency figures of merit (HF-FOM) contribute to decreased overall power loss in high-frequency settings. This study explores the effects of cell topology and JFET width on the electrical characteristics of 1.2kV SiC MOSFETs, designed and fabricated with both linear and hexagonal cell topologies under identical design and process conditions. The results indicate that while hexagonal cells present a lower specific ON-resistance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text { (Ron,sp }$</tex> ) compared to linear cells, they also exhibits a reduced breakdown voltage and an increased reverse transfer capacitance, which ultimately results in a lower figure-of-merit (FOM) and HF-FOM. Notably, as JFET width increases, R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf>,sp decreases, whereas <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{r}\mathrm{s}\mathrm{s}}$</tex> increases, with more significant variations observed in hexagonal topologies for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{c}_{\mathrm{r}\mathrm{s}\mathrm{s}}$</tex>. Depending on the requirements of the application scenario, a judicious selection of cell topology and JFET width is necessary to achieve a balance between ON-state loss and switching loss.

articleTitle: Effect of Ceramic Array Package Pinout Types on Solder Joints Thermal Reliability
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: For the board-level assembly process of ceramic components, the thermal deformation mismatch between the PCB and the ceramic shell/substrate due to the different thermal expansion coefficients often leads to thermal fatigue failure of the interconnect solder joints in the process of frequent on/off or alternating between cold and hot with the surrounding environment. At present, the pinout types of ceramic array packages include eutectic solder balls, Sn10Pb90 solder balls, copper wrapped solder column, and micro-coil spring, etc. By examining the material properties of the pinout structure, the thermal reliability of the interconnect structure of each package was studied by combining finite element analysis and temperature cycling acceleration test. Firstly, the methods of the finite element simulation were introduced. In view of the morphological structure of the pinout and solder joints, the board level assembly finite element models of different pinout types were established. Then, the temperature alternating load was applied to the ceramic grid array assembly, and the thermal deformation response of the solder joints was performed to find the weak links of the solder joints array. The thermal fatigue life of the interconnect solder joints for different pinout types were then evaluated.

articleTitle: Optimization of Pin Fin Structure for Uniform Temperature Distribution in Multi-Chip Parallel-Connected Power Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In electronic devices, power modules are usually used to control and convert electrical energy, and are widely used in various fields, such as communications, industrial control, automotive electronics, etc. With the increase of power density and performance requirements of electronic equipment, power modules will generate a lot of heat at high power operation. If the heat generated by these power modules cannot be effectively dissipated, the device temperature will rise, affecting the performance and service life of electronic components. In serious cases, may cause device performance degradation, frequent failures or even damage. Therefore, optimizing the heat dissipation design of the power module, improving the heat dissipation efficiency and reducing the temperature is of great significance for improving the stability and extending the service life of the equipment. In this paper, the finite element analysis of ANASYS ICEPAK. was carried out to establish the fluidity-heat coupling analysis model of different radiator structures and the chip junction temperature distribution under different PIN spacing and shape was simulated. The results show that the heat dissipation performance of hexagonal PIN is better than that of cylindrical PIN structure. PIN spacing 1.7 minimum pressure drop, minimum junction temperature difference between chips, the best heat dissipation effect. Finally, the optimal heat sink structure design is found, and the heat dissipation performance of the module is optimized.

articleTitle: Comparative Study on the Bonding Property of Laser and Reflow Soldered Sn-37Pb/Ni-P Micro-Joints after Isothermal Aging and Multiple Reflow
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Laser soldering is becoming increasingly popular in microbumps joint due to its noncontact and confined heat, rapid joining time, and straightforward mechanization. This study examines the internal structure and fracture features of Sn-37Pb/Ni-P microbumps fabricated by laser soldering and reflow soldering techniques. This study examines the impact of isothermal ageing and periodic reflowing on the microbumps. The experimental results showed that laser soldering of microbumps produced a fine, loose (Cu, Ni)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> intermetallic compound (IMC), whereas reflow soldering of microbumps resulted in the creation of a small plane-like, lumpy (Cu, Ni)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> IMC. The (Cu, Ni)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> particles underwent isothermal ageing at a temperature of 150 °C, resulting in a transformation of their structure into a scallop shape with a notable aspect ratio. These particles were soldered using a laser in microbumps. In contrast, in microbumps that were soldered using reflow soldering, the particles developed into irregular lumps. The thickness of the IMC in microbumps increased in a parabolic manner as the ageing time increased. Nevertheless, the IMC thickness in laser-soldered microbumps was consistently significantly smaller than that in reflow-soldered microbumps.
