The breaking point of both connected procedures had a significant decline after 100 hours of ageing, and subsequently maintained a similar level as the ageing time increased to 400 hours. Throughout the process involving several reflows, the morphology of (Cu, Ni)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> particles in both laser soldered and reflow soldered microbumps grow into large irregular lumps, and the IMC thick of laser soldered microbumps grows sharply after one time reflowing, then grow over time within both scenarios. The breaking strength of both soldered procedures for microbumps reduced slightly as the reflowing times increased. Hence, laser soldering proves to be efficient in lowering the thickness of IMCs and maintaining the structural strength of microbumps even after undergoing isothermal ageing and numerous reflow operations, comparable to traditional reflow soldering.

articleTitle: Research on Reliability Risk-Based Microstructure Evaluation Method for Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The reliability of design, process, inner microstructure and material used in integrated circuit is the key to determining the inherent reliability level of the device itself. With the continuous updating and iteration of integrated circuit manufacturing processes, the size of process microstructure is getting smaller and the integration degree is getting higher. As a result, issues related to circuit design layout, manufacturing process, packaging process, and material reliability have gradually become key influencing factors affecting the reliability level of integrated circuits themselves. How to conduct quality inspection and reliability evaluation on newly developed integrated circuits, effectively identify defects and weak links that affect device quality and application reliability, and fully verify the true reliability level of devices, has very important practical significance. This study proposes a reliability risk based integrated circuit microstructure evaluation method, which analyzes the key elements that affect device reliability in advance and establishes corresponding testing and evaluation items. Through physical testing and verification of the device, the real reliability risks of the device can be identified and provide a basis for device design, process improvement, selection, and application design. This method aims to provide integrated circuit users with an effective means of quality inspection and reliability evaluation to ensure the inherent reliability of microelectronic devices.

articleTitle: Thermo-Mechanical Reliability of Micro-joints in a RF Packaging with Through Glass Via (TGV) Interposer
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Through-glass via (TGV) interposer is a good candidate for the integration of radio frequency (RF) device owing to its excellent electrical properties of low signal crosstalk and low insulation loss. However, micro-joints in packaging are at the risk of fatigue under thermal loadings because of high thermal stresses induced by thermal mismatch. In this study, the thermo-mechanical reliability of copper micro-bumps and solder joints in a typical RF package with TGV interposer was evaluated by finite element method (FEM) based on Coffin-Manson and Darveaux fatigue model, respectively. To improve the accuracy, the elastoplastic model was employed for copper micro-bumps and Anand viscoplastic model for SAC305 solder. The results indicated that SAC305 solder joints are more susceptible to fatigue than copper micro-bumps under thermal cyclic loading. According to a further single-factor analysis, the suggestions for a longer fatigue life of micro-joints were presented, including an appropriate increase in the coefficient of thermal expansion and a reduction in the thickness of the TGV interposer.

articleTitle: Research on online junction temperature monitoring method for SiC MOSFETs based on high current conduction voltage drop method
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As a typical representative of third-generation semiconductor power devices, silicon carbide (SiC) devices have gradually become the core components of power electronic systems. The reliability of SiC devices has become one of the research hotspots under high temperature and high pressure working conditions. Junction temperature measurement is a key focus of research on the thermal reliability of power semiconductor devices. Therefore, online monitoring of the junction temperature of SiC metal oxide semiconductor field effect transistors (MOSFETs) is of great significance and value. Online monitoring is a method for extracting thermal electrical parameters. This method utilizes the device itself as a temperature sensing component, mapping chip temperature information to external electrical variables. It not only obtains the average junction temperature of the device, but also has advantages such as low cost, fast response, and easy online monitoring. This article proposes an online junction temperature detection method based on the high current conduction voltage drop method, which involves taking the average junction temperature of the device but also offers advantages such as low cost, fast response, and ease of online monitoring. Firstly, the device is calibrated to form a three-dimensional mapping relationship between voltage drop, leakage source current, and junction temperature. Then, a voltage sampling circuit and a current sampling circuit are designed and implemented. Finally, the opened device is subjected to infrared thermal imaging to obtain the device junction temperature and verify the accuracy of the online junction temperature.

articleTitle: Organic Reductor Assisted Cu-Cu Low Temperature Bonding in Air Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Three-dimensional packaging will chip in three-dimensional space for stacking interconnections, interconnection technology is particularly important, and Cu-Cu direct interconnect technology has a small pitch, high temperature resistance, high reliability and so on, in the memory device, image sensing and so on has been widely used. Copper-copper (Cu-Cu) direct bonding belongs to the metal-metal bonding, under certain bonding process conditions (high temperature, vacuum or reducing atmosphere, pressure and other factors), Cu atoms diffuse with each other to realize interconnection bonding, these conditions limit the wide application of Cu-Cu direct bonding technology. In this paper, Cu nanowires were prepared in alkaline solution using electrochemical technique, and ethylene glycol and propylene glycol were used as solvents to add different amounts of polyvinylpyrrolidone, which was configured as an organic protectant to protect the Cu nanowires, and the hot-pressing bonding experiments were carried out at 250 °C. The resistance test and shear strength test of the obtained joints revealed that the strength of the bonded joints in air environment could be improved when the content of polyvinylpyrrolidone (pvp) reached a certain amount, and the effect was better than that of ethylene glycol when glycerol was used as a solvent. Finally, the phenomenon was explained in terms of volatility and reducibility. The results of the study show that copper nanowire surfaces protected by the organics of propylene triol combined with polyvinylpyrrolidone can realize high-strength bonding in a low-temperature air environment.

articleTitle: Enhancing Light Extraction Efficiency and Luminance for Perovskite Light-Emitting Diodes Using Nanoporous Array Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Perovskite light-emitting diode (PeLED) have risen as potential contenders for advanced optoelectronic devices. As the critical performance metric for PeLED, the external quantum efficiency (EQE) is a pivotal parameter for assessing the proficiency of optoelectronic devices in the transformation of electrical energy into photovoltaic energy, ascertained through the internal quantum efficiency (IQE) and the efficiency of light extraction efficiency (LEE). Despite significant progress in EQE, given by IQE approaching unity, LEE remains disappointing and hinders the realization of efficient PeLEDs. In this study, we introduce a novel quantum dots (QDs) nano-porous substrate (NPS) that ameliorates the total internal reflection phenomenon in PeLED. Compared to traditional PeLED, the QD-NPS PeLED enhances the LEE by 2.8 times and achieves a 3.0-fold increase in the maximum luminance, promising widespread applications in display technology, and medical imaging, among other fields.

articleTitle: Research on the Mechanism of Assembly Stress on Solder Joint Fatigue Life of Large Size FCBGA Package
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Heatsinks are indispensable in the field of electronic package, and the thermal dissipation requirements of component are increasing year by year. To enhance the thermal efficiency, it is general required that heatsinks fix the component with higher compressive force. High pressure implies the potential to affect the reliability of ball grid array (BGA) solder joints. This paper focuses on a large size flip chip ball grid array (FCBGA) package and verifies the feasibility of predicting the fatigue life of solder joints under compressive load and temperature cycle conditions through experiments and numerical methods. It also investigates the impact of typical and new types of heatsinks on the temperature cycle reliability of solder joints. In addition to this, corresponding analyses have been conducted on factors such as the material of the compression fixture and the pretension force of assembly.

articleTitle: A FEM-BEM Coupling Scheme for Elastic Dynamics Problems in Electronic Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In the field of electronic packaging structure reliability research, the Finite Element Method (FEM) is recognized as an effective and reliable approach for numerical simulation. Concurrently, the Boundary Element Method (BEM) is noted for its unique advantage of requiring discretization only at the boundary, which significantly reduces the degrees of freedom and potentially enhances the accuracy of analyses. This characteristic makes BEM particularly useful for analyzing multiscale structures in electronic packaging. Nevertheless, both methods have their limitations: FEM necessitates elements within the internal domain, making it computationally intensive, while BEM is most effective with linear problems and can be less versatile with nonlinear issues. Considering these factors, this paper introduces a FEM-BEM coupling algorithm designed to address the transient elastic dynamic response problem in electronic packaging structures. This approach is designed to leverage the strengths and mitigate the limitations of both the FEM and BEM. During the numerical simulation, the model is initially segmented into FE and BE domains. The FE domain is solved using ABAQUS, while the BE domain is analyzed through a self-written boundary element program. The BE domain functions as a specialized type of finite element, where its equivalent stiffness and load are determined by invoking the boundary element program via the User-Defined Element subroutine (UEL). These results are then integrated into the finite element system. Numerical examples demonstrate that the proposed FEM-BEM coupling method is both effective and feasible for analyzing the dynamic response of electronic packaging structures.

articleTitle: Effect of Porosity in Copper Nano-Sintering on the Reliability of Power Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the in-depth research on third-generation semiconductors, many issues related to power devices have begun to emerge, with the foremost being the problem of package interconnection reliability. The chip bonding layer serves as a key component in ensuring the normal operation of power devices, as it facilitates the physical and electrical interconnection between the chip and the substrate. As a result, there has been significant research in the field of interconnection. Currently, nano-metal particles are considered an ideal choice. This is because they possess the ability to fuse between particles at lower temperatures, forming characteristics similar to bulk metals, thereby exhibiting high performance and good reliability. As a novel chip bonding method, nano-silver particles have attracted widespread attention. However, their application is constrained due to issues such as cost and susceptibility to electromigration. In comparison to silver, copper boasts a lower cost and excellent resistance to electromigration. Additionally, it exhibits similar electrical and thermal conductivity properties to silver. These factors have propelled nano-copper particles into the spotlight as a new connecting material. This article aims to optimize the sintering process using the single-factor method. The sintering process optimization includes sintering time and pressure, with sintering temperatures ranging from 200°C, 250°C, to 300°C, and sintering pressures varying from 1 MPa, 3 MPa, to 5 MPa. Sample preparation and sintering experiments will be conducted using the optimized sintering process, and the resulting samples will be tested to calculate the shear strength under different conditions. Subsequently, finite element analysis will be employed, considering the volume of porosity in the sintered layer as part of the sintered layer volume. A perfect sintered layer without voids will be modeled, and the sintered layers with different porosities obtained from experiments will be considered as a new material. Material parameters such as Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio for the sintered layer under different porosities will be calculated. These material parameters will be input into the model to assess the impact of different porosities on the reliability of double-sided heat dissipation power devices, including temperature cycling (TC) and the fatigue life of the sintered layer. Finally, it will be concluded that maintaining the porosity of the sintered layer between 15% to 20% is most appropriate. This will serve as a reference for reducing device stress and enhancing reliability.

articleTitle: Finite Element Simulation and Power Cycling Failure Analysis of IGBT Device Wire Bonding Joints
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: IGBT devices have the advantages of high input impedance, good thermal stability, high current density, low on-state voltage drop, etc., and are widely used in new energy, rail transportation, electric vehicles, industrial applications, and household appliances. Currently, the main method for bonding IGBT devices is ultrasonic wedge bonding using thick Al wires. However, both the bonding process and the complex service conditions of IGBTs can cause a series of reliability issues for the devices. This article used finite element simulation analysis methods to analyze the failure modes and failure mechanisms of micro-interconnection wire bonding joints in the system-level packaging of IGBT power device. The impact of power cycling loads on the devices was analyzed, and the influence of Al wire bonding point span was also studied. This will help extend the service life of power devices, providing guidance for their structural design and bonding processes.

articleTitle: A Study on Glass Surface Activation Process to Enhance Glass-Metal Adhesion Strength in Glass Advanced Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Due to its excellent characteristics (high-modulus, low losstangent, CTE match), glass substrates have great market potential to replace, or eliminate silicon interposers to achieve high-density, high-bandwidth, and low-power glass advanced packaging systems. However, the poor adhesion strength between glass and metal is one of the major technical bottlenecks of glass packaging, resulting in glass-metal delamination. This paper focuses on the study of glass surface activation mechanism to improve glass surface hydrophilicity, and thus to increase the adhesion strength between glass surface and seed layer. The adhesion strength between glass and seed layer was characterized by cross-hatch peel adhesion test and cantilever beam tensile test. The results show strong adhesion between glass surface and sputtered Cu/Ti-Cu seed layer. The adhesion strength reaches the highest 5B adhesion level, and is larger than 4.9 N/cm according to the cross-hatch peel adhesion test. The cantilever beam tensile test also shows that the adhesion is strong enough so that glass cracks first before seed layer de-laminates. Finally, ~12 μm thick Cu was electroplated, followed by dual-beam focused ion beam (DB-FIB) characterization. The DB-FIB images show that no de-lamination occurred among plated Cu, Ti-Cu seed layer and glass surface.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Power Module Manufacturing: Large Area Sintering with Silver Pastes for Enhanced Performance and Cost-Effectiveness
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: To meet the increasing heat dissipation requirement of high-power-density power modules, novel packaging materials are greatly necessary. Ag sintering with excellent thermal conductivity, is not only gradually applied in the die attach, but also considered as the best candidate to replace the traditional Pb-containing solder alloy for large-area module attach. In this study, experimental research and Finite Element Analysis (FEA) simulations have been conducted to compare the performance of modules employing traditional soldering with large area sintering. The findings unequivocally illustrate the superior thermal and structural characteristics of large area sintering with silver pastes. The results demonstrate that large area sintering with silver pastes enables the attainment of equivalent power outputs with a diminished number of Silicon Carbide (SiC) chips, while upholding acceptable Tj thresholds, thereby furnishing substantial cost-effectiveness. Evidently, large area sintering with silver pastes is exceptionally well-suited for the forthcoming generation of power modules, offering heightened performance, augmented power density, and noteworthy cost-effectiveness. In summary, large area sintering with silver pastes is well-suited for future power modules, offering higher performance, increased power density, and improved cost-effectiveness.

articleTitle: Substrate Integrated Waveguide Dual-Bandpass Filter for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this paper, a glass-based millimeter-wave (mm-W) dual-bandpass filter (DBPF) with the substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) structure based on TE301 mode is proposed. The two passbands of bandpass filter (BPF) are controlled by the size of the iris and the resonant cavity. By adjusting the coupling strength between different resonant cavities to match the poles, the design goal of dual-passband filtering is achieved. To facilitate its fabrication, the proposed DBPF is designed based on through glass via (TGV) technology. The TGV technology has the advantages of high cost-effectiveness and large-scale production. The simulation results of the proposed DBPF show that, the center frequencies of the dual passband are 79.4GHz and 93GHz, respectively, and the insertion loss in the band is 1.258dB and 1.690dB. The design has obtained samples through experiments, and the measurement results are similar to the simulation results. The center frequencies of the dual passband are 79.5GHz and 93GHz, respectively. The insertion loss is 1.009dB and 0.922dB in the band, respectively.

articleTitle: Degradation Analysis of Double Trench-Gate SiC MOSFETs Under Single Surge Current Stress
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this work, the degradation processes and mechanisms of commercial double trench gate SiC MOSFETs under single surge current (SSC) stresses are delved into. Based on comprehensive characterizations on device parameters before/after SSC stresses, we elucidate degradation behaviors exhibited by these MOSFETs. Notably, when SSC reaches the maximum value, the stability of the threshold voltage (Vth) and on-state resistance (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ds,on</inf>) suggests that the gate oxide for these MOSFETs is not obviously influenced by SSC stresses. Additionally, scanning acoustic microscopy (SAM) analysis confirm the reliability of package. Through directly measuring the I-V characteristics of the body diode, the damage to body diode is identified as the primary cause of device failure, resulting the increase of the drain leakage current (Idss) and the loss in blocking capability. This work contributes usefully to the refinement of surge reliability assessment for SiC MOSFETs.

articleTitle: Research on Liquid Cooling Test Technology of Ceramic Substrate Packaging Embedded Microchannel
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In order to achieve the liquid cooling test of embedded microchannels in ceramic substrates, a test method of liquid cooling is designed, and special test equipment and test flow are developed in this paper. The equipment mainly consists of three aspects: refrigeration, coolant delivery, and electrical components. To meet the thermal testing requirements, a ceramic thermal test chip is designed and fabricated using a multilayer co-firing process to simulate chip heating and test package heat dissipation performance. Furthermore, the feasibility of using liquid metal and nanofluids as working fluids is investigated to enhance heat dissipation effectiveness. Experimental results indicate that due to high viscosity, existing liquid metals are not suitable for products with ceramic substrate packaging embedded microchannel. However, all five commercialized nanofluids show promising application effects, with diamond nanofluid No. 3 demonstrating the best heat dissipation performance.

articleTitle: Interconnection-Varied Warpage Modeling of Sintered-Nanosilver-Connected Power Modules with a Heatsink Considering Time Sequence Efforts
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The nanosilver sintering techniques are gaining increasing popularity in the packaging of wide bandgap (WBG) semiconductors for their superior characteristics of high electrical conductivity, low interconnection thermal resistance, and high working reliability. However, there is residual deformation and stress after sintering, which will not only reduce the module's heat dissipation capacity but also shorten its operating life. Therefore, the investigation of the thermal residual stresses and deformations induced by the sintering processes is a key issue in packaging a module. Since the nanosilver paste maintains solid throughout the sintering processes and only changes on the interface connection, it is difficult to accurately simulate the influences caused by the sintering processes on the residual stress and warpage using conventional numerical models with element-birth-and-death. In this paper, a time sequence method with the variation in interconnection is proposed to model the deformations and stresses generated in the nanosilver sintering processes. In the proposed method, the nanosilver layer is divided into several solder blocks, and the connection processes are realized by varying the interconnection situations of the bricks and the connecting components. The proposed methodologies are used in simulating the warpage and residual stresses of a heatsink that is sintered with three modules, and the warpage characteristics of the heatsink are discussed. The simulation method can guide the processing optimization for mitigating the warpage caused by the packing sequence.

articleTitle: Thermal Deformation Analysis for Power Device During the Reflow Process
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: During the reflow soldering process of power device, due to the mismatch of CTE (Coefficient of Thermal Expansion) among different materials, the copper strip of leadframe (LF) inevitably suffer thermomechanical stress. For typical power device package TO220 with inner insulation (II-TO220) structure, delamination was found between the LF and ceramic occasionally. In order to solve the this defect mode, both simulation & experiment conducted. Firstly, provided an engineer estimating method. Through this estimating method, equivalent results of the air layer thickness and the contact thermal resistance can be obtained, this will provide a refer for other package of power devices. Secondly, the transient temperature simulation results coupled with the transient stress, the Anand model and birth-death element technology are adopted to simulate the thermal deformation of the II-TO220 packaging structure. Through thermal stress analysis of the reflow soldering process, find the largest thermal deformation of II-TO220 is at LF edges, where is more likely to produce weak soldering, voiding, cracking. At last, pre-bending can help avoid this defect. Corresponding to more other new package development, this simulation system can help give accurate pre-bending design.

articleTitle: Investigation of Photosensitive Polyimide with Photolithography Process and Mechanical Behavior for Wafer-Level Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the rapid growth of the 5G, artificial intelligence (AI) and Internet markets, the demand for highly integrated and high-reliability chips has greatly expanded, but the development of packaging structures and the enhancement of chip computing power have brought about changes in materials, structures and processes. A thermal mismatch between encapsulation materials can easily lead to defects in the package structure, such as cracks, warpages, and interfacial delamination. Therefore, it is urgent to solve the problem of chip packaging interaction. In wafer-level packaging such as fan-out integrated packaging technology, photosensitive polyimide (PSPI) materials are often used as dielectric layers in RDL due to their excellent thermomechanical and thermodynamic properties, good adhesion and corrosion resistance, which can directly photolithography RDL patterns and simplify the photolithography process. Nevertheless, in general, the CTE of PSPI films in-plane ranges from 40 to 80 ppm/°C, but the CTE of copper metal is much lower about 17 ppm/°C, and the CTE of Silicon is the lowest about 2.8 ppm/°C C. Due to the CTE mismatch among the silicon substrate, the copper metal layer, and the PSPI film, the warpage problem and interface delamination are serious, resulting in the degradation of package reliability. The photolithography process of PSPI material affects its mechanical properties. The mechanical properties will directly affect the design process and the reliability evaluation. Therefore, it is important to optimize the photolithography process, perform a comprehensive mechanical behavior analysis, and establish a reasonable material constitutive model before proceeding with the design and rapid reliability assessments. To solve the above problems, this work mainly explores the photolithography process and mechanical properties of PSPI films. It establishes a finite element simulation model through photolithography tests, thermal expansion properties and viscoelastic mechanical properties experiments, evaluating the reliability in advanced packaging processes. We found that by optimizing the lithography process, the physical properties of PSPI films can be effectively improved, the defects of PSPI films can be reduced, and the thickness uniformity can be improved. In addition, the mechanical properties are greatly affected by temperature, and both stress and modulus decrease rapidly as the temperature increases. And the viscoelastic properties of PSPI films can be well reflected by the prony series. The research results provide effective technical support for solving the reliability analysis of wafer-level packaging and will promote the development of wafer-level packaging.

articleTitle: The Study on Reliability and Failure Mechanism of Micro-coil Spring Board-Level Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Micro-coil spring is a new technology for large-scale integrated circuit interconnection to replace traditional solder columns due to its ability to absorb the mechanical stress generated by external vibration and withstand the shear force caused by CTE mismatch. In this paper, the board-level interconnection structure was fabricated soldered with graphite fixtures using vapor phase reflow soldering process. The soldering quality was measured by optical observation as well as X-ray examinations. The board-level micro-coil spring structure survived temperature cycle tests, endurance vibration test as well as impact tests. The interface was not changed after temperature cycle test. The fracture mode was ductile in the impact tests.

articleTitle: Synthesis and Characterization of a Novel Alkaline-Developable Photosensitive Polymer for Solder Resists
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In recent years, photosensitive polymer materials are widely used in the field of advanced packaging of integrated circuits due to their convenience in photolithography processing, such as packaging photoresist, photosensitive polyimide (PSPI), photosensitive solder resist, etc. PSPI has excellent mechanical, thermal, and photolithographic properties and is widely used in IC packaging, MEMS, OLED, and other fields. But these PSPIs require the use of non-environmentally friendly organic developers such as cyclopentanone, or highly irritating and hazardous strong alkaline developers such as tetramethylammonium hydroxide (TMAH), and the developed patterns usually require high temperature of 250–400 °C to achieve completely cured. These shortcomings limit its application fields. In this paper, we designed and synthesized a PSPI resin with both carboxyl and vinyl groups to solve the above problems, and the structure of the resin was determined by Fourier transform infrared spectra (FT-IR) and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${}^{\mathbf{1}}\mathbf{H}$</tex> NMR spectroscopy. The resin with a cured temperature less than 200 °C has high mechanical properties (elongation at break higher than 80%, tensile strength higher than 140 MPa, and Young's modulus higher than 2.5 GPa) and thermal properties (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{T}_{\mathbf{g}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{T}_{\mathbf{5}\%}$</tex> higher than 300 °C and 510 °C, respectively). By adjusting the content of carboxyl and vinyl groups of the PSPI resin, and then mixing the resin with cross-linking agents and initiators, the resin can be developed with weakly basic aqueous developers such as sodium carbonate (Na<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>), and the scanning electron microscope (SEM) images show that the resolution ratio of the developed pattern can be as high as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{10}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex>. Therefore, the low-temperature curing and alkaline-developable photosensitive polymer synthesized in this work has excellent properties, and is environmentally friendly, and avoids the soluble problem of organic developers during the development process, which is compatible with the photosensitive solder resist process. It is expected to be used in advanced packaging substrate with the requirements of high heat resistance and high reliability.

articleTitle: Modeling and Optimization of Coaxial Annular Through Silicon via Based on a Temperature Range
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Through silicon vias (TSVs) provide support for chip-to-chip vertical interconnection of three-dimensional integration. It is essential to investigate the temperature-dependent electrical characteristics of TSVs to ensure the stable operation of integrated circuits in a severe temperature range. In this paper, a coaxial annular through silicon via (CA-TSV) based on a wide temperature range and design optimization are studied. The RLGC parasitic parameter extraction equations are proposed in an equivalent lumped circuit model coupled with the temperature-dependent properties of the materials. Circuit and electromagnetic field simulations are performed in the frequency range of 0.1~50 GHz and the temperature range of -40~100 °C. The excellent accuracy of the theoretical model is verified. However, signal integrity is found to deteriorate slightly when the temperature increases. Therefore, a feasible metal-dielectric-metal CA-TSV (MDM-TSV) is proposed to enhance the signal integrity of CA-TSV in a wide temperature range. The input impedance and scattering parameters of the MDM-TSV are remarkably optimized compared to the CA-TSV.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Spherical MnSe Nanoparticle as Cathode Material for Wearable Aqueous Zinc Ion Battery
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (ZIBs) have attracted significant interest due to their inherent safety, high specific capacity, and cost-effectiveness. The positive electrode material, which hosts <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${Zn}^{2+}$</tex> ions, is critical for the discharge capacity and cycling stability of these batteries. In this study, we synthesized manganese selenide via the hydrothermal method to serve as the positive electrode material. The electrochemical evaluations revealed that manganese selenide exhibits superior properties. At a discharge rate of 0.5C, it achieved a stable specific capacity of 141.5 mAh/g with a capacity retention of 68.3% after 100 cycles. These results highlight the potential of manganese selenide nanoparticles as effective cathode materials for flexible ZIBs.

articleTitle: Heterogeneous Integration of Diamond-on-Chip-on-Interposer for High-Performance Thermal Management in Supercomputing 2.5D Chiplets Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the advancement of various emerging technologies, the relentless drive for miniaturization and performance enhancement in semiconductor devices has significantly raised power density, presenting formidable thermal challenges. Efficient thermal management has become crucial for the advancement of advanced semiconductor technology, impacting the reliability, performance, and longevity of these devices. This study aims to tackle these thermal challenges by harnessing the superior thermal conductivity of diamond within the 2.5D interposer packaging, which is increasingly vital in high-performance computing and power electronics. We propose an innovative Diamond-Si bonding scheme utilizing a metal nano interlayer and validate its impact on the cooling performance in multi-chiplet, high-compute, and high-power scenarios through thermal simulations. We elaborate on the preparation process for plasma-activated low-temperature bonding samples and evaluate the bonding quality. Additionally, thermal simulations are conducted on multiple chiplets, including a high-performance supercomputing chip and two High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) chips. Thermal modeling shows that integrating a diamond heat spreader reduces the maximum temperature in a realistic 2.5D chiplets packaging by more than 20% with power density higher than I.SW/mms. Thls study presents a highly promising strategy for heterogeneous integrated heat dissipation technology, laying the foundation for superior thermal management solutions in advanced chiplet packaging.

articleTitle: Significantly Enhanced Insulation Resistance Degradation of BaTiO3-Based MLCCs with High Temperature Stability via Defect Engineering
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Base metal electrodes-multilayer ceramic capacitors (BME-MLCCs) are important equipment components enabling electronic devices to achieve excellent performance, muti-functionality and high integration, which are considered to be a fascinating device for a diverse range of electric applications. However, the service lifespan of MLCCs mainly depends on the insulation resistance (IR) degradation behavior. To solve this problem, the current-voltage (I-V), capacitor-voltage (C-V), thermally stimulated depolarization current (TSDC) characteristics and highly accelerated life test (HALT) of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{BaTiO}_{3}$</tex> based BME-MLCCs with superior temperature coefficient of capacitance (TCC) were investigated systematically. It is found that the IR degradation behavior is closely related to the accumulation and migration of oxygen vacancies and space charges. It can be observed from the I-V results that the Ohmic, Schottky type conduction occurs with the increase of dc field in all samples, while Poole-Frenkel effect was only observed in specific samples <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">w</sup>ith the <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">re</sup>laxati<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</sup> of trapped space charges and poor reliability. This work explores the degradation mechanism of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{BaTiO}_{3}\text{-MLCCs}$</tex> insulation resistance and provides a feasible strategy to improve its reliability.

articleTitle: Optimization Design and Flow Field Characteristics Study of Cleaning Process Tank for Wafer Wet
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The wafer cleaning process is an important link throughout the entire wafer manufacturing and packaging, and is one of the important factors affecting wafer performance and yield. As integrated circuit feature sizes shrink and wafer sizes increase, coupled with the increase in requirements for wafer surface granularity indicators, the requirements for controlling the uniformity of process chemical tank cleaning in tank cleaning equipment are getting higher and higher. Based on fluid dynamics and mechanical design theory, this paper conducts design research on the chemical tank of the wet cleaning process based on the working characteristics of the wafer tank cleaning equipment. The mathematical model and numerical model of the tank fluid field were established, and finite element analysis software was used to analyze the internal flow field of the tank. In order to improve the uniformity of the flow of chemical liquid in the tank, the effects of the incident angle of the liquid inlet hole, the diameter of the liquid inlet hole, and the number of liquid inlet holes on the uniformity of the flow of chemical liquid in the tank were analyzed, and the structural parameters of the tank were optimized. Establish a numerical model of the tank structural field, perform fluid-solid coupling analysis on the tank, and obtain the stress and displacement change nephograms of the tank. This article has certain reference value for the design optimization of the process chemical tank in tank cleaning equipment and the analysis of the flow field and structure of the tank.

articleTitle: Optimization of the Adhesion and Thermal Conductivity of Thermal Interface Materials for Chip Immersion Cooling via Grafting Polar Groups
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Conventional heat dissipation methods struggle to meet chips' thermal management needs, leading to the adoption of submerged liquid cooling technology. Traditional thermal interface materials (TIMs) have limitations in thermal conductivity and adhesion. To address this, a novel TIM is developed using methylhydrosiloxane polydimethylsiloxane and vinyl terminated polydimethylsiloxane as matrix, with 2-Hydroxyethyl acrylate (HEA) grafting to enhance adhesion properties. Our research also explored the effect of varying spherical aluminum powder sizes. The optimized TIMs achieve a high thermal conductivity of 5.20 W m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>K<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>, adhesion strength of 4.18 ± 0.18 MPa, and adhesion energy of 729.55 ± 282.63 J m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2</sup>. Our TIMs effectively address thermal management challenges of chip, providing an efficient solution for submerged liquid cooling systems and advancing electronic packaging technology.

articleTitle: Application of Nano Copper Paste in Large-Area Sintering: A Study on Enhancing Its Sintering Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Silicon carbide power chips require interconnection materials with high thermal and electrical conductivity, stability at high temperatures, and resistance to electro migration. Nano-metal sintering technology, particularly using nano-silver and nano-copper, has emerged as a promising solution. This study investigates the large-area sintering (LAS) performance of different substrates and printing thicknesses. The results show that pure copper (Cu) substrates provide superior bonding compared to nickel (Ni)-plated ones, and the sintered layer thickness varies significantly with stencil thickness. The presence of a cross-shaped channel improves the volatilization of organic compounds, reducing porosity. These findings highlight the potential of nano-metal sintering materials in enhancing the reliability and performance of high-power chips.

articleTitle: Simulation Study on the Impact Mechanism of Traps on AlGaN/GaN HEMT
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this article, the mechanism of the influence of concentration and energy levels of traps in the GaN buffer layer on the saturation current and threshold voltage of depletion-mode GaN HEMT devices is investigated. The GaN HEMT device was simulated and calibrated through sentaurus TCAD software. By introducing a trap model and systematically studying the effects of trap parameters such as concentrations and energy levels, the influence of these traps on the electrical properties of GaN HEMT was studied. The results showed that these traps will cause the degradation of GaN HEMT devices, mainly manifested as a reduction in saturation current and a positive shift in threshold voltage. As the concentration of traps increases, the electrical characteristics of GaN HEMT degrade more seriously. In addition, deep level traps have a stronger ability to capture electrons than trap states in shallow energy levels, and have a more obvious impact on saturation current and threshold voltage. The research findings provide important theoretical guidance for optimizing device fabrication and trap management, and help to further improve the reliability and performance of GaN HEMT devices.

articleTitle: Through Glass via (TGV) Filling Process With Conductive Silver Paste Based on 3D Printing Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Filling is one of the most costly and intricate steps in through glass via (TGV) manufacturing. Conductive silver paste has a remarkable bonding strength with glass and excellent electrical properties. In this study, conductive silver paste was used to fill TGVs with a diameter of 100 μm and a depth of 400 μm via 3D printing technology, and Daisy chain wiring was performed at the same time. Subsequent testing evaluated the electrical and mechanical properties of the produced Daisy chain. The results demonstrate a resistivity of 8.42× 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> Ω·m for the silver paste within the through vias, and the silver paste in the wiring layer exhibits a peak shear force of 23 gf. In conclusion, the integration of 3D printing technology for filling TGVs and wiring with conductive silver paste significantly simplifies the TGV filling process, and the electrical and mechanical performance are reliable.

articleTitle: UV laser processing of super-hydrophilic graphene films with good electrical conductivity for high-voltage micro-capacitors
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Laser-induced graphene (LIG) technique has significant advantages in the applications of micro energy storage devices including micro-supercapacitors (MSCs) due to its low cost, high efficiency and scalability. However, it is still a big challenge to simultaneously achieve super-hydrophilic graphene films with good conductivity, especially using efficient and low-cost methods. In this work, a two-step laser processing technique was proposed to address this issue. The technique employs a UV picosecond laser to scan twice on a KOH-coated polyimide film to in-situ fabricate LIG films with unique microstructures and rich oxygen-containing groups. The resulting LIG films have super-hydrophilic (a contact angle of 0°) and even capillary properties. The capillary rise height reaches 30 mm after a LIG sample strip comes into contact with water for 3.2 seconds. Moreover, the low sheet resistance (78.6 Ω square<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>) of resulting LIG films demonstrate its good conductivity. Thus, 10 series-connected LIG electrodes can be used for high-voltage MSCs of 10 V with an areal capacitance of 0.32 mF cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2</sup>. Therefore, the super-hydrophilic LIG electrodes with rapid response characteristics are expected to extend their applications to the field of micro-electronics and beyond.

articleTitle: Accurate Capacitance Modeling of 3D Capacitor Based on Coaxial Through Silicon Via
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this work, multi-conductor transmission lines (MTLs) theory is used to establish the analytical model of three-dimensional (3D) capacitor implemented by coaxial through-silicon via (CTSV) array, which considering the influence of silicon substrate and the coupling capacitance between CTSVs. At the same time, the parasitic capacitance associated with redistribution layer (RDL) is considered by introducing conformal mapping method and the scalar potential integral equation (SPIE), making it possible to estimate the capacitance of the 3D capacitor accurately and quickly. By comparing extraction results of simulator with the computation of capacitor composed of 1, 2, 3 and 5 CTSVs, the accuracy and calculation speed of proposed model are verified, with the average deviation around 3% for capacitance at 10GHz and significant reduction in runtime.

articleTitle: Electro-thermo-mechanical Reliability of Low Melting-point Solder Joints in Metal Oxide Varistor Packages under High Surge Current Densities
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Metal oxide varistor (MOV) is a ceramic electronic component, which is extremely sensitive to overvoltage and is widely used in overvoltage protection devices. The resistance of MOV increases as the voltage across its terminals rises, thus it serves as a voltage divider for the electronics. In order to connect the MOV to the circuit, there is a common method at present to interconnect the electrode with the MOV by soldering process. Under extreme conditions, the solder joint becomes the key point of the entire device, so it is necessary to evaluate the performance of the solder. For the scenario of varistor applications, there are two main aspects to evaluate the performance of the solder: surge current test and short circuit current test. Currently, there is a main issue, that is, the joint in MOV device soldered by low melting-point eutectic Sn-58Bi solder usually fails when subjected to surge current. To investigate the root cause of solder joint failure and the fundamental mechanism under surge current, this study first examines the temperature rise and stress response characteristics of Sn-xBi (x=58, 40, 30, 20, 10) solder joints under the current surge. Subsequently, the influence of Bi content on temperature and stress distributions of solder joints during the surge test is analyzed to further elucidate the failure mechanism. The study identifies three factors significantly influencing temperature and stress distributions in the whole surge test, and their effects and underlying mechanisms are thoroughly studied and analyzed.

articleTitle: Reliability Analysis and Optimization of Silicon Bridge Interconnect Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The use of silicon bridge interconnect packaging technology is becoming increasingly widespread in High-Performance Computing (HPC) systems. However, Material thermal expansion mismatches in silicon bridge packaging cause chip warping and bridge stress, directly impacting chip performance and reliability. This study optimizes silicon bridge interconnect packaging processes and structures to reduce chip warping and silicon bridge stress.First, the viscoelastic behavior of the underfill curing process in silicon bridge interconnect packaging is measured using Dynamic Mechanical Analysis (DMA). Next, a 3D finite element simulation model is established to emulate the warpage and stress behaviors of silicon bridge interconnect packaging during flip-chip bonding and underfill processes, with an analysis of potential failure modes and causes. Finally, orthogonal experiments with Grey Relational Analysis optimize chip warpage and silicon bridge stress, identifying the best parameters for silicon bridge interconnect packaging. Results indicate that significant warpage deformation occurs in the chips during both flip-chip bonding and the underfill curing shrinkage process. The concentration of stress on silicon bridges may lead to failures such as fractures or cracks in the silicon bridges. Following optimization of the processes and structures, notable improvements are observed in both chip warpage and silicon bridge stress. Our research improves warp control and reduces failure risks in silicon bridges, providing a valuable guide for silicon bridge interconnect technology application.

articleTitle: Molecular Dynamics Study of GaN Thin Films Deposited on Non-polar m-plane of A1N Substrate
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The GaN deposited on polar surfaces exhibits significant spontaneous polarization effects, which can cause Quantum Confinement Stark Effect. However, growing on non-polar surfaces can avoid these issues. This study used molecular dynamics method to investigate the epitaxial growth of GaN thin film on non-polar m-plane (1–100) at different temperatures. The variation of the surface morphology and the crystalline structure of simulation system were discussed in detail. The simulation results showed that as the epitaxial temperature rises, the mobility of surface atoms along [0001] direction was significantly higher than that along [11–20] direction, so that the small island structure on the surface were connected along [0001] direction. In addition, the increase in temperature was beneficial for improving the atomic migration ability, which leads to the number of wurtzite atoms increases and the number of amorphous atoms decreases.

articleTitle: Study on Hygro-Thermal Mechanical Reliability of Epoxy Molding Compound for GaN SMD
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The application of high-voltage Gallium Nitride (GaN) surface mount devices (SMD) in new energy automobiles can significantly increase the efficiency and power density of on-board charger (OBC) and DC/DC converters. However, due to the extreme application environments of high temperature, high humidity, and high pressure in automobiles, the used epoxy molding compound (EMC) of packaged devices requires high moisture and temperature resistance, which is more desirable for SMD products. This paper investigates the moisture absorption and diffusion characteristics of two commonly used EMCs based on Fick's Law and obtains relevant moisture diffusion parameters. The moisture diffusion behavior and hygro-thermal stress distribution of the two EMCs for the same transistor outline lead-less (TOLL) packaged device are simulated using finite element method. Based on automotive application requirements, standard reliability tests are conducted on two types of GaN TOLL SMD encapsulated by these two EMCs. The results show that the influence of hygroscopic stress is more severe than that of thermal stress in GaN TOLL SMD and the EMC with lower moisture absorption provides better reliability.

articleTitle: Effect of Sintered Silver Phase Coarsening on the Fatigue Characteristics of SiC Power Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The evolution of the porous microstructure of sintered silver in service can significantly affect the reliability of power modules, but there are few studies that elucidate the specific mechanisms of this effect. In this work, the impact of phase coarsening of sintered silver die attach layer on the fatigue characteristics in SiC power modules is examined by finite element method (FEM). The porous structure model of sintered silver die attach is established based on a Gaussian filtering technique to simulate the phase coarsening of sintered silver in power modules under service condition. Significant stress concentrations are observed at the chip/sintered silver interface. Furthermore, the phase coarsening affects the stress distribution and heat dissipation of the sintered silver die attach layer, resulting in that a power module is more susceptible to fatigue failure. The Coffin-Manson fatigue model is employed to predict the fatigue lifetime of power modules. It is found that the phase coarsening of the sintered silver can severely reduce the fatigue lifetime of SiC power modules.

articleTitle: Study on Thermo-Compression Bonding with Non-Conductive Paste Process Technology and Reliability of Flip Chip
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As an important interconnect technology for 3D integrated package, the bonding quality and reliability of the thermo-compression bonding with non-conductive paste process is the key to the stable operation of chip devices. NCP can act as both flux and underfill for flip chip bonding, so the process requires strict temperature control to ensure that the upper and lower micro-bumps contact and melt bonding are achieved before NCP curing, and in addition, the process window is further narrowed to reduce the trapping of filler particles after bonding. In this paper, the experiment of thermo-compression bonding with non-conductive paste process was carried out with Sn-3.5Ag electroplated copper pillar with a diameter of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$40\mu\mathrm{m}$</tex>, and the effects of bonding pressure, bonding temperature, bonding time and abutment temperature on morphology of the micro-bumps were studied. After the isothermal aging treatment, the influence of the size of micro-convex dots on the growth of IMC was investigated, and it was found that the Ni barrier layer effectively inhibited the growth of IMC.

articleTitle: Synthesis and Properties Study of Low Dielectric UV Curable Epoxy Resin/Fluorocarbon Composites
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The development and application of low-dielectric solder resist for FCBGA is a critical research area in electronic packaging. With the advancement of high-frequency communication technology, there are increasing demands for solder resist (SR) used as coating materials to have low dielectric constant, low dielectric loss, and high thermal resistance. In this study, a photosensitive and alkali-soluble resin was synthesized by reacting acrylic acid with epoxy resin to introduce photosensitive double bond groups, followed by a reaction with anhydride to generate carboxyl groups. Fluorocarbon fillers were incorporated into the system to further reduce the dielectric constant and dielectric loss of SR films. This paper discussed the effects of different fluorocarbon contents on the dielectric, thermal, photolithography, and mechanical properties of SR films in detail, and showed great great industrial application prospects.

articleTitle: Research on Plasma Electrodeless High-Precision Spectral Calibration Light Source with Wide Spectrum Range
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Spectral calibration sources are essential for the calibration and characterization of spectroscopic detection equip-ment. This paper presents the design of an inductively coupled light source as a spectral calibration source. We employed a longitudinal magnetic field inductive discharge design, conducted a simulation analysis of the magnetic field distribution within this design, and solved the drift-diffusion equations to obtain the electron temperature and energy distribution of the generated plasma. The designed RF circuit has a stable resonant frequency at 13 MHz, and the operating power can be adjusted between o and 20 W. This device demonstrates excellent performance and stability, offering a longer lifespan compared to traditional calibration sources.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Output Voltage of a Piezoresistive MEMS Pressure Sensor Using Finite Element Modelling
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this paper, based on a 3D finite element model of a piezoresistive MEMS pressure sensor developed previously using FreeFem++, the output voltage of the device is calculated via three approaches. In the first approach, the output voltage is calculated using the widely used empirical formula for the Wheatstone bridge circuits, and thus, it is called the empirical result. In the second approach, firstly, the mean stresses are obtained within the four P-type resistors and the resistivity of the resistors is calculated using the constitutive relation of piezoresistivity. Then a steady state equation of the electric potential is solved and the electric potentials are extracted at the corner of the Cu interconnects. Thus, their difference yields the output voltage and it is called the semi-empirical result. However, within the resistors, the distribution of stresses are in fact quite inhomogeneous and thus their resistivity is also inhomogeneous. Hence, in the third approach, the resistivity of the four resistors are determined as functions of the stresses within the resistors using the constitutive relation of piezoresistivity. Then the electrical potential is also obtained numerically and the output voltages are extracted. The result obtained using the third approach is thus called the numerical result, which is the accurate output voltage of the pressure sensor determined numerically. During the simulations, the influences of different thicknesses of the silicon diaphragm, different widths of the P-type silicon resistor, and different distances between the center of the diaphragm and the midpoint of the P-type silicon resistor, are studied. The three results mentioned above are compared. Simulations show that the three results qualitatively agree with each other with the output voltage from the third approach being 30% higher. We argue, though the widely used empirical result leads to a less accurate output voltage, but it can still achieve the purpose of aiding the design of a piezoresistive MEMS pressure sensor satisfactorily.

articleTitle: Research on Reliability of Potting Adhesive in Ceramic Substrate
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Wire bonding was the most widely used electronic packaging technology at present. In the actual application process, the components had the characteristics of high-density assembly. Accordingly, the wire bonding characterized by small pads, fine spacing and multiple layers. In this paper, 800 bonding points were set in the range of 13.9 mm × 13.9 mm. The diameter of the bonding wire was 18 μm and the center distance was 52 μm. Four layers of bonding surface arranged and the wire bonding process was soldering process with gold ball. In order to prevent failure of wire bonding, potting adhesive technology added behind the wire bonding process. The process could fix the gold wires and played the role of insulation protection. Through modeling and simulation, the potting adhesive could transfer the stress concentration point of the ceramic substrate from the inside to the outside. The highest value reached at 150 °C, when the stress was 33.24 MPa. Viewed from the outside, the potting adhesive was intact after the implementation, but it cracked after several temperature cycling tests. Interestingly, the gold wire protected by the potting adhesive remained intact, but the ceramic substrate cracked. Through mechanical analysis, this related to the internal stress of potting adhesive. The internal stress related to coefficient of thermal expansion and elastic modulus. The bending strength of ceramic substrate decreased with the increase of times of temperature cycling. When the internal stress reached 55.93 MPa, the ceramic substrate cracked. Finally, experimental verification gave two solutions. One was to reduce the application temperature and the other was to replace the potting adhesive. In the ceramic packaging, wire bonding and potting adhesive technology were compatible, which had guiding significance for the subsequent high-density packaging.

articleTitle: Study on Short-Circuit Characteristics of Semi-Super-Junction SiC MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this paper, the short-circuit (SC) characteristics of conventional and semi-super-junction (semi-sj) SiC MOSFETs are investigated using 2D numerical simulation, revealing a possible short-circuit failure mechanism and performance degradation mechanism of SiC MOSFET. Comparing the short-circuit characteristics of the two devices, it is found that the semi-sj SiC MOSFET exhibits superior short-circuit characteristics and relatively weak performance degradation due to the introduction of the P-pillar region. Meanwhile, combined with the static characterization of the devices, it is found that the semi-sj SiC MOSFET has better overall performance. In addition, the short-circuit reliability of semi-sj SiC MOSFETs can be further optimized concerning device structural parameters such as the thickness and doping concentration of the N-type bottom auxiliary layer and the thickness of the gate oxide layer.

articleTitle: Development of Thermo-Compression NCF Bonding Process with High Throughput for 3DS DRAM
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence and high-end servers, demands for high bandwidth memory (HBM) and 3D stacked dynamic random access memory (3DS DRAM) is becoming more and more urgent. This is mainly based on Through-Silicon-Via (TSV) 3D multilayer stacked advanced packaging, making the application of thermo-compression bonding (TCB) process more and more common. The step-bond method is mainly used in TCB combined with pre-applied non-conductive film (TC-NCF) process, as an important component of the TCB process. This method has good product quality and high reliability, but low UPH. In this paper, another pre-bond + post-bond method has been developed for 3DS DRAM, in order to improve the UPH of TC-NCF process. The advantages and disadvantages of two methods were compared in this paper. The Selection of raw materials and process parameters such as force, temperature, time were investigated, by using simulation and engineering experiments. The product quality including solder joint formation and reliability was confirmed through cross section, optical microscope and reliability testing. The results indicate that the pre-bond + post-bond method has a higher UPH, but a smaller process parameter window and stricter requirements for time control in the process. As the result, one TC-NCF method with good product quality and high UPH was developed, resulting in a 50% increase in UPH.

articleTitle: Research on the Signal Impedance Optimization Method on 2.5D Si-Interposer Design
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With advancements in AI, big data, and cloud computing technologies, 2.5D and 3D packaging solutions are increasingly utilized to enhance IC performance. However, the presence of substantial parasitic capacitance leading to low characteristic impedance underscores the importance of optimizing characteristic impedance. This paper introduces a L-compensation method employing T-coil to enhance the impedance optimization of the 2.5D Si-interposer of DDR5 from micro bump to C4 bump. The optimized design markedly enhances the signal characteristic impedance matching and reduces return loss, significantly improving both eye width and eye height. This optimization approach is easy to implement without additional space costs and can be extended to other high-speed interface signals.

articleTitle: Improved Resolution in Advanced Packaging Metrology Through Advanced Nano-Focus X-Ray Sources
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In the pursuit of ‘More Moore’ and ‘More than Moore’, the interest in X-ray source technology has intensified since many of the traditional methods to measure and control semiconductor manufacturing such as optical or electron-based metrology methods are running out of steam. Heterogeneous integration and advanced packaging offer the possibility to optimize and increase the performance of devices while keeping costs down. As the dimensions of the electrical connects are continuously reduced in size and pitch this enables more connections and faster communication. At the same time, this puts increased demand on the resolution of the metrology tool as critical defect dimensions of the electrical interconnects such as micro-bumps and through silicon vias (TSV) are getting smaller down to sub-micrometer level. The proposed solutions involve acoustic, optical, electrical and X-ray imaging techniques. However, X-rays have a clear advantage as it can probe large 3D volumes and measure the internal structure of devices non-destructively. For advanced packaging and heterogenous integration, the resolution of the X-ray reconstruction topographies has previously been a key limitation. In this communication it is shown that detailed submicron analysis of HBM micro-bumps and TSVs is possible with X-ray tools.

articleTitle: High-Speed Electrodeposition of Low-Stress Copper-Diamond Composite Coatings on Ceramic Substrate for Reliability Improvement in Power Device Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Direct copper plated (DPC) ceramic substrates have been widely used for power device packaging due to their outstanding thermal performance. For deep UV LEDs., thick copper dams with a thickness of more than 400 μm are usually prepared on the substrate surface to achieve hermetic packaging. However, under the influence of high heat flux, the sharply increased stress mismatch between the substrate and the thick copper coating becomes prominent, and the substrate inevitably suffer from serious reliability problems such as warping and cracking. On account of these deficiencies, this study presented a low-stress copper-diamond composite material by high-speed electrodeposition. The composite coatings were prepared using a new-style electrodeposition solution formula at a high electrodeposition rate of 90 μm/h. The diamond particles were well embedded in the copper matrix without interfacial defects. The coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) (9.44 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−6</sup>/°C) and the warping value (0.124%) were reduced by 46% and 78%, respectively, compared with pure copper coatings. The thermal conductivity (TC) reached as high as 572 W/(m.K). The high-speed electrodeposited copper-diamond composites can simultaneously improve the thermal performance and reduce the inner stress of the thick coating, which is an ideal structure coating material for enhancing the packaging reliability of power devices.

articleTitle: Transmission Performance and Crosstalk Analysis of TSV array Based on Differential GSSG Layout
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In the realm of large-scale 3D integrated circuits, a substantial number of Through-Silicon Vias (TSVs) must be integrated to realize vertical signal transmission. TSV arrays play a crucial role in achieving high-density 3D vertical interconnection. The presence of crosstalk and noise between TSVs can significantly impede transmission performance. Consequently, there has been a notable focus on developing compact, high-performance TSV arrays. In this work, the transmission characteristics and crosstalk noise of TSV arrays based on differential GSSG (Ground-Signal-Signal-Ground) layout are investigated. A series of signal TSV and ground TSV arrays were designed to study the high-frequency performance of different TSV arrays. The simulation outcomes reveal that single TSV exhibit the lowest insertion loss for both signal lines and ground lines. Signal TSV array tends to induce more severe crosstalk compared to single TSV, whereas multiple ground TSVs can enhance noise shielding and ensure signal integrity. Furthermore, the study extensively investigated the influence of aspect ratio and TSV pitch on transmission performance.

articleTitle: Wafer Warpage Simulation and Correction for 3D Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the approaching limit of Moore's law, traditional system -level chip design faces challenges for cost and manufacturing difficulty. 3D packaging as a way to transcend Moore improves the development of integrated density to continue the development of Moore's law. During the 3D packaging process, the chip stack needs to greatly reduce the thickness of each chip to reduce the thickness of the overall stacking module. With the decrease in the thinness of the wafers, due to the effects of the surface function layer of the wafer, the wafer curvature value will increase violently, which will affect the multi -chip stacking process. This article proposes a wafer thinning and warranty control process, which provides a qualified thinning chip for multilayer chip stacking. Establish a wafer -warming equivalent model through the finite element method, and through the optimization of the effect model, the wafer warpage is corrected and controlled, and the application of the model in actual engineering is achieved at the same time.

articleTitle: Size-effect on the undercut and dimension compensations in wet etching for micromachined quartz crystal microstructures
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the growth of wearable electronic gadgets, microfabrication for quartz crystal devices is becoming increasingly significant. However, the dimensional compensation of quartz fabrication has not been reported in the past decades. Therefore, in this paper, the effect of dimensions on undercut was explored. It was discovered that a smaller undercut was produced by a wider hard mask. And two kinds of dimensional compensation solutions for quartz fabrication are proposed, which are based on the etching results and was firstly used to fabricate ultra-compact tuning forks with 32.768 kHz. And the deviation of the actual fabricated dimensions from the designed one was only 0.7%. The etching symmetry of was improved by 96.3%. These strategies demonstrated fantastic potential for improving process precision in fabrication.

articleTitle: Design of a High-power Density Power Module with Large-area (10 mm × 10 mm) SiC MOSFETs for Traction Inverter Application
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this paper, the design of a high-power density power module using large-area SiC MOSFETs (10 mm × 10 mm) is presented. The performance of the proposed flip-chip double-side cooling power module is compared to a traditional double-side cooling power module in both thermal and electrical characteristics. In comparison to multiple regularsized chips, the large-area chips allow higher current output on a single chip, which offer a more flexible layout and lower thermal resistance in double-side cooling (DSC) module. Additionally, there is no current imbalance problem in a single chip module. The results indicate that power circuit parasitic inductance of the proposed module is 5.36 nH, which is 29.07% lower than the one based on regular-sized (5 mm × 5 mm) power devices. By using flip-chip technology instead of bonding wire, the parasitic inductance of the signal loop is reduced to 3.61 nH, representing a 36.88% decrease compared to the wire-bonding module. Moreover, the thermal resistance of the proposed module is 0.232 K/W, which is 12.9% lower.

articleTitle: Research on Pull-Off Strength Test Method of Cross-Surface SiP Device
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the continuous shrinking of the integrated circuit process, Moore's Law has been severely challenged[1]. The semiconductor industry is entering the post-Moore era, and various packaging technologies have been rapidly developed. However, for SiP device with different surface structure(Cross-Surface SiP), it is difficult to implement the pull-off strength test of the interposer due to multiple chips are inverted on the interposer at the same time, and the sizes and heights of each chip are different. At present, there is no universal test standard in the industry. This paper proposes two specific pull-off strength test methods based on a Cross-Surface SiP device. Experimental research was carried out by preparing test samples and designing necessary tools. The test results show that both test methods can meet the requirements of GJB548C-2031 for chip pull-off strength test, and the results are qualified. Constructing the device geometry model by industrial software, and the trend of stress and strain at multiple positions of the device during loading was analyzed and compared by two pull-off strength test methods through simulation. The simulation results show that the first test method will cause uneven stress distribution. In the test process, the uneven stress distribution may cause other effects outside the test. During the loading process of the second test method, the stress is uniform which can better meet the loading requirements in the test standards.

articleTitle: Temperature Gradient Control and Packaging Technologies for Co-Packaged Optics
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As the demand for computing power driven by generative artificial intelligence continues to increase, the need for data transfer and communication between different components of AI systems is also constantly rising. However, the traditional electrical I/O combined with pluggable optical modules fail to meet the application demands in terms of bandwidth, cost, and power consumption. Co-packaged optics (CPO) is widely regarded as a key solution and development trend for future data center optical interconnects. By integrating Photonic integrated circuits (PICs) and electronic integrated circuits (EIC) on a shared substrate, the CPO solution provides shorter electrical interconnection length, higher bandwidth and energy efficiency. The main challenge in CPO is the susceptibility of optical chips to high temperatures, leading to thermal fragility. Optical chips commonly feature fiber pigtail fixed with UV adhesive and DFB lasers employing flip-chip configuration, both vulnerable to high-temperature packaging processes.
