The packaging temperature is usually required to be below 100°C, which is incompatible with high-temperature processes such as reflow soldering used for electronic chips packaging. In this work, we propose an low temperature Co-packaged technique. The Application-Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC) chips and optical engine were packaged on a substrate, achieving a PAM-4 transmission of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4\times 50\ \text{Gbps}$</tex>. The measured bit error rate of the receiver is less than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 10^{-4}$</tex>, when the input optical power is -13 dBm. We believe that this research provides a significant solution for researchers in the fields of optical communication and data centers, accelerating industry development.

articleTitle: A New Modeling Approach to Evaluate the Impact of Randomly Distributed Pores on Heat Transfer Performance for Sintered Layer
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Due to the small size and complex microstructure of the actual sintered layer, it is challenging to determine the influence of pore characteristics on the heat transfer performance of the sintered layer through experiments. Therefore, This paper proposes a new method for constructing a three-dimensional pore model. This new model accurately represents the randomness in pore distribution and irregularity in pore shapes, providing a more realistic simulation of the thermal behavior in the sintered layers. Utilizing finite element analysis, the study investigates the impact of pore characteristics on the heat transfer performance of sintered layers. It is found that under a porosity of 10%, the average heat flux for a uniformly distributed pore model is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$9.39\times 10^{8}\mathrm{W}/\mathrm{m}^{2}$</tex>, while for two randomly distributed pore models, the average heat flux is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.01\times 10^{9}\mathrm{W}/\mathrm{m}^{2}$</tex>. It can be concluded thatpore distribution has a certain promoting effect on effective thermal conductivity. When small pores merge into larger ones, the pore throat area increases, leading to an increase in heat flux and consequently an increase in thermal conductivity. Additionally, the presence of smaller pores, due to their smaller temperature gradients, can also increase thermal conductivity. The effects of pore arerelated to their positions and distributions, indicating that pore porosity alone cannot be the sole criterion for evaluation. Furthermore, it's crucial to take into account the size, shape distribution, and continuity of the pores.

articleTitle: Preparation and Dielectric Properties of a Novel Fluorinated Polyimide Containing Bulky Lateral Groups
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Along with the advances in the three-dimensional stacking IC packaging technology, the electronic crosstalk, signal loss of the advanced electronic packaging redistribution layer (RDL) are becoming more and more serious, and it is urgent to develop high-performance packaging materials, especially RDL dielectric materials with low dielectric constant (Dk) and low dielectric loss (Df) under high frequency conditions. In this study, a novel diamine monomer named 6FpyDA was successfully synthesized via Suzuki coupling reaction, Michael addition reaction, and Dehydrogenation reaction. A series of polyimide films were fabricated through conventional two-step thermal imidization process. The influence of the content of 6FpyDA on the dielectric properties of PI was investigated. It was found that the dielectric constant and dielectric loss of the PI decreased gradually with the increase of the content of 6FpyDA. Under 10 GHz, the dielectric constant reaches as low as 2.38 and the dielectric loss is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5\times 10^{-4}$</tex>, showing excellent low dielectric properties. The introduction of bulky asymmetric rigid side groups and trifluoromethyl groups in the molecular chain were supposed to be the reason, which make the PI molecular chain exhibits a lower polarizability and a larger free volume between the molecular chains. The mechanical properties and thermal stability of PI are gradually enhanced with the increase in 6FpyDA content, leading to a tensile strength of up to 130 MPa. This exceptional comprehensive performance demonstrates its significant potential in the field of microelectronics packaging. Consequently, this study offers valuable insights for the fabrication of low dielectric intrinsic polyimides.

articleTitle: A Physical-Based Deep Learning Model for Thermal Process Simulation in FC-BGA Package
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Heat transfer analysis is crucial in electronic packaging design due to the coefficient of thermal expansion mismatch, which can cause mechanical failure. However, the classical numerical computation method is expensive which makes it hard to satisfy the electronic packaging design. With the rapid development of deep learning, it has widely been used in plenty of areas. In this work, we design a deep-learning model to study the transient thermal simulation with complex structures and various materials. The Rothe method is used to train the model. Numerical simulations have verified the high efficiency of the DL model.

articleTitle: Long-Term Superhydrophobicity at Copper-Based Interface with Micropillar Structure for Droplet Condensation
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Phase-change heat transfer is an effective technology for dissipating heat, and one of the key factors to influence the process is the wetting behaviour of the interface. Therefore, preparing a stable metal-based superhydrophobic interface to keep droplet on the Cassie state is of significant importance. In this study, the Cassie state model is optimised as a means of designing the hill-like curved micropillar array with tunable diameter, space, and height. This results in the achievement of a stable copper-based superhydrophobic interface. Non-silicon microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) fabrication process is then used to create a uniform and robust copper-based microstructure superhydrophobic interface. By regulating the diameter and space, the micropillar array with a space-diameter ratio greater than 2 exhibits a 48.2% improvement in hydrophobicity compared to a smooth copper surface, in accordance with theoretical calculations. In addition, by varying the height of the micropillar, the interface can exhibit the lotus effect with the height-diameter ratio greater than 0.5, thereby enhancing the liquid exchange rate at the condensation interface.

articleTitle: Plasma-etching Enhanced Dynamic Friction Polishing for Single Crystal Diamond Films
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In view of the high time-consuming and inefficiency polishing of diamond, this paper uses inductively coupled plasma (ICP) etching technology to treat the surface of single crystal diamond, and then obtains an ultra-smooth surface with the roughness as low as 0.39 nm over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{100}\ \boldsymbol{\mu}\ \mathbf{m}^{\mathbf{2}}$</tex> through dynamic friction polishing (DFP). The material removal principle is confirmed by the test results of atomic force microscope (AFM) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscop (XPS), the surface of the etched diamond has a direct phase transformation from crystalline to amorphous carbon, greatly improving the subsequent polishing rate and quality. It is of great significance to realize the high-level industrialization of diamond.

articleTitle: Effect of the Off State/Half-On State/On State Electrical Stresses on the Reliability of Packaged D-Mode GaN/AlGaN HEMTs
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this study, different typical electrical stresses (ES) were applied to the depletion mode GaN/AlGaN high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) to simulate the application scenarios in real production and life. By applying three kinds of typical electrical stress, we observed the device static obvious changes in the electrical parameters are as follows: (1) Compared with the original device, the threshold voltage VTH of the device has obvious left drift, and the transconductance and Rds,on decrease under the Off State electrical stress; (2) Under the Half-On State/On State electrical stress, the threshold voltage of the device is positively skewed, the on-resistance Rds,on increases, and the saturation leakage current Idsat decreases significantly. The experiments reveal the dependence of threshold voltage (VTH), peak transconductance (Gmmax) and saturation leakage current (Idsat) on different stress modes, which provides an intentional reference for the quality and reliability of subsequent GaN/AlGaN HEMTs practical production applications.

articleTitle: Ni-P UBM Can Inhibit IMC Overgrowth of Sn58Bi Solder During Soldering Process
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: This work focuses on the low-temperature eutectic Sn58Bi material as the research solder, and conducts soldering experiments at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$180^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> for 1 s, 30 s, 300 s, and 600 s on two types of UBMs: Cu and Ni-P/Cu. Analysis of the IMC growth on the interface revealed that Sn58Bi solder generated <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ni}_{3}\text{Sn}_4$</tex> IMC on Ni-P/Cu and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{CU}_{6}\text{Sn}_5$</tex> IMC on Cu substrate. By measuring the wetting angle of the solder joint, it is known that the wetting angle obtained by soldering Sn58Bi on Cu is always smaller than that on Ni-P/Cu UBM, indicating that it reacts more quickly on Cu and has better wetting properties, which is related to the solubility of Sn in Cu and Ni. Measuring the interface IMC thickness, it was found that the thickness of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Cu}_{6}\text{Sn}_5$</tex>; -IMC is always greater than that of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ni}_{3}\text{Sn}_4$</tex>, and both do not become thicker with increasing soldering times. Further ball pushing experiments revealed that the shear strength of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ni}_3\text{Sn}_4$</tex> was higher than that of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{CU}_6\text{Sn}_5$</tex> at a welding temperature of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$180 ^\circ \mathrm{C}$</tex>. Overall, a Ni-P coating with good surface quality can effectively suppress the excessive growth of interface IMC in Sn58Bi solder during use, and the solder joint strength is better.

articleTitle: High-Power Deep-Ultraviolet Light-Emitting Diodes with All-Inorganic Hermetic Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this work, a high-hermetic packaging structure was fabricated for high-power DUV-LEDs by pulsed laser welding. The packaging structure is primarily comprised of a quartz lens with Kovar frame and a three-dimensional direct plated ceramic (3D-DPC) substrate with copper dam. The quartz lens with Kovar frame was welded to the copper dam of 3D-DPC substrate in an overlap configuration. The parameters of pulsed laser welding were optimized in order to obtain a high-strength, crack-free welding joint. The packaging module was welded with a peak laser power of 120 W, a pulse width of 2 ms, and an overlap rate of 80%. The weld surface is bright and well-formed, and no welding defects such as cracks or pores are observed. The emission intensity peak of the packaged DUV-LED is at 280 nm, with a peak width at half height of 12 nm. At a driving current of 700 mA, the voltage of the packaged DUV-LED is 12.04 V, while the light output power is 376.4 mW. respectively. The average leakage rate of the packaging structure is 1.25×l0<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−9</sup> Pa.m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>/s and the welding joint exhibited a high shear strength of 257.6 MPa. Our work provides a valuable reference for the reliable and robust packaging of DUV-LEDs at the board level.

articleTitle: Electrical Simulation Model to Improve Through-Silicon Capacitor(TSC) Capacitance
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Inspired by Through-silicon vias (TSV), a capacitor structure, called Through-silicon Capacitor(TSC), integrates a MIM capacitor in the silicon interposer. TSC requires less chip area and offers higher capacitance density, which can be used as high-value decoupling capacitor in three dimensional integrated circuits (3D-IC). However, TSC has the drawback of complex preparation process and equivalent series resistance. The insulator layer material and quality in the MIM capacitor can also greatly affect its performance. In this study, the thermal-mechanical stress simulation shows that the minimum centre distance of two TSCs is 92 μm for further study. Then the capacitance formula of TSC is derived qualitatively, and several key parameters such as the the insulator layer thickness, dielectric constant, trench diameter and trench depth are designed for electrical simulation. With a series of improvements on these parameters, the TSC capacitance density can be increased to 467.09 nF/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Then the equivalent circuit diagram of TSC is designed, and the parasitic effect shows the increase of electrode thickness deeply decreases the parasitic resistance. The variation of parasitic inductance is not closely related to trench size. The performance of TSC can be greatly optimized in terms of electrico-thermal-mechanical stress properties, whose design is also compatible with the IC process.

articleTitle: Research on the Influence of Solder Layer Defects on Chip Junction Temperature
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: MOSFETs offer a number of benefits relative to traditional power devices. These include a higher switching frequency, higher operating temperature, and higher breakdown voltage. As a result, there has been considerable interest in these devices within the industry. However, alongside this interest, it has become clear that the reliability of MOSFETs is becoming increasingly significant in the research domain. This is because MOSFETs are used in a wide variety of applications in a range of different fields. One of the most significant causes of failure in MOSFET modules is solder layer degradation, which encompasses solder layer delamination and voids. This paper therefore investigates the impact of solder layer voids on the electrical and thermal characteristics of MOSFET modules. Firstly, a simplified finite element model is established, and an electro-thermal simulation analysis is carried out under power cycle conditions. Secondly, finite element models of different defective solder layers are established. The results of the simulations conducted using the aforementioned models are then compared and analyzed. The analysis reveals that the temperature on the chip rises in direct proportion to the increase in defect area, while the current density of the solder layer also increases significantly with the expansion of void area. This provides a certain reference point for the subsequent study of solder degradation.

articleTitle: Stress analysis and signal integrity analysis of CSP solder joints under thermally torsional loading
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The three-dimensional finite element model and electromagnetic simulation model of CSP(Chip Scale Package) solder joint are established by using ANSYS software and HFSS software respectively. The stress distribution of CSP solder joint model under the combined action of thermal power and torsional load is analyzed. Four structural factors including solder joint height, solder joint diameter, PCB board thickness and solder pad height were selected for orthogonal test. Variance analysis showed that PCB board thickness was significant, and range analysis showed that the order of structural factors affecting the maximum stress of solder joints was:PCB board thickness> solder joint height> solder joint diameter> solder pad height. The signal integrity of CSP solder joint is analyzed, and the influence of different high frequency signals on the signal integrity of CSP solder joint is obtained. Finally, the influence of CSP solder joint structure on return loss is analyzed by single factor.

articleTitle: A Case Study of Delamination Failure Analysis of PTFE Substrate for High Frequency and High Speed PCB
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the development of electronic communication technology, polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) material is widely used in the manufacture of high frequency and high speed printed circuit boards. For ordinary printed boards, delamination and blistering are common problems in its use, and there are many studies in the industry, but there are few studies and introductions on the delamination failure of PTFE substrates. In this paper, the reason of delamination of a double-layer PTFE substrate is analyzed by SEM&EDS, metallographic cross section and thermal stress test. It is found that the delamination may be related to the immersion of organic solvents (alcohol, isopropanol, acetone, etc.). Further, the PTFE substrate is immersed in different organic solvents for thermal stress test, and the results reproduce the delamination failure phenomenon. The mechanism of delamination is studied by fluorescence permeation technique, it was found that organic solvents could invade the gap between filler/glass fiber and PTFE, resulting in delamination of PTFE substrate.

articleTitle: Multi-scale Finite Element Simulation of 2.5D Advanced Packaging for Integrated Circuits during Manufacturing Process
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Under the new demands drived by artificial intelligence and high-performance computing, 2.5D packaging has become a typical advanced packaging technology. This paper proposes a multi-scale modeling and simulation method to focus on the reliability issues of integrated circuit 2.5D packages in various process manufacturing stages, such as underfill curing, epoxy molding compound (EMC) curing, and solder reflow between the interposer and the substrate. This paper establishes a model comprising underfill, EMC, interposer and substrate, and adopts multi-scale finite element analysis to study the 2.5D packaging deformation and stress patterns during the underfill and EMC curing processes, as well as solder reflow and other manufacturing processes. The deformation and stress behaviors of the 2.5D package throughout these processes are tracked. The results show that after curing the package exhibits a convex morphology with a warp value of 79.57μm for EMC, 22.72μm for the underfill layer, and 78.73μm for the silicon interposer layer. The warping deformation of EMC will affect the overall warping trend of the package. The Mises Stress values of the stress concentration areas in the EMC, base filler layer, and interposer layer increased by 42.29%, 12.38%, and 10.22% compared to the global model. After solder reflow, the maximum equivalent stress in the micro solder balls is found at the edge of the solder ball array, with a maximum stress value of 39.67 MPa. The maximum value of stress in each component of the package appeared at the mutual contact area of each component.

articleTitle: In-Situ Observation and Thermo-Mechanical Stress Analyses of Flip Chip Reflow Process via SEM-DIC Coupled Method
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The reliability of Flip Chip package is often compromised due to cracks in-between chips and underlying electronics, especially pre-solder and solder resist cracks, observed during the reflow process. These failures primarily caused by the mismatch in the coefficients of thermal expansion (CTE) between different materials, which cause the critical stress in intermetallic compounds on the copper pad layer and solder bump. Though failure and crack at bump are critical for Flip Chip package, the fracture mechanism of bump crack is still not well understood, and the resulting mechanical behaviors are even more complicated. To build a better understanding of the failure, this study introduces an innovative approach that combines Digital Image Correlation (DIC) and Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) for in-situ observation and quantitative characterization of the Flip Chip reflow process. Using a miniature heat loading platform in SEM, we track the sample as the temperature changing and further determine the strain field evolution via DIC. The result indicates that strain and stress concentrations primarily occur at the solder bumps edge leading to delamination and potential crack initiation. Large strain and hence stress field is also observed in the Y direction within the polyamide layer which leads to a potential failure risk. This detailed analysis provides insights into the thermal-mechanical stress distributions, ultimately aiming to improve the reliability of Flip Chip packages during thermal reflow tests.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Integrated System for Embedded Microchannel Cooling with Manifolds
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Driven by the demand for computing power by artificial intelligence big data models, integrated circuit chips are developing in the direction of increasing the number of transistors and increasing the chip area, which results in an increase in power. Increased power of computing chips poses challenges for thermal management. In the trend of miniaturization of electronic devices, efficient heat dissipation of high-power electronic components in a restricted space is increasingly important. Single-phase liquid cooling with embedded microchannels in chips provides low thermal resistances and high-efficiency heat exchange in a compact manner. But at present embedded cooling is still in the laboratory stage, the liquid supply system used is large, the reliability test for the liquid supply system is less, and the embedded microchannel integrated cooling system with liquid supply capacity needs to be further miniaturized. In this paper, an integrated thermal management method integrating pump and embedded microfluidics for high power chips is proposed, and the prototype of the microsystem is designed and developed. The overall size of the system is less than 13 cm3. A platinum film resistor is designed on the surface of embedded microchannel chip to simulate the heat dissipation of an actual chip. The liquid supply part is manufactured by 3D printing technology. The cooling capability of embedded microchannel and the liquid flow reliability of integrated embedded microfluidic system were tested respectively. The results show that when the chip power is 206W, the chip surface temperature rise can be controlled below 75°C. Under the flow rate of 118ml/min, after 96 hours of continuous cooling test, the system shows no reliability problems such as leakage and structural damage. This work integrates the embedded microchannel liquid cooling system as a whole and miniaturizes the system on the premise of ensuring its heat dissipation ability and working reliability, which has practical significance to promote the integration and industrialization of embedded cooling.

articleTitle: Reliability Analysis of Board Level Assembly with Different Lead Extraction Methods in HTCC Ceramic Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Temperature cycling is one of the important tests for assessing the reliability of packaging products at the board level. Ceramic lead flat packaging shell (CQFP/CSOP) is suitable for surface mount. Due to the mismatch of thermal expansion coefficients between ceramic materials and PCB materials, the device is prone to cracking at the solder joint between the lead and PCB during temperature cycling, leading to failure. The lead plays a role in stress buffering and release between the PCB and the ceramic tube shell. In response to the above situation, this article conducts simulation and experimental verification on the temperature cycling resistance of tube shells with different lead wire lead out forms. Comparing the temperature cycling resistance of different lead out forms of tube shells, a temperature cycling test was conducted on the tube shell, and the failed pins were metallographically sliced. The experiment verified the accuracy of the simulation, and the position of the maximum simulated stress point was the same as the experimental failure position. And calculate the number of temperature cycle lifetimes using the Coffin Manson formula, which is the same as the number of failed temperature cycles in the experiment. By comparing and analyzing the effects of different pin lead out schemes, bending heights, and welding lengths on the temperature cycling resistance of ceramics through simulation. The experimental and simulation results show that the higher the bending height of the lead wire, the higher the number of cycles of temperature fatigue life. When the lead wire adopts a top surface lead out forming structure, the temperature cycle life is much higher than other structures.

Author Keywords: High temperature co firing ceramic shell

articleTitle: Liquid Metal Thermal Interface Material for Packaging: Compatibility and Reactivity Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With advancements in packaging technology, the demand for enhanced heat dissipation capabilities is increasing. Consequently, research on metallic thermal interface materials with high heat dissipation capacities is emerging as a future trend. Liquid metal thermal interface materials, in particular, are attracting attention due to their distinctive properties. Unlike traditional thermal pastes or pads, liquid metals offer superior thermal conductivity and can conform to irregular surfaces, ensuring efficient heat transfer between components. Additionally, owing to the malleable nature of liquid metal, it can maintain coverage of the heat dissipation material even under significant thermal stress, thereby reducing the loss of heat dissipation performance. Consider of environmental protection and related concerns, gallium (Ga) emerges as the most suitable choice for liquid metal heat dissipation materials. This study investigates the feasibility of using liquid Ga as a thermal interface material (TIM), and identifies suitable metals for heat sink interfaces through a comparative analysis of the growth rates of intermetallic compounds (IMCs) formed between Ga and metals. Microstructural analysis can monitor the growth rate of the Ni-Ga IMC. The results show that the use of liquid Ga as TIM1, in combination with the nickel-gold interface of the heat sink, is one of the suitable materials for thermal management of the package.

articleTitle: Study on the influence of viscoelastic degree of curing of underfill on the warpage of fan-out packaging based on the generalized Maxwell model
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: At present, fan-out packaging has become the mainstream chip packaging technology and is considered one of the latest and most promising technologies. However, after the filler is filled and cured into the mold, the problem of chip warpage due to stress is unavoidable. Therefore, accurately predicting the viscoelastic behavior of the underfill during the curing process can help predict warpage and reasonably improve the packaging structure to reduce the warpage effect. In this paper, the influence of the curing degree of the bottom filling layer on the warpage of the chip during the curing process of liquid bottom filling was investigated. The study began with the experimental characterization of temperature-dependent material properties of the underfill system, through dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) and thermodynamic analysis. In addition, the heat of reaction and degree of cure during curing are measured by differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) testing. In order to save computing power, reduce the difficulty of simulation calculation, and the model has a high degree of symmetry, 1/4 of the simulation model was taken for research. The model consists of a substrate, a bottom filling, a micro-bump, an RDL layer, a chip and an EMC layer. Due to the focus on the viscoelastic mechanical behavior of the bottom filler, the RDL layer is simplified to two layers of PI polyamide sandwiched between a copper layer. The temperature load given to the entire model was 25°C to 110°C for 20 minutes, then back to room temperature. The simulation results show that significant changes in warpage occur after the underfill reaches 90% cure degree. Specifically, starting from the cooling stage, the warpage decreases substantially and reaches zero at a certain temperature point. Finally, reverse warpage forms at room temperature, changing from a “smile” to a “frown.”.

articleTitle: Study on the Effect of Fillers on Hygrothermal Properties of Underfill via in-Situ SEM-DIC Characterization
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Underfill is a critical material in advanced packaging, widely used in flip-chip interconnection to enhance packaging reliability. Polymer systems, primarily composed of epoxy resin and silica, are the most commonly used functional composite materials for underfill. However, moisture diffusion significantly impacts the performance of epoxy resin systems, posing a threat to product reliability. Previous studies have been focused on the chip level, utilizing wet-heat aging experimental methods and corresponding characterization techniques for performance analysis. In this study, the epoxy resin bulk material was subjected to aging treatment at 121°C and 100% relative humidity using an aging test chamber. Three-point bending fatigue crack propagation experiments were conducted using a universal testing machine, and scanning electron microscopy was employed to analyze the debonding behavior of different samples. Finally, in-situ three-point bending tests were carried out to observe microscale deformations in real-time, with the use of Digital Image Correlation (DIC) to quantify strain fields at the crack tip. Ultimately, in combination with positron annihilation experiments, the impact of humid aging environments on epoxy resin composite systems was analyzed.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Performance of Micro-Bump Flip-Chip Packaging Enhanced by Copper Paste
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In the rapidly evolving domain of microelectronics packaging technology, the pursuit of alternatives to traditional solder materials is driven by the imperative need for enhanced mechanical performance, reliability, and environmental sustainability. This study delves into the utilization of Cu paste as an interconnect material in Flip-Chip packaging, specifically focusing on micro-bumps with a diameter of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$20\mu\mathrm{m}$</tex>. The investigation centers on the effects of various sintering pressure conditions (lMPa, 3MPa, 5MPa, and 10MPa) on the mechanical and electrical performance of the packages. The experimental findings reveal that the samples sintered under the pressure of 5MPa exhibited the highest shear strength of 31.87MPa, suggesting a significant improvement over traditional solder-based packages. Conversely, sintering at 10MPa resulted in a reduction of shear strength to 28.78MPa, indicating a nuanced relationship between sintering pressure and mechanical performance. Regarding electrical performance, all samples maintained a resistivity around <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$13.5\Omega$</tex>, marginally surpassing the traditional solder resistivity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$14.2\Omega$</tex>. Thermal shock tests based on the JEDEC standard No. 22-A104-B were conducted on samples sintered at 1MPa. The tests, comprising 50, 100, 500, and 1000 cycles, were designed to simulate extreme operational conditions and assess the packaging's thermal stability and durability. This work substantiates the viability of Cu paste as a superior alternative to traditional solders, with enhancements observed in both mechanical strength and electrical resistivity.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Framework to Predict the Thermal Fatigue Lifetime of SiC Module with Sintered Silver Layer
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Sintered nano-silver is a widely used interconnect material in the third generation of power semiconductors, and is often used for service in extremely high-temperature environments due to its advantages of high melting temperature, making the reliability of interconnection more and more important for the overall reliability of the third-generation power semiconductor device. Different from traditional fatigue life prediction methods, a thermal fatigue lifetime dataset is collected based on Coffin-Manson thermal fatigue model and finite element simulations in this paper. A data-driven method based on the Support Vector Regression (SVR) model for predicting fatigue lifetime of sintered nano-silver layer is developed. The analysis includes identifying the key factors influencing interconnect reliability, and determining the main factors affecting the thermal fatigue lifetime of SiC modules. The results show that increasing the thickness of the sintered nano-silver interconnecting layer can enhance the lifetime of the interconnect structure, while elastic modulus and chip thickness negatively impact the lifetime of the sintered silver layer. The prediction accuracy and stability of the proposed data-driven SVR model are discussed and studied.

articleTitle: A Practical Evaluation Methodology for High-end POL Converters with Multiple Outputs
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In a high-density computation note of the data centre, at least 4~6 point-of-load (POL) converter modules (a specific product family of DC-DC converters) are installed to provide sufficient high current to the CPUs/GPUs. Normally this type of DC-DC converter takes about more than 20% of the total area of the motherboard, therefore the performance of that will highly affect the whole computation rack. This paper proposed a practical evaluation methodology for power converters, especially for the high-end POL converters with multiple outputs which are the representative products in the power electronics industry. The evaluation of a four-output POL converter is given as an example. Experiments show that the proposed methodology is feasible and can evaluate the performance of a POL converter comprehensively and accurately.

articleTitle: An Investigation of Process Parameters Effects on Void Formation in Fluxless Solder Paste for Power Module Packaging Applications via Formic Acid Vacuum Reflow Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The soldering process, essential for electrical and mechanical connections in the microelectronics industry, is crucial for IGBT die attachment as well. This paper investigates the impact of the vacuum reflow process on IGBT assembly using fluxless solder paste activated by formic acid. The paste demonstrates excellent print quality, formability, and consistent solder joint formation. Achieving satisfactory wetting, it compares favorably to traditional solder materials. Key optimized parameters include reflow temperature profiles, activation, and vacuum conditions, such as preheat time, time above liquid (TAL), peak temperature, formic acid concentration, and vacuum ratio. Crucially, formic acid's concentration and activation duration play significant roles in reducing void percentages, effectively decreasing voids from 7.5% to as low as 1%. Vacuum pressure also critically influences void behavior, with reductions in pressure resulting in increased void percentages from 1% to a high of 30%. This study underscores the potential of fluxless solder methodology as a sustainable and economic advancement in the power electronics industry.

articleTitle: A New Method of TGVs for Fast Filling of Metal Paste
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Through glass via (TGV) is a technology based on the wafer-level fabrication of glass substrates to realize vertical interconnection of electrical signals, which has the advantages of high frequency, low transmission loss, and high insulation, and has a wide range of application prospects in the fields of RF chip and sensing chip packaging. In order to provide a new method for fabricating TGVs, this study investigates the use of laser-induced etching to complete glass microvias construction and screen thick film printing to complete the metal filling of glass microvias. By examining the relationship between the concentration of the corrosion solution, reaction time, and microporous morphology in laser-modified glass, a standardized procedure for creating various glass microvias was developed; By observing the sidewall and surface morphology of glass microporous metals with microvia sizes of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$68 \mu\mathrm{m}, 85 \ \mu\mathrm{m}$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$128 \mu\mathrm{m}$</tex>, and testing the shrinkage and resistivity of microporous metals. The experimental results show that the glass microvia surface fabricated in this work is free of stress cracks. In addition, the shrinkage of the TGV sidewall metal paste is less than 9%, the resistivity is less than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.4 \times 10^{\wedge}(-4)\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$</tex>, and an aspect ratio as high as 15:1. Therefore, the research work in this paper provides a novel fabrication method for the fast and low-cost fabrication of TGVs.

articleTitle: A Compact LTCC Multi-Layer Balanced Filter for Microwave Application
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: A compact multi-layer balanced filter comprised of a Marchand balun and a lowpass filter realized by low temperature cofired ceramic (LTee) technology is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the broadside-coupled stripline is applied to meet the demands towards multi-layer structures in order to make full use of the advantage of L Tee technology. Then, a technique is introduced to adjust the even mode impedance by optimizing the coupling factor, which can be utilized to improve the device's operating performance. Based on the multi-layer structure, the size of the compact L Tee balanced filter is optimized to 3.2 mm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times 2.0$</tex> mm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times 2.7$</tex> mm. Through simulation, the proposed balanced filter demonstrates to be in consistent with the design specification and shows its feasibility to be implemented for system-in-package (SiP). In general, the present work offers an in-depth view and serves as a significant guidance for designing a compact L Tee balanced filter with great performance for microwave application.

articleTitle: Low-Temperature Pressureless Copper Sintering Under Formic Acid Atmosphere
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the development of power devices and the application of third-generation semiconductor materials (SiC and GaN), the electronics device tends to be high power density, high operating voltage and high operating temperature. However, traditional die bonding materials would break down at high temperature hindering the development of WBG semiconductors. Thus, sintered copper is regarded as an advanced materials due to its low price, excellent thermoelectric properties, and better resistance to electromigration. Nonetheless, the easy oxidation of copper and the high sintering temperature limit the application of sintered copper technology. In this paper, a low-temperature pressureless copper sintering method is described. Formic acid atmosphere was used to eliminate oxide particles from copper paste and oxide layer from copper substrate for high quality Cu-Cu interconnects. We also focus on the influence of temperature and atmosphere on pressureless sintered copper joints. Sintering was carried out at 210°C, 240°C, 270°C and 300°C for 30 minutes under formic acid and nitrogen. The results of shear test and scanning electron microscope (SEM) show that formic acid can significantly improve the sintering properties of copper particles. And the shear strength can reach 35.5 MPa at 240°C, which is 45.5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>(∽11 MPa) higher than nitrogen environment. In addition, single-chip devices were made for thermal resistance measurement and the results show that formic acid assisted sintered copper joints have a good thermal resistance of 0.653 K/W.

articleTitle: Improvement of Fe-Ni Filling Performance by Complex Agents for the On-Chip Inductor Application
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the trend of miniaturization of electronic products, the integration of passive devices has become a feasible way to save space. In the field of electronic packaging, the concept of on-chip power supply system has been proposed, which vertically stacks passive components such as inductors, capacitors, and resistors on the chip, enabling device functionality to be achieved in areas of chip size. In order to improve the performance of integrated micro inductors as much as possible, this study mainly uses electrodeposition method to prepare Fe-Ni alloy thin films as inductive magnetic materials in the amino sulfonate system. The citric acid and lactic acid were replaced by a new complexing agent (such as Ethylene Diamine Tetraacetic Acid, EDTA) in the new electroplating solution. The scanning electron microscopy (SEM) was used to observe the coating morphology and the confocal laser scanning microscope (CLSM) was used to observe the filling profiles. In order to meet the needs of on-chip inductor magnetic cores of different shapes, the flatness of the electroplating pattern was also measured. A good filling performance was achieved on the patterns of linear patterns and circular patterns without leakage plating and microvoids. Above all, the Fe-Ni filling performance was improved by adopting the complex agents. This study helps to deepen our understanding of Fe- Ni magnetic thin film materials for on-chip inductors.

articleTitle: High-density embedded silicon fan-out (H-eSiFO) process for a CMOS operational amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Embedded Silicon Fan-out (eSiFO) packaging is considered one of the ideal advanced packaging technologies due to its suitability for heterogeneous integration and its exceptional electrothermal performance. This study employed the H-eSiFO process to package a CMOS operational amplifier chip, analyzing the impact of various packaging process steps such as chip thinning and dicing, surface passivation, and the fabrication of the redistribution layer on chip performance. A corresponding test circuit was designed for the packaged chip to conduct functional performance tests. The results indicate that this packaging method does not adversely affect the chip's performance, demonstrating the potential of H -eSiFO in the advanced packaging of Chiplet.

articleTitle: Research on the Reliability of Packaging Interfaces Based on Silicon Bridge Embedment
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the development of microelectronic package, high computing power has become the new trend. Due to short interconnection distance, small parasitic parameters, and good heat dissipation, embedded packaging has attracted increasing attention in the industry. In embedded package, silicon bridge structures can achieve high bandwidth and low-cost local interconnection performance. This is an important method for enhancing integrated circuit performance through structural and process innovations based on existing equipment and materials. Intel has verified the signal integrity of silicon bridge structures with very high bandwidth interconnects. The reliability of embedded silicon bridge structures is particularly important. Fig. 1 shows the embedded silicon bridge structure surrounded by Ajinomoto Build-up Film (ABF), a polymer material with many pores. Especially in humid work environments, moisture can enter the ABF due to their moisture absorption characteristics. This can cause mismatched moisture expansion and thermal expansion due to the difference of materials, which generates larger stress and decreases the interface stress between ABF and silicon bridge. During unbiased highly-accelerated temperature and humidity stress test (uHAST), delamination at the interface between the silicon bridge and the dielectric, was observed in embedded packaging structures. To further explore the delamination failure mechanism at the interface, the study was conducted.

articleTitle: Effects of Silver Particle Size on Thermal Expansion Behavior of Low-Temperature-Sintered Silver Paste
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Silver conductive paste is a common interconnect material in semiconductor chip electronic packaging engineering. The usage temperature of soldered silver paste generally ranges from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$200^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$350^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>, and the main functional phase component is silver nanoparticles. The particle size of the powder significantly affects the thermal expansion coefficient of the silver paste sintered samples. In this study, five different particle sizes of silver powders with average particle sizes of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$30/60/80/100/200\text{nm}$</tex> were selected, and low-temperature sintered silver paste was prepared using the same process. The sintered samples of the silver paste were prepared at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$400^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> with the same process, and the density and compressive mechanical properties of the samples were analyzed. The thermal expansion characteristics of the silver sintered bodies between <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$200^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$350^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> were analyzed using Hot-Stage Microscope and Dilatometer. The results showed that all the silver powder could achieve sintering at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$400^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>. The smaller the average particle size, the larger the thermal expansion coefficient of silver paste sintered body. Silver sintered bodies with a particle size within 100nm can maintain good mechanical and electrical properties. The sintered bodies of silver powders with an average particle size of 30nm and 60nm had high thermal expansion coefficients resulting in higher thermal stresses during high-temperature usage. By selecting the particle size of silver powder, the thermal expansion behavior of the silver paste sintered body can be effectively adjusted to meet the packaging requirements under different operating temperature conditions.

articleTitle: Thermomechanical Behavior and Reliability of Redistribution Layers with Ni-plated Cu Traces for High Power Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The re-distribution layer (RDL) has been widely used in various high-performance applications because it greatly increases package density by rearranging the I/O terminals of the chip to an area with available space. However, the increase in current density and frequency in the Cu trace layer generates a large amount of Joule heat, especially in high power scenarios, which causes internal stresses in the RDL due to the mismatch of coefficients of thermal expansion (CTE) of different materials in the RDL, leading to reliability issues such as interface delamination between Cu trace and polyimide (i.e., Cu/PI interface), wafer warpage and so on. Aiming at providing guidance for the structural optimization of the Cu RDL in high-power applications, this study performs 3D finite element simulations to characterize the thermomechanical behavior of conventional Cu RDLs in fan-out wafer-level packages at different currents and Cu trace thicknesses, so as to predict potential failure sites and modes. A novel Ni-plated RDL is also used to comparatively investigate the effects of the ratio of Cu to Ni and the total thickness of the metal trace layer on the thermomechanical behavior of the Cu-Ni RDL. The results show that both Cu and Cu-Ni RDLs exhibit current crowding and stress concentration at straight trace sections and pad corners, with the maximum stresses appearing at pad edges. The interfaces between the metal trace, under bump metallization (UBM), and solder balls are critical for RDL reliability. For Cu RDL, increasing the thickness of the Cu trace can reduce current density and temperature, but result in an increase in maximum stress. So, a suitable Cu thickness needs to be selected for high-power applications. Besides, the raise of Ni content leads to the increase of the maximum stress and maximum current density in Cu traces, while the maximum temperature depends on its thickness. However, due to the superior adhesion of Ni to PI, its effect on interfacial reliability needs to be further investigated.

articleTitle: Finite Element Analysis of Planar Inductors With Soft Magnetic Encapsulation Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The rise of 5G, artificial intelligence, and other applications drives the demand for planar inductors based on PCB processes, due to the advantages of compatible processes, flat shapes, high power densities, reduced volumes, etc. In this paper, six kinds of soft magnetic encapsulation materials (SMEs) were selected to prepare planar dual-layer spiral inductors (PDSI). The actual PDSI device, as well as the six kinds of SMEs, were then processed. Based on the tested relative permeability of SMEs, FEM models were built and calibrated through the actual PDSI structures. Furthermore, FEM models of single-layer, double-layer, and multilayer inductors were established respectively, with analysis of the differences in magnetic properties. The results reveal that both Land Q of the PDSI exhibit a positive linear correlation with the relative permeability of the SMEs, and SMEs with high permeability limit the magnetic leakage. The multilayer inductor could achieve similar Land <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex> values with a smaller area compared with the planar inductor. However, the increase in thickness limits their application in thin devices. The models can be adjusted to match the SME properties and size parameters of the actual manufacturing process, contributing to simplified calculations for inductor design and performance analysis. Based on such analysis, the planar inductor designs based on in-house SME and PCB-compatible processes are adjusted for high-frequency applications.

articleTitle: Parasitic RLGC Properties of High-density Through-Glass Via
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The increasing demands for high-performance signal transmission in microelectronic systems have led to the development of advanced integration techniques, such as three- dimensional (3-D) integration. Through-glass via (TGV) technology offers superior electrical characteristics compared to conventional silicon and PCB. However, the parasitic RLGC parameters of high-density TGVs lead to signal attenuation, distortion, and reflection, posing challenges to signal integrity. In this paper, the HFSS electromagnetic simulation software is employed to analyze the transmission performance of high-density TGVs with a Ground-Signal-Ground (GSG) transmission structure across the 10–50 GHz frequency range. The parasitic RLGC parameters are extracted, and solution formulas for the parasitic inductance and resistance of TGVs in three morphologies are derived. Additionally, the contribution of TGV internal inductance to total parasitic inductance is also discussed. The results of this work provide insights into signal transmission in high-density TGVs, contributing to the development of microsystem integration.

articleTitle: An SEM-Based Finite Element Analysis of Cu-Ag Sintered Joints on Thermal Shock Reliability
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Copper-silver (Cu-Ag) composite sintered joints are increasingly investigated in power module die-attach applications due to their cost-effectiveness and resistance to electromigration. However, the inherent porosity in such materials results in mechanical failures, such as cracking and delamination, especially during thermal shock (TS) tests. This research investigated the enhancement of thermal shock resistance in copper-silver sintered materials through the solvent modulation of epoxy resin to fill the sintering voids. Firstly, two types of copper-silver composite joints (with and without epoxy resin) were produced under identical conditions. Afterwards, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) cross-sectional analysis, electrical and thermal conductivity tests, as well as TS tests, were conducted. Then, a model based on finite element method (FEM) model was developed, using Python image processing code and the reconstructed SEM cross-section images. Such simulation, validated by experimental results, is capable of analyzing the influence of epoxy for such composite sintered joints. Though epoxy reduced the electrical and thermal conductivity, it improved the shear strength and thermal shock resistance with a more evenly distributed thermal stress within the sintered joint. This research demonstrated the importance of solvent modulation of Cu-Ag sintered joints for thermal shock reliability analysis.

articleTitle: Optimization of Creep Constitutive Modeling of Lead-Free Solder Using Gene Expression Programming Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this paper, the GEP method is utilized to derive an ontological model for creep data, focusing on the mechanical properties and structural deformation mechanisms of solder at different scales. By analyzing the effect of micro-and meso-structural morphology on the material, experimental validation is provided for the construction of an ontological model that depicts the viscoplasticity of Pb- Free solder in detail. Iterative optimization of a larger population of experimental samples will drive the development of a fine-grained intrinsic model that will be supported by solid theoretical and empirical evidence, advancing the field towards deeper understanding and innovation. In this study, the GEP algorithm is used to fit the intrinsic model of solder creep and is shown to have good fitting results. The advantages of GEP in equation model fitting are the simplicity of its heuristic algorithm, the ease of its implementation and its good optimization results. In addition, GEP is highly flexible, adaptable and robust to noisy data. After comparing the experimental data simulations, it is found that GEP is able to accurately analyze and predict in the establishment and optimization of creep model, which brings an important contribution to the field of solder research.

articleTitle: A Low-Temperature Ag-Ag Direct Bonding Technology Towards Ten-Thousand-Level Microbumps Arrays Utilizing Plasma-Induced Grown Nanoparticles of Silver Oxide
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the development of microelectronics technology, the semiconductor industry has entered the postMoore's Law era. Many semiconductor manufacturing companies have showcased their 3D integration solutions, such as Foveros of Intel and AMD's 3D V-Cache. The current mainstream approach to 3D stacking involves utilizing through silicon vias (TSV), Cu micro-bumps, and lead-free solder to achieve 3D-IC packaging or heterogeneous integration. However, the formation of brittle intermetallic compounds (IMCs) and the manifestation of size effects can lead to higher electrical resistance and severe reliability issues in solder-based micro-bumps for 3D-IC packaging. Recently, our group has invented a novel interconnection technology through Ag-Ag direct bonding, utilizing plasma-induced grown nanoparticles of silver oxide, whose process was designed for 3D-ICs interconnects. Through controlling the surface morphology of plasma-induced grown silver oxide, this technology can effectively overcome the initial asperities on the bonding surface, thus accommodating larger surface roughness (> 100 nm). In this work, for the first time, we have demonstrated the application of this technology to achieve “point-to-point” bonding with a high-density micro-bump array at tenthousand-level, whereby finding the optimal bonding parametric settings. The wafer-level copper micro-bump arrays (diameter < 30 μm) are prepared by using photolithography, electroplating, and chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) processes, and Ag is deposited as the all-metal bonding layer using magnetron sputtering technology. Subsequently, plasma-induced nanoparticles of silver oxide (Plasma-induced Ag2O NPs) have grown on the Ag layer with our patented technology. More importantly, we design a new bonding scheme with a “two-steps” process to achieve lowtemperature solid-state bonding with high-density micro-bump array at the ten-thousand-level, which comprised with two stages: the pre-bonding stage and the final bonding stage. Due to the excellent plastic deformation ability of Ag, the prebonding stage allows for pre-deformation of the Ag layer, ensuring sufficient contact between micro-bumps, thereby providing more engineering tolerance for the flatness of the chip substrate. The final bonding stage provides adequate temperature and time, which allows the silver oxide nanoparticles to fully decompose, thereby promoting the diffusion and rearrangement of Ag atom at the bonding interface. Additionally, the scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and focused ion beam microscopy (FIB) are used to observe the morphology of the micro-bump array and the bonding interface. Shear force testing is used to assess the shear strength of the bonding interface. This study has provided a low-cost alternative technology for the advanced 3D-ICs packaging interconnection method and paved the way for the future development towards high-density interconnection applications.

articleTitle: Exploring New Interconnection Materials and Techniques for High-Reliability IC Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Accompanied by the increasing electrification and informationization in various devices and equipment, electric circuits (IC) are required to work in complicated and harsh environments. This significantly challenges the reliabilities of interconnections that bear electron current, heat, and mechanical loading. This research focuses on improving the reliability of interconnections serving at high-density current, wide temperature range, and high temperature, by exploring novel materials/techniques including i) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta\text{Sn}$</tex> structure and orientation control technique, ii) SnGaX full solid-solution (SS) solder alloys, and iii) Sn-CuNi and Ga-Al transient liquid phase bonding (TLPB) technique. Controlling <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta\text{Sn}$</tex> structure and orientation is realized by harnessing the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta\text{Sn}$</tex> heterogeneous nucleation using seed crystal, and this technique can be applied to Sn-based solder joints to combat reliability problems such as electromigration that is heavily influenced by the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta\text{Sn}$</tex> orientation. The SnGaX SS solder is a novel patented material that takes advantage of Ga solid solution strengthening to achieve balanced strength and ductility. As opposed to the typical third-generation Pb-free solder Innolot that is too strong to bear plastic deformation, SnGaX SS solder demonstrates a good thermal cycling performance. Sn-CuNi and Ga-Al TLPB provide new solutions for power electronic assembling and they show good mechanical performance and low cost.

Index Terms: Field Emission Gun Scanning Electron Microscopy

articleTitle: The Effect of Plasma Surface Activation Treatment on Capillary Flow Wettability of the Underfill Adhesive in the Standoff Gap of Si/Underfill/Si Bonded Structure in 3D ICs
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The activation effects of mixed 02/ Ar plasma on the underfill capillary flow wettability in 100 µm sub-gap layers using radio-frequency capacitively coupled plasma (RF CCP) and microwave electron cyclotron resonance plasma (MW ECR) are systematically investigated in this study. To mimic the die/underfill/substrate structure in actual 2.5D/3D integrated packaging, the Si/underfill/Si adhesion structure is designed. Results demonstrate that as the proportion of O2 in mixed 02/ Ar plasma increases, the surface energy at the substrate center rises steadily. Moreover, the enhancement of surface energy is greater using MW ECR than RF CCP, enabling rapid wetting and dispensing of underfill on both die and substrate layers. Surface energy components measurements reveal that the contribution of mixed 02/ Ar plasma to the surface energy of substrate is primarily due to an increase in the polar component. Analysis results of X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) surface chemical compositions of the substrate center after plasma treatment show a decrease in the carbon contamination peak and the generation of specific polar functional groups (C=O, O-C=O, Si-OH). Subsequent underfill dispensing and curing after plasma activation treatment result in reduced delamination in the Si/underfill/Si structure, along with a decrease in porosity. This comprehensive characterization of plasma surface activation treatment brings a better understanding of plasma modification, plasma equipment, and the enhancement of reliability in advanced packaging.

articleTitle: Failure Mechanisms Investigation of Through Glass via (TGV) Under Thermal Annealing and Shock
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: 2.5D advanced packaging technology is a promising solution for “more than Moore”. TGV interposer has attracted growing attention for the high-frequency applications in 2.5D advanced packaging due to its low dielectric constant and loss tangent, etc. Some typical failure modes of TGV structure were discussed in the previous literatures. However, there is a lack of systematic research on the failure mechanisms of TGV under annealing and thermal shock condition. This paper focused on the failure mechanisms of TGV under different thermal conditions using both experimental and simulation methods. Annealing experiment was carried on the TGV sample at 400 °C for different periods. Crack appeared in the glass at the top corner of TGV after annealed at 400 °C for 5 min. With the increasing annealing period from 5 min to 30 min at 400 °C, the protrusion height of TGV increased from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.61\ \mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.21\ \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>, and the simulated protrusion height increased from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.50\ \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.89\ \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>. The FEA simulation result showed that stress concentration was located in the top corner of TGV, the stress was 1456.63 MPa at 400 °C for 5 min. TGV samples were subjected to 0, 300, 500 and 1000 cycles under the condition of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-55\ ^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> to 150 °C. Glass will crack around TGV-RDL after 300 thermal shock cycles. The stress was found concentrated around TGV-RDL according to FEA, which was 370.34 MPa. Crack appeared at the bottom corner of the TGV after 1000 cycles. The equivalent plastic strain at the bottom corner of TGV increased from 1.09 to 3.64 with the cycles increased from 300 to 1000. This article analyzes failure mechanisms of TGV and provides design guidelines for the pretreatment process of TGV. The simulation result offers information for the reliability evaluation of TGV.

articleTitle: Study of Ga-21.5In-10Sn/Cu Liquid-Solid Interfacial Reaction and Reaction Barrier Layer
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Gallium-based liquid metal combines metallic conductivity and liquid mobility, and is the material of choice for wearable flexible electronics. However, flexible interconnect structures represented by Ga-21.5In-10Sn/Cu undergo spontaneous reactions at the liquid-solid interface, leading to interfacial instability, which reduces the reliability of the flexible devices and causes the failure of liquid-metal-based electronic devices. Therefore, it is necessary to inhibit the spontaneous interfacial reaction of Ga-21.5In-10Sn/Cu in order to improve its reliability. Ni, Ni-P and Ni-Co alloy coatings are difficult to react with Ga-21.5In-10Sn at room temperature and the preparation process is well established, so these three coatings are used as a reaction blocking layer between Ga-21.5In-10Sn and copper. The results show that, when heated at 50°C for 1h, the interfacial reaction between Ga-21.5In-10Sn and Cu occurs, and more brick intermetallic compounds CuGa2 are generated; However, there is no intermetallic compound with Ni-P/Cu, Ni/Cu, and Ni-Co/Cu, indicating that there is no interfacial reaction between Ga-21.5In-10Sn and the three coatings, and that the three coatings have a certain reaction blocking effect. Under the condition of 120°C and heating for 1 h, the integrity of the Ni-P coating is destroyed and intermetallic compounds are produced, losing the blocking effect on the interfacial reaction; on the other hand, the Ni and Ni-Co coatings still do not produce intermetallic compounds, which can obviously inhibit the interfacial reaction between Ga-21.5In-10Sn/Cu and improve the reliability of the flexible devices. The upper temperature limit of the pure Ni coating as a reaction barrier for Ga-21.5In-10Sn/Cu is as high as 200°C. At a higher temperature of 280°C, the Ni and Ni-Co coatings can be used to inhibit the reaction of Ga-21.5In-10Sn/Cu. At a higher temperature of 280°C for 1 h, Ni-Co as Ga-21.5In-10Sn/Cu reaction barrier still shows excellent chemical inertness. In addition, the Ni-P coating has poor electrical conductivity, while Co has higher electrical conductivity than Ni. Among these three types of barrier layers, the conductivity of Ni-Co is more favorable. Therefore, Ni-Co has better application prospects as a reactive barrier layer for liquid metal Ga-21.5In-10Sn.

articleTitle: Study on Warpage of Flip Chip Structure Based on Finite Element Analysis and Machine Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Warpage has always been a challenge in package, large value of warpage will lead to a series of problems such as delamination, crack et al. Finite element analysis (FEA) has been widely used in package, because of its comprehensive theory, diverse methods, convenient modification and low cost. Meanwhile, machine learning (ML) is good at constructing complex relationship between multiple features and target variables. Nowadays, the packaging structure is increasingly complex, and it is increasingly difficult to analyze and optimize directly according to the mechanical properties of materials, and ML is a potential solution. In this paper, we combine FEA with ML to study the warpage issue in a flip-chip structure. Three ML methods, polynomial regression, support vector machine (SVM), and artificial neural network (ANN) are used. Finally, the optimal results of ML are verified using FEA. A Flip Chip Ball Grid Array (FCBGA) structure was constructed in Abaqus and the CTE and Young's modulus of five materials were chosen as variables. The results show that, first of all, all of three ML models can excellently construct the mapping relationship between the ten variables of the ML model and the warpage value. The R-square index for all three models reaches above 0.999. In addition, traditional ML methods such as polynomial regression can achieve better results than SVM and ANN for warpage problems. Finally, it also indicates that compared to commonly used methods such as response surface methodology (RSM), the ML model can consider the impact of more variables on the results and optimize the warpage more effectively. This paper demonstrates the feasibility of using the ML algorithm for regression, prediction, and optimization of results in finite element analysis and applies it to warpage simulations.

articleTitle: Design Optimization and Performance Evaluation of Direct Liquid Single-Phase Jet Impingement Heat Sink for High-Performance Computing Chips
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: This study introduces a prototype of direct liquid jet impingement heat sink for flip-chip (FC) packaged high-performance computing chips. The direct jet impingement heat sink was fabricated using 3D printing technology, with its structure and geometric parameters optimized. Experiments were conducted to determine the cooling capacity of the heat sink under various heat fluxes, where thermal test vehicle (TTV) chips were employed to emulate the heat generation of high-performance computing chips. Experimental results reveal a cooling capacity of 1000W, with a maximum temperature rise of about l06.63°C compared to the inflow. Under uniform heat flux conditions, the experimental and numerical results are in strong agreement, with a maximum deviation of only 1.77°C. However, under conditions of hot spot heat flux and background heat flux, larger deviations emerge between experimental and numerical results, primarily due to the absence of coolant boiling in the numerical model. In future studies, optimization of heat sink structure and investigation of 3D printing materials will be conducted to enhance cooling efficiency and durability, while more precise and volume manufacturing techniques are supposed to be used to advance the proposed direct liquid jet impingement heat sink technology.

articleTitle: Characterization Analysis for High-Temperature Evolution Features of Fine Silver Sintered Joints
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the continuous change of microelectronics technology and the urgent requirements of industrial development, electronic devices are developing in the direction of high-frequency, highly integrated and highly intelligent. Especially in some application areas, electronic devices need to face high temperature, strong radiation, high current density and other harsh service environment. This brings great challenges to the packaging technology of power chips in the device. At present, among the solutions for high-temperature power chip packaging, silver sintering technology can realize the requirements of low-temperature connection and high-temperature service, and has excellent thermal conductivity and conductivity and high-temperature reliability, which is a good interconnect technology solution for power chip packaging improvement, and there is an urgent need to carry out the related interconnect process, failure mechanism, and reliability assessment research work. This paper focuses on microfine silver sintered interconnect joints, focusing on silver sintering under different interconnect processes, and explores the sinter layer testing and characterization methods. Through the electrical and thermal characterization of sintered silver specimens under different sintering processes, a non-destructive test method is explored to analyze the feasibility of sintered layer resistance changes, with the goal of obtaining an effective test to the change process after sintering at different temperatures to achieve non-destructive quality testing of sintered silver joints and to provide a basis for the design of reliability tests for power chip packaging.

articleTitle: Research on Novel Thermal Management Technology in the Field of Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The escalation in power density and the trend towards miniaturization in electronic devices have led to an increase in both power consumption and heat flux density in integrated circuits (ICs). This surge compromises the performance, reliability, and longevity of ICs, posing a critical threat to their operational integrity. Consequently, the advancement of integrated circuits towards greater miniaturization, enhanced integration, reduced energy consumption, and elevated performance is significantly hampered by the inefficacies of existing thermal management technologies. Traditional cooling solutions, such as air cooling, liquid cooling, and heat spreader coatings, despite providing thermal mitigation in earlier generations of IC technology, now fall short due to their high costs, low thermal conductivity efficiency, issues with thermal expansion, and environmental implications. These challenges underscore the urgent need for more efficient thermal management solutions to support the future evolution of integrated circuits. Emerging thermal management technologies, including microchannel cooling, thermoelectric cooling, advanced thermal interface materials, piezoelectric pump-driven microfluidic cooling, and three-dimensional integrated package cooling, represent promising avenues for addressing the thermal bottlenecks in IC development. This paper proposes a sustainable and effective thermal management strategy, juxtaposing traditional thermal management methodologies against these innovative technologies. Through a multidimensional comparison, it elucidates the superior efficacy of new thermal management solutions in meeting the evolving demands of integrated circuits. Furthermore, it delves into future research directions and articulates the principal challenges confronting the field.

articleTitle: Efficient Prediction of Equivalent Thermo-Mechanical Properties for Embedded Unit Cells in Reliability Simulations of Complex Circuit Wiring Structures Using a Transformer-CNN Model
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In the field of reliability simulation and analysis of complex circuit wiring structures, the remarkable effectiveness of the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) in wiring diagram recognition has shown great potential for predicting the equivalent performance of partitions of complex wiring structures.
