Considering the heavy computational burden of simulation and the fact that the planes of complex wiring structures have long-range disordered and short-range ordered structural features, it is necessary to consider the influence of the long-range surroundings on their short-range partitions, which can be achieved by using the Embedded Unit Cell (EUC) modelling approach. Simply applying a CNN model can capture the wiring features, but it cannot accurately learn the relationship between such central regions in complex wiring structures that are influenced by the surrounding regions. This paper introduces a Transformer-CNN hybrid deep learning model, which extracts local features from partitioned wiring diagrams using CNN and employs a Transformer to learn the relationships among them through a self-attention mechanism, and finally discusses the learning accuracy and efficiency. This method aims to create a more efficient process for predicting the equivalent thermo-mechanical properties of EUC partitions in reliability simulations of wiring structures. The results demonstrate that the model performs excellently in terms of prediction accuracy and efficiency. The model predicts that the coefficient of determination (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) between the values of four types of anisotropic equivalent thermo-mechanical properties (Young's modulus, shear modulus, Poisson's ratio, and coefficient of thermal expansion) and the results of simulation are all higher than 0.99, a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) less than 0.000646, indicating the model's ability to accurately learn and map equivalent thermo-mechanical property values from the wiring diagrams. Handling over 260,000 datasets, the model required 29 hours for training and only 1 hour for prediction, less than one-tenth the time needed for simulations, enhancing the efficiency of the EUC modeling method for engineering reliability analysis of complex circuit wiring structures.

articleTitle: New Homogenization Method for Equivalent Thermal Expansion Coefficient of Wiring Structures Using Embedded Unit Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Thermal mismatch, as a crucial factor affecting the thermal reliability of IC products, is of great importance to control. Due to the presence of multi-level cross-scale structures inside IC products, considering the constraints of computational resources, it is inevitable to homogenize the complicated structures within IC products to simplify the models during finite element simulations. Among these structures, routing structures like RDL, BEOL, and conductive layers in PCBs, exhibit significant heterogeneity, resulting in severe thermal mismatch issues. Therefore, homogenizing the thermal-mechanical performance of wiring structures is essential for controlling thermal mismatch in IC products. This paper proposes a partition homogenization approach based on the embedded unit cells for wiring layers, combined with mesoscopic finite element analysis, to calculate the equivalent thermal expansion coefficient of wiring structures in IC products. In this paper, 30 samples of wiring structures were randomly selected. Each sample was partitioned, and the equivalent thermal expansion coefficients of each partition were calculated using the above homogenization methods. The homogenized partitions were then assembled to establish the corresponding equivalent models. Furthermore, pixelated detailed models were established for each wiring structure sample as a reference, and the thermal expansion simulation results of the equivalent models were compared to validate the rationality of using embedded cells to calculate the equivalent thermal expansion coefficients of wiring partitions. Additionally, compared to the periodic unit cell, using embedded unit cell to homogenized the thermal expansion coefficients of each partition can avoid the assumption of periodic response in classical homogenization theories, better aligning with the non-periodic structural characteristics of wiring layers and providing certain advantages in equivalent accuracy. The entire process was implemented through batch processing scripts, ensuring the efficiency of the partition homogenization process. Finally, the limitations of the partition homogenization method were briefly discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Investigation of Power Device Solder Void Formation by Two-Phase Flow Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Higher power capabilities and efficiencies require a shift from wire-bonded power packages to copper clip-bonded power packages, with larger clip and die expected. This trend has resulted in larger clip-attach and die-attach areas, creating challenges with higher rates of solder voiding, and resulting in deterioration in thermal and electrical resistance, as well as package reliability. There is a high demand to understand the formation and growth mechanisms of solder voids. When direct process observation is not practical, visualization by numerical analysis is a feasible way to explore the reaction process inside the solder. This study applies the Volume of Fluid (VOF) method to track the interface evolution between solder flux bubbles and molten liquid solder to depict the flux evaporation and relevant dynamic processes within the liquid solder. A combination of 2D and 3D domain Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations reveal that the clip with slots has fewer and smaller solder voids formed compared to the full coverage clip. The reflow soldering experiment result validated this trend. The 2D domain results indicate that evaporated flux bubbles are trapped by solder-repelling spots near or passing through, revealing an incomplete solder wetting formation mechanism. The 3D domain results show that clip warping can cause uneven outlet areas with different outgassing velocities, leading to voids forming around small outlets. The combination of 2D and 3D domain CFD simulations is proved to be an effective way to provide visual scenarios to explain solder flux behavior during the reflow process and can serve as an applicable technique to theoretically evaluate further optimization methods.

articleTitle: Simulation and Experimental Analysis of Contactless Chip Pickup Process Based on a Vortex Flow Gripper
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Chip pickup and transfer is a critical process in 3D heterogeneous integration (3D HI). With the rapid advancement in chip thinning and interconnect density in the post-Moore era, mechanical scratches and electrostatic interference on the chip surface caused by traditional vacuum pickup cannot be ignored. Therefore, the development of a pneumatic stable noncontact chip pickup method is the key to maintain high yields in 3D HI. This paper designs a noncontact pickup gripper based on vortex flow for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$50{\mu m}$</tex> ultra-thin chips. A guard structure of the gripper was designed, which can maintain the position of stable state after multiangle loading and improve the loading fault-tolerance. We explored the underlying mechanism of pneumatic noncontact pickup through computational fluid dynamics simulation (CFD). Further, a high-precision vortex platform was built by integrating high-precision motion module, levelling and positioning module, air circuit module, sensing and testing module and control module. Based on the experimental platform, we investigated the pickup force characteristics, radial pressure distribution, and oscillations for different intake pressure and analyzed their influence on the noncontact pick-up effect. Stable noncontact pickup of target chips was achieved finally with inlet pressure more than 20 kPa. This study provides research methods and optimization ideas for stable noncontact picking of microchips, offering theoretical and experimental bases for selecting the optimal air intake pressure in practical applications.

articleTitle: Finite Element Modeling Optimized by Solder Joint Morphology Simulation for Electrical-Magnetic-Thermal-Force Multi-Physical Field Coupling of PCB Assemblies
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Analyzed the overall system reliability by coupling the effects of multi-physical field conditions. Proposed a method of finite element multi-physical fields whole-process analysis for soldered printed circuit board assemblies of various devices (BGA, CGA, QFP, SOP, DIP). The calculation is completed through the ANSYS platform, coupling multi-physical fields finite element simulation contains electric-magnetic-thermal-vibration fields. The lowest free energy principle of free liquid surface is introduced to calculate the surface morphology evolution of solder joints. Solidify surface files formed by the morphology simulation, improved the accuracy of the finite element three-dimensional model successfully. Decoupled of multi-physical fields processes by applying magneto-electric fields' thermal and force effects to thermal cycling and vibration analysis, achieved full fields coupled finite analysis. Life prediction was carried out using the mechanical properties obtained from the above finite element calculations through three-interval model, obtained life expectancy results for different types of devices.

articleTitle: New Equivalent Approach and Optimized Strategy for Evaluating Warpage Characteristics in PCB Milling Process
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In the production of large-scale multi-layer Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs), warpage is a common phenomenon that can lead to various reliability issues during assembly and packaging, ultimately affecting the quality and yield of the final products. This study aims to provide a comprehensive assessment of PCB warpage during the milling process by examining the underlying stress and strain mechanisms. A novel equivalent method of the milling process was developed, and the impact of milling process on PCBs under static conditions were analyzed using finite element analysis (FEA). The research concentrated on the warpage evolution and the forces exerted at the milling boundaries. Both the Rectangular Plate (RP) model and the Notched Rectangular Plate (NRP) model were employed to simulate the lamination and milling processes. The high level of morphological agreement between the simulation results and the measurements from shadow moiré analysis substantiates the validity of this approach. The average error in warpage values was found to be 3.4%, verifying the reliability and accuracy of the simulation. Additionally, the impact of differences in stiffness between the milled and residual areas on PCB warpage was discussed.

articleTitle: Numerical Modeling and Validation of Silicone-Type Receiving Layer for Micro-LED Laser-Based Mass Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Micro-LED display technology distinguishes itself within a plethora of display technologies by delivering high photoelectric conversion efficiency, superior energy yield ratio, as well as response times in the nanosecond regime. As one of the highly effective ways for mass transferring of Micro-LEDs, laser-based mass transfer can rapidly and accurately transfer Micro-LED chips to a target substrate. However, the scarcity of in-depth research into receiving materials for Micro-LED laser-based mass transfer and the limitations of contemporary testing methodologies have significantly impeded the advancement of Micro-LED receiving materials. In this study, we propose a numerical modeling approach for a silicone-type receiving layer material tailored to Micro-LED laser-based mass transfer process and corroborate the feasibility and practical utility of this model through bespoke impact testing. Furthermore, utilizing this technique, we predict the impact response of silicone-type receiving material under conditions typical for Micro-LED dimensional mass transfer. The findings reveal that for a silicone-type receiving layer material with a thickness of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{273}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex> subjected to impact velocities of 5 m/s, 10 m/s, 15 m/s, and 20 m/s, the corresponding experimental impact depths are: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{14.95}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m},\ \mathbf{20.56}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m},\ \mathbf{25.99}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{69.2}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex> —closely mirroring the simulated depths of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{11.18}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m},\ \mathbf{14.93}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m},\ \mathbf{21.49}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{63.96} \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex>, thus affirming the viability of the modeling technique. Predictive experiments at Micro-LED scale suggest that within a certain range, increases in the thickness and area of silicone-type layer imprints reduce the chip's final kinetic energy, indicating a direct, positive correlation between the dimensions of the receiving material and the efficiency of chip reception. This research presents pivotal insights into the future landscape of Micro-LED packaging materials and enriches our understanding of the laser-based transfer process.

articleTitle: Stress Analysis and Optimization of POP Stacked Solder Joints Under Power Cyclic Loading
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: A finite element analysis model of POP stacked solder joints was established, and the stress distribution of POP stacked solder joints under power cyclic loading was analyzed based on the ANAND intrinsic model. The height of the upper solder j oint, the height of the lower solder joint, the thickness of the top PCB, and the thickness of the middle PCB are selected as the structural parameters, and the stress of the solder j oint is taken as the target value. 27 groups of test combinations with different parameter levels are designed, modeled and simulated by Taguchi's test method, and the bi-objective optimization of the stress of the upper solder joint and the stress of the lower solder joint is carried out by the grey correlation method. The results show that both top and bottom solder joint stresses decrease with the increase of top solder joint height and bottom solder joint height, and increase with the increase of top substrate thickness and middle substrate thickness; The optimum combination of structural parameter levels is 0.35 mm for the top solder joint height, 0.28 mm for the bottom solder joint height, 0.1 mm for the top substrate thickness, and 0.3 mm for the middle substrate thickness, the maximum stresses of the optimized upper and lower solder joints decreased by 0.38 MPa and 0.417 MPa, respectively, which realized the optimization of the structural parameters of the solder joints.

articleTitle: Efficient and Accurate Calculation of Equivalent Thermal Conductivity of Wiring Structures in Mesoscopic Scale and Intelligent Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the development of artificial intelligence and autonomous driving technologies, the complexity of the conductive layers (CDLs) in the integrated circuit (IC) is increasing, leading to severe thermomechanical reliability issues. To ensure the reliability, temperature distribution must be accurately simulated. It is impractical to capture all wiring structure features during modeling, so partition homogenization methods have been proposed. However, most current equivalence methods still have limitations when dealing with complex microstructures. Thus, the equivalent thermal conductivity (ETC) calculation method based on mesoscopic finite element analysis (MFEA) was proposed, which fully takes into account the detailed structural characteristics of each partition to batch calculate the their ETCs through automated scripts, and ultimately to achieve efficient and accurate simulation of the macroscopic temperature field. The superiority of the proposed method in predicting the temperature distribution of IC products with complex wiring structures was verified by comparing the results of the proposed method in this paper with those obtained from linear interpolation model (LIM) and series-parallel model (SPM) methods. To further improve the computational efficiency of ETC, the study also introduced Global Context Vision Transformers (GC ViT) for fast predicting ETC, which provides the possibility that this equivalent method can meet the industrial requirements for efficiency. In conclusion, the scheme in this study not only provides an efficient simulation strategy for the thermal management design of IC products, but also opens up new possibilities for the future application of deep learning techniques in material property prediction and complex system modeling in a wider range of engineering fields.

articleTitle: Strain Rate Effect on Indentation Behavior of Polycrystalline Sintered Silver Nanoparticles Based on Crystal Plasticity Finite Element Method
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Based on crystal plasticity finite element simulation, this study explores the meso-scale mechanical behavior of polycrystalline sintered silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) under different strain rates and indentation depths using the nanoindentation method. A three-dimensional finite element indentation model of polycrystalline sintered AgNPs was constructed in ABAQUS, and the mechanical behavior of the polycrystalline sintered AgNPs was investigated under different indentation depths (500nm, 100nm, and 2000nm) and strain rates <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(0.05\mathrm{s}^{-1},0.1\mathrm{s}^{-1}, \text{and}\ 0.2\mathrm{s}^{-1})$</tex> conditions for indentation tests. As the representative parameters, the material properties, such as load-displacement curves, hardness, cumulative shear strain and the crystal orientation, were investigated. The experimental results show that the effect of indentation strain rate on the load-displacement curve is obvious, and the applied load on the indenter increases with the increase of strain rate. This underlines the strain rate effect of sintered AgNPs at the mesoscopic scale. In addition, the indentation strain rate and hardness are significantly associated in a linear relationship, indicating that the hardness is extremely sensitive to the indentation strain rate, and thus the plastic deformation behavior is significantly affected by the loading rate.

articleTitle: Simulation Studies of Hygro-Thermal-Vapor Induced Stresses and Interface Delamination in High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) Package With Different Numbers of Stacked Chips During Reflow Process
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In recent times, there has been a pressing need for research and development (R&D) initiatives aimed at improving the reliability, endurance, and cost efficiency of high bandwidth memory (HBM). This necessity arises from the escalating demand for sophisticated applications like high-performance computing (HPC) and artificial intelligence (AI). Within the realm of reliability concerns, issues pertaining to package damage and failure resulting from the absorption of moisture by polymer materials have gained significant prominence. This investigation involves the development of finite element models depicting stacked DRAM chips with various layer counts (N=2, 4, 8, 12, 16, and 20). The chips undergo preconditioning treatment at 85°C/85% relative humidity (RH) with a duration of 168 hours, followed by reflow to ascertain the distribution of moisture concentration. To examine moisture diffusion during the reflow process, the so-called internal source method is adopted. Considering the hygro-thermal-vapor loads, the distribution of von Mises stress at the peak reflow soldering temperature is determined. The findings of the simulations indicate that the moisture content within the package is not fully saturated post-preconditioning. Moreover, the region of unsaturation expands with an increase in the number of stacked chip layers, except for an unusual decline observed at N = 20. Throughout the reflow process, moisture desorption occurs rapidly. Nonetheless, a substantial amount of moisture persists within the HBM package at the final phase of reflow process, leading to the generation of saturated vapor pressure, thereby facilitating interfacial crack propagation and delamination. In HBM packages subjected to hygro-thermal-vapor loads, the topmost or bottommost chips exhibit heightened susceptibility to cracking and delamination.

articleTitle: A Study of the $\mu$ -Solder Joint on Ajinomoto Build-up Film using the Solder on Pad (SOP) process for Multi-Chip Module
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Ajinomoto Build-Up Film (ABF), prized for its superior properties compared to other chip substrates, serves as a crucial insulator for CPUs and has become an integral component in personal computers. The Solder On Pad (SOP) technique enhances the mountability of its flip chip bonding process. This research delved into the microstructural and mechanical evolution of SAC305 solder joints on ABF fabricated by the SOP technique. The results reveal that a partial crack emerged at the Ti/Pt/Au/SAC305 interface after 200 thermal cycles, eventually extending to span the entire width of the solder joint following 500 cycles. The morphologies of Ni-Sn IMCs exhibited a transition from scallop-shaped to needle-shaped, and eventually to chunk- shaped. Thermal cycling significantly affected the indentation work of both <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta-\text{Sn}$</tex> and IMC phases. Decreases were observed in both the elastic and plastic work of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta-\text{Sn}$</tex> phase after thermal cycles, along with a decline in the elastic work ratio (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> IT). Consequently, the equivalent elastic modulus and hardness of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta-\text{Sn}$</tex> diminished, indicating a deterioration in its mechanical properties. A similar trend was observed in Ni-Sn IMC phase. Based on our previous research, deformation induced by CTE difference led to rotation of heterogeneous lattice, resulting in deviations in grain orientation and recrystallization. Sub-grain formation occurred concurrently with an increase in dislocation density and activation of various slip systems. The energy stored during this deformation ultimately manifested in crack propagation.

articleTitle: Design and Modeling of Non-Uniform through-Glass Vias and its Optimization Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this study on 3D ICs with glass substrates, we address the challenges of non-uniform TGVs causing signal delay and loss, especially in high-frequency circuits. We introduce a method to calculate parasitic RLGC parameters for these structures, using a Gaussian function to model sidewall roughness and enhance parameter precision. Findings show that higher tapers and roughness increase losses and delays. Validation samples fabricated via laser bonding and tested up to 40 GHz confirm the accuracy of our calculations. Additionally, by controlling the laser-induced wet etching (LIWE) process, we effectively optimize the sidewall roughness of TGVs, significantly reducing it from 2.7 µm to 32 nm.

articleTitle: Stress Analysis and Gray Relation Optimization of QFP Solder Joints Under Torsional and Bending Loading
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The Quad Flat Pack (QFP) technology not only meets the needs of component miniaturization and the increase in the number of 1/0 terminals, but also provides a solution for low-cost, excellent heat dissipation, and high-frequency applications. The reliability of the QFP solder joints is closely related to the overall performance of the electronic device, so this paper is based on ANSYS to analyze and optimize the stress of QFP solder joints under torsion and bending loading conditions. Four factors, namely, solder joint width, solder joint thickness, PCB thickness and solder type, and four-level design orthogonal test are selected, and the influence degree of each factor on the stress of solder joints under two kinds of loading is ranked based on Range Analysis, and then further analysis of variance (ANOV A) is used to conclude that the PCB thickness and solder type have significant influence on both torsional and bending stresses, and the width of the solder joints and the thickness of the solder joints are not significant. Finally, a bi-objective optimization of the maximum solder joint stresses under two loading conditions is carried out by the gray correlation degree, and the optimal parameter combinations under two loading conditions are derived: the width of the solder joints is 0.50 mm, the thickness of the solder joints is 0.11 mm, the thickness of the PCB is 1.0 mm, and the solder material is 62Sn36Pb2Ag. Compared to the original scheme, the maximum stresses of solder joints of the optimized combinations in the two loading conditions are reduced by 6.2 MPa and 8.1 MPa, respectively, which achieve the goal of optimization of solder joint stresses. Compared with the original scheme, the maximum stress of solder joints in the two loading states of this optimized combination is reduced by 6.2 MPa and 8.1 MPa, which achieves the goal of optimizing the stress of solder joints.

articleTitle: Electro-Thermo-Mechanical Simulation Analysis Of Multichip SiC MOSFET Power Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Compared to the traditional single-sided cooling (SSC) power module, the double-sided cooling (DSC) power module has become a rapidly growing research field in the electric vehicle (EV) sector. However, current sharing and thermal coupling issues among multichip modules are still big challenges in the double-sided cooling silicon carbide (SiC) MOSFET power module. In this paper, a new multichip Flip chip double-sided cooling modules (FCDSC) design scheme is proposed. The design incorporates the Gate-free wire and all-sintered silver method to fabricate the module, while the module spacer is made of CuMo material. In a simple straight layout, the distance between adjacent dies is large enough to avoid heat concentration and junction temperature differences resulting from the thermal coupling effect. Thermal, electrical, and mechanical properties of the multichip FCDSC power module were analyzed from the aspects of electrothermal coupling, under different power losses, temperatures, and temperature cycling, and electrical test. The multichip FCDSC modules have a better heat dissipation effect than the conventional modules and the thermo-mechanical stresses caused by the mismatch of the coefficients of thermal expansion (CTE) are lower and the parasitic inductance of the modules has been reduced, achieved a notable reduction of 12% in current imbalance, ensuring impressive current equalization.

articleTitle: Molecular Simulation Study on Sputter-Deposited Copper-Titanium UBM for Wafer-Level Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the continuous increase in functionality and feature size of heterogeneous integrated module, the three-dimensional integration technology has emerged<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[12]</sup>. The interconnection between the convex points is crucial for achieving chip three-dimensional stacking, and the preparation of high-reliability micro-convex points is of great significance for the further development of microelectronic packaging technology<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[13]</sup>. One of the key steps in the fabrication of wafer convex points is the UBM (Underball Metal) process. During the preparation of the UBM thin film, a chemical reaction occurs between the Cu film and the Si substrate, resulting in the formation of copper silicide compounds, which can lead to a decrease in the reliability of the Cu film<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[14]</sup>. Titanium, as an adhesion layer and barrier layer, enhances the adhesion between Cu and Si and reduces the diffusion of Cu into Si. Currently, research on Ti substrates and Cu films is limited to experimental studies<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[15]</sup>, and the mechanism of the interaction between Ti substrates and Cu films is not yet clear. In this study, a deposition model was established using molecular dynamics, with Ti as the substrate and Cu as the deposited atoms, to simulate the physical vapor deposition (PVD) process of Cu atoms deposited on the Ti substrate<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[16]</sup>. The study investigated the effects of incident energy, substrate temperature, and incident angle on the growth of Cu atomic deposition on the Ti substrate. The changes in film surface roughness and layer coverage during the process were specifically analyzed. The research showed that during the deposition sputtering process, incident energy is the most critical factor. When the incident energy is 0.1 eV, the film grows in an island-like structure; when the incident energy is 10 eV, the film grows in a layered structure. At a substrate temperature of 300K, in the 0th layer at the interface between the film and the substrate, only a few atoms undergo diffusion, with Cu atoms accounting for 0.05 and Ti atoms accounting for 0.12 in the 0th and 1st layers, respectively. When the temperature is raised to 500K, the degree of interface mixing increases, and the strength of interface mixing further increases, with Cu atoms accounting for 0.32 and Ti atoms accounting for 0.3 in the 0th and 1st layers, respectively. The impact of incident angle is relatively small, with lower incident angles resulting in better film quality. When the incident angle is 0°, the root mean square roughness is 2.056A, and when the incident angle is increased to 45°, the root mean square roughness is 2.4003A, indicating an increase in surface roughness. However, at this point, the Cu film surface exhibits a “groove” shape, which reduces the film quality. The research results have deepened the understanding of the mechanism of the interaction between the Ti substrate and Cu film in the UBM process, and provided valuable theoretical references and basis for optimizing process parameters.

articleTitle: Research on mechanism of improving the cut-off frequency of terahertz Schottky diodes in air-bridge structures by structure optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In the realm of air bridge structures for Schottky barrier diodes operating in the millimetre wave or terahertz band, cut-off frequency serves as a critical metric for gauging device performance. This research holds significance in guiding device design and enhancing performance by refining the device's architecture, thereby reducing capacitance values and elevating cut-off frequency without adding complexity to the manufacturing process. In this study, we investigate how the shape and spacing of mesas or pads impact device capacitance through electrostatic field simulations, leveraging Maxwell's capacitance matrix and mutual capacitance matrix. Simulation analysis and experimental validation reveal that devices with circular Schottky contact electrode pads and minimal pad area exhibit lower capacitance values. Furthermore, we observe that the capacitance of the device initially decreases and then increases with the length of the air bridge. An optimal air bridge length exists that minimizes the capacitance of the device. This research offers valuable insights for refining these devices.

articleTitle: Ageing Characteristics of Novel Thermal Interface Materials Based on Poly(Ionic Liquid)s and Liquid Metal
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Thermal interface materials (TIMs) play a crucial role in managing heat transfer in electronics. However, the high-density chiplet packaging also poses challenges to the mechanical reliability of TIMs. The conventional organic silicon system faces technical hurdles such as poor flexibility and weak adhesion, necessitating the development of next-generation TIMs. Previous studies have demonstrated that poly(ionic liquid)s (PILs) exhibit superior adhesion and mechanical properties compared to conventional polymer matrices, alongside self-healing capabilities. These characteristics make PIL-based TIMs feasible. To further validate their practical viability, in-depth studies on their thermal, mechanical, and reliability properties are needed. In this study, we investigated the preparation and aging behavior of TIM based on poly(ionic liquid)s and liquid metal. These TIMs were synthesized by simply combining PILs with liquid metal in solvent, followed by drying. Their physical characteristics, including thermal conductivity and mechanical properties, were thoroughly analyzed. To assess the reliability via aging characteristics of PILs-based TIMs, we employed X-ray chip inspection system to observe coverage variations of TIMs under different aging conditions. Our results show that these TIMs exhibit excellent thermal stability. After high temperature storage aging tests, the coverage of pure P[OVIm]NTf<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and P[OVIm]NTf<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/LM (18 vol%) were maintained at 99.15% and 99.12%, respectively, with coverage decreases of only 0.84% and 0.71%. This minimal reduction in coverage demonstrates their suitability for practical applications. In summary, our study emphasizes the aging performance of poly(ionic liquid)s-based TIMs and underscores their potential as replacements for conventional organic silicon systems. This research provides valuable insights into the preparation of high-performance chip-level TIMs.

articleTitle: Pool Boiling Enhancement of Copper Powder-Mesh Composite Surface Based on Screen Printing for High-Power Electronics Cooling
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the rapid development of high-power electronic devices, heat dissipation has become one of the key issues limiting evolution. Pool boiling, as a typical phase change heat transfer technology, is a promising solution to this high-power heat dissipation problem. The pursuit of efficient pool boiling based on the structural surface has been a research goal. In this study, a copper powder-mesh composite surface was proposed based on screen printing technology to optimize pool boiling performance. This novel composite surface is obtained by locally screen printing of ultra-fine copper powder in copper mesh. The optimized composite surface achieves a critical heat flux (CHF) of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$214.1\ \mathrm{W}/\text{cm}^{2}$</tex> and a heat transfer coefficient (HTC) of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$38.4\ \mathrm{W}/(\text{cm}^{2}\cdot \mathrm{K})$</tex> at a heat flux of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$90.7 \mathrm{W}/\text{cm}^{2}$</tex>, which is improved by 116.3% and 644.2% over conventional smooth copper surfaces, respectively. The combined fine pores of the micro-powder and high permeability of the copper mesh enable rapid bubble formation and effective liquid supply, preventing dry-out phenomenon and significantly enhancing the pool boiling heat transfer performance. Benefitting from flexible and reliable screen-printing technology, this locally printed composite surface shows great potential for thermal application in high-power electronic devices.

articleTitle: Vertical Thermal Design and Modeling for Integrated Power Amplifier WBLGA SiP Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: System-in-Package (SiP) technology is pivotal for attaining high performance and miniaturization in power electronics, steering design trends. Mandatory integration of power amplifiers for uninterrupted signal transmission exacerbates thermal issues due to prolonged high-power operation, necessitating low-power limitations to maintain temperature standards within SiP packging. This work establishes thermal resistance nodes, facilitating the development of a 3D thermal resistance network model for a WBLGA-64Pin SiP packaging, quantitatively examining key heat dissipation impediments. It highlights substrate and die attach materials as prime targets for thermal resistance optimization. A novel vertical configuration for the PA chip employing solder mask apertures, high thermal conductivity die attach materials, a 7x7 GND pad array, and inter-metal layer substrate vias is introduced, significantly reducing junction-die attach <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{R}_{\text{JD}})$</tex> and die attach-substrate <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{R}_\text{DS})$</tex> resistances, thereby optimizing the junction-to-ambient thermal resistance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{R}_\text{JA})$</tex> of the SiP. Comprehensive analyses on these modifications illustrate improved thermal flow dynamics within the PA chip, culminating in an optimized SiP. Results reveal that, relative to conventional approaches, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{R}_\text{JA}$</tex> of the optimized SiP package structure with a 25-array substrate via configuration has been reduced by 63.26%, thereby enabling the power handling of the PA chip to be elevated from 0.49 W to 1.74 W, representing a 255.10% increase. Moreover, on the basis of enhancing the substrate's heat dissipation capability, substituting the die attach material in the DA layer or concurrently improving the heat dissipation at the underside of the package substrate proves effective in augmenting the thermal management capabilities of the WBLGA power chip.

articleTitle: Forming Mechanism of Cu@Ag Composite Preforms by Electromagnetic Compaction for Power Electronics
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Unlike conventional solder preforms, Cu@Ag composite solder joint can be directly achieved at low temperatures and pressure by Cu@Ag composite preforms prepared through the electromagnetic compaction (EMC) technology. The high compactness of the preforms is mainly attributed to the extreme force applied to the Cu@Ag powders in a rapid time during the forming process. In this work. the rapid forming mechanism of Cu@Ag preforms was elaborated. The Cu@Ag solder preforms were prepared at different compacting voltages. By observing the microstructure and element distribution, it was found that the compactness of the Cu@Ag composite preforms improved as the voltage increased. Diffusion interconnection phenomenon occurred between different Cu@Ag particles, as well as at the Cu core/Ag shell interfaces. The finite element simulation of the compacting process revealed that the Cu@Ag particles were plastically deformed during the forming process, while the stresses and equivalent strains were concentrated in the bonding area of the particles. Moreover, molecular dynamics simulations were also used to investigate the interfacial diffusions at the particle/particle and core/shell interfaces. It was noted that the increasing voltage enhanced the diffusion degree and the compactness of the Cu@Ag solder preforms. Additionally, the dislocation evolutions and numbers were also analyzed to deeply understand the deformation mechanism during the EMC forming process.

articleTitle: High Inductance Density Solenoid Inductors Based on Glass Blind Groove for 3-D Glass Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Nowadays, the manufacture of glass-based integrated devices are typically accomplished using the through glass vias (TGVs) and redistribution layer (RDL) technologies. However, traditional RDL using photolithography is a complex and costly process, and inevitably introduces considerable parasitic parameters at the junction of surface lines and vias. To address these challenges, a proactive approach involving the prefabrication of glass blind grooves has emerged. Nevertheless, current blind groove fabrication relies on lithography and etching, which impose limitations on aspect ratio and shape control. In this paper, based on TGV technology, a novel approach is proposed to replace the traditional RDL process with glass blind groove technology, and the reliability of the glass blind groove is analyzed. This strategy has significantly simplified the process steps and reduced manufacturing costs, and both blind grooves and through-vias can be simultaneously produced by the laser-induced wet etching (LIWE) technology. Glass blind grooves can be achieved with an adjustable aspect ratio. As an example, an inductor using glass blind groove technology is fabricated and measured. An inductance density of 65.7 nH/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex> factor of 40 can be achieved. The proposed 3-D solenoid inductor can be demonstrated a dual advantage of high integration and performance, which provides a new idea for the preparation of three-dimensional integrated devices.

articleTitle: Simulation of Quantum Chip Packaging Based on Superconducting Material Interconnection System
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the rapid development of big data, artificial intelligence, Internet of Things and other technologies, quantum computers have emerged. It has unparalleled advantages in the fields of complex problem optimization, physical system simulation and encryption. Among them, superconducting quantum computing has become the mainstream direction of quantum computer development due to its advantages of scalability and process compatibility. However, there is no mature process integration scheme for large-scale quantum computer packaging technology with more than 100 bits. In this paper, for the packaging requirements of general-purpose large-bit superconducting quantum chips, a process simulation study based on the interconnection system of low-temperature superconducting In bumps and Al bonding filaments is carried out. Through the optimization of the interconnection structure of the package box structure, SMA terminals, high-speed substrate and other interconnection structures, the parasitic capacitance-generating structure is localized, electromagnetic leakage patterns are clarified, and a multilevel interconnection scheme with good electromagnetic shielding and low loss is obtained. Optimization of In bump and Al bonding process, the interconnect optimization scheme of substrate slotting and three-wire bonding is obtained, with insertion loss > -ldB and reflection loss >-20dB. The overall insertion loss of the multilevel interconnect structure is > -3dB and reflection loss >-15dB, which meets the demand of high-quality signal transmission. The results of this study demonstrate the quantum chip signal transmission and simulation modeling method, and provide a new idea for the cross-scale finite element electromagnetic simulation of superconducting quantum chips.

articleTitle: Thermal Conductivity Simulation of Sintered Nano-Silver for High-Power Electronic Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Under the working conditions of high-power electronic devices, the heat generated by electronic chips has been attracting much attention to be designed and optimized to be transferred using various methods. Die-attach materials with higher thermal conductivity are preferred to efficiently dissipate the heat generated during chip operation. Optimal thermal management ensures the operational capacity of electronic devices, especially under harsh working scenarios, and improves the reliability of high-power electronic chips for long-term and reliable service. Previous studies have shown that porosity and pore distribution have significant impacts on the heat transfer performance of sintered materials with mesoscale defects. In this paper, a mesoscale finite element model is established to evaluate the thermal conductivity of sintered nano-silver in a typical double-sided cooling packaging structure for high-power modules, exploring the effects of porosity and pore distribution on thermal conductivity. This provides a theoretical guideline for improving the mechanical reliability of electronic packaging materials and structures. Based on the Fourier's law, the thermal conductivity of sintered nano-silver materials is theoretically estimated. To further improve the prediction accuracy in practice by considering mesoscale defects, two boundary conditions (heat flux-in and heat flux-out) are applied in the mesoscale finite element model of the die-attach materials, and the accuracy of the predicted thermal conductivity is verified. Finally, by incorporating additional parameters into the finite element model, the influences of pore characteristics and arrangement on the heat transfer performance of the sintered nano-silver material are discussed and summarized. The results show that pores significantly hinder heat transfer within the material, and heat concentration around the pores causes the temperature gradient inside the sintered layer to become inhomogeneous, leading to uneven thermal expansion and deformation. Therefore, it is recommended to optimize the sintering process and parameters to achieve a more uniform pore distribution and lower porosity. This improvement is crucial for enhancing the heat dissipation of high-power electronic devices, particularly under harsh operating conditions.

articleTitle: Efficient Synthesis and Excellent Performance of Low-Temperature Sintering Cu@Ni Nanoparticle Materials for Power Electronic Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Sintering interconnection technology based on Cu nanopaste material, due to its outstanding electrical, thermal properties, and electrical-migration resistance, it is gradually emerging as an appealing alternative for power electronic packaging in third-generation semiconductor devices (the service temperature of >350 °C). However, the characteristics of Cu nanoparticles (NPs), such as susceptibility to oxidation and the requirement for reduced-atmosphere sintering, constrain their application into AI chip and other fields of CSP and SiP. In this work, we successfully synthesized small-molecular-weight organics (~OAM) coated Cu@Ni NPs with small size (42 nm) and uniform distribution by one-step reduction after directly mixing conventional copper salts and nickel salts. Results demonstrated that the rapid coating of small-molecular-weight organics leads to the formation of a uniform and dense core-shell structure of Cu@Ni NPs, where the oxidation of Cu core is inhibited. Meanwhile, the sintering joints with a high shear strength of ~60.5 MPa were prepared through ultrasonic-assisted sintering (UAS) Cu@Ni nanopaste, significantly surpassing the shear strength of SnPb solder. The strengthening effect of joints may originate from the removal of residual organics by the unique friction effect of USW, and the ultrafast diffusion between Cu and Ni atoms with the increase of pressure and temperature. This offers broad commercial prospects for packaging in third-generation semiconductors and other power devices.

articleTitle: Influence of Copper Substrate Microstructure on the Wettability of Sn-Based Brazing Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Electronic products continue to evolve towards miniaturization, lightness, and high performance, thus setting higher standards for microelectronic packaging technology. The wettability of solder on the substrate surface typically affects the quality and lifespan of solder joints. As a cutting-edge precision manufacturing technology, femtosecond laser can create various micro-nano composite structures on material surfaces. Therefore, three types of micro-structures were prepared using femtosecond laser, and the impact of variations in microstructure pattern spacing and shape on wettability was analyzed. The study found that the wetting angle was smallest on the circular structure, and as the spacing increased, the wetting angle consistently showed a trend of initially increasing and then decreasing. These intriguing findings offer new perspectives for future analysis of wettability.

articleTitle: 2.5D Chip-Package Warpage Analysis Using RVE-Based Homogenization Method
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: 2.5D package enhances interconnect density and system performance by integrating chips on an interposer silicon layer, simplifying vertical connections. Despite its benefits, challenges like warpage due to thermal expansion coefficient mismatches and complex multiscale structures hinder its practical application. Traditional finite element analysis struggles with the size differences in elements from TSVs to overall package structures. This study introduces an equivalent modeling strategy using homogenization theory and the Representative Volume Element (RVE) method to simplify the complex 2.5D package into a multi-layer plate model. Finite element analysis with this equivalent model accurately predicts warpage, aligning well with detailed model results, validating the model's accuracy. Sensitivity analysis on structural parameters and material properties further investigates their impact on warpage. The findings offer valuable insights for optimizing 2.5D package design and improving IC performance.

articleTitle: Fabrication of Crack-Free LTCC Substrates with Large Aspect Ratio and Metal Pillar Embedded Cavities
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Multilayer low temperature co-fired ceramics (LTCC) substrates have excellent electromechanical properties and flexible structural design, making them a preferred choice for fabricating high-density integrated microsystems. However, manufacturing complex embedded structures and large cavities in LTCC substrates still poses significant technical challenges. This work aims to improve the manufacturing techniques to address these issues and achieve reliable production of LTCC substrates with embedded metal pillar arrays and high aspect ratio microchambers. The side length of the chamber cavity is as large as 22 mm and the width-to-depth ratio is more than 38. Fugitive tapes are used as sacrificial materials. Several key fabrication processes are investigated, including laser drilling/cutting of single ceramic layers, sacrificial material drilling and firing, lamination, and low-temperature co-firing. A new two-step segmented lamination process has been proposed to prevent defects from occurring under isostatic pressure. Substrates free of cracks, delamination or collapses have been successfully fabricated and full evaporation of SVM has been achieved. The interlayer misalignment is smaller than 30 μm and the surface warpage is merely 13 μm The pressure resistance of the microchamber cavity in the substrate reaches 6 atm or more. Due to their excellent manufacturing quality, these LTCC substrates show great potential in high-efficiency liquid cooling and high-pressure applications.

articleTitle: Cross-Scale Finite Element Analysis of PCBA Reflow Soldering Processes
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Printed circuit board assembly (PCBA) is an important integrated circuit product. For the reliability of printed circuit board assembly in the reflow soldering manufacturing process, this paper establishes a printed circuit board (PCB) model based on the Meso scale finite element method to reflect the wiring distribution of wiring layers, and establishes a package structure including substrate, chip, epoxy plastic sealing material, solder joints, The package structure and PCB constitutes the model of the printed circuit board assembly, Then presents a finite element analysis of the reflow process of a PCBA, systematically and comprehensively researches the effect of temperature on the warping deformation and stress distribution of the PCBA in the process of reflow soldering and conducts experimental verification. The results show that the simulation results and experimental results of PCB warpage are increased with the increase of temperature and decreased with the decrease of temperature, and the relative error of warpage between measured and simulated values are within 15%. The stress value increases with the increase of temperature, and the maximum stress value is 362.8 MPa. The stress distribution is related to the distribution of wiring. The warpage deformation of the package body and the PCB affect each other due to the molding of the solder joints. The location of the maximum stress in the package is on the solder joint array in the package, and the maximum stress value is 31.5 MPa. The solder joints with the maximum stress value are located at the edges of the solder joint array, and the maximum stress and strain regions are at the upper surface edges of the solder joints. This work contributes to the reliability study and optimized design of integrated circuit products.
